**The exposition of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾ (12:1)**

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: We have already mentioned the differences of the people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) concerning the interpretation of His words, ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book﴾, and the view we choose regarding its interpretation has been given earlier, sufficiently to make its repetition here unnecessary. [[See what has passed, pp. 9–12.]]

* *

As for His words, ﴿These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾, the people of ta'wil differed in its interpretation.

Some of them said: its meaning is: ﴿These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾: it made clear its lawful and its unlawful, its right guidance and its guidance.

Mention of those who said this:

18768. Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, saying: al-Walid ibn Salama al-Filastini narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid informed me, from his father, concerning the words of God, may He be exalted: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾, he said: It made clear its lawful and its unlawful. [[The report 18768: al-Walid ibn Salama al-Filastini al-Urdunni, judge of Jordan, a liar who fabricated hadith and attributed them to trustworthy narrators. Biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/6, Mizan al-I'tidal 3:271, and Lisan al-Mizan 6:222. And "'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid ibn Jabr" is extremely weak; Sufyan said: a liar. Ahmad said: "He did not hear from his father; he is nothing." Passed as no. 636.]]

18769. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words: ﴿These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾, he said: Indeed, by God, it is clear; God made clear its guidance and its right direction. [[In the printed edition: "tarkibuhu" (its composition); in the manuscript: "barliyhi". I have inferred the correct reading from the word that follows it.]]

18770. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His words: ﴿These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾, he said: God made clear its right direction and its guidance.

* *

Others said regarding this:

18771. Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, saying: al-Walid ibn Salama narrated to us, saying: Thawr ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Mu'adh, that he said concerning the words of God, may He be mighty and majestic: ﴿the Clear Book﴾, he said: It made clear the letters that fell from the tongues of the non-Arabs, and they are six letters. [[The report 18771: al-Walid ibn Salama al-Filastini, a liar, passed as no. 18768. Thawr ibn Yazid al-Kala'i, trustworthy and sound in hadith, passed as no. 3196. Khalid ibn Ma'dan ibn Abi Karib al-Kala'i, a trustworthy Successor, whom the group related from, passed as nos. 2070 and 9224. The flaw in this report is al-Walid ibn Salama.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that it should be said: its meaning is: these are the verses of the Clear Book for whoever recites it and reflects upon what is in it of its lawful and unlawful, its prohibitions, and the rest of what it contains of the various kinds of its meanings. This is because God, may His praise be majestic, informed that it is "clear" (mubin), and He did not restrict its clarification to some of what is in it rather than all of it; so it applies to all of it, since all of it is clear regarding what is in it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verses 2–3:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an, that you might understand﴾ (2)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed We have sent down this Clear Book as an Qur'an in Arabic, to the Arabs, because their tongue and their speech is Arabic. So We sent down this Book in their language, so that they might understand it and comprehend from it. This is His saying: ﴿that you might understand﴾.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories, in that We have revealed to you this Qur'an, though you were before it among the unaware﴾ (3)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His praise, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "We relate to you," O Muhammad, "the best of stories," by Our revelation to you of this Qur'an, through which We inform you about past reports, the accounts of earlier nations, and the books We sent down in bygone ages [[See the explanation of "al-qasas" (narratives) above, p. 539, footnote 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿though you were before it among the unaware﴾. He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Though you, O Muhammad, were before We revealed it to you among those unaware of that, not knowing it or any part of it, [[See the explanation of "al-ghafla" (heedlessness) above, p. 545, footnote 2, and the references there.]] as related by:

18772 Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾ from the earlier books and the past affairs of God among the nations = ﴿though you were before it among the unaware﴾.

* *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in response to his Companions' request that he relate stories to them.

Mention of the narration to that effect:

18773 Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me, saying: Hakkam al-Razi narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Amr al-Mala'i, from Ibn Abbas, who said: They said: "O Messenger of God, if only you would relate (stories) to us!" He said: Then it was revealed: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾. [[The two reports 18773 and 18774: "Ayyub ibn Sayyar, Abu Abd al-Rahman" — I have not found him under this kunya; rather they mention "Ayyub ibn Sayyar al-Zuhri al-Madani," whom al-Bukhari gave the kunya "Abu Sayyar." Al-Bukhari said: "munkar al-hadith" (rejected in narration), and Ibn Hibban said: "He used to invert chains and raise mursal reports." He is biographed in al-Kabir 1/1/417, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/248, Mizan al-I'tidal 1:134, and Lisan al-Mizan 1:482, and it seems he is the same person; he has two kunyas, "Abu Abd al-Rahman" and "Abu Sayyar." He transmitted the first as a marfu' report traced to Ibn Abbas, and the second as a mawquf report. See also the hadith of Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i, traced as marfu' to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, no. 18776. This may be among what Ayyub ibn Sayyar inverted.]]

18774 Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Sayyar Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Amr ibn Qays, who said: They said: "O Prophet of God," and he mentioned the like of it.

18775 Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Awn ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) became weary with a weariness, so they said: "O Messenger of God, tell us!" So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿God has sent down the best discourse﴾ [Qur'an 39:23]. Then they became weary with another weariness and said: "O Messenger of God, tell us something above the discourse and below the Qur'an!" meaning the narratives. So God revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the Clear Book. Indeed We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an, that you might understand. We relate to you the best of stories in that We have revealed to you this Qur'an, though you were before it among the unaware﴾. So they wanted discourse, and He guided them to the best discourse; and they wanted narratives, and He guided them to the best narratives. [[Report 18775: "Awn ibn Abd Allah ibn Utba ibn Mas'ud," who narrated from his father and his paternal uncle in mursal form. This report al-Suyuti cited in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:3 through Awn ibn Abd Allah from Ibn Mas'ud, so it is mursal. Al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul: 203.]]

18776 Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Khallad al-Saffar informed us, from Amr ibn Qays, [from Amr ibn Murra], from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd, who said: The Qur'an was sent down upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and he recited it to them for a time. Then they said: "O Messenger of God, if only you would relate (stories) to us!" So God revealed: ﴿Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾, to His saying: ﴿that you might understand﴾, the verse. He said: Then he recited it to them for a time, and they said: "O Messenger of God, if only you would narrate to us!" So God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿God has sent down the best discourse, a Book consistent, repeating﴾ [Qur'an 39:23]. Khallad said: Another man added to it, they said: "O Messenger of God—" or Abu Yahya said: a word was lost from my book— so God revealed: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of God?﴾ [Qur'an 57:16]. [[Report 18776: "Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ghalib al-Baghdadi, al-Attar, al-Darir," kunya "Abu Yahya," the teacher of al-Tabari. He narrated from Ibn Ulayya, Abd Allah ibn Numayr, al-Shafi'i, Wahb ibn Jarir and others. Trustworthy; biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/266, and Tarikh Baghdad 5:306. "Amr ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi al-Anqazi," trustworthy, acceptable in narration, passed as nos. 6139, 12369, 13258. "Khallad al-Saffar" is "Khallad ibn Isa al-Abdi," also said to be "Khallad ibn Muslim," whose kunya is "Abu Muslim." Trustworthy, passed as no. 3014. "Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i," trustworthy, passed many times. "Amr ibn Murra al-Muradi al-Jamali," trustworthy, whose narrations were recorded by the whole group, and he is the one who narrates from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, passed many times. His name was missing from the chain in the manuscript and printed edition; I added it between brackets, because Ibn Kathir quoted this report in his tafsir 4:411 from this place in al-Tabari's tafsir, and it appeared correctly there, as it is recorded by al-Hakim and others, as you will see in the takhrij. "Mus'ab ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas," a trustworthy Successor, whom the whole group narrated from, narrating from his father, passed as nos. 9841, 11450, 16633. This report was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2:345 through this same chain, and he said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. But al-Hakim said: "Khallad ibn Muslim narrated to us," and al-Dhahabi said: "The correct form is: Khallad Abu Muslim al-Saffar, and his father's name is Isa," and I had already noted the difference regarding his father's name. Al-Wahidi also quoted it from al-Hakim in Asbab al-Nuzul: 203, and neither of them contains this addition from Khallad at the end of the hadith.

Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:3, adding its attribution to Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, al-Bazzar, Abu Ya'la, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿When Joseph said to his father: "O my father, I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me"﴾ (4)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And if you were, O Muhammad, among the heedless concerning the report of Joseph son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, [then know that] when he said to his father Jacob son of Isaac: ﴿O my father, I saw eleven stars﴾ ;" meaning: I saw in my dream eleven stars.

* *

It has been said: The dreams of the prophets were revelation (wahy).

18778. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me﴾, he said: The dreams of the prophets were revelation.

18779. Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿I saw eleven stars﴾, he said: The dream concerning them was revelation.

* *

It is mentioned that the eleven stars he saw in his dream, prostrating along with the sun and the moon, were:

18780. Ali ibn Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from Jabir, who said: A Jewish man called "Bustana the Jew" came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to him: "O Muhammad, inform me about the stars that Joseph saw prostrating to him: what are their names?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent and did not answer him with anything, and Gabriel descended to him and informed him of their names.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then sent for him and said: "Will you believe if I inform you of their names?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "Jarban, al-Tariq, al-Dhayyal, Dhu'l-Kanafat, [[In the printed edition: "Dhu'l-Kitfayn"; I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what Ibn Kathir quoted from this place in al-Tabari's tafsir in his own tafsir. As for the rest of the names, I was unable to vouch for their vocalisation.]] Qabis, Wathab, Amudan, al-Faliq, al-Musbih, al-Darrouh, Dhu'l-Far', al-Diya', and al-Nur." The Jew said: "By God, these are indeed their names!"

[[The report 18780: al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr al-Fazari, abandoned (matruk), has passed several times, under nos. 249, 5523, 5792, 11335. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, namely Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Sabit, is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), has passed several times, the last under no. 11526. He narrates from Jabir as a mursal (a report in which the companion is omitted from the chain). It was said to Yahya ibn Ma'in: "Did Abd al-Rahman hear from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas?" He said: "No." It was asked: "From Abu Umama?" He said: "No." It was asked: "From Jabir?" He said: "No, it is mursal." This report was cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:4, and he said: "Sa'id ibn Mansur, al-Bazzar, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Uqayli, Ibn Hibban in al-Du'afa', Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim and he authenticated it, al-Hakim and he authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym and al-Bayhaqi together in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa, narrated it from Jabir." I did not find the place of this report in al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim, but it is strange that he authenticated it, for this report was transmitted solely by al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr, who is weak in narration and abandoned. Al-Jawzajani even said: "He is fallen (saqit) because of his partiality and the wonders in his narrations; he is the transmitter of the hadith about the stars of Joseph." Al-Uqayli denounced his narration about naming the stars that Joseph, peace be upon him, saw. See Tahdhib al-Tahdhib and Mizan al-l'tidal 1:268, where he mentions the report via Ibn Hibban with its chain. See there also the differences over the names of the stars, and consult Dala'il al-Nubuwwa of Abu Nu'aym, for I did not find it there.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me﴾ means: I saw the sun and the moon prostrating in my dream.

* *

And [He said] "prostrating" (sajidin) [using the masculine plural form], although the stars, the sun and the moon are referred to with the feminine forms "fa'ila" and "fa'ilat", not with the suffix of the masculine plural (waw and nun). [Because the waw and nun] are the marker of the plural of the names of male human beings, or jinn, or angels. [[What is between the brackets, I think, has fallen out of the text, so I have added it so that the sentence is correct.]] It was said in this manner because prostration (sujud) is an action of those whose male names take the yā' and nūn or the wāw and nūn in the plural. So the plural of their names was placed in the manner of the plural of the names of those who perform this act, as in His saying: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings﴾ [Surah al-Naml: 18].

* *

And [He said] "I saw them" (ra'aytuhum), although it had been said: "Indeed I saw eleven stars" ; so the verb was repeated. This is in accordance with the dialect of one who says: "I spoke to your brother, I spoke to him," for emphasis of the verb through repetition.

* *

It has also been said: The eleven stars were his brothers, and the sun and the moon were his parents.

Those who said this:

18781. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿When Joseph said to his father: O my father, I saw eleven stars﴾: the stars are his brothers, eleven stars; ﴿and the sun and the moon﴾, meaning by that: his parents.

18782. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon﴾ ... the verse, he said: He saw his parents and his brothers prostrating to him. Then if it is said to him: "From whom?" He said: "If it is true, then Ibn 'Abbas has explained it."

18783. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿eleven stars, and the sun and the moon, I saw them prostrating to me﴾, he said: The stars: his brothers; and the sun and the moon: his parents.

18784. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His saying: ﴿I saw eleven stars﴾: his brothers; "and the sun": his mother; "and the moon": his father.

18785. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan said: [They were] his parents and his brothers.

18786. It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿I saw eleven stars﴾: they are the brothers of Joseph; ﴿and the sun and the moon﴾: they are his parents.

18787. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿O my father, I saw eleven stars﴾, the verse: [They were] his parents and his brothers. He said: His brothers disparaged him, and they were prophets, [[The manuscript is also like this, or something close to "nafa" (banished), written without dots, and I do not know what he intended.]] and they said: "Was he not content that his brothers should prostrate to him, until his parents prostrated to him!" when this reached them.

* *

It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: The stars are his brothers, and "the sun and the moon" are his father and his maternal aunt; [this is] from an unpraiseworthy line of transmission, so I dislike mentioning it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 5:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, lest they plot against you a scheme. Indeed, Satan is to man a clear enemy."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, mighty is His remembrance, says: Ya'qub said to his son Yusuf: "O my son, do not relate your vision", this one, "to your brothers, lest they envy you" [[See the explanation of "al-qasas" (relating) above, p. 551, footnote 1, and the references there.]] "and so they plot against you a scheme", meaning: they will seek to harm you with ruinous designs, show you enmity, and obey Satan concerning you. [[See the explanation of "al-kayd" (scheming) above, p. 361, footnote 1, and the references there.]] ﴿Indeed, Satan is to man a clear enemy﴾, meaning: Indeed Satan is an enemy to Adam and his offspring; he has made his enmity clear to them and manifested it. [[See the explanation of "mubin" (clear) in the linguistic indexes above, under the root (b-y-n).]] He means: beware of Satan lest he incite your brothers against you through envy of you, if you relate your vision to them.

* *

Ya'qub said this because he had already perceived envy from his brothers before that, [[In the printed edition: "hasadahu" with a possessive suffix; I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is very good.]] as:

18788 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: Ya'qub settled in Syria, and his concern was Yusuf and his brother. His brothers envied him when they saw their father's love for him. Yusuf saw in a dream that eleven stars, and the sun and the moon, were prostrating to him. He related it to his father, who said: ﴿O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, lest they plot against you a scheme﴾, the verse.

* *

The scholars of Arabic differed concerning the reason for the particle "lam" (to) in His saying ﴿lest they plot against you a scheme﴾ (fa-yakiduu laka kaydan).

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: its meaning is: "so they devise for you a scheme." It is unlike His saying: ﴿If you are interpreters of dreams﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 43], where they intended that the verb reach the object through "li" just as it reaches it through "bi" (the preposition). As you say: "I presented him food" (qaddamtu lahu ta'aman), meaning "I presented it to him." And He said: ﴿The food that you have sent forward for them﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 48]. Similar is His saying: ﴿Say: "Allah guides to the truth"﴾ [Surah Yunus: 35]. He said: If you wish, it may be that ﴿fa-yakiduu laka kaydan﴾ means "fa-yakiduuka" (so they scheme against you), and the "lam" is like His saying: ﴿for their Lord they fear﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 154], and it was said "li-rabbihim yarhabun" when it is in place of "rabbahum yarhabun."

* *

Some of them said: the "lam" was added here as it is added in their saying "I praised you" (hamidtu laka) and "I thanked you" (shakartu laka), and "I praised you" (hamidtuka) and "I thanked you" (shakartuka). He said: this is a "lam" brought in by the verb. So likewise His saying: ﴿fa-yakiduu laka kaydan﴾ — you say: "fa-yakiduuka" or "yakiduu laka," so that "fa-yaqsudunaka" and "yaqsiduu laka" (they aim at you). He said: "kaydan" is an emphatic (infinitive of emphasis).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 6:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of events, and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, just as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise.﴾ (12:6)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, reporting the statement of Jacob to his son Joseph when he related to him his dream: ﴿And thus will your Lord choose you﴾, meaning, just as your Lord showed you the stars, the sun and the moon prostrating to you, so will your Lord choose you (yastafeekum, i.e., select you for distinction) [[See the explanation of "al-ijtiba'" (choosing) above, vol. 13, p. 341, note 1, and the references there.]], as:

18789 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr al-'Anqazi narrated to us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿And thus will your Lord choose you﴾, he said: "He will select you."

18790 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of events﴾, he said: "He chose him, selected him, and taught him the interpretation of events (ta'wil al-ahadith), which is the 'interpretation of events' (ta'wil al-ahadith)."

* *

As for His words: ﴿and teach you the interpretation of events﴾, meaning: your Lord will teach you the knowledge of what people's accounts (ahadith) will come to, concerning what they see in their dreams. That is the interpretation of dreams (ta'bir al-ru'ya). [[See the explanation of "al-ta'wil" (interpretation) above, p. 93, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

18791 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿and teach you the interpretation of events﴾, he said: "The interpretation of dreams."

18792 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿and teach you the interpretation of events﴾, he said: "The interpretation of speech: knowledge and speech." [[In the printed edition: "knowledge and forbearance (al-hilm)"; I have adopted what is in the manuscript, and it is permissible.]]

And Joseph was the most skilled of people at interpretation, and he recited: ﴿And when he reached his maturity, We gave him judgment and knowledge﴾ (12:22).

* *

As for His words: ﴿and complete His favor upon you﴾, by His choosing you, selecting you, and teaching you the interpretation of events; ﴿and upon the family of Jacob﴾, meaning: upon the people of Jacob's religion and creed, from his offspring and others [[See the explanation of "al-al" (family) above, vol. 13, p. 85, note 1, and the references there.]]; ﴿just as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac﴾, by taking the former as a friend (khalil) and rescuing him from the fire, and ransoming the latter with a great sacrifice, as in:

18793 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Abu Ishaq informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His words: ﴿and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, just as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac﴾, he said: "His favor upon Abraham was that He saved him from the fire, and upon Isaac that He saved him from slaughter."

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Knowing﴾ of the places of favor, and of who is worthy of being chosen and of the blessing, ﴿Wise﴾ in His management of His creation [[See the explanation of "Knowing" (alim) and "Wise" (hakim) in the lexical indexes under the roots ('-l-m) and (h-k-m).]].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 7:

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, in Joseph and his brothers are signs for those who ask.﴾ (12:7)

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, in Joseph and his brothers﴾ — the eleven — ﴿are signs﴾, meaning lessons and reminders [[See the entry on "ayah" (sign) in the linguistic indices under the root (a-y-y) in the preceding volumes.]] — ﴿for those who ask﴾, meaning those who ask about their news and stories. And He, may His praise be mentioned, intended by this His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

* *

That is because it is said: God, blessed and exalted, sent down this surah to His Prophet, teaching him in it what Joseph suffered from those nearest to him, his brothers, of envy, together with God's honouring of him, as consolation to him for what he would endure from those nearest to him and his relatives among the polytheists of Quraysh. [[In the printed edition: "from his harm and his relatives", but the correct reading is what I have established, and what led to it is what he had entangled himself in a few lines earlier. See the preceding note.]] Thus Ibn Ishaq used to say:

18794 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: God, blessed and exalted, only related to Muhammad the story of Joseph, and the transgression of his brothers against him and their envy of him, when he mentioned his dream, because of what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw of the transgression and envy of his people when God, mighty and majestic, honoured him with prophethood, so that he might take him as an example. [[In the printed edition: "liyatasa bihi", but I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct.]]

* *

The reciters differed over the recitation of His saying: ﴿signs for those who ask﴾. The majority of the reciters of the regional centres recited it as "āyātun" in the plural form.

* *

It is related from Mujahid and Ibn Kathir that they recited it in the singular.

* *

The more correct of the two recitations is the recitation of those who read it in the plural, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 8:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When they said: Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we, though we are a band. Indeed our father is in clear error.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed there were in Joseph and his brothers signs for the one who asks about their affair, when the brothers of Joseph [[In the printed edition: "qalu ikhwatu Yusuf" (they said: the brothers of Joseph), which is faulty; the printer misread the manuscript, where the copyist had intended to write "qalu" and then wrote "qal".]] said, ﴿Joseph and his brother [from his mother] are dearer to our father than we, though we are a band﴾, meaning: we are a group with numbers, eleven men.

* *

The "'usbah" (band) of people are ten or more; it has been said: up to fifteen. It has no singular from its own form, like the nafar (group) and the rahat (company).

* *

﴿Indeed our father is in clear error﴾: they mean, indeed our father Jacob is in error regarding his conduct, in preferring Joseph and his brother from his mother over us in affection. And by "mubin" (clear) he means that it is an error which reveals itself to be an error to whoever considers it and looks at it [[See the explanation of "mubin" in the lexical indexes earlier under (b-y-n)]].

* *

And according to what we have said on this, the people of interpretation have spoken.

Mention of those who said so:

18795. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿when they said: Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we﴾: he said, they mean Benjamin. He said: and they were ten.

18796. ... He said: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Indeed our father is in clear error﴾: he said, in error concerning our affair.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd, regarding His saying ﴿though we are a band﴾, said: "al-'usbah" is the group.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 9:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Kill Joseph, or cast him out to some land, so that your father's face will be free for you, and after him you will be a righteous people.﴾ (9)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His Majesty says: The brothers of Joseph said to one another: "Kill Joseph, or cast him out into some land of the lands," meaning a place on the earth. (So that your father's face will be free for you) means: so that your father's face will be free for you from being occupied with Joseph, for he has occupied him away from us and turned his face away from us toward him. (And after him you will be a righteous people) meaning that they would repent of killing Joseph and of the sin they would be committing in it, and by their repentance from killing him, after Joseph's destruction, they would become a righteous people.

* *

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

18798- Ibn Wakic related to us, he said: Amr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Kill Joseph, or cast him out to some land, so that your father's face will be free for you, and after him you will be a righteous people﴾, he said: "You will repent of what you have done, or of your deed."

On the interpretation of His words, "A speaker among them said, 'Do not kill Joseph, but throw him into the depths of the well; some of the travellers will pick him up, if you are going to do [anything]'" (12:10):

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, He says: A speaker among the brothers of Joseph said, "Do not kill Joseph."

* *

It has been said that the speaker of this was Ruwbil, who was a maternal cousin of Joseph.

Mention of those who said this:

18799. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "Do not kill Joseph": It was mentioned to us that he was Ruwbil, the eldest of the people, and he was a maternal cousin of Joseph, so he forbade them from killing him.

18800. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding "Kill Joseph," up to His words "if you are going to do [anything]": He said: It was mentioned to me, and Allah knows best, that the one among them who said this was Ruwbil, the eldest of the sons of Ya'qub, and he was the most upright in opinion regarding him.

18801. al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words "Do not kill Joseph": He said: He was the eldest of his brothers, and he was a maternal cousin of Joseph, so he forbade them from killing him.

* *

It has been said that the speaker of this among them was Shim'un. [[The narration no. 18831 will mention another name, that he was the speaker of that, and he is: Yahudha.]]

Mention of those who said this:

18802. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words "A speaker among them said, 'Do not kill Joseph'": He said: He was Shim'un.

* *

As for His words, "and throw him into the depths of the well," meaning: throw him into the bottom of the well, where its news is hidden.

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this.

The majority of the reciters of the people of Madinah recited it: "Ghayabat al-Jubb" in the plural.

* *

The majority of the reciters of the rest of the regions recited: "Ghayabati al-Jubb" in the singular "al-ghayabah."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The recitation with the singular is more beloved to me.

* *

And "al-Jubb" is a well.

* *

It has been said that it is the name of a well in Bayt al-Maqdis.

Mention of those who said this:

18803. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: regarding "the depths of the well," he said: a well in Bayt al-Maqdis.

18804. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words "the depths of the well": He said: a well in Bayt al-Maqdis.

* *

And "al-ghayabah" is everything that conceals something, so it is "ghayabah"; and "al-jubb" is a well that is not lined.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

18805. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding "the depths of the well," in some of its sides: at its bottom.

18806. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words "and throw him into the depths of the well," he said: in some of its sides.

18807. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, the like of it. [[Narration 18807: "al-Hasan ibn Muhammad" is al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Za'farani, the teacher of al-Tabari, biographied in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/36. "Abd al-Wahhab" is Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-Majid al-Thaqafi, who has passed many times.]]

18808. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "and throw him into the depths of the well," he said: It was said by their eldest, the one who stayed behind. He said: "al-Jubb" is a well in al-Sham.

18809. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "Throw him into the depths of the well," meaning: the well-shaft.

18810. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: "al-Jubb": the well.

* *

As for His words, "some of the travellers will pick him up," meaning: some of the passing travellers on the road will take him, "if you are going to do [anything]," meaning: if you are going to do what I say to you. It is mentioned that some of the Bedouin picked him up.

18811. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "some of the travellers will pick him up," he said: some people among the Bedouin picked him up.

* *

It is mentioned from al-Hasan al-Basri that he recited: "taltaqithu ba'du al-sayyarah" with a ta'.

18812. Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me this, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Harun, from Mutar al-Warraq, from al-Hasan.

* *

It seems that al-Hasan, in making the verb feminine with "ba'd al-sayyarah," held that the action of a part of it is the action of the whole.

The Arabs do this in the predicate of "kana" when the subject is a genitive construction (muḍāf) attached to a feminine noun, where the predicate about a part of it is a predicate about the whole. This is like the words of the poet: [[It is Jarir.]]

"I see the passing years have taken from me
As the crescent's thinning takes from the new moon"

[[This verse was previously cited, explained and its sources given at 11:86. In the manuscript and printed edition here it reads "ara", while there and in his Diwan it reads "ra'at".]]

So he said "akhadhna minni" (they have taken from me), though he began the predicate with "al-marr" (the passing), since the predicate about "al-marr" is a predicate about "al-sinin" (the years). And as another said: [[I do not know who said it.]]

"When a leader of theirs dies, another leader rises,
And the people of the villages and churches submit to him."

[[The meanings of the Qur'an by al-Farra' in the explanation of this verse.]]

So he said "fadanat lahu" (submitted to him), and the predicate was about the people of the villages, because the predicate about them is like the predicate about the villages. Whoever says this does not say "fadanat lahu ghulam Hind," because "ghulam" (the boy), if it were dropped from speech, would not be indicated by "Hind," whereas the predicate about "the village" indicates its people.

For if it were said "fadanat lahu al-qura" (the villages submitted to him), it would be known that it is a predicate about its people. Likewise "ba'd al-sayyarah": if "ba'd" were dropped and it were said "taltaqituhu al-sayyarah" (the caravan will pick him up), it would be known that the predicate is about a part or the whole, and the predicate about "al-sayyarah" indicates it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 11:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿They said, "O our father, what is [wrong] with you that you do not entrust us with Joseph while we are indeed his sincere advisers?"﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, the Exalted, says: The brothers of Joseph said to their father Ya'qub, when they had conferred among themselves and agreed upon separating him from his father: ﴿O our father, what is [wrong] with you that you do not entrust us with Joseph?﴾, so that you would leave him with us when we go out of the city to the desert, ﴿while we are indeed his sincere advisers﴾, guarding him and watching over him. [[See the explanation of "naṣaḥa lahu" (to be sincere toward him) previously, p. 305, note 2.]]

The exegesis of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Send him with us tomorrow, to enjoy himself and play, and indeed we will be his guardians﴾ (12:12)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The readers (qurra', the transmitters of the canonical recitations, or *qira'at*) differed over the recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of Medina recited it as "yarta'i wa-yal'ab," with a kasra on the ʿayn of "yarta'i" and with the yā' in "yarta'i wa-yal'ab," meaning the form *yaftaʿil* from *al-ruʿy* (pasturing): "irtaʿaytu, fa-ana artaʿī" (I pastured, so I pasture). It is as if they took the meaning of the speech to be: "Send him with us tomorrow, that he may pasture the camels and play, ﴿and indeed we will be his guardians﴾."

The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it as "arsilhu maʿanā ghadan yarta'ˈ wa-yal'ab," with the yā' in both verbs and a sukun on the ʿayn, from their saying "rataʿa fulān fī mālihi" (so-and-so indulged in his wealth), when he took his pleasure in it, enjoyed it and spent it on his desires. Among this is their saying in a proverb: "al-qayd wa-l-ratʿa" (the fetter and the comfortable life). [The proverb was recorded by al-Maydani in his *Amthal* 2:39, by al-Mufaddal al-Dabbi in his *Amthal*, p. 62, by al-Mufaddal ibn Salama in his book *al-Fakhir*, pp. 170 and 241, and in *Lisan al-ʿArab* (r-t-ʿ). Its origin is that ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣaʿq was captured by the tribe of Shakir, from Hamdan, and they treated him well. He had left his people thin, and he fled from Shakir. When he reached his people, they said: "O ʿAmr, you left us thin, and today you are fat?" He said: "The fetter and the ratʿa," and so it became a proverb. The *ratʿa* means abundance.] And from this is the saying of al-Qutami:

"Do you disbelieve after death was turned back from me,
and after your gift of a hundred luxuriant (camels)?"
[The verse was cited earlier with its takhrij and explanation, vol. 1, p. 116, note 1.]

* * *

Some of the readers of Basra recited "tartaʿ" with the nūn, and "nalʿab" with the nūn in both, with a sukun on the ʿayn of "narta'" (nartaʿ).

**18813** – Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to me, saying: al-Qasim related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Harun, who said: Abu ʿAmr used to recite "narta' wa-nalʿab" with the nūn. He said: I said to Abu ʿAmr: "How do they say 'nalʿab' (we play), when they are prophets?" He said: "They were not prophets on that day."

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The recitation most correct in my view is the recitation of the one who recites both words with the yā' and with the sukun on the ʿayn of "yarta'," because the people only asked their father to send Joseph with them, and they deceived him by telling him about their request for that, regarding what was in Joseph's sending with them of joy, delight and vigor at going out to the open desert, its spaciousness, and his playing there, not by telling him about themselves.

* * *

This is also what the people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwil) have said.

Those who said that:

**18814** – Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿Send him with us tomorrow, to enjoy himself and play﴾, he said: he means: he strives and is energetic.

**18815** – al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: ﴿yarta' wa-yal'ab﴾: he said: he amuses himself, is energetic and strives.

**18816** – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿Send him with us tomorrow, to enjoy himself and play﴾, he said: he is energetic and amuses himself.

**18817** – al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab related to us, from Saʿid, from Qatada, similar to it. [Report 18817: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Zaʿfarani. See the explanation of this chain earlier, no. 18807.]

**18818** – Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada: ﴿yarta' wa-yal'ab﴾, he said: he strives and amuses himself.

**18819** – al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to me, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: ﴿yarta' wa-yal'ab﴾, he said: he diverts himself and plays.

**18820** – It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿yarta' wa-yal'ab﴾: he diverts himself and plays.

**18821** – Ibn Wakiʿ related to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿yarta' wa-yal'ab﴾, he said: he is energetic and plays.

**18822** – ... [the chain continues]: ʿAmr related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿Send him with us tomorrow, to enjoy himself and play﴾, he said: he amuses himself.

**18823** – [The chain continues]: al-Husayn ibn ʿAli related to us, from Shaybān, from Qatada: ﴿Send him with us tomorrow, to enjoy himself and play﴾, he said: he is energetic and plays.

**18824** – al-Harith related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz related to us, saying: Nuʿaym ibn Damdam al-ʿAmiri related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding His words: ﴿Send him with us tomorrow, to enjoy himself and play﴾, he said: he strives and is energetic. [Report 18824: Nuʿaym ibn Damdam al-ʿAmiri. I have not found a biography of him except in *Lisan al-Mizan* 6:169, where it says: "Nuʿaym ibn Damdam, and al-Dahhak, with a hadith on wudu'. Some have weakened him. End." He was narrated from by Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, Qabisa ibn ʿUqba, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Salih al-Kufi and others. Al-Bukhari mentioned his narration in the biography of ʿImran ibn Humayri (?) but did not give him a separate entry. I do not know to this day of any weakening of him. It has been mentioned earlier, in the entry on ʿImran, that Ibn Hibban named his father Jihdam, and it is said: Dam'aj. I say: both are mistakes, for his hadith was recorded by al-Bazzar, al-Tabarani and al-Harith ibn Abi Usama in their chains, and Abu al-Shaykh in *Kitab al-Thawab*, all from the narration of ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Aban, who said: from Nuʿaym ibn Damdam, from ʿImran ibn Humayri, as occurs in al-Bukhari. End of what al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said, and it is of great benefit. al-Tabari added in the chain that he was al-ʿAmiri.]

* * *

It seems that those who recite "yarta'i wa-yal'ab" with the kasra on the ʿayn of *yarta'i* interpret it in the way that:

**18825** – Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "Send him with us tomorrow, that he may pasture and play," he said: he pastures his sheep, and looks around and understands, so he knows what a man knows.

* * *

Mujahid used to say about it what follows:

**18826** – al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Shababa related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "narta'i" – by watching over one another, we guard each other, we keep watch and guard.* [*"Nataka'alu" from their saying "ka'alahu," meaning he guarded, pastured and watched over him.]

**18827** – Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "narta'i," he said: one of us guards the other, we keep watch.

**18828** – al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid =

**18829** – And al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Jaʿfar related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similar to it.

**18830** – al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, similar to it.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: So the meaning of the speech is: "Send him with us tomorrow, that we may amuse ourselves, play, enjoy ourselves and be energetic in the desert, and we will guard him from anything that would reach him that he dislikes or that would harm him."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verses 13–14:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Indeed, it grieves me that you take him away, and I fear that the wolf will devour him while you are heedless of him."﴾ (13)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: Ya'qub said to them, "Indeed, it grieves me that you take him with you into the desert" [see the explanation of "grief" (al-huzn) above, p. 142, note 2, and the references there], "out of fear for him from the wolf, that it might devour him, while you are heedless of him," meaning you are unaware. [See the explanation of "heedlessness" (al-ghaflah) above, p. 551, note 2, and the references there.]

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "If the wolf devours him while we are a group, then indeed we would be losers."﴾ (14)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: The brothers of Yusuf said to their father Ya'qub, "If the wolf devours Yusuf in the desert, while we are eleven men with him guarding him" (and they are the "group" [al-'usbah] [see the explanation of "'usbah" above, p. 562]), "then indeed we would be losers" [innā idhan la-khāsirūn], meaning: then indeed we would be helpless, ruined. [See the explanation of "loss" (al-khusran) above, in the lexical indices under (kh-s-r).]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verses 13–14:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Indeed, it grieves me that you take him away, and I fear that the wolf will devour him while you are heedless of him."﴾ (13)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: Ya'qub said to them, "Indeed, it grieves me that you take him with you into the desert" [see the explanation of "grief" (al-huzn) above, p. 142, note 2, and the references there], "out of fear for him from the wolf, that it might devour him, while you are heedless of him," meaning you are unaware. [See the explanation of "heedlessness" (al-ghaflah) above, p. 551, note 2, and the references there.]

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "If the wolf devours him while we are a group, then indeed we would be losers."﴾ (14)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: The brothers of Yusuf said to their father Ya'qub, "If the wolf devours Yusuf in the desert, while we are eleven men with him guarding him" (and they are the "group" [al-'usbah] [see the explanation of "'usbah" above, p. 562]), "then indeed we would be losers" [innā idhan la-khāsirūn], meaning: then indeed we would be helpless, ruined. [See the explanation of "loss" (al-khusran) above, in the lexical indices under (kh-s-r).]

**The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:** ﴿So when they took him away and agreed to put him into the depths of the well. And We revealed to him: "You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs, while they do not perceive."﴾ (12:15)

Abu Ja'far said: The sentence contains an omitted element, whose mention has been dropped because what remains makes clear what was left out. It is: "So he sent him with them." Then ﴿when they took him away and agreed﴾ means: their opinion was united, and they resolved (ﷻ) to put him ﴿into the depths of the well⟩ [[See the explanation of "al-ijma'" (agreement, consensus) above, pp. 147–148.]] [[See the explanation of "ghayabat al-jubb" (the depths of the well) above, pp. 565–566.]]. As follows:

18831 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, it grieves me that you take him away﴾, the verse. He said: [Ya'qub said]: "I will not send him with you; I fear that the wolf will devour him while you are heedless of him." ﴿They said: "If the wolf devours him while we are a group, then indeed we would be losers."﴾ So he sent him with them. They took him out, and he was honored among them. When they went out with him to the wilderness, they showed him enmity. His brother began to strike him, so he would seek help from another, who would strike him as well. He found none of them merciful [[See what I have said regarding "ja'ala" (began/made) and its like, that they are verbs of beginning, and they have a place in expression that nothing else can fill. See vol. 11, note 1.]]. They beat him until they nearly killed him. He began to cry out and say: "O my father! O Ya'qub! If only you knew what the sons of the slave-women have done to your son!" When they nearly killed him, Yahudha [[See above, p. 565, note 1, on the name of this speaker, and that he was "Ruben" or "Simeon," and there Yahudha is not mentioned.]] said: "Did you not give me a covenant that you would not kill him?" So they took him to the well to cast him down. They began to lower him into the well, and he clung to the edge of the well.

They tied his hands and stripped off his shirt. He said: "O my brothers! Return my shirt to me, that I may cover myself with it in the well!" They said: "Call upon the sun, the moon, and the eleven stars, and let them keep you company!" He said: "I do not see anything." They lowered him into the well until, when he reached halfway down, they let him drop, intending that he would die. There was water in the well, and he fell into it, then he took refuge on a rock in it and stood upon it. He said: When they cast him into the well, he began to weep, and they called out to him. He thought it was mercy that had come upon them, so he answered them. They wanted to crush him with a rock to kill him, but Yahudha stood up and prevented them, and said: "You have given me a covenant that you would not kill him!" Yahudha used to bring him food.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So when they took him away and agreed﴾, the "wa" (and) has been inserted in the response (to "lamma," when), as Imru' al-Qays said:

*So when we passed the courtyard of the tribe, and [the one] who leaned toward us was the belly of a low land with winding sand dunes.* [[From his famous Mu'allaqah. It will come in the tafsir 17:73 (Bulaq edition). In the printed edition it read "dhi hiqaf," and I have restored this narration from the manuscript.]]

Here the "wa" has been placed in the response to "lamma," and the sentence in its original form is: "So when we passed the courtyard of the tribe, [it] leaned toward us." Likewise: ﴿So when they took him away and agreed﴾, because His words "agreed" are the response.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We revealed to him: "You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs"﴾, meaning: We revealed to Yusuf: "You will surely inform your brothers" ﴿of this affair of theirs﴾, meaning: of this deed of theirs that they did to you, ﴿while they do not perceive﴾, meaning: while they do not know and are not aware.

* *

Then the people of interpretation (ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning intended by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His words: ﴿while they do not perceive﴾.

Some of them said: He meant by this that Allah revealed to Yusuf that Yusuf would inform his brothers of their deed against him, that which they did: casting him into the well, selling him, and all the rest of what they did to him, while his brothers did not perceive the revelation of Allah to him of that.

Those who said this:

18832 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And We revealed to him﴾, to Yusuf.

18833 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And We revealed to him: You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs﴾. He said: We revealed to Yusuf: "You will surely inform your brothers."

18834 – ... He said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "And We revealed to him: You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs, while they do not perceive." He said: He revealed to Yusuf, while he was in the well, that he would inform them of what they had done, while they did not perceive that revelation.

18835 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: ﴿And We revealed to him﴾, he said: to Yusuf.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: We revealed to Yusuf concerning what his brothers were doing to him, while his brothers did not perceive that Allah had informed him of that.

Those who said this:

18836 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And We revealed to him: You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs, while they do not perceive﴾, concerning what Allah made Yusuf aware of regarding their affair while he was in the well.

18837 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And We revealed to him: You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs, while they do not perceive﴾. He said: Allah revealed to Yusuf, while he was in the well, that he would inform them of what they had done to him, while they did not perceive that revelation.

18838 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, similarly, except that he said: "that he would inform them."

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: Yusuf would inform them of their deed against him, while they did not perceive that it was Yusuf.

Those who said this:

18839 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿while they do not perceive﴾, meaning: while they do not perceive that it is Yusuf.

18840 – al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sadaqah ibn 'Ubadah al-Asadi narrated to us, from his father, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: When the brothers of Yusuf entered, he recognized them while they did not recognize him. He said: The drinking-cup was brought, and he placed it on his hand, then he struck it and it resounded. He said: "This cup informs me that you had a brother from your father called Yusuf, whom he preferred over you, and that you took him and cast him into the depths of the well!" He said: Then he struck it again and it resounded. "You came to your father and said: 'The wolf has eaten him,' and you brought his shirt stained with false blood!" He said: Then some of them said to others: "This cup is indeed informing him of your news!" Ibn 'Abbas said: We do not think this verse was revealed except concerning them: ﴿that you will inform them of this affair of theirs, while they do not perceive﴾.

[[Report 18840: "Sadaqah ibn 'Ubadah ibn Nushayt al-Asadi," who narrated from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and Musa ibn Isma'il, among others, narrated from him. He is biographed in al-Kabir 2/2/298 and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/433. And his father, "'Ubadah ibn Nushayt al-Asadi," narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and from him his son Sadaqah narrated. He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/96. They did not mention any criticism of him or of his son. Nevertheless, in my view the report is not sound. Sufficient as a defect is that it contradicts the explicit text of the Qur'an. Had it been correct, it would have been more fitting that he said this to them when they entered upon him, saying to them: "Do you know what you did to Yusuf and his brother when you were ignorant?" at the end of the surah.]]

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on the verses 16–17:

﴿And they came to their father in the evening, weeping. They said: "O our father, we went racing (nastabiq) and left Yusuf by our belongings, and the wolf devoured him. But you would not believe us, even though we were truthful."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: The brothers of Yusuf came to their father, after they had thrown Yusuf into the bottom of the well, in the evening, weeping.

* *

It was said: The meaning of His words ﴿nastabiq﴾ is "we shoot arrows (nantadil)" from "racing (al-sibaq)" [[See the explanation of "al-istibaq" above, 3:196 / 10:391.]], as related:

18841. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: They came to their father in the evening, weeping. When he heard their voices he was alarmed and said: "What is wrong with you, my sons? Has something happened to your sheep?" They said: "No!" He said: "Then what has become of Yusuf?" They said: ﴿O our father, we went racing and left Yusuf by our belongings, and the wolf devoured him﴾! The old man wept and cried out at the top of his voice, and said: "Where is the shirt?" They brought him the shirt with false blood on it. He took the shirt and laid it over his face, then wept until his face was stained with the blood of the shirt.

* *

As for His words ﴿But you would not believe us﴾, they mean: "You will not accept as true our claim that Yusuf was devoured by the wolf, even though we are truthful!" As related:

18842. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿But you would not believe us﴾, he said: "You will not accept us as truthful!"

....................................................................................

...................................................................................

...................................................................................

* *

[If someone says: ﴿and even though we were truthful﴾ and His words [[This insertion between the brackets is necessary for the sentence to make sense. I suspect that some of al-Tabari's text has fallen out, which is why I placed lines of dots before it, since I see that he did not complete the explanation of the verse as he usually does in all that has preceded.]] ﴿even though we were truthful﴾, either it is a report from them that they were not truthful, which would be a denial by them of themselves; or it is a report from them about their father, that he would not believe them even if they told him the truth. For you know that if they had told their father the truth, he would have believed them?

It is said: The meaning is neither of these two, rather the meaning is: "You will not believe us, even though we are of the people of truth who are not accused, because of your bad opinion of us and your suspicion of us."]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 18:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they came with his shirt, stained with false blood.﴾ He said, "Rather, your souls have beautified for you a matter. So patience is most fitting. And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe." (18)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿And they came with his shirt, stained with false blood.﴾ Allah called it "false" because those who brought the shirt, while it was on it, were lying. They said to Ya'qub, "It is the blood of Yusuf," but it was not his blood; rather, it was the blood of a young goat (sakhlah), as has been said. [[The "sakhlah" is the young of a sheep or goat, of the goats or the sheep, whether male or female.]]

Those who said this:

18843 – Ahmad ibn Abd al-Samad al-Ansari narrated to me, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And they came with his shirt, stained with false blood.﴾ He said: The blood of a young goat. [[The narration 18843: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Samad ibn Ali ibn Isa al-Ansari al-Zurqi, Abu Ayyub, a teacher of al-Tabari, well known and acceptable. He is biographed in Ta'rikh Baghdad 4:270, and Lisan al-Mizan 1:214. al-Tabari narrated from him in his history 5:22, in one place only. See also what will follow, no. 18855.]]

18844 – al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿And they came with his shirt, stained with false blood.﴾ He said: The blood of a young goat, a sheep.

18846 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿with false blood.﴾ He said: The blood of a young goat, a sheep.

18847 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His saying: ﴿with false blood.﴾ He said: That blood was false; it was not the blood of Yusuf.

18848 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿with false blood.﴾ He said: The blood of a young goat, a sheep.

18849 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿with false blood.﴾ He said: With the blood of a young goat.

18850 – Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: They slaughtered a young kid of the goats, then smeared the shirt with its blood, then came to their father. Ya'qub said: "If this is a wolf, how compassionate it is! How did it eat his flesh and not tear his shirt? O my sons, what did the sons of the slave-women do to you, O Yusuf!"

18851 – al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And they came with his shirt, stained with false blood.﴾ He said: If a beast had eaten him, it would have torn the shirt.

18852 – al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us with his chain, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it, except that he said: If a wolf had eaten him, it would have torn the shirt.

18853 – Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And they came with his shirt, stained with false blood.﴾ He said: If the wolf had eaten him, it would have torn it.

18854 – Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to me, saying: Uthman ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Qurrah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: The shirt of Yusuf was brought to Ya'qub. He began looking at it, seeing traces of blood but seeing no tear in it. He said: "O my sons, did I not know the wolf to be gentle?"
