He said: "O my sons, by Allah, did I not know the wolf to be gentle?" [[The narration 18855: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Samad al-Ansari, see the previous narration no. 18843.]]

18856 – Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, from Imran ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan, who said: When the brothers of Yusuf came to their father with his shirt, he began turning it over and saying: "Did I not know the wolf to be gentle? It ate my son and spared his shirt!"

18857 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And they came with his shirt, stained with false blood.﴾ He said: When they came to the Prophet of Allah Ya'qub with his shirt, he said: "I see no trace of a beast, nor of a thrust, nor of a tear."

18858 – Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿with false blood.﴾ False blood; it was not the blood of Yusuf.

18859 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mujalid informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: They slaughtered a kid and smeared the shirt with its blood. When Ya'qub looked at the shirt, intact, he knew that the people had lied to him. He said to them: "If this were a wolf, it would be gentle, since it spared the shirt and did not spare my son!" So he knew that they had lied to him.

18860 – Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Sayfan, from Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And they came with his shirt, stained with false blood.﴾ He said: When the shirt of Yusuf was brought to Ya'qub and he saw no tear in it, he said: "You have lied! If a beast had eaten him, it would have torn his shirt!"

18861 – Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Ishaq al-Azraq and Ya'la narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Simak, from Amir, who said: There were three signs in the shirt of Yusuf: "when they came with his shirt stained with false blood." He said: And Ya'qub said: "If the wolf had eaten him, it would have torn his shirt."

18862 – al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya narrated to us, from Simak, from Amir, who said: He used to say: There were three signs in the shirt of Yusuf: when it was cast upon his father's face and he regained his sight; when it was torn from behind; and when they came with his shirt stained with false blood.

18863 – Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Amir, who said: There were three signs in the shirt of Yusuf: the rent, the blood, and when it was cast upon his father's face and he regained his sight.

18864 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Amir narrated to us, saying: Qurrah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: When the shirt of Yusuf was brought to Ya'qub, he saw the blood but did not see the rent, and said: "Did I not know the wolf to be gentle?"

18865 – ..... Hammad ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Qurrah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

* *

If someone says: How is it said ﴿with false blood﴾ when you know it was real blood, undoubtedly, and if it was not, it was the blood of Yusuf?

It is said: There are two views on this:

The first: that it was said ﴿with false blood﴾ because a lie was told about it, as one says "the night is the crescent" and as it is said: ﴿so their trade did not profit﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah 16]. This is a view that some of the grammarians of Basra held.

The other view: that it is an infinitive used in the sense of a passive participle. Its meaning: they came upon his shirt with blood that was lied about, just as one says "he has no intellect nor is he intellected," and "he has no strength nor is he strengthened." The Arabs often do this, placing the passive participle in the position of the infinitive and the infinitive in the position of the passive participle, as the shepherd (al-Ra'i) said:

Until, when they left for his bones
no flesh, nor for his heart, a mind [[Jamharat ash'ar al-Arab 175, and elsewhere, from his well-known ode, which he composed for Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, whose tax-collector had attacked the people of al-Ra'i among the Banu Numayr, because Qays had a Zubayrid leaning...]]

And that is what some of the grammarians of Kufa said. [[This is al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, in his commentary on this verse.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He said: "Rather, your souls have beautified for you a matter."﴾ Exalted is His remembrance, says: Ya'qub said to his sons, who informed him that the wolf had eaten Yusuf, contradicting their report: "The matter is not as you say. ﴿Rather, your souls have beautified for you a matter﴾," meaning: rather, your souls adorned for you a matter concerning Yusuf and made it appealing, so you did it, as:

18866 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "He said ﴿Rather, your souls have beautified for you a matter﴾," he said: He says: rather, your souls adorned for you a matter.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So patience is most fitting﴾, it means: my patience regarding what you did to me concerning Yusuf is most fitting patience, or: it is most fitting patience.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾, it means: and I seek Allah's help to sufficiency against the evil of what you describe of lies. [[See the explanation of "describing" (al-wasf) above, 12:10, 11, 152.]]

* *

It has been said: "The fitting patience" is the patience in which there is no distress.

Those who said this:

18867 – Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿So patience is fitting﴾, he said: there is no distress in it.

18868 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18869 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18870 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mujahid: ﴿So patience is fitting﴾, without distress.

18871 – ..... Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18872 – ..... Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya, from Habban ibn Abi Jabalah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about His saying: ﴿So patience is fitting﴾. He said: Patience with no complaint in it. He said: One who laments has not been patient. [[Narration 18872: Habban ibn Abi Jabalah al-Misri, one of the ten whom Umar sent to instruct the people of Egypt, previously mentioned at nos. 2195, 10180. As for Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya, I do not know who he is; in a similar chain at no. 10180 my brother thought he might be Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn An'am, but it is agreed that in both places it is Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya, which distances it from error and distortion, unless he is one of the narrators from Habban whom we do not know. Perhaps it will come later in the commentary to clarify it. See also the chain that follows.]]

18873 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya informed us, from Habban ibn Abi Jabalah: that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about His saying: ﴿So patience is fitting﴾. He said: Patience with no complaint in it. [[Narration 18873: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya, see the previous note.]]

18874 – ..... al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿So patience is fitting﴾: there is no distress in it.

18875 – al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18876 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from a man, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿So patience is fitting﴾, he said: without distress.

18877 – al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: al-Thawri narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18878 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from some of his companions, who said: It is said: three things are from patience: that you do not speak of your pain, nor of your calamity, nor praise yourself.

Al-Thawri informed us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit: that Ya'qub, the Prophet ﷺ, had lost his eyebrows, so he would lift them with a cloth. He was asked: "What is this?" He said: "The length of time and the abundance of sorrows!" So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed to him: "O Ya'qub, are you complaining of Me?" He said: "O Lord, a sin I committed; forgive it for me."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾. [[See the explanation of "describing" above, p. 584, note 1, and the references there.]]

18879 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾, that is, against what you lie about.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 19:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And a caravan came, and they sent their water-drawer, and he let down his bucket. He said, "Good news! This is a boy!" And they concealed him as merchandise, but Allah was Knowing of what they did.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: A caravan of travellers on the road came, ﴿and they sent their water-drawer﴾ (the one who goes to the watering place and the stopping place; "his coming to it" means his arrival there and entering it [[See the explanation of "al-Warid" (the one who comes to water) in what has preceded, 15: 466.]]). ﴿And he let down his bucket﴾ means he sent his bucket down into the well.

* *

It is said: "adlaytu al-dalw fi al-bi'r" (I lowered the bucket into the well) when you send it into it; and when you draw water with it, you say: "dalawtu adlu dalwan" (I drew water with the bucket).

* *

In the speech there is an omission, which is dispensed with because of what has been mentioned indicating it, so it is left out. That is: ﴿And he let down his bucket﴾ = so Yusuf caught hold of it and came out, and the one who lowered it said: ﴿Good news! This is a boy!﴾

* *

According to what we have said regarding this, reports have come from the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil).

Those who said that:

18880 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿And a caravan came, and they sent their water-drawer, and he let down his bucket﴾ — Yusuf caught hold of the rope and came out. When the owner of the rope saw him, he called out to a man among his companions called "Bushra": ﴿Good news! This is a boy!﴾

18881 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿They sent their water-drawer and he let down his bucket﴾ — the boy clung to the bucket, and when he came out he said: ﴿Good news! This is a boy!﴾

* *

18882 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿They sent their water-drawer﴾ — he says: they sent their messenger. When he lowered his bucket, the boy clung to it ﴿= (He said, "Good news! This is a boy!")﴾.

* *

They differed concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿Good news! This is a boy!﴾

Some of them said: it is the good news given by the one who lowered his bucket to his companions, upon his finding Yusuf, that he had found a slave [[See the explanation of "al-Bushra" (good news) in the lexical indexes (b-sh-r) of what has preceded.]].

Those who said that:

18883 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿He said, "Good news! This is a boy!"﴾ — they rejoiced over him when they drew him out. It is a well in the land of Bayt al-Maqdis, whose location is known.

18884 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Good news! This is a boy!﴾ — he said: their water-drawer gave them good news when he found Yusuf.

* *

Others said: rather, it is the name of a specific man from the caravan, whom the one who lowered the bucket called when Yusuf came out of the well clinging to the rope.

Those who said that:

18885 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Good news! This is a boy!﴾ — he called a man among his companions called "Bushra," and said: ﴿Good news! This is a boy!﴾

18886 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Khalaf ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿Good news! This is a boy!﴾ — he said: the name of his companion was "Bushra."

18887 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿Good news! This is a boy!﴾ — he said: the name of the boy was "Bushra"; he said: "Ya Bushra," as you would say "Ya Zayd."

* *

The readers differed in their recitation of this:

The majority of the readers of Medina recited it as "Ya Bushrayya" (يا بُشْرَيَّ), with the ya of possession affirmed, but they assimilated the alif into the ya seeking the kasra which is required before the ya of possession of the speaker, as in their saying "ghulami" and "jariyati" in every case. This is from the dialect of Tayy [[And also the dialect of Hudhayl, as al-Asma'i said.]], as Abu Dhu'ayb said:

They preceded my "hawayya" and dispatched themselves to their desire, so they were cut off, and for every side there is a place of fall.

[[His Diwan (in Diwan al-Hudhaliyyin) 1: 2, and Sharh al-Mufaddaliyyat: 854, and others; and it is one of Abu Dhu'ayb's marvels, which he says about his sons who died, whom the plague preceded in a single year; they were five: "Awdā banīya (they perished, my sons), and they left me a grief, after sleep, and a tear that does not cease.
"They preceded my hawayya..." ....
"So I remained after them in a toilsome life, and I suppose I am a follower who will be overtaken."
He says: They preceded me with what they chose of death and departure, and they went at a swift pace to what they chose, so death cut them off, taking them one after another. And for every side there is a fall which he does not miss; wherever God decreed death for him, it overtook him.]]

* *

The majority of the readers of Kufa recited: ﴿Yā bushrā﴾ with the ya unvoweled (lengthened) and without the possessive.

When it is recited thus, it admits of two interpretive possibilities:

One of them is what al-Suddi said: that it is the name of a man whom the water-drawer called by his name, as one says "Ya Zayd" and "Ya 'Amr," so "Bushra" is in the nominative position as the vocative.

The other: that he intended to attribute the good news to himself, and dropped the ya while intending it, so it is singular with the intention of attribution, as the Arabs do in the vocative, saying "Ya nafs, isbiri" and "Ya nafsi, isbiri," and "Ya bunayya, la taf'al" and "Ya bunayyi, la taf'al," so it is left singular and raised, with the intention of attribution. Sometimes they attribute and so it takes the kasra, as you say "Ya ghulamu aqbil" and "Ya ghulami aqbil."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferred recitation to me in this is the recitation of the one who recites it with the ya unvoweled and without tanwin of the ya; because if it is the name of a specific man, it was known among them, as al-Suddi said, and that is the correct recitation without doubt [[In the printed and the manuscript: "fa-dhalika hiya...", and what I have established is better.]]. And if it is from giving good news, then it admits of that when it is recited thus, as I have explained.

As for the doubling and the attribution of the ya, it is an anomalous reading, which I do not see as a valid recitation, though it is a known dialect; because the consensus of the authoritative readers is against it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾, the people of interpretation differed concerning its interpretation.

Some of them said: the water-drawer who came to the water and his companions from the merchants who were with them concealed him, and they said to their companions: "He is merchandise which we were entrusted with by some people of Egypt," because they feared that if they knew how much they had bought him for, they would demand a share in him.

Those who said that:

18888 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾ — he said: the owner of the bucket and whoever was with him; they said to their companions: "We have only been entrusted with him," fearing that they would take a share in him if they knew his price. And his brothers followed them, saying to the bucket-lowerer and his companions: "Secure him, lest he run away!" until they halted him in Egypt. He said: "Who will buy me and be given good news?" The king bought him, and the king was a Muslim.

18889 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "fearing that they would make them partners in him if they knew of him; and his brothers followed them, saying to the bucket-lowerer and his companions: 'Secure him, lest he run away!' until they halted him in Egypt" [[In the printed: "until they halted him", and I have established what is in the manuscript, which is correct; see this report at no. 18892.]] — and the rest of the report is like the report of Muhammad ibn 'Amr.

18890 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid =

18891 - ... He said: and Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "fearing that they would share in him, if they knew his price."

18892 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "fearing that they would make them partners in him if they knew his price." And he also said: "until they halted him in Egypt."

18893 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾ — he said: when the two men bought him, they feared that the caravan would say "We bought him," and they would ask them for a share, so they said: "If they ask us what this is, we will say: merchandise which the people of the water entrusted to us." That is His words: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾ among themselves.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: the merchants concealed him from one another.

Those who said that:

18894 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾ — he said: the merchants concealed him from one another.

18895 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mujahid: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾ — he said: the merchants concealed him from one another.

* *

Others said: the meaning is: they concealed the sale of him.

Those who said that:

18896 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾ — he said: they concealed his sale.

18897 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to us, from Jabir, from Mujahid: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾ — he said: they said to the people of the water: "He is only merchandise."

* *

Others said: by His words: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾ is meant the brothers of Yusuf, that they concealed the matter of Yusuf, that he should be their brother; they said: "He is a slave of ours."

Those who said that:

18898 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾ — meaning: the brothers of Yusuf concealed his matter and hid that he should be their brother. Yusuf concealed his matter, fearing that his brothers would kill him, and chose sale. His brothers mentioned him to the caravan's water-drawer, and he called his companions and said: "Ya Bushra! This is a boy for sale!" So his brothers sold him.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who said: "The water-drawer of the caravan and his companions from his fellow travellers concealed the matter of Yusuf, that they had bought him, fearing that they would make them partners, and they said to them: 'He is merchandise which the people of the water entrusted to us'" — because it comes right after the report about him, so for what follows it to be a report about him is more fitting than for it to be a report about one who is not directly connected to the report about him [[See the explanation of "al-Israr" (concealment) in what has preceded, 15: 103, 239.]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And God is Knowing of what they do﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: God has knowledge of what the sellers and buyers of Yusuf did concerning his matter; nothing of that is hidden from Him. But He left off changing it, so that His prior decree in His knowledge would proceed concerning him and concerning them, and so that He would show the brothers of Yusuf, Yusuf and his father His power in it. [[See the explanation of "'Alim" (Knowing) in what has preceded in the lexical indexes ('-l-m).]]

* *

This, although it is a report from God, may He be exalted, about Yusuf His prophet ﷺ, is also a reminder from God to His prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and a consolation from Him to him for what he suffered from his nearest kin and relatives who were polytheists, of harm concerning him. He says: So be patient, O Muhammad, over what has befallen you for God's sake; for I am able to change what these polytheists inflict upon you, just as I was able to change what Yusuf suffered from his brothers while they were doing to him what they did. My leaving that was not out of contempt for Yusuf in My sight, but because of My prior knowledge concerning him and his brothers. Likewise, My leaving the changing of what these polytheists inflict upon you is not out of contempt for you in My sight, but because of My prior knowledge concerning you and them; then your affair and their affair will end in your superiority over them and their submission to you, just as the affair of Yusuf's brothers ended in their submission to Yusuf with lordship over them, and Yusuf's superiority over them. [[At this point the twelfth part of our manuscript ends, and at its end is written: "The twelfth part is complete, by the praise and help of God, and may God bless our master Muhammad, his family, companions and peace. It is followed at the beginning of the thirteenth part, God willing, by: The interpretation of His words: ﴿They sold him for a paltry price, a few dirhams counted; and they were among those who held him in disregard.﴾ The completion of it was in the blessed month of Ramadan, in the year 715 AH."

Followed by the thirteenth part, whose beginning reads:

"In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
Lord, make it easy."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 20:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price, counted out dirhams, and they were of those who were indifferent to him﴾ (20)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His remembrance, ﴿And they sold him﴾, meaning: the brothers of Joseph sold Joseph.

* *

= As for when one wishes to report that he bought it, one says: "ishtaraytuhu" (I bought it). [[See the discussion of "al-shira'" (purchase) earlier, 14:150, note 4, and the references there.]] From this is the verse of Ibn Mufarragh al-Himyari:

"I sold a cloak, would that I had been... before the cloak I was a ..."

He means: "I sold a cloak," and he was a slave who belonged to him. [[The verse, its takhrij and explanation were given earlier, 2:341, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

18899 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibrahim related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Mughirah, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, that he disliked buying and selling for the Bedouin. He said: The Arabs say: "ushir li kadha wa kadha" (buy for me such and such), meaning: sell for me such and such. And he recited this verse: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price﴾, saying: They sold him, and his sale was unlawful.

18900 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Shababah related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: The brothers of Joseph, eleven men, sold him when the one who lowered his bucket drew him out.

18901 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

18902 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Abu Najih, from Mujahid.

18903 - And Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

18904 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

18905 - ... Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And they sold him﴾, he said: Ibn Abbas said: "So he was sold among them."

18906 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price﴾, he said: They sold him.

18907 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, similarly.

18908 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "So his brothers sold him for a paltry price."

* *

Others said: What is meant by His saying: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price﴾ is the caravan (al-sayyarah), who sold Joseph for a paltry price.

Mention of those who said that:

18909 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price﴾, "they are the caravan who sold him."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two opinions regarding this is the view of the one who said: The interpretation of this is: The brothers of Joseph bought Joseph for a paltry price [[In the printed edition: "they bought, the brothers of Joseph. Joseph", which is corrupt; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]. That is because Allah, mighty and majestic, has informed that those who bought him concealed the purchase of Joseph from their companions, for fear that they would ask them to share in it, by claiming that he was merchandise. They did not say that except out of desire for him to be exclusively theirs, and to cheapen the price at which they bought him, since they bought him, as His praise says: ﴿for a paltry price﴾. Had his buyers been among his brothers who were indifferent to him, their saying to their companions, "He is merchandise," would have had no meaning, and their buying him, while they were indifferent to him, would have had no sense, unless they were overpowered in their minds; for it is impossible that a sound-minded person buys what he is indifferent to without someone compelling him to do so, and then lies about his matter to people by saying, "He is merchandise, I did not buy him," while being indifferent to him. Rather, this statement is from one who is stingy with his goods, because of their value in his eyes, and because of what he hopes for of a precious price for them and an abundance of profit.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿paltry﴾ (bakhs), it means: deficient.

* *

It is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "bakhastu fulanan haqqahu" (I cheated someone of his right) when I wronged him, meaning: he wronged him and diminished him from what is due to him of fulfilment: "abkhasuhu bakhsan". From it is His saying: ﴿And do not diminish people's things﴾ [Surah Hud: 85]. What is intended is: for a paltry price that is diminished and deficient, so "bakhs", which is a verbal noun, is put in place of the passive participle, as it is said: ﴿with false blood﴾, when it really means "with blood in which there is falsehood" [[See the explanation of "bakhs" earlier, 15:262, note 4, and the references there.]].

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of this.

Some of them said: It was called ﴿paltry price﴾ because it was unlawful for them.

Mention of those who said that:

18910 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Al-Muharibi related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price﴾, he said: "al-bakhs" is the unlawful.

18911 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Ali ibn Asim related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿for a paltry price﴾, he said: unlawful. [[Report 18911: In the printed edition, an entire line of the manuscript was omitted, so it ran the two reports 18911 and 18912 as a single chain: "... Ali ibn Asim, from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj", and I restored it to its original from the manuscript.]]

18912 - It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: Its price was paltry, unlawful; it was not lawful for them to eat it.

18913 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price﴾, he said: They sold him for a paltry price; he said: its sale was unlawful and its purchase was unlawful.

18914 - Al-Qasim related to me, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak: ﴿for a paltry price﴾, he said: unlawful.

18915 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿for a paltry price﴾, he says: it was not lawful for them to eat its price.

* *

Others said: The meaning of "bakhs" here is: injustice.

Mention of those who said that:

18916 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding his saying: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price﴾, he said: "al-bakhs" is injustice. And the sale of Joseph and its price was unlawful for them.

18917 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Qatadah said: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price﴾, he said: injustice.

* *

Others said: By "bakhs" in this context is meant: little.

Mention of those who said that:

18918 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Qays, from Jabir, from Ikrimah, who said: "al-bakhs" is little.

18919 - Al-Harith related to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz related to us, saying: Qays related to us, from Jabir, from Ikrimah, similarly.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained the correct view on this.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿counted out dirhams﴾ [[See the explanation of "ma'dudah" earlier in the lexical indexes under ('-d-d).]], He, mighty and majestic, means that they sold him for dirhams that were not weighed, deficient and not full, because of their indifference to him.

* *

It has been said: "ma'dudah" (counted) was said only so as to make known that they were fewer than forty, because in that era they did not weigh what weighed less than forty dirhams, since the smallest and least of their weights was the uqiyyah, and the weight of the uqiyyah was forty dirhams. They said: By His saying "ma'dudah" He only indicated the small number of dirhams with which they sold him.

* *

Some of them said: They were twenty dirhams.

Mention of those who said that:

18920 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Zuhayr, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from Abdullah, who said: What Joseph was bought for was twenty dirhams.

18921 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Al-Hammani related to us, saying: Sharik related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from Abdullah: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price, counted out dirhams﴾, he said: twenty dirhams.

18922 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf al-Bakali, regarding His saying: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price, counted out dirhams﴾, he said: twenty dirhams.

18923 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us = and Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us = from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf al-Shami: "paltry, dirhams", he said: they were twenty dirhams. [[Report 18923: "Nawf al-Shami" is himself "Nawf ibn Fudalah al-Bakali", who has been mentioned many times before. The printed edition changed it and wrote "Nawf al-Bakali".]]

18924 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Al-Hammani related to us, saying: Sharik related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf, similarly.

18925 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His saying: ﴿for a paltry price, counted out dirhams﴾, he said: twenty dirhams.

18926 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: 'Amr related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿counted out dirhams﴾, he said: they were twenty dirhams.

18927 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: it was mentioned to us that it was sold for twenty dirhams = ﴿and they were of those who were indifferent﴾.

18928 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, similarly.

18929 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Abu Idris, from 'Atiyyah, who said: The dirhams were twenty dirhams, which they divided, two dirhams each.

* *

Others said: Rather, their number was twenty-two dirhams, each of Joseph's brothers, who were eleven men, took two dirhams from them.

Mention of those who said that:

18930 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿counted out dirhams﴾, he said: twenty-two dirhams.

18931 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying: ﴿counted out dirhams﴾, he said: twenty-two dirhams for Joseph's brothers, [and the brothers were] eleven men. [[This addition is necessary and was dropped by the copyist, because he had dropped the beginning of the report and then written it in the margin, so perhaps he forgot part of it.]]

18932 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying: ﴿counted out dirhams﴾ =

18933 - ... he said: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

18934 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

* *

Others said: Rather, they were forty dirhams.

Mention of those who said that:

18935 - Al-Harith related to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz related to us, saying: Qays related to us, from Jabir, from Ikrimah: ﴿counted out dirhams﴾, he said: forty dirhams.

18936 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: They sold him, and his price, for which they sold him, did not reach an uqiyyah; that is because people in that era used to trade in uqiyyahs, so whatever fell short of an uqiyyah was "adad" (counted); God says: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price, counted out dirhams﴾, meaning it did not reach an uqiyyah.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this is to say: God, mighty is His remembrance, informed that they sold him for counted dirhams, not weighed, and He did not specify the amount of that by weight or number, nor did He place any indication of it in a book or in a report from the Messenger, ﷺ. It may be that it was twenty, or it may be twenty-two, or it may be forty, and less or more than that. Whichever it was, they were counted, not weighed; and there is no benefit in knowing the amount of their weight that would bear on religion, nor does ignorance of it bring any harm. Belief in the apparent meaning of the revelation is obligatory, and what lies beyond it is set aside for us, the burden of knowing it.

[[This is one of Abu Ja'far's criteria, which recur in his book, though not mentioned at every place. It is the judgment between him and those who claim he went in his interpretation toward belief for much of what he reported, which no sound report from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, nor a rational argument requiring acceptance, supports.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they were of those who were indifferent to him﴾, He, mighty is His remembrance, says: The brothers of Joseph were indifferent to Joseph, not knowing his honour with God, nor recognising his station with Him; yet they wished to come between him and his father, so that the face of his father would be theirs alone, and to cut him off from closeness to him, so that the benefits that were directed to Joseph, to the exclusion of them, would be directed to them.

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

18937 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Abu Marzuq, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿and they were of those who were indifferent to him﴾, he said: They did not know of his prophethood and his station with God.

18938 - It was reported from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿and a caravan came﴾ and it stopped at the well, ﴿so they sent their water-drawer﴾, and he drew water and brought out Joseph, and they rejoiced that they had found a boy whose knowledge and station with his Lord they did not know, so they were indifferent to him, and sold him. Its sale was unlawful, and they sold him for counted dirhams.

18939 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to me, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak: ﴿and they were of those who were indifferent to him﴾, he said: his brothers were indifferent, so they did not know his station with God, his prophethood and his place.

18940 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: His brothers were indifferent to him; they did not know his station with God.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 21:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife, "Make his residence honorable; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son." And thus did We established Joseph in the land, and that We might teach him the interpretation of events. And Allah is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know﴾ (21).

Abu Ja'far said: He, mighty is His praise, says: "And the one who bought Joseph from his seller in Egypt said..."

* *

It is mentioned that his name was "Qitfir."

18941 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The name of the one who bought him was Qitfir. [[The narration: 18941 - Al-Tabari narrated it in his History 1: 172. In the manuscript, in both places it reads "Qutaifin," and in the History before the report "Qutayn," and in the report "Qitfir."]]

* *

It was also said: His name was Itfir ibn Ruhayb, and he was the 'Aziz, who was over the treasuries of Egypt. The king at that time was al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid, a man from the Amalekites. Thus:

18942 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq [[The narration: 18942 - Al-Tabari narrated it in his History 1: 172.]].

* *

It was also said: The one who sold him in Egypt was Malik ibn Dhu'r ibn Buwayb ibn 'Aqfan ibn Madyan ibn Ibrahim. [[In the History 1: 172: "Di'r" with an unpointed dal; in the printed edition here it was "'Anqa'," and in the manuscript "'Afqa" without a final nun. In the printed edition it was "Thuwayb," which is unpointed in the manuscript, so I followed what is in the History.]] Thus:

18943 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas.

* *

= ﴿And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife﴾. Her name, as Ibn Ishaq mentioned, was Ra'il bint Ra'a'il.

18944 - Ibn Humayd narrated this to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq.

* *

﴿Make his residence honorable﴾: he means: make honorable the place of his stay, which is where he dwells and resides.

* *

It is said: "So-and-so dwelt in such-and-such a place" when he resided there.

* *

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

18945 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Make his residence honorable﴾, his position; she was the wife of the 'Aziz.

18946 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife, "Make his residence honorable,"﴾ he said: his position.

18947 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: he was bought by the king, and the king was a Muslim.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son﴾, it is mentioned that the buyer of Joseph said this to his wife when he handed him over to her, because he had no child and did not approach women. So he said to her: "Honor him; perhaps he will suffice us for some of what we suffer in our affairs, when he understands the matters with which he is charged and knows them," = ﴿or we may adopt him as a son﴾, meaning: or we may take him in adoption.

18948 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Itfir, as was related to me, was a man who did not approach women, and his wife Ra'il was a beautiful, pampered, well-fed woman, in wealth and worldly comfort. [[The narration: 18948 - Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History 1: 172, 173.]]

18949 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah, who said: The most perceptive of people are three: the 'Aziz, when he perceived in Joseph and said to his wife: ﴿Make his residence honorable; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son﴾; and Abu Bakr, when he perceived in 'Umar; and the woman who said: ﴿O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy﴾ [Surah al-Qasas: 26].

18950 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Joseph was taken to Egypt, and the 'Aziz, the king of Egypt, bought him, and took him to his house and said to his wife: ﴿Make his residence honorable; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son﴾.

18951 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah, who said: The most perceptive of people are three: the 'Aziz when he said to his wife: ﴿Make his residence honorable﴾, while the people in it were disinterested; and Abu Bakr when he perceived in 'Umar and appointed him as successor; and the woman who said: ﴿O my father, hire him﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And thus did We establish Joseph in the land﴾, He, mighty is His remembrance, says: Just as We rescued Joseph from the hands of his brothers, who had resolved to kill him, and brought him out of the well after he had been thrown into it, and brought him to honor and high position with the 'Aziz of Egypt, so We established him in the land, and placed him over its treasuries. [[On tamkin (establishment), see the earlier discussion: 11: 63 and 12: 315.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and that We might teach him the interpretation of events﴾, He, mighty is His remembrance, says: So that We might teach Joseph the interpretation of dreams [[On ta'wil (interpretation), see the earlier discussion: 15: 560, note 1, and the references there.]], We established him in the land, as follows:

18952 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿from the interpretation of events﴾, he said: the interpretation of dreams.

18953 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18954 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and that We might teach him the interpretation of events﴾, he said: the interpretation of dreams.

18955 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and that We might teach him the interpretation of events﴾, he said: the interpretation of dreams.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is predominant over His affair﴾, He, mighty is His remembrance, says: Allah is dominant over Joseph's affair, governing, managing and safeguarding him.

* *

The pronoun in His saying: ﴿over His affair﴾ refers to Joseph.

* *

It was related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding the meaning of "predominant" what follows:

18956 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And Allah is predominant over His affair﴾, he said: "Fa''al" (an intensive form). [[It is possible to read "fa'al" with the 'ayn doubled, from "fi'l" (act), but I prefer to read it as "fa-'al," with fa' as a conjunction followed by "'al" from "'uluw" (height). As for the first, I can hardly accept it.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾, it means: but most of the people, those who were indifferent to Joseph and sold him for a base price, and the people of Egypt among whom he came to be sold, do not know what Allah will do with Joseph, and that Joseph's affair will return to Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 22:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when he reached his full strength and maturity, We gave him judgment and knowledge. Thus do We reward the good-doers﴾ (12:22).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His mention, says: When Yusuf reached his full strength (ashudd), meaning: when he reached the limit of his strength and vigour in his youth and prime. This falls between eighteen and sixty years of age, and it was said: up to forty years. [[See the explanation of "al-ashudd" above, 12:222.]]

* *

It is said of it: "The man's ashudd has passed," meaning his strength. It is a plural, like "al-adurr" and "al-ashurr," [[The manuscript and the printed edition have this as given to me; however, in the manuscript it reads "al-asar" and "sar," and these two words have also been mentioned above, 12:222. I had thought there that they were corrupted, but it is strange that the corruption should persist in both places. Perhaps the correct reading is "al-adab," the plural of "dabb" (lizard). Whatever the case, this is something I have not clarified or known, and above every possessor of knowledge is One who knows.]] though no singular of this form has been heard from its own wording. By analogy, its singular should be "shadd," just as the singular of "al-adurr" is "durr," and the singular of "al-ashurr" is "shurr," as the poet said: [[I do not know who said it.]]

"Has it been anything but that the ashurr increased, and the war of kings destroyed the abundant wealth?" [[In the printed edition: "kathura al-ashadd" ("the strong ones increased"); in the manuscript it is with the letter ra'. I have not found this verse anywhere else.]]

And Humayd said:

"And there has come, if the blamers would be persuaded, after the ashudd, four complete [years]." [[I have not found it anywhere else, and I do not know whether it is from the rajaz with "al-ashadd" or "al-ashurr."]]

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning what Allah meant by "reaching the ashudd" in this place.

Some of them said: It means thirty-three years.

Those who said so:

18957 – Ibn Wakic and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, both saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "And when he reached his ashudd": he said: thirty-three years.

18958 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18959 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18960 – It was narrated to me from Ali ibn al-Haytham, from Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, from Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Mujahid, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say concerning His saying: "And when he reached his ashudd," he said: a few and thirty years.

* *

Others said: Rather, it means twenty years.

Those who said so:

18961 – It was narrated to me from Ali ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: "And when he reached his ashudd," he said: twenty years.

* *

It is related from Ibn Abbas through a channel not deemed acceptable that he said: it is between eighteen years and thirty. I have already explained the meaning of "al-ashudd."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings, in terms of truth, is to say: Allah informed that He gave Yusuf judgment and knowledge when he reached his ashudd. The "ashudd" is the end of his strength and youth. It is possible that He gave him that when he was eighteen years old; it is possible that He gave it to him when he was twenty years old; it is possible that He gave it to him when he was thirty-three years old. There is no indication of this in the Book of Allah, nor a report from the Messenger ﷺ, nor a consensus of the Community, as to which of these it was. Since this is not established through the channel you have mentioned, the correct approach is to say about it what Allah, mighty and majestic, said, until a proof is established through a sound report of what has been said on this matter, through a channel that must be accepted, and then it will be accepted.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿We gave him judgment and knowledge﴾, He, exalted is His mention, says: We then bestowed upon him understanding and knowledge. [[See the explanation of "al-hukm" above, 6:538, and the earlier language indexes under (h-k-m).]] As:

18962 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "judgment and knowledge," he said: intellect and knowledge before prophethood.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Thus do We reward the good-doers﴾, He, exalted is His mention, says: Just as We recompensed Yusuf, by granting him judgment and knowledge because of his obedience to Me, and by establishing him in the land, and by rescuing him from the hands of his brothers who intended to kill him, so too do We reward whoever does good in his deeds, obeys Me in My command, and refrains from what I have forbidden him of My disobediences. [[See the explanation of "al-jaza'" and "al-ihsan" above, in the language indexes under (j-z-y) and (h-s-n).]]

* *

This, although its outward meaning applies to every good-doer, is in fact directed at Muhammad, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ. Allah, mighty and majestic, says to him: Just as I did this for Yusuf after what he suffered from his brothers, and endured the trials he endured, I established him in the land and made the lands smooth for him, so too will I do for you: I will deliver you from the polytheists of your people who seek you with enmity, I will establish you in the land, and I will give you judgment and knowledge, for that is My recompense to the people of good-doing in My command and My prohibition.

* *

18963 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "Thus do We reward the good-doers," he said: the guided ones.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 23:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him from himself, and she closed the doors and said, "Come, you." He said, "I seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, he is my lord; he has made my residence good. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: The wife of the ruler (al-Aziz) sought to seduce Yusuf, she in whose house Yusuf was [Yusuf], from himself, [[The addition between the brackets is necessary; the sentence is not sound without it.]] that he should have intercourse with her, as:

18964 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And when he reached his maturity, the one in whose house he was sought to seduce him from himself, the wife of the ruler."

18965 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And sought to seduce him, the one in whose house he was, from himself﴾ He said: she loved him.

18966 -.... He said: My father narrated to me, from Isra'il, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, he said: She said: "Come here."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And she closed the doors﴾, it means: the woman closed the doors of the houses upon herself and upon Yusuf, when she desired him and sought to seduce him, door after door.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And she said, "Hayta laka"﴾, the reciters differed in its recitation. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra recited it: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ with a fatha on the ha' and the ta', meaning: come, draw near and approach, as the poet said to Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him: [[I do not know now who the speaker is.]]

Convey to the Commander of the Faithful ... the brother of Iraq, when we come to him ... that Iraq and its people ... are necks turned toward you, so hayta hayta [[Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah 1:305, and al-Lisan (hyt), (ʿnq). His saying "necks toward you" means they are inclining toward you, as if they had twisted their necks toward you out of longing or expectation.]]

He means: come and draw near.

* *

Those who read it in this way interpreted it in a manner similar to what we have said:

18967 - Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Makhrami narrated to me, he said: Abu al-Jawab narrated to us, he said: Ammar ibn Ruzayq narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ He said: come to you. [[Report 18967: "Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak al-Makhrami", a teacher of al-Tabari who has appeared many times before.

"Abu al-Jawab" is "al-Ahwas ibn Jawab al-Dabbi", who narrated from Sufyan al-Thawri, Sa'ir ibn al-Khums, Ammar ibn Ruzayq, and others. He was trustworthy, though he sometimes erred. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/59, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/328.

"Ammar ibn Ruzayq al-Dabbi", "Abu al-Ahwas", is trustworthy, passed under number 10191.]]

18968 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ He said: come to you.

18969 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, he said: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ You say: come to you.

18970 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, he said: Hammad narrated to us, from Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, that he used to read this word: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ with a fatha, meaning: come to you.

18971 - al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said, his saying: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ He said: You say: come to you.

18972 - Ahmad ibn Suhayl al-Wasiti narrated to me, he said: Qurrah ibn Isa narrated to us, he said: al-Nadr ibn Arabi al-Jazari narrated to us, from Ikrimah, mawla of Ibn Abbas, regarding his saying: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ He said: come to you = he said: it is in the Hawrani dialect. [[Report 18972: "Ahmad ibn Suhayl al-Wasiti", a teacher of al-Tabari. al-Hakim said: "In his narrations there are some strange reports," and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy and said: Habays ibn Abd Allah al-Nahshali narrated from him in Wasit. He is biographed in Mizan al-I'tidal 1:48, and Lisan al-Mizan 1:185.

As for "Qurrah ibn Isa", I have not found anyone by this name. But the one who narrates from "al-Nadr ibn Arabi" is "Bishr ibn Ubays ibn Marhum al-Attar", biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/362.

As for "al-Nadr ibn Arabi al-Jazari al-Bahili", he is trustworthy with no harm, passed under numbers 1307, 5864. In the printed edition it was "al-Nadr ibn Ali al-Jazari", which differs from the manuscript and is an error.]]

18973 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, his saying: ﴿And she said, Hayta laka﴾ al-Hasan said: He says: come to you.

18974 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ Some of them say: come to you.

18975 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿And she said, Hayta laka﴾ He said: come to you = and it is in Coptic.

18976 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata narrated to us, from Amr, from al-Hasan: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ He said: a word in Syriac, meaning: upon you.

18977 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ He said: come to you.

18978 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Khalaf ibn Hisham narrated to us, he said: Mahbub narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ He said: come to you.

18979 -.... He said: Affan narrated to us, he said: Hammad narrated to us, from Asim, from Zirr: ﴿Hayta laka﴾, meaning: come.

18980 - al-Harith narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, he said: al-Thawri narrated to us, he said: It reached me regarding his saying: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ He said: come to you.

18981 - Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, he said: Abu Ubayd narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas that he read: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ and said: she calls him to herself.

18982 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God exalted: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ He said: an Arabic language, by which she calls him.

18983 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same, except that he said: a language in Arabic, by which she calls him to herself.

18984 - al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Shababah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, exactly like the report of Muhammad ibn Amr.

18985 - al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

18986 - Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, he said: al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ with a fatha on the ha' and the ta', and he said: You say: come to you.

18987 - al-Harith narrated to me, he said: Abu Ubayd said: al-Kisa'i used to relate it = meaning: ﴿Hayta laka﴾. He said: and he said: it is a dialect of the people of Hawran that reached the Hijaz, its meaning being "come." He said: Abu Ubaydah said: I asked an learned elder from the people of Hawran, and he mentioned that it is their language, which they know.

18988 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ He said: come.

18989 - Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his saying: ﴿And she said, Hayta laka﴾ He said: come to me.

* *

Some of the early reciters read it: "Hi'tu laka" with a kasra on the ha', a damma on the ta', and a hamza, meaning: I have prepared myself for you, from the speaker's saying: "hi'tu lil-amr, uhayy'u hay'atan" (I prepared myself for the matter).

Among those narrated from him this reading are Ibn Abbas, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, and a group other than them.

18990 - Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, he said: al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, from Aban al-Attar, from Qatadah: that Ibn Abbas read it thus, with a kasra on the ha' and a damma on the ta'. Ahmad said: Abu Ubaydah said: I do not know it except with a hamza.

18991 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Aban al-Attar, from Asim, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami: "Hi'tu laka", meaning: I have prepared myself for you.

18992 -.... He said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, the same.

18993 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, he said: Ikrimah used to say: I have prepared myself for you.

18994 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, he said: "Hi'tu laka", Ikrimah said: I have prepared myself for you.

18995 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, he said: Hammad narrated to us, from Asim ibn Bahdalah, he said: Abu Wa'il used to say: "Hi'tu laka": meaning, I have prepared myself for you. And Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' and al-Kisa'i used to deny this reading.

18996 - It was related to me from Ali ibn al-Mughirah, he said: Abu Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna said: I witnessed Abu Amr, and Abu Ahmad asked him = or Ahmad = and he was knowledgeable in the Qur'an [[This addition between the brackets is from Abu Ubaydah's book, Majaz al-Qur'an 1:305. His saying "la'ala'" is a pearl seller, and it is also said "la'" and "lal'" (with a doubled hamza after the ha' and alif) on the pattern of "najjar".]] [and he was a pearl seller, then he grew old and sat in his house, and the Qur'an was taken from him, and he was with the judges, so he was asked] about the saying of the one who said: "Hi'tu laka" with a kasra on the ha' and a hamza on the ya'. Abu Amr said: [sa] [[Thus the word is written in the manuscript, and in the printed edition "yansa", and in Majaz al-Qur'an "bansa" (with a kasra on the nun, a sukun on the ba', a kasra on the sin, followed by a ya'). I am in doubt about all of this, and I fear it may be "absbas" (with a fatha, then sukun, then fatha), and "al-absbas" means falsehood, and "al-absabas" is similar.]] meaning: falsehood. He made it "fa'alat" from "tahayya'at" (I prepared myself). This is the trench [[The "trench" is the trench of Shapur, which he dug from the city of "Hit", extending across the edge of the desert to Kazima, on the side near Basra, and he placed guards upon it. Abu Ubaydah explained it fully in al-Majaz, so refer to it there.]] so he presented the Arabs until he reached Yemen: do you know anyone who says: "Hi'tu laka"? [[Report 18996: this is the exact text of Abu Ubaydah's words in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:305-306.]]

18997 - al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Kisa'i did not relate "Hi'tu laka" from the Arabs.

* *

The majority of the reciters of Medina read it: "Hiyta laka" with a kasra on the ha', a sukun on the ya', and a fatha on the ta'.

* *

Some of the Meccan reciters read it: "Hayta laka" with a fatha on the ha', a sukun on the ya', and a damma on the ta'.

* *

Some of the Basran reciters, namely Abd Allah ibn Ishaq, read it: "Hayta laka" with a fatha on the ha' and a kasra on the ta'.

* *

Some narrators have recited a verse of Tarafah ibn al-Abd concerning "hayt" with a fatha on the ha' and a damma on the ta', which is:

"My people are not the most distant when, if a caller from the clan says 'hayt'..." [[I have not found this verse elsewhere.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable reading in this matter is the reading of those who recite: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ with a fatha on the ha' and the ta', and a sukun on the ya', because it is the well-known language among the Arabs, to the exclusion of others, and because it is, as has been mentioned, the reading of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

18998 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: al-Thawri informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, who said Ibn Mas'ud said: I have heard the readings, and I heard them as close to one another; so recite as you were taught, and beware of excess and disagreement, for it is only like the saying of one of you: "halumma" and "ta'al". Then Abd Allah recited: ﴿Hayta laka﴾. I said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, some people recite it: "Hayta laka"; Abd Allah said: I recite it as I was taught, which is more beloved to me. [[Report 18998: this is a sound chain; a similar account has passed many times, and will come later by shorter routes. This report was related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 8:274, 275), in abridged form. Abu Dawud also related it in abridged form in his Sunan 4:52, 53, numbers 4004, 4005. Abu Ja'far related it earlier by other routes, abridged, without "hayta laka", at number 48, at the beginning of the book. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, in al-Fath, discussed it fully.]]

18999 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, he said: I heard Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud recite this verse: ﴿And she said, Hayta laka﴾. He said: They said to him: We used to recite it only as "Hayta laka". Abd Allah said: I recite it as I was taught, which is more beloved to me. [[Report 18999: a repetition of the earlier report, abridged.]]

19000 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, he said: Abd Allah said: ﴿Hayta laka﴾. Masruq said to him: Some people recite it: "Hayta laka". He said: Leave me, for I recite as I was taught, which is more beloved to me. [[Report 19000: a repetition of the two earlier reports, by another sound route, abridged.]]

19001 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Adam al-Asqalani narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Ibn Mas'ud, he said: ﴿Hayta laka﴾ with a fatha on the ha' and the ta', and without a hamza. [[Report 19001: an abridgement of the earlier reports, by sound routes.]]

* *

Abu Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna mentioned that the Arabs do not form the dual, plural, or feminine of "hayta"; they keep it in one form in every case, and the number is shown only by what follows it, as with gender. He said: You say to one person "hayta laka", to two "hayta lakuma", to a group "hayta lakum", and to women "hayta lakunna". [[See Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu Ubaydah 1:305.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He said, "I seek refuge in Allah"﴾, He, may His praise be exalted, says: Yusuf said when the woman called him to herself and said to him, "Come to me": I seek protection in Allah from what you call me to, and I seek refuge in Him from it. [[See the explanation of "ʿādha" above, 15:352, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, he is my lord⁠—he has made my residence good﴾, it means: Indeed, your husband, my master, [[See the explanation of "al-Rabb" above, 1:141-142 / 12:385-386, and elsewhere in the indices of language (rbb).]] as:

19002 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿I seek refuge in Allah; indeed, he is my lord﴾ He said: my master.

19003 -.... He said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih: ﴿Indeed, he is my lord﴾ He said: my master.

19004 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Shababah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

19005 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

19006 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

19007 - al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿I seek refuge in Allah; indeed, he is my lord, he has made my residence good﴾ He said: my master, meaning: the husband of the woman.

19008 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿I seek refuge in Allah; indeed, he is my lord﴾ meaning: Itfir. He says: indeed, he is my master.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He has made my residence good﴾, it means: He has made my standing good, honored me, and entrusted me, so I will not betray him, as:

19009 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: ﴿He has made my residence good﴾ He entrusted me with his house and his family.

19010 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿He has made my residence good﴾ so I will not betray him regarding his family.

19011 - al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿He has made my residence good﴾ He said: Yusuf means his master, the husband of the woman.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾, it means: Indeed, he does not attain permanence, and whoever does wrong does not prosper, so he would do what is not his to do. And what you call me to of immorality is wrongdoing and betrayal of my master, who entrusted me with his household, as:

19012 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾ He said: what you call me to is wrongdoing, and whoever acts by it will not succeed.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 24 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Lord. Thus [it was], that We might avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.﴾ (24)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: It is mentioned that when the wife of the ruler (al-'Aziz) desired Joseph and sought to seduce him, she began to mention to him the beauties of his person and to express her longing for herself, as follows:

19013 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾. He said: She said to him, "O Joseph, how beautiful is your hair!" He said, "It is the first thing to fall from my body." She said, "O Joseph, how beautiful is your face!" He said, "It is for the dust to consume." She did not cease until she made him covetous, and he desired her and she desired him, and they entered the room, and she locked the doors, and he went to untie his trousers. Then, behold, he saw the image of Ya'qub standing in the room, having bitten on his finger, saying: "O Joseph, do not have intercourse with her [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "tuwaqi'uha" without "la", and I have restored it from the History.]] For your likeness, if you do not have intercourse with her, is like the bird in the air of the sky that cannot be caught. And your likeness, if you have intercourse with her, is like it when it dies and falls to the earth, unable to defend itself. And your likeness, if you do not have intercourse with her, is like the difficult bull that is not worked upon. And your likeness, if you have intercourse with her, is like the bull when it dies and the ants enter the base of its horns, unable to defend itself." So he tied his trousers and went out running [["ishtadda", he hastened, ran swiftly.]]. She caught up with him, seized the back of his shirt from behind and tore it, until she pulled him out of it and he fell. Joseph threw him off and ran toward the door. [[The report: 19013 - Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History 1: 173.]]

19014 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: She bent over him - meaning the woman - enticing him at one time and frightening him at another, and calling him to the pleasure of the need men have for her beauty, loveliness and possession, while he was a young man in his prime who felt the lust men feel; until he was softened toward her by what he saw of her infatuation with him, and he did not fear her until he desired her and she desired him, until they were alone in some of her rooms.

* *

The meaning of "al-hamm bi al-shay'" (intent toward a thing) in the speech of the Arabs is a person's inner speech about having intercourse with it, so long as he has not actually done it. [[See the explanation of "al-hamm" previously at 9: 199 / 10: 100 / 14: 158, where it was not explained sufficiently, and I explain it here.]]

* *

As for what occurred of Joseph's intent toward the woman and her intent toward him, the people of knowledge have said about this what I shall mention, namely:

19015 - Abu Kurayb, Sufyan ibn Wakī' and Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who was asked what the intent of Joseph reached. He said: He untied the money belt and sat between her [thighs] as one who circumcises [[His words "majlis al-khatin" refer to one who circumcises a boy or a girl; in the printed History of al-Tabari it reads "majlis al-ha'iz", but the manuscript of the Tafsir has "al-khatin" everywhere, and the explanation of "al-himyan" will come in no. 19022; in al-Lisan it is "the drawstring of the trousers".]] = the wording of the report is that of Abu Kurayb. [[The report: 19015 - Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History 1: 173, with this same chain.]]

19016 - Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, saying: He heard 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid say that Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾, said: He sat between her [thighs] as one who circumcises, and untied the money belt.

19017 - Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hassani, 'Amr ibn 'Ali and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas being asked: How far did Joseph's intent go? He said: He untied the money belt, and sat between her [thighs] as one who circumcises.

19018 - Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas: How far did Joseph's intent go? He said: She lay on her back for him, and he sat between her legs.

19019 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, concerning ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾: He said: She lay on her back for him, and he untied his garments.

19020 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Qabisah ibn 'Uqbah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾, what did it reach? He said: She lay on her back for him and he sat between her legs and untied his garments = or her garments.

19021 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas how far Joseph's intent went? He said: She lay on her back, and he sat between her legs to remove his garments.

19022 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakī' narrated to us = and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Nafi' ibn 'Umar, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about His words ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾: how far did Joseph's intent go?
