19023 - Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard al-A'mash, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾, he said: He untied the trousers down to his buttocks [[In the printed edition: "hatta al-tiban", which is a small pair of trousers about a span long covering the heavy private parts, and is not correct. In the manuscript at this place: "al-tabn", undotted; then in no. 19024 it reads "hatta waqa'a 'ala al-tantayn", and then in no. 19029 also "'ala al-thanat"; the editor has rendered all of them as "al-tiban" with one spelling, and I have preferred to write "alyatayh" in two places and "alyatih" in the last instances, because I found the report from Mujahid in al-Qurtubi 9: 166 as "hal al-sarawil hatta balagha al-alyatayn", and if written as in al-Qurtubi it would be correct; "al-alyah" (with a fatha on the hamza) is the buttock of people and others, and the two of humans are "alyatan", and it is said "innahu la-dhu alyat", as if each part were considered an "alyah" and then pluralized on this basis.]] and she lay on her back for him.

19024 - Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hassani narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Su'ayr narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾: He said: He untied his trousers until they fell upon his buttocks. [[See the previous note; in the printed edition it was "'ala al-tiban".]]

19025 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾: He said: He sat between her as a man sits with his wife.

19026 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah narrated to me: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾: He said: As for her desire for him, she lay on her back for him = and as for his desire for her, he sat between her legs and removed his garments.

19027 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: How far did Joseph's intent go? He said: She lay on her back for him, and he sat between her legs, removing his garments.

19028 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn al-Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ikrimah, who both said: He untied the trousers and sat between her as one who circumcises.

19029 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi narrated to us, from Sharik, from Jabir, from Mujahid: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾: He said: She lay on her back, and he untied his garments until they reached his buttocks. [[" Ayat" is the plural of "alyah"; see what preceded on p. 36, note 1.]]

19030 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾: He said: He loosened the drawstring of his trousers.

19031 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: I witnessed Ibn 'Abbas being asked about the intent of Joseph, how far did it reach? He said: He untied the money belt, and sat between her as one who circumcises.

* *

If someone says: How is it permissible to ascribe such a thing to Joseph, when he is a prophet of God?

It is said: The people of knowledge differed on this.

Some of them said: Whoever among the prophets was tested with a sin, God only tested him with it so that he would be in a state of fear of God, exalted is He, whenever he remembered it, and would strive in obedience out of apprehension of it, and not rely upon the vastness of God's pardon and mercy.

* *

And others said: Rather, God tested them with that to make them know the place of His blessing upon them, by His forgiving them and His leaving off punishing them for it in the Hereafter.

* *

And others said: Rather, God tested them with that in order to make them leaders for the people of sins in hope of God's mercy, and in not despairing of His pardon for them if they repent.

* *

As for others who opposed the sayings of the early generations and interpreted the Qur'an by their own opinions, they stated various sayings on this.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: The woman certainly desired Joseph, and Joseph would have desired her, intending to strike her or to harm her because of her desire for him concerning what she wanted of harm; had it not been that Joseph saw the proof of his Lord, which restrained him from what he intended of harming her. It was not that she refrained of her own accord. They said: The evidence for the correctness of this is His words: ﴿Thus [it was], that We might avert from him evil and immorality.﴾ They said: So "evil" is what he had intended of harming her, and it is other than "immorality".

* *

And others among them said: The meaning of the speech is: She certainly desired him, and her report ended there. Then the report about Joseph began, and it was said: "And Joseph would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Lord." As if they directed the meaning of the speech to the fact that Joseph did not desire her, and that God only informed that Joseph would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Lord, but he saw the proof of his Lord and did not desire her, as is said: ﴿And had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except a few.﴾ [an-Nisa': 83].

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What invalidates these two sayings is that the Arabs do not place the answer of "law" (lawla) before it; one does not say "I stood up, were it not for Zayd," meaning "Were it not for Zayd, I would have stood up." Moreover, both are opposed by all the people of knowledge of the interpretation of the Qur'an, from whom its interpretation is taken.

* *

And others among them said: Rather, the woman certainly desired Joseph, and Joseph desired the woman, but their desire was an inclination between doing and leaving, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "tamthilan minhuma", which is an error. "At-tamyil" means preference, i.e., which of the two you take and which you leave. It is said: "Indeed I incline between those two matters, and I weigh between them: which of them I should ride, or which is better."]] neither a resolution nor a determination. They said: There is no blame in inner speech, nor in the mention of the heart, when there is no resolution or action with them.

* *

As for the "proof" (burhan) that Joseph saw, because of which he abandoned committing the sin, the people of knowledge differ about it.

Some of them said: He was called to the prohibition of committing the sin.

Those who said this:

19032 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: He said: He was called: "O Joseph, will you commit fornication, and be like the bird whose feathers have fallen, which tries to fly but has no feathers?"

19033 - ... He said: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He did not yield to the call until he saw the proof of his Lord, which he said was the image of the face of his father = Sufyan said: biting on his finger = and he said: "O Joseph, will you commit fornication, and be like the bird whose feathers have gone?"

19034 - Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hassani narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: He was called: "O son of Ya'qub, do not be like the bird that has feathers; when it commits fornication its feathers fall off, or it sits without feathers." He said: He did not yield to the call, and did not add more to this. = Ibn Jurayj said: And others narrated to me that he saw his father biting on his finger.

19035 - Abu Kurayb narrated to me, saying: Wakī' narrated to us = and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us =, from Nafi' ibn 'Umar, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: He said: He was called but did not hear, so it was said to him: "O son of Ya'qub, do you want to commit fornication, and be like the bird whose feathers have been plucked, with no feathers?"

19036 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Talhah, from 'Amr al-Hadrami, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: It reached me that when Joseph sat between the legs of the woman and was untying his money belt, he was called: "O Joseph son of Ya'qub, do not commit fornication, for when the bird commits fornication its feathers fall out." He turned away, then was called again and turned away, and then his father Ya'qub appeared to him biting on his finger, and he stood up.

19037 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Qabisah ibn 'Uqbah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He was called: "O son of Ya'qub, do not be like the bird which, when it commits fornication, its feathers fall off, and it remains without feathers!" But he did not obey the call, and was startled.

19038 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: He was called: "O son of Ya'qub, you must not be like the bird that has feathers; when it commits fornication its feathers fall off" = he said: "or it sits without feathers" = he did not yield to the call at all, until he saw the proof of his Lord, so he trembled and fled.

19039 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: He was called: "O son of Ya'qub, will you commit fornication, and be like the bird whose feathers have fallen, which tries to fly but has no feathers?"

19040 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, from Hammam ibn Yahya, from Qatadah, who said: Joseph was called and it was said: "You are recorded among the prophets, and you do the deeds of fools?"

19041 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: He was called: "O Joseph son of Ya'qub, will you commit fornication, and be like the bird whose feathers have been plucked, with no feathers?"

* *

Others said: The "proof" which Joseph saw, because of which he refrained from committing the sin, was the image of Ya'qub, peace be upon them both, threatening him.

Those who said this:

19042 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi narrated to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: He said: He saw the image = or: the likeness = of the face of Ya'qub biting on his finger, and his desire came out from his fingertips.

19043 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: He said: Ya'qub appeared to him and struck him in the chest, and his desire came out from his fingertips. [[The report: 19043 - "'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi", which has occurred many times; in the printed edition and manuscript it was "'Amr ibn al-'Anqazi", the name of his father having dropped.]]

19044 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: He said: He saw the image of his father's face, saying with his hand thus = and he spread out his hand = and his desire came out from his fingertips.

19045 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakī' narrated to us = and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us =, from Sufyan, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: He said: Ya'qub appeared to him biting on his fingers, and struck his chest, and his desire came out from his fingertips.

19046 - Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed me, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: He said: He saw the image of Ya'qub placing his fingertip on his mouth, threatening him, and he fled.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 24 (part 2 of 2):**

19047. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Yahya ibn Abbad told us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim told us, saying: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah relate, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾, that he said: "When he saw Ya'qub on the ceiling of the house." He said: "So his desire, which he had been feeling, was removed, until he went out running toward the door of the house, and the woman followed him."

19048. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us (and Ibn Waki' told us, saying: my father told us), from Qurrah ibn Khalid al-Sadusi, from al-Hasan, who said: "They claim, and God knows best, that the ceiling of the house split open, and he saw Ya'qub biting on his fingers."

19049. Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, that he said: "He saw the image of Ya'qub biting on his finger, saying: 'Yusuf! Yusuf!'"

19050. Ibn Waki' told us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, similarly.

19051. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Amr al-Anqazi told us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, he said: "He saw the image of the face of Ya'qub, and his desire came out from his fingertips."

19052. Ibn Waki' told us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from Ali ibn Badhimah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "He saw a picture in which was the face of Ya'qub, biting on his fingers, so he pushed it in its chest, and his desire came out from his fingertips. 19053. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman informed him: "The proof that Yusuf saw was Ya'qub."

19054. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Isa ibn al-Mundhir told us, saying: Ayyub ibn Suwayd told us, saying: Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli told us, from al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, the like of it.

19055. Ibn Waki' told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, he said: "Ya'qub was presented to him."

19056. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Hakkam told us, from Amr, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the like of it.

19057. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, he said: "Ya'qub."

19058. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Shababah told us, saying: Warqa' told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

19059. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

19060. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, and al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Ya'qub was presented to him."

19061. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "He sat with her as a man sits with his wife, until he saw the image of Ya'qub on the walls." [[In the printed edition: "on the wall," and I have retained what is in the manuscript, which is correct.]]

19062. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, he said: "Ya'qub was presented to him."

19063. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who said: "It was called out: 'O son of Ya'qub, do not be like the bird that has feathers, for when it commits adultery it sits without feathers.' He did not turn to the call and sat down, then he raised his head and saw the face of Ya'qub biting on his finger, so he got up in fright, out of shame before God. That is the saying of God: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, the face of Ya'qub."

19064. Ibn Waki' told us, saying: My father told us, from al-Nadr ibn Arabi, from Ikrimah, who said: "Ya'qub was presented to him, biting on his fingers."

19065. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Nadr ibn Arabi, from Ikrimah, the like of it.

19066. Al-Harith told me, saying: Abd al-Aziz told us, saying: Qays told us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "Ya'qub was presented to him, so he pushed it in its chest, and his desire came out from his fingertips."

19067. ... He said: Abd al-Aziz told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ali ibn Badhimah, who said: "Every man of them would have twelve sons born to him, except Yusuf, who had eleven, because of what came out of his desire."

19068. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Shurayh said: "I heard Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far say: 'So great was Yusuf's desire that it came out from his fingertips.'"

19069. Ibn Waki' told us, saying: Ya'la ibn Ubayd told us, from Muhammad al-Khurasani, who said: "I asked Muhammad ibn Sirin about His saying: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, and he said: 'Ya'qub was presented to him, biting on his fingers, saying: "Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Khalil Allah! 19070. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told me, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayi told us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, he said: "He saw Ya'qub biting on his finger, saying: 'Yusuf!'"

19071. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, who said: Qatadah said: "He saw the image of Ya'qub, and said: 'O Yusuf, do you do the deeds of the wicked, while you are written among the prophets?' So he felt shame before him."

19072. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: "He saw a sign of the signs of his Lord, by which God restrained him from his disobedience. 19073. ... He said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, that Ya'qub was presented to him while he was biting on one of his fingers.

19074. Ya'qub told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Salim informed us, from Abu Salih, who said: "He saw the image of Ya'qub on the ceiling of the house, biting on his finger, saying: 'O Yusuf! O Yusuf!' This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾."

19075. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Amr ibn Awn told us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Mansur and Yunus, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, he said: "He saw the image of Ya'qub on the ceiling of the house, biting on his finger."

19076. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Amr ibn Awn told us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Isma'il ibn Salim, from Abu Salih, the like of it, and he said: "biting on his finger, saying: 'Yusuf! Yusuf!'"

19077. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi told us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn Atiyyah, who said: "Yusuf looked at the image of Ya'qub biting on his finger, saying: 'O Yusuf!' That is when he restrained himself, got up, and fled."

Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Al-Hammani told us, saying: Shurayk told us, from Salim and Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, he said: "He saw a picture in which was the face of Ya'qub, biting on his fingers, so he pushed it in its chest, and his desire came out from between his fingers."

It was reported to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: "A sign from his Lord. * *

Others said: "Rather, the proof that Yusuf saw was what God, mighty and majestic, had threatened against the people who commit adultery."

Those who said this:

19084. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Abu Mawdud, who said: "I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: 'He raised his head to the ceiling of the house, and there was a writing on the wall of the house: ﴿And do not approach fornication; indeed, it is an indecency and an evil way﴾.'" [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: ﴿Indeed, it was an indecency and hatred and an evil way﴾; this is another verse, the verse on marrying what the fathers married of women (Surah al-Nisa, 22), and the mention of "hatred" is undoubtedly a scribal error. 19085. Ibn Waki' told us, saying: My father told us, from Abu Mawdud, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: "Yusuf raised his head to the ceiling of the house when he resolved, and he saw a writing on the wall of the house: ﴿And do not approach fornication; indeed, it is an indecency and an evil way﴾."

19086. ... He said: Zayd ibn al-Habbab told us, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, he said: "Had it not been for what he saw in the Qur'an of the magnification of adultery."

19087. Yunus told us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, from Abu Sakhr, who said: "I heard al-Qurazi say concerning the proof that Yusuf saw: 'Three verses from the Book of God: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians﴾ and so on [Surah al-Infitar, 10], and His saying: ﴿And you are not in any affair﴾ and so on [Surah Yunus, 61], and His saying: ﴿Is then He who is standing over every soul in what it has earned?﴾ [Surah al-Ra'd, 33].'" Nafi' said: "I heard Abu Hilal say the same as al-Qurazi said, and he added a fourth verse: ﴿And do not approach adultery﴾."

19088. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Abu Ma'shar informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, concerning: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, he said: "What God had forbidden him of adultery."

* *

Others said: "Rather, he saw the image of the king."

Those who said this:

19089. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, meaning: "The signs of his Lord. He was shown the image of the king."

19090. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: "Some of the people of knowledge, as it has reached me, used to say: 'The proof that Yusuf saw, by which evil and indecency were turned away from him, was Ya'qub biting on his finger, and when he saw him he fled in alarm.' Some of them say: 'It was only the apparition of Itfir, his master, when he drew near the door, for when he fled from her and she pursued him, they found him at the door.'"

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of these sayings is that it should be said: God, His praise be exalted, informed of the desire of Yusuf and the wife of the chief, each of them toward the other, "had he not seen the proof of his Lord." That was a sign from God that restrained him from committing the indecency that Yusuf had desired. It is possible that this sign was the image of Ya'qub, and it is possible that it was the image of the king, and it is possible that the threat was in the verses which God mentioned in the Qur'an concerning adultery. No conclusive proof establishes which of these it was, or from which. The correct approach is to say what God, blessed and exalted, has said, to believe in it, and to leave what is beyond that to its All-Knowing One.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Thus, that We might avert from him evil and immorality﴾, God, exalted be His remembrance, says: Just as We showed Yusuf Our proof to restrain him from the indecency he had desired, so We also arrange for him, in every matter that comes upon him of concern about what he does not approve of, what will restrain and repel him from it, so that We may turn him away from committing what We have forbidden him, and from practicing adultery, in order to purify him from the filth of that. [[See the explanation of "turning away" (al-sarf) in what has preceded, vol. 15, p. 254, note 3, and the references there.
= And the explanation of "immorality" (al-fahsha') in what has preceded, vol. 12, p. 547, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, he was of Our sincere servants﴾: the readers differed in reciting it.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa recited it ﴿Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants﴾ with a fatha on the lam of "al-mukhlasin," on the interpretation: Indeed Yusuf is of Our servants whom We have chosen for Ourselves, and selected for Our prophethood and messengerhood.

* *

Some of the readers of Basra recited: "Innahu min ibadina al-mukhlisin" with a kasra on the lam, meaning: Indeed Yusuf is of Our servants who made their monotheism and worship sincere to Us, so they associated nothing with Us, and worshipped nothing other than Us.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position on this is to say: They are two well-known readings, which many readers have recited, and their meanings are in agreement. For whoever God has chosen for Himself and selected is one who sincerely devotes monotheism and worship to God, and whoever makes the monotheism and worship of God sincere, and does not associate anything with God, is among those whom God has made sincere. So whichever of the two a reciter recites, he is correct in what is right.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And they raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back, and they met her husband at the door. She said: "What is the penalty for one who intended evil against your wife, except that he be imprisoned or suffer a painful punishment?"﴾ (12:25)

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, majestic is His praise, means: Yusuf and the wife of the 'Aziz raced to the door of the house. [See the discussion of "al-istibaq" (racing) earlier in this work, vol. 15, p. 577, note 2, and the references there.] As for Yusuf, he fled from committing the abomination, for he had seen the proof of his Lord, and so he repelled her. As for the woman, she pursued Yusuf in order to fulfil her need from him, the need for which she had solicited him. She overtook him and seized his shirt, pulling him back toward her and preventing him from leaving through the door. ﴿She tore his shirt from the back﴾ means: she ripped it from behind, not from the front, because Yusuf was the one fleeing and she was the one pursuing. [See the discussion of "ad-dubur" (the back) earlier in this work, vol. 14, p. 15, note 4, and the references there.] As related:

19091 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and they raced to the door﴾, he said: He and the woman raced to the door, ﴿and she tore his shirt from the back﴾.

19092 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When he saw the proof of his Lord, he broke away from her fleeing, and she pursued him, and she seized his shirt from behind and tore it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they met her husband at the door﴾, He, majestic is His praise, means: they came upon her master, [See the discussion of "alfa" (to find/meet) earlier in this work, vol. 3, pp. 306–307.] who was the woman's husband, ﴿at the door﴾, meaning: at the door. [See the discussion of "lada" (at) earlier in this work, vol. 6, p. 407.] Like the following:

19093 - Al-Harith narrated to me, who said: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, who said: al-Thawri narrated to us, from a man, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and they met her master﴾, he said: Her master: her husband; ﴿at the door﴾, he said: at the door.

19094 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Ishaq narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said regarding "al-sayyid" (master): the husband.

19095 - Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his saying: ﴿and they met her master at the door﴾, i.e., at the door.

19096 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, who said: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and they met her master at the door﴾, he said: He was sitting at the door, and her paternal cousin was with him. When she saw him she said: "What is the penalty for one who intended evil against your wife? He solicited me against myself, so I pushed him away from myself, and I tore his shirt." Yusuf said: "Rather, she solicited me against myself, and I fled from her, and she overtook me and tore my shirt." Her cousin said: "The evidence of this is in the shirt. If the shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is among the liars; but if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is among the truthful." So the shirt was brought, and he found it torn from the back. He said: ﴿Indeed, it is from your guile; indeed, your guile is great. Yusuf, turn away from this, and ask forgiveness for your sin; indeed, you were among the sinners.﴾

19097 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿and they met her master at the door﴾: Itfir, standing at the door of the house. She said, in fear and alarm: ﴿What is the penalty for one who intended evil against your wife, except that he be imprisoned or suffer a painful punishment?﴾ and she smeared him in that place with the accusation, fearing that her husband would accuse her of the foul act. Then he spoke, and his words were truthful: ﴿She solicited me against myself.﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿She said: What is the penalty for one who intended evil against your wife﴾, He, exalted is His remembrance, means: the wife of the 'Aziz said to her husband when they found him at the door, fearing that he would accuse her of immorality: What is the reward for a man who intended adultery with your wife, except that he be imprisoned, [See the discussion of "al-jaza'" (penalty/recompense) earlier in the glossary of terms, under the root j-z-y.] or except a painful punishment? That is, painful, causing agony.

* *

As for why He said: ﴿except that he be imprisoned or suffer a painful punishment﴾, it is because His saying ﴿except that he be imprisoned﴾ carries the meaning of "except imprisonment," so "punishment" is coordinated with it; this is because "an" (that) together with what it governs functions as a noun.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on the words of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿He said, "It was she who sought to seduce me from myself." And a witness from her family testified: "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars. But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful. So when he saw that his shirt was torn from the back, he said, 'Indeed, it is of your guile, [you women]. Indeed, your guile is great.'"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, the Exalted, says: Yusuf said, when the wife of the ruler (al-'Aziz) falsely accused him of desiring her in immorality, denying her claim and rejecting what was attributed to him: "It was not I who sought to seduce her; rather, it was she who sought to seduce me from myself." [[See the explanation of "al-murawada" (seeking to seduce) above, pp. 24, 25.]]

* *

It has also been said: Yusuf would not have mentioned this had she not accused him before her master of what she accused him of.

Those who said this:

19098 - Muhammad ibn 'Umarah narrated to me, he said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Shaiban informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf al-Shami, who said: Yusuf did not intend to mention it until she said: ﴿What is the recompense for one who intended evil to your family, except imprisonment or a painful punishment?﴾ (the verse). He said: So he became angry and said: ﴿It was she who sought to seduce me from myself.﴾ [[The report 19098: in the printed edition it reads "Nawf al-Shaybani," which is a plain error arising from the poor writing of the manuscript, though it is fairly clear. The correct reading is "Nawf al-Shami," who is "Nawf ibn Fudalah al-Bakali al-Himyari al-Shami." See what preceded at no. 18923 and the commentary on it.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, the scholars differed concerning the nature of the witness.

Some of them said: He was a child in the cradle.

Those who said this:

19099 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Four spoke while in the cradle while they were infants: the son of Pharaoh's hairdresser, the witness of Yusuf, the companion of Jurayj, and 'Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him. [[The report 19099: al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, Abu al-Hasan al-'Attar, narrated from Hammad ibn Salamah, and al-Humaydi and his son 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-'Ala' narrated from him. Trustworthy in narration. Biography in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/358.]]

19100 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: 'Isa, and the companion of Yusuf, and the companion of Jurayj — meaning: they spoke in the cradle. [[The report 19100: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, a liar, abandoned in hadith. He has passed several times, the last being no. 17616, 18439. However, the hadith of Abu Hurayrah in its full form is narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 6: 344–348), and Muslim in his Sahih 16: 106, and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 8057, 8058 with a sahih chain. See the commentary of my brother, may Allah have mercy on him.]]

19101 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Za'idah narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: A child.

19102 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: He was a child in the cradle.

19103 - Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, he said: Ayyub ibn Jabir narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: A child. [[The report 19103: Ayyub ibn Jabir ibn Sayyar al-Yamami, weak. Biography in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/410, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/242, and Mizan al-I'tidal 1:132.]]

19104 - Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, he said: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, with the like of it.

19105 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Sharik, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: He was a child in his cradle.

19106 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Husayn, from Hilal ibn Yasaf: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: A child in the cradle.

19107 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Abu Marzuq, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: A child whom Allah caused to speak. It is also said: One of sound opinion, by his own opinion. [[His saying "one of sound opinion, by his own opinion" means the witness was a man of sound judgment who gave that opinion by his own reasoning. See the following report, no. 19127.]]

19108 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: 'Affan informed us, he said: Hammad narrated to us, he said: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Four spoke while they were infants," and he mentioned among them the witness of Yusuf. [[The report 19108: the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib is a long hadith, narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad, nos. 2822, 2823, 2824, 2825, and at its end: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Four infants spoke: 'Isa son of Maryam, the companion of Jurayj, the witness of Yusuf, and the son of Pharaoh's hairdresser," but this last statement was not traced back to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Its chain is sahih.]].

19109 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾: they claim that he was a child in the house.

19110 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My uncle narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: He was a child in the cradle.

* *

Others said: He was a man with a beard.

Those who said this:

19111 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He had a beard.

19112 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: He was among the close associates of the king.

19113 - ... And with this chain: My father narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Hudayr, who heard 'Ikrimah say: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: He was not a child, but a wise man.

19114 - Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, he said: 'Imran ibn Hudayr narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, and it was mentioned in his presence: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾; they said: He was a child. He said: He is not a child, but a wise man. [[The report 19114: 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Sabbah al-Mismai, trustworthy. Biography in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/354.]]

19115 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: He was a man.

19116 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: A man.

19117 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: A man.

19118 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: A man.

19119 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Isra'il informed us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: One with a beard.

19120 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The cousin of her family was the witness from her family.

19121 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Isra'il informed us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: One with a beard.

19122 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Ghassan narrated to us, he said: Isra'il narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: One with a beard.

19123 - al-Harith narrated to me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, he said: Qays narrated to us, from Jabir, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: He was among the close associates of the king.

19124 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: A wise man who was from her family.

19125 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: A wise man from her family.

19126 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: He was a man.

19127 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, he said: Hushaym informed us, from one of his companions, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: A man who had an opinion, who gave his opinion.

19128 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: It is said: The witness was only an adviser, a man from the people of Itfir, and he used to seek help from his opinion; except that he said: "I testify that if his shirt is torn from the front, then she has spoken the truth and he is of the liars." [[The report 19128: the source of this statement is not identified, and the text is as it stands.]]

* *

It has also been said: The meaning of His words ﴿And a witness testified﴾ is: a judge gave judgment.

19129 - It was narrated to me from al-Farra', from Mu'alla ibn Hilal, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid.

* *

Others said: By the witness, He meant only the torn shirt.

Those who said this:

19130 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: His shirt is torn from the back, and that is the testimony.

19131 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Shababah narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His words: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾: his shirt is torn from the back, and that is the testimony.

19132 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾: he was not of mankind.

19133 - ... He said: Hafs narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, he said: He was of the command of Allah, and he was not human.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is the view of those who said: He was a child in the cradle, on account of the report we have cited from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he mentioned those who spoke in the cradle, and he mentioned that one of them was the companion of Yusuf.

* *

As for what Mujahid said, that it was the torn shirt, it has no meaning, because Allah, the Exalted, reported about the witness who testified to this that he was of the woman's family, saying: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, and it is not said of a shirt that it is of a man's family or a woman's family.

* *

As for His words: ﴿If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars﴾, this is because the one pursued, when he is fleeing, is seized from behind; so it was known that if the tear were from the front, he would not have been fleeing and pursued, but rather one who was pursuing and being repelled, and that would be testimony against his lie.

19134 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: He said: "I testify that if his shirt is torn from the front, then she has spoken the truth and he is of the liars." That is because a man only desires a woman facing her, ﴿and if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful﴾, because a man does not approach a woman from behind. He said: It is not fitting for the truth to be anything but that. So when al-'Aziz saw his shirt torn from the back, he knew it was from her guile, and said: ﴿Indeed, it is of your guile; indeed, your guile is great.﴾

19135 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, he said — meaning: the witness from her family: the shirt judges between them: (If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars; and if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful. So when he saw his shirt torn from the back, he said: Indeed, it is of your guile; indeed, your guile is great.)

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The "an" (that) which would normally follow "the testimony" was omitted, because he took the testimony to mean "speech," as if he said: "And a speaker from her family said: If his shirt..." — just as it is said: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 11], because he took the enjoining to mean "saying."

* *

As for His words: ﴿So when he saw his shirt torn from the back﴾, it is a report about the husband of the woman, who was the one who said to her: Indeed, this act is of your guile — that is, your handiwork, meaning the handiwork of women — ﴿indeed, your guile is great﴾.

* *

It has also been said: It is a report about the witness, that he was the one who said that.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on the words of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿He said, "It was she who sought to seduce me from myself." And a witness from her family testified: "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars. But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful. So when he saw that his shirt was torn from the back, he said, 'Indeed, it is of your guile, [you women]. Indeed, your guile is great.'"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, the Exalted, says: Yusuf said, when the wife of the ruler (al-'Aziz) falsely accused him of desiring her in immorality, denying her claim and rejecting what was attributed to him: "It was not I who sought to seduce her; rather, it was she who sought to seduce me from myself." [[See the explanation of "al-murawada" (seeking to seduce) above, pp. 24, 25.]]

* *

It has also been said: Yusuf would not have mentioned this had she not accused him before her master of what she accused him of.

Those who said this:

19098 - Muhammad ibn 'Umarah narrated to me, he said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Shaiban informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf al-Shami, who said: Yusuf did not intend to mention it until she said: ﴿What is the recompense for one who intended evil to your family, except imprisonment or a painful punishment?﴾ (the verse). He said: So he became angry and said: ﴿It was she who sought to seduce me from myself.﴾ [[The report 19098: in the printed edition it reads "Nawf al-Shaybani," which is a plain error arising from the poor writing of the manuscript, though it is fairly clear. The correct reading is "Nawf al-Shami," who is "Nawf ibn Fudalah al-Bakali al-Himyari al-Shami." See what preceded at no. 18923 and the commentary on it.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, the scholars differed concerning the nature of the witness.

Some of them said: He was a child in the cradle.

Those who said this:

19099 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Four spoke while in the cradle while they were infants: the son of Pharaoh's hairdresser, the witness of Yusuf, the companion of Jurayj, and 'Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him. [[The report 19099: al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, Abu al-Hasan al-'Attar, narrated from Hammad ibn Salamah, and al-Humaydi and his son 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-'Ala' narrated from him. Trustworthy in narration. Biography in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/358.]]

* *

As for what Mujahid said, that it was the torn shirt, it has no meaning, because Allah, the Exalted, reported about the witness who testified to this that he was of the woman's family, saying: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, and it is not said of a shirt that it is of a man's family or a woman's family.

* *

As for His words: ﴿If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars﴾, this is because the one pursued, when he is fleeing, is seized from behind; so it was known that if the tear were from the front, he would not have been fleeing and pursued, but rather one who was pursuing and being repelled, and that would be testimony against his lie.

19134 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: He said: "I testify that if his shirt is torn from the front, then she has spoken the truth and he is of the liars." That is because a man only desires a woman facing her, ﴿and if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful﴾, because a man does not approach a woman from behind. He said: It is not fitting for the truth to be anything but that. So when al-'Aziz saw his shirt torn from the back, he knew it was from her guile, and said: ﴿Indeed, it is of your guile; indeed, your guile is great.﴾

19135 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, he said — meaning: the witness from her family: the shirt judges between them: (If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars; and if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful. So when he saw his shirt torn from the back, he said: Indeed, it is of your guile; indeed, your guile is great.)

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The "an" (that) which would normally follow "the testimony" was omitted, because he took the testimony to mean "speech," as if he said: "And a speaker from her family said: If his shirt..." — just as it is said: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 11], because he took the enjoining to mean "saying."

* *

As for His words: ﴿So when he saw his shirt torn from the back﴾, it is a report about the husband of the woman, who was the one who said to her: Indeed, this act is of your guile — that is, your handiwork, meaning the handiwork of women — ﴿indeed, your guile is great﴾.

* *

It has also been said: It is a report about the witness, that he was the one who said that.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on the words of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿He said, "It was she who sought to seduce me from myself." And a witness from her family testified: "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars. But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful. So when he saw that his shirt was torn from the back, he said, 'Indeed, it is of your guile, [you women]. Indeed, your guile is great.'"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, the Exalted, says: Yusuf said, when the wife of the ruler (al-'Aziz) falsely accused him of desiring her in immorality, denying her claim and rejecting what was attributed to him: "It was not I who sought to seduce her; rather, it was she who sought to seduce me from myself." [[See the explanation of "al-murawada" (seeking to seduce) above, pp. 24, 25.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is the view of those who said: He was a child in the cradle, on account of the report we have cited from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he mentioned those who spoke in the cradle, and he mentioned that one of them was the companion of Yusuf.

* *

As for what Mujahid said, that it was the torn shirt, it has no meaning, because Allah, the Exalted, reported about the witness who testified to this that he was of the woman's family, saying: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾, and it is not said of a shirt that it is of a man's family or a woman's family.

* *

As for His words: ﴿If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars﴾, this is because the one pursued, when he is fleeing, is seized from behind; so it was known that if the tear were from the front, he would not have been fleeing and pursued, but rather one who was pursuing and being repelled, and that would be testimony against his lie.

19134 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: He said: "I testify that if his shirt is torn from the front, then she has spoken the truth and he is of the liars." That is because a man only desires a woman facing her, ﴿and if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful﴾, because a man does not approach a woman from behind. He said: It is not fitting for the truth to be anything but that. So when al-'Aziz saw his shirt torn from the back, he knew it was from her guile, and said: ﴿Indeed, it is of your guile; indeed, your guile is great.﴾

19135 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, he said — meaning: the witness from her family: the shirt judges between them: (If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars; and if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful. So when he saw his shirt torn from the back, he said: Indeed, it is of your guile; indeed, your guile is great.)

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The "an" (that) which would normally follow "the testimony" was omitted, because he took the testimony to mean "speech," as if he said: "And a speaker from her family said: If his shirt..." — just as it is said: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 11], because he took the enjoining to mean "saying."

* *

As for His words: ﴿So when he saw his shirt torn from the back﴾, it is a report about the husband of the woman, who was the one who said to her: Indeed, this act is of your guile — that is, your handiwork, meaning the handiwork of women — ﴿indeed, your guile is great﴾.

* *

It has also been said: It is a report about the witness, that he was the one who said that.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Joseph, turn away from this, and ask forgiveness for your sin, for you were indeed among the sinners﴾ (29)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is what has been related from Ibn 'Abbas: it is a report from God, exalted is His remembrance, about the words of the witness, that he said to the woman and to Joseph.

* *

By His words ﴿Joseph﴾ he means: O Joseph. ﴿Turn away from this﴾ means: turn away from mentioning what she did toward you in soliciting you, so do not mention it to anyone. [See the explanation of "i'rad" (turning away) above, vol. 15, p. 407, footnote 1, and the references there.] As related:

19136. Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿Joseph, turn away from this﴾: "Do not mention it." ﴿And ask forgiveness﴾, you (the woman), [means]: ask your husband, meaning: ask him not to punish you for the sin you committed, and to pardon it and conceal it for you.

* *

﴿For you were indeed among the sinners﴾ means: you were indeed among those who sinned in soliciting Joseph to yield himself to you.

* *

From this it is said: "khati'a" (he erred) in the matter of sin, "yakhta'u" (he errs), "khit'an" and "khata'an" (error). [See the explanation of "khati'a" above, vol. 2, p. 110, and vol. 6, p. 143.] As His exalted words say: ﴿Indeed, killing them was a great sin﴾ [Surah al-Isra, 31], and "al-khata'" (error) is in the matter [of unintentional wrong].

It is also reported for "al-sawab" (correctness) that it is "al-sawab" and "al-sawb," [In the printed and manuscript texts: "also al-sawab, and al-sawb," and it seems that the correct reading is what has been given. I fear it may be: "wal-khata'" and "al-khata'" in the matter, and it is reported for "al-sawab ...", meaning the short and long forms.] as the poet said:

"By your life, my error and my correctness are upon me, and what I destroyed is wealth..."

[Nawadir Abi Zayd: 47; Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara: 140; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah, vol. 1, p. 241; al-Lisan (s-w-b). From verses he says to his wife: "Did Umamah not say on the day of ghul: ... the ropes were cut for Ibn Ghalfa..." "Leave me, for my error and my correctness..." "If Umamah sees me, my wealth has diminished, and humiliation from raiding has distracted me..." "Then I may amuse myself with intoxicated companions; for me there is the connected lineage and the friendships."]

And the verse of Umayyah is recited:

"Your servants err, and You are Lord, with Your two hands are the deaths and the decrees..."

[His Diwan: 4; al-Lisan (kh-t-'); (h-t-m). Before the verse: "Your peace, our Lord, every dawn, free of what blame befits You..." After it: "On the day when some of them say: Would that your mother were barren."]

from "khati'a al-rajul" (the man erred).

* *

It has been said: "﴿For you were indeed among the sinners﴾" is not said as "sinful women" (feminine plural), because he did not intend by it a report about women; rather he intended a report about one who does such an act and thereby errs.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 30:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And women in the city said, "The wife of the chief minister is seeking to seduce her servant boy from himself. He has certainly captivated her with love. Indeed, we see her in clear error."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He says: The women discussed the matter of Yusuf and the matter of the wife of the chief minister in the city of Egypt, and what was between them spread there and was not concealed, and they said: ﴿The wife of the chief minister is seeking to seduce her fatan (fata)﴾ [see the explanation of "al-murawada" (seeking to seduce) earlier, p. 53, note 1, and the references there], meaning her servant ['abd] [see the explanation of "al-fata" (young man) earlier, 8:188] ﴿from himself﴾, as follows:

19137 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The report spread in the town, and the women discussed his affair and hers, and said: ﴿The wife of the chief minister is seeking to seduce her fata from himself﴾, meaning: her servant.

* *

As for "al-'Aziz" (the chief minister), it means "the king" in the speech of the Arabs, and from it is the verse of Abu Du'ad:

A pearl which a merchant dived for ... was displayed before a 'Aziz on a day of drizzle.
[I have not found this verse anywhere else.]

He means by al-'Aziz: the king, and it derives from "al-'izzah" (might).
[See the explanation of "al-'izzah" in the lexical indexes earlier under ('-z-z).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He has certainly captivated her with love﴾, it means: the love of Yusuf has reached the shaghaf (innermost covering) of her heart, entered beneath it, until it overcame her heart.

* *

And "shaghaf al-qalb" (the shaghaf of the heart) is its covering and its sheath in which it is contained, and it is this that al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani meant in his saying:

And a concern has come between that and an entering that enters ... as the entering of a shaghaf which the fingers seek.
[His Diwan: 38; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:308, and others, with variation in its transmission; and before it: "When I rebuked old age for youth, and I said: 'Will you not desist, while white hair is restraining?'"
"The fingers" means the fingers of physicians. Al-Tabari took it as "shaghaf" with a fatha, while the lexicographers take it as "shughaf" (with a damma on the shin), which is a disease that seizes beneath the ribs on the right side; when it reaches the spleen it kills its sufferer. This is the more correct of the two.]

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

19138 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Amr ibn Dinar informed me that he heard 'Ikrimah say concerning His saying: ﴿has captivated her with love﴾: "His love entered beneath the shaghaf."

19139 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Shababah related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿He has certainly captivated her with love﴾: "His love entered into her shaghaf."

19140 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿He has certainly captivated her with love﴾: "His love entered into her shaghaf."

19141 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿He has certainly captivated her with love﴾: "His love was in her shaghaf."

19142 - ... He said: Ishaq related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similar to the report of al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Shababah.

19143 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿He has certainly captivated her with love﴾, he says: "He made her attached (infatuated) with love."

19144 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿He has certainly captivated her with love﴾, he said: "He overcame her."

19145 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us = and Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: my father related to us = from his father, from Ayyub ibn 'A'idh al-Ta'i, from al-Sha'bi: ﴿He has certainly captivated her with love﴾, he said: "al-mashghuf" is the one in love, and "al-mash'uf" (with the letter 'ayn, which was in the printed edition with a ghayn, an error; al-Sha'bi intended to distinguish between them) is the insane.
[Report 19145: Ayyub ibn 'A'idh al-Mudlaji al-Ta'i, trustworthy, previously mentioned under nos. 10338, 10339.]

19146 - ... And with this chain he said: related to us, my father, from Abu al-Ashhab, from Abu Raja' and al-Hasan: ﴿He has certainly captivated her with love﴾. One of them said: "He has pierced her (baṭana-ha) with love." The other said: "He has sincerely (ṣadaqa-ha) loved her."

19147 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: ﴿He has captivated her with love﴾, he said: "He has pierced her with love." Ya'qub said: Abu Bishr said: The people of Madinah say: "Qad baṭanaha hubban."

19148 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, who said: I heard him say concerning His saying: ﴿He has captivated her with love﴾: "He pierced her with love." And the people of Madinah say that.

19149 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us, from Qurrah, from al-Hasan: ﴿He has captivated her with love﴾, he said: "He has pierced with her with love."
[In the manuscript: "baṭana la-ha"; see no. 19151.]

19150 - al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abu Qaṭan related to us, saying: Abu al-Ashhab related to us, from al-Hasan: ﴿He has captivated her with love﴾, he said: "His love pierced her."

19151 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan: ﴿He has captivated her with love﴾, he said: "He pierced with her."

19152 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿He has captivated her with love﴾, he said: "Her love for him penetrated her innermost."

19153 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿He has captivated her with love﴾, i.e.: "He has attached her (infatuated her)."

19154 - al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿He has captivated her with love﴾, he said: "He has attached her with love."

19155 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: al-Muharibi related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: It is the love that clings to the heart.

19156 - I was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: ﴿He has captivated her with love﴾, say: "She perished from it through love." And "al-shaghaf" is the shaghaf of the heart.

19157 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿He has captivated her with love﴾, he said: "And al-shaghaf is a membrane over the heart which is called 'the tongue of the heart'" [so it is in the printed edition and the manuscript; I incline to think the correct reading is "libas al-qalb" (the garment of the heart), since they said in explaining the word: "al-shaghaf: the sheath of the heart, a membrane beneath it like a veil, and its core," and they said "it is the covering of the heart," and Abu al-Haytham said: "It is said of the veil of the heart, a fatty layer that serves as a garment for the heart, the shaghaf."], he says: the love entered the membrane until it reached the heart.

* *

The reciters differed regarding the reading of this.

The majority of the reciters of the great cities read it with a ghayn: ﴿qad shaghafa-ha﴾, according to the meaning of the interpretation I have described.

* *

And Abu Raja' read it: "qad sha'afa-ha" with an 'ayn. [So it is in the manuscript: "sha'afa-ha"; I suspect the correct form is "shughifa bi-ha, idha kana huwa yuhibbuha" (she was smitten with her, when he loved her), in the passive, but what he said is something not known.]

19158 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Abu Qaṭan related to us, saying: Abu al-Ashhab related to us, from Abu Raja': "qad sha'afa-ha."

19159 - ... He said: Khalaf related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Abu al-Ashhab, or 'Awf, from Abu Raja': "qad sha'afa-ha ḥubban," with an 'ayn.

19160 - ... He said: Khalaf related to us, saying: Mahbub related to us, who said: 'Awf recited it: "qad sha'afa-ha."

19161 - ... He said: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us, from Harun, from Usayd, from al-A'raj: "qad sha'afa-ha ḥubban," and said: "sha'afa-ha" when he himself loved her.

* *

Those people directed the meaning of the statement towards the love having overwhelmed her entirely.

* *

And some of the scholars of Arabic speech among the Kufans used to say: it is from the saying of the speaker: "qad shu'ifa bi-ha" (she was smitten with him), as if he took her in every direction, from "sha'af al-jibal," which are their summits.

* *

It is narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that he said: "al-shaghf" is the shaghf of love, and "al-sha'f" is the sha'f of an animal when it is startled.

19162 - al-Harith related this to me, from al-Qasim, who said: It is narrated from Abu 'Awanah, from Mughirah, from him.

= al-Harith said: al-Qasim said: Ibrahim holds that the origin of "al-sha'af" is alarm. He said: And so it is, as Ibrahim said regarding the origin, except that the Arabs sometimes borrow the word and place it in other than its place. Imru' al-Qays said:

"Will you kill me, when I have captivated her heart, as the camel with mange is captivated by the tall man?"
[From his Diwan: 142; and al-Lisan, "sha'af"; and others, from the excellent qasidah, in which he mentions his beloved and her husband: ...]

He said: "sha'af al-mar'ah" (captivating a woman) is from love, and "sha'af al-mahnu'ah" (the scabby camel) is from alarm, so he likened the anguish and burning of love to that.

* *

And Ibn Zayd said regarding this:

19163 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿He has certainly captivated her with love﴾: "Indeed 'al-shaghf' and 'al-sha'f' are different: 'al-sha'f' is in hatred, and 'al-shaghf' is in love."

* *

What Ibn Zayd said has no meaning, because "al-sha'f" in the speech of the Arabs means the generality of love, too well known for anyone knowledgeable in their speech to be unaware of it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in our view is ﴿qad shaghafa-ha﴾ with a ghayn, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, we see her in clear error﴾, they said: indeed we see the wife of the chief minister, in her seeking to seduce her servant from himself, and the overwhelming of his love upon her, is in error regarding the act, and deviation from the right path, "clear" for whoever considers it and knows that it is misguidance, error, not correct nor right. [See the explanation of "al-dalal" (misguidance) and "mubin" (clear) in the lexical indexes earlier under (d-l-l) and (b-y-n).] And their saying what they said of that, and their discussing what they discussed of her affair and Yusuf's affair, was, as it is mentioned, a scheme from them, to make Yusuf appear to them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 31 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared for them a reclining-couch, and gave each one of them a knife, and said, "Come out before them." And when they saw him, they magnified him and cut their hands, and said, "Perfect is Allah! This is not a human; this is none but a noble angel."﴾ (12:31)

Abu Ja'far said: His, the Exalted's, remembrance means: When the wife of the chief heard of the scheming of the women who spoke in the city, what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned of them =
* *
And their scheming was what:
19164 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So when she heard of their scheming﴾, he said: of their speech.
19165 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When the women made that public, from their saying: "She is seeking to seduce her servant!" as a scheme against her, so that she might show them Yusuf, and he was being described to them for his beauty and comeliness: (﴿So when she heard of their scheming^[See the explanation of "scheming" above, 15:49, footnote 1, and the references there.]﴾ she sent for them and prepared for them a reclining-couch).
19166 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his saying: ﴿So when she heard of their scheming﴾: that is, of their talk, ﴿she sent for them﴾, he says: she sent to the women who were talking about her affair and Yusuf's.
* *
﴿And prepared﴾: an "af'ala" form from al-'Itad (preparation), which is the readiness; its meaning: she prepared for them ="muttaka'" (a reclining-couch), meaning: a seat for food, and what they lean upon of cushions and pillows:
* *
= and it is a "mufta'al" form from the saying of one who says "ittaka'a" (he leaned), and it is said: "Set down for him a muttaka'," meaning: that upon which one leans.
* *
The people of interpretation have said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.
Those who said that:
19167 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn al-Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾, he said: food, drink, and a reclining-couch.
19168 -.... He said: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾, he said: that upon which they recline.
19169 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾, he said: a seat.
19170 -.... He said: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Abu al-Ashhab, from al-Hasan, that he used to recite: ﴿muttaka'an^[The reading of al-Hasan with a long vowel and a hamza at the end; Ibn Khalawayh mentioned this reading in Shawadh al-Qira'at p. 63 from al-Hasan, and Abu Hayyan mentioned it in his tafsir 5:302, attributing it to al-Hasan and Ibn Hurmuz, and said: "with the long vowel and the hamza. It is a mufta'al form from al-ittika', except that he elongated the fatha so that an alif was produced from it, as they said: 'And you, from the calamities, where you are thrown... and from the blame of men, by one who is removed.'" That is: "bi-muntazah," so he elongated.]], and he would say: it is the seat and the food.
19171 -.... He said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us: whoever recites "mutkan," lightly, means food. And whoever recites ﴿muttaka'an﴾, means the reclining-couch.
* *
So this which we have mentioned from those whom we have mentioned concerning the interpretation of this word is the meaning of the word and the interpretation of "muttaka'," and that she prepared for the women a seat in which was a reclining-couch, food, drink, and citron. Then some of them explained "muttaka'" as food, in the sense of reporting what it was prepared for; and some as reporting citron, since the speech includes: ﴿and gave each one of them a knife﴾, because a knife is indeed prepared for citron and similar things that are cut with it. And some as the "bazmawurd" (a sweetmeat).
19172 - Harun ibn Hatim al-Muqri' narrated to me, saying: Hushaym ibn al-Zubarqan narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, regarding his saying: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾, he said: the bazmawurd.
* *
Abu 'Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna said: "Muttaka'" is the cushion one leans upon. And he said: some people claimed it is citron. He said: this is the most false falsehood on earth, but perhaps with the "muttaka'" there was citron that they ate.
* *
Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam related the saying of Abu 'Ubaydah, then said: The jurists are more knowledgeable about interpretation than he. Then he said: and perhaps it is some of what has been lost from Arabic speech, for al-Kisa'i used to say: much of Arabic speech has been lost, its people having died out.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The statement that the jurists are more knowledgeable about interpretation than Abu 'Ubaydah, as Abu 'Ubayd said, is beyond doubt; however, Abu 'Ubaydah did not stray far from the truth in this statement. Rather, the matter is as he said: that whoever says of "muttaka'" that it is citron has only explained what was prepared in the assembly in which the reclining-couch was, and for which the knives were given, because it is known that knives are not prepared for a reclining-couch except for tearing it!^[He means: unless they gave them knives so that they might tear the cushions and pillows, which are the muttaka'.] And they did not give them knives for that.
* *
And among what clarifies the correctness of that statement which we have mentioned from Ibn Abbas is that "muttaka'" is the seat.
Then it was narrated from Mujahid, from him, that:
19173 - Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Salt narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah narrated to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch and gave each one of them a knife﴾, he said: she gave them citron, and gave each one of them a knife.
* *
So Ibn Abbas, in this narration of Mujahid, clarified what the women were given, and turned away from explaining the meaning of "muttaka'," since its meaning was known.
* *
Those who said regarding the interpretation of "muttaka'" what we have mentioned:
19174 - Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: Fudayl ibn Iyad narrated to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾, he said: the citron (turunj).
19175 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Awf, who said: I was told from Ibn Abbas that he used to recite it: "mutkan" lightly, and he would say: it is the citron.
19176 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from Atiyyah: "And prepared for them a reclining-couch," he said: food.
19177 - Yaqub and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, both saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding his saying: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾, he said: food.
19178 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, the like of it.
19179 - Ibn Bashshar and Ibn WakI' narrated to us, both saying: Ghundar narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding his saying: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾, he said: food.
19180 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.
19181 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: whoever recites ﴿muttaka'an﴾ it is food, and whoever recites it "mutkan," lightening it, it is the citron.
19182 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿muttaka'﴾, he said: food.
19183 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
19184 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid =
19185 - And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
19186 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: whoever recites "mutkan," lightly, it is the citron.
19187 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, similarly.
19188 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, who said: I heard some of them say: the citron.
19189 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾, that is, food.
