19190 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of it.
19191 -.... He said: Yazid narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from Ikrimah, regarding his saying: ﴿muttaka'﴾, he said: food.
19192 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾, meaning the citron.
19193 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾, and the muttaka', the food.
19194 -.... He said: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾, he said: the food.
19195 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his saying: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾, he said: food.
19196 - It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding his saying: ﴿muttaka'an﴾, that it is everything that is cut with a knife.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: Allah, His remembrance being exalted, said, reporting about the wife of the chief and the women who talked of her affair in the city: ﴿And gave each one of them a knife﴾, meaning by this, Mighty is His praise: she gave each of the women who attended her a knife, to cut with it of the food what is cut with it. That is what she is reported to have given them, whether citron, or the bazmawurd, or other things that are cut with a knife, as:
19197 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿And gave each one of them a knife﴾, and citron to eat.
19198 - Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Salt narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah narrated to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And gave each one of them a knife﴾, he said: she gave them citron, and gave each one of them a knife.
19199 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And gave each one of them a knife﴾, to cut with it from their food.
19200 - Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his saying: ﴿And gave each one of them a knife﴾, and she gave them citron and honey, so they would cut the citron with the knife and eat with the honey.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: In this word is a clarification of the correctness of what we have said and chosen regarding His saying: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾. That is because Allah, His remembrance being exalted, reported the wife of the chief giving the women the knives, and omitted the purpose for which she gave them the knives, since it was known that knives are not handed to one invited to an assembly except to cut what is eaten when it is cut with them. So the listener's understanding of her giving her companions the knives sufficed, without mentioning for what purpose she gave them that. Likewise, the mention of her preparing for them the reclining-couch sufficed, without mentioning what the reclining-couch is prepared for of foods, drinks, fruits, and kinds of diversion that attend assemblies; due to the listeners' understanding of the intended meaning, and the indication of His saying: ﴿And prepared for them a reclining-couch﴾ upon it. As for the "muttaka'" itself, it is specifically what we have described and nothing else.
* *
And His saying: ﴿And she said, "Come out before them." So when they saw him, they magnified him﴾, means, Exalted is His remembrance: the wife of the chief said to Yusuf: ﴿Come out before them,﴾ so Yusuf came out before them = ﴿So when they saw him, they magnified him﴾, means, Mighty is His praise: when the women saw Yusuf they esteemed him greatly and exalted him.
* *
The people of interpretation have said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.
Those who said that:
19201 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿Akbarnahu﴾, they esteemed him.
19202 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
19203 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih. He said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
19204 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿So when they saw him, they magnified him﴾, that is: they esteemed him.
19205 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿And she said, "Come out before them,"﴾ to Yusuf = ﴿So when they saw him, they magnified him﴾, they exalted him.
19206 - Ismail ibn Sayf al-Ajli narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Abis narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Suddi say regarding his saying: ﴿So when they saw him, they magnified him﴾, he said: they esteemed him. [[The report 19206: "Ismail ibn Sayf al-Ajli," a shaykh who appeared in Tabari's narration No. 3843, and my brother noted there that he found no biography for him, and thought him to be "Ismail ibn Sayf, Abu Ishaq," but he definitively asserted this. And Allah knows best.
And "Ali ibn Abis al-Asadi," weak, passed as No. 11233.]]
19207 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his saying: ﴿Come out before them﴾, so he came out, and when they saw him they esteemed him greatly and were astonished.
19208 - Ismail ibn Sayf narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Ali al-Hashimi narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, regarding his saying: ﴿So when they saw him, they magnified him﴾, he said: they menstruated. [[The report 19208: "Ismail ibn Sayf al-Ajli," see No. 19206.
And "Abd al-Samad ibn Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Abbas al-Hashimi," who was an amir in Mecca, and al-Uqayli mentioned him among the weak narrators. He is biographied in Mizan al-I'tidal 2:132, and Lisan al-Mizan 4:21.]]
19209 - Ali ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his saying: ﴿So when they saw him, they magnified him﴾, he says: they esteemed him.
19210 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: This statement — I mean the statement narrated from Abd al-Samad, from his father, from his grandfather, regarding the meaning of "Akbarnahu," that it means they menstruated — if it did not intend that they menstruated out of their veneration of Yusuf and their magnifying of the beauty and comeliness Allah had apportioned to him, and what women experience of such things upon seeing him, then it is a statement with no meaning. Because the interpretation of that is: when they saw Yusuf they esteemed him greatly; the pronoun in "Akbarnahu" refers to Yusuf, and there is no doubt that it is absurd that they should menstruate over Yusuf. But the report, if it is authentic from Ibn Abbas as narrated, then it is likely that its meaning was that they menstruated because of the beauty and comeliness of Yusuf which they esteemed in themselves, and experienced what women experience of such things.
* *
Some narrators have claimed that some people recited, regarding "akbarna" in the sense of menstruated, a verse which I do not think has a basis, since it is not known among narrators, namely:
"We approach women in their states of purity, and not / we approach women when they have akbarna ikbaran." [[Lisan al-Arab (kabara).]]
And he claimed its meaning is: when they menstruate.
[[Abu Mansur al-Azhari narrated from Abu al-Haytham that he said: "I asked a man from Tayy, and said: O brother of Tayy, do you have a wife? He said: No, by Allah, I have not married, though I was promised to a cousin of mine. I said: What is her age? He said: She has akbarat — or kabarat. I said: What is akbarat? He said: She menstruated." Al-Azhari said: "And if this word is correct in the language with the meaning of menstruation, it has a fine explanation. That is because a woman, when she first menstruates, has left the limit of childhood for the limit of adulthood, so it is said to her: akbarat, that is, she menstruated, and entered the limit of adulthood which makes commands and prohibitions binding upon her."]]
* *
His saying: ﴿And cut their hands﴾: the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that.
Some of them said: its meaning is that they gashed their hands with the knife, while they thought they were cutting the citron.
Those who said that:
19211 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿And cut their hands﴾, gashing them, gash after gash, with the knife.
19212 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And cut their hands﴾, he said: gash after gash with the knives.
19213 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid =
19214 -.... He said: And Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And cut their hands﴾, he said: gash after gash with the knife.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 31 (part 2 of 2):

19215 – Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And they cut their hands" – He said: The women began to slash their hands, thinking that they were cutting citron.

19216 – Ismaʿil ibn Sayf related to us, saying: ʿAli ibn ʿAbis related to us, saying: I heard al-Suddi say: "There were knives in their hands along with the citron, so they cut their hands, and the blood flowed, and they said: 'We blame you for loving this man, and we have cut our hands and the blood has flowed!'"

19217 – Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: They began to slash their hands with the knife, and they did not think except that they were slashing the citron; their minds had gone from what they had seen!

19218 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah: "And they cut their hands," and they slashed their hands.

19219 – Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Salt related to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah related to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: They began to cut their hands while they thought they were cutting citron.

19220 – Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: "And they cut their hands," he said: They began to slash their hands, and they were not aware of it.

19221 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: [The women] said to Yusuf: "Go out to them," so he went out to them. [Allah says:] "When they saw him, they exalted him," and their minds were overwhelmed with amazement when they saw him, so they began to cut their hands with the knives they had, not understanding anything of what they were doing. [Allah says:] "And they said: 'Far be God [from imperfection]! This is not a human being.'"

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: they cut their hands until they severed them, and they were unaware.

Those who said this:

19222 – Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: They cut their hands until they threw them away.

19223 – al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq related to us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "And they cut their hands," he said: They cut their hands until they threw them away.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct view on this matter is to say: Allah informed about them that they cut their hands while they were unaware, in order to magnify Yusuf; it is permissible that this was a cutting that severed, and it is permissible that it was a cutting that merely gashed and scratched. There is no statement more correct on this than submitting to the apparent sense of the revelation.

* *

19224 – Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbdullah, who said: Yusuf and his mother were given a third of beauty.[[The narrations 19224–19227 are a mawquf hadith with a sound chain, mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:17 through various routes and with different wordings, and cited by al-Haythami with this wording in Majma al-Zawa'id 8:203, and with a different, longer wording. He said: "Narrated by al-Tabarani as mawquf, and its narrators are the narrators of the sahih," then mentioned this abridged version and said: "Narrated by al-Tabarani, and it is apparent that it is an error." The longer original wording is: "Yusuf and his mother were given two-thirds of the beauty of people."]]

19225 – Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbdullah, the same.

19226 – ... And with this chain, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbdullah, who said: A third of beauty was apportioned to Yusuf and his mother.

19227 – Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us; and Ibn Waki related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbdullah, who said: Yusuf and his mother were given a third of the beauty of character.

19228 – Ahmad ibn Thabit and ʿAbdullah ibn Muhammad al-Razi related to me, both saying: ʿAffan related to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, saying: Thabit informed us, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: Yusuf and his mother were given half of beauty.[[Narration 19228: "Ahmad ibn Thabit ibn ʿAttab al-Razi" (Farkhuwayh), a teacher of al-Tabari, is a liar; he was mentioned under no. 2055. "ʿAbdullah ibn Muhammad al-Razi," a teacher of al-Tabari, I do not know; in the History it reads: "ʿAbdullah ibn Muhammad and Ahmad ibn Thabit al-Shayyan..." and I do not know what this is. "ʿAffan" is ʿAffan ibn Muslim al-Saffar, a trustworthy narrator and a teacher of Ahmad and al-Bukhari, mentioned under no. 5392; the group recorded from him. "Hammad ibn Salamah" is trustworthy, mentioned many times. "Thabit" is Thabit ibn Aslam al-Bunani, a trustworthy Successor, mentioned many times. This report has a sound chain, and the lying of "Ahmad ibn Thabit" does not harm it, for the trustworthy narrators have transmitted it: Ahmad recorded it in his Musnad 3:286, from ʿAffan himself, with this wording. Al-Hakim recorded it in al-Mustadrak 2:570, through Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Saghani, Muhammad ibn Ghalib ibn Harb, and Ishaq ibn al-Hasan ibn Maymun, all from ʿAffan ibn Muslim, with a similar wording, and said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. Al-Tabari also recorded it in his History 1:173 through this same route.]]

19229 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Abu Muʿadh, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: Yusuf and his mother were given a third of the beauty of the people of the world, and the people were given two-thirds; or he said: Yusuf and his mother were given two-thirds, and the people were given a third.

19230 – Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us; and Ibn Waki related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Rabiʿah al-Jurashi, who said: Al-Hasan was divided into two halves: Yusuf and his mother Sarah were given half of the beauty, and the other half was shared among all the rest of creation.

19231 – Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Rabiʿah al-Jurashi, who said: Beauty was divided into two halves: a half was apportioned to Yusuf and his mother, and the half to the rest of mankind.

19232 – Ibn Waki and Ibn Humayd related to us, both saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Rabiʿah al-Jurashi, who said: Beauty was divided into two halves, and a half was given to Yusuf and Sarah, and a half was given to the rest of creation.[[Narrations 19230–19232: "Rabiʿah al-Jurashi" – there is disagreement about his father's name and about whether he was a Companion. It was said that his father's name was "Rabiʿah ibn ʿAmr" and "Rabiʿah ibn al-Ghaz"; see his biography in al-Isabah, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/1/256, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/472, and Ibn Saʿd in al-Tabaqat 7/2/150, who said: "In some reports he accompanied the Prophet (ﷺ) and narrated from him; he said he was trustworthy, and he was killed on the day of Marj Rahit in Dhu al-Hijjah in the year 64."]]

19233 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from ʿIsa ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan: Yusuf and his mother were given a third of the beauty of the world, and the people were given two-thirds.

* *

As for His words, "And they said: Far be God [from imperfection]!", the reciters differed in reading it.

The majority of the Kufan reciters read: "ḥāsha lillāh" with a fatḥah on the shin and the yā' omitted.

* *

Some Basran reciters read it with the yā' affirmed: "ḥāshā lillāh."

* *

There are also dialectal forms not read with, such as "ḥāshā Allāh," as the poet said: [[This is al-Jumayh, Munqidh ibn al-Tammah al-Asadi, and it is attributed to Sabrah ibn ʿAmr al-Asadi.]]

ḥāshā Abī Thawbān inna bihi ... ḍannan ʿani al-malḥāti wa al-shatmi

[[Al-Mufaddaliyyat 718; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu ʿUbaydah 1:310; al-Khizanah 2:150; al-ʿAyni (in the margin of al-Khizanah) 4:129; al-Lisan (ḥashā) in two places, with two versions. It is from a poem of his in which he satirized the Banu Rawahah ibn Qutay'ah ibn ʿAbs, and he excepts from them ʿAmr ibn ʿAbdullah, Abu Thawban, saying: "The Banu Rawahah look when the assembly (nadi) looks, with thick, blunt noses. Except Abi Thawban, indeed Abu Thawban is not a dull, heavy-witted mute, ʿAmr ibn ʿAbdullah; indeed he has restraint against quarrelling and abuse." In the manuscript it reads "Abi Thorwan," and in one place in al-Lisan "Abi Marwan," as if copied corruptly from the reading "Thorwan," if correct; al-Mufaddal related it as "ḥāshā Abā Thawbān" with an accusative. "Al-nadi" means the assembly, and he meant its people. "Al-anaf" is the plural of "anaf," and "al-khutham" is the plural of "akhtham," meaning one with a large, fleshy nose, neither slender nor refined, and it is a dispraise. "Al-bakmah" means the mute, and "al-fadam" means the slow-witted, heavy in understanding. "Al-malhah" is a noun of place from "lahawtu al-rajul wa lihyatahu," meaning when you press someone with blame; he apparently means quarrelling.]]

* *

It was reported from Ibn Masʿud that he used to read with this dialect: "ḥashā Allāh" and "ḥāshi Allāh," [[In the printed edition, "ḥashā Allāh" is omitted; I have restored it from it.]] with the shin and the alif vowel-less, combining two sukūns.

* *

As for the reading, it is only in one of the first two dialects. Whoever reads "ḥāsha lillāh" with a fatḥah on the shin and omission of the yā', he intended the dialect of the one who says "ḥāshā lillāh" with the yā' affirmed, but he omitted the yā' because it is frequent on the tongues of the Arabs, just as the Arabs omitted the alif in their saying "lā abā lighayrika" and "lā abā lishāniika," meaning "lā aban lighayrika" and "lā aban lishāniika."

* *

Some scholars of Arabic speech claimed that the Arabs' saying "ḥāshā lillāh" has two uses in speech:
First: exoneration (tanzih).
Second: exception (istithna'). In this place, in our view, it means exoneration of God, as if it were said: "Ma'adh Allah" (God forbid).

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: As for the view on the reading of it: it is said that the reciter has the choice in his recitation of whichever of the two readings he wishes, either the reading of the Kufans or the reading of the Basrans: "ḥāsha lillāh" and "ḥāshā lillāh," because they are two well-known readings and two recognized dialects with one meaning. What is other than this is dialects with which recitation is not permissible, because we do not know of any reciter who recited with them.

* *

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said on this.
Those who said this:

19234 – Ibn Waki related to us, saying: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And they said: Ḥāsha lillāh," he said: Maʿādh Allāh (God forbid).

19235 – Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, "Ḥāsha lillāh": Maʿādh Allāh.

19236 – al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And they said: Ḥāsha lillāh": Maʿādh Allāh.

19237 – al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Shababah related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his words: "Ḥāsha lillāh": Maʿādh Allāh.

19238 – ... He said: ʿAbd al-Wahhab related to us, from ʿAmr, from al-Hasan: "Ḥāsha lillāh": Maʿādh Allāh.

19239 – al-Harith related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz related to us, saying: Yahya related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

As for His words, "Ma hadha basharan" (this is not a human), he means: they said, "This is not a human," because they had not seen anyone among humans in the beauty of his form, so they said: If he were of humankind, he would be like some of the human forms we have seen, but he is from the angels, not from humankind, as:

19240 – Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: "And they said: Ḥāsha lillāh, this is not a human (basharan)": Humans are not like this!

* *

This reading is the one with which the majority of the readers of the metropolitan cities recited. And:

19241 – It was narrated to me from Yahya ibn Ziyad al-Farra', who said: Daʿamah ibn Rajaʾ al-Taymi related to me – and he was a ghazzaʾ [[In the printed edition it reads "ghurra," and the correct form is what I have given, as it is in Maʿani al-Qur'an.]] – from Abu al-Huwayrith al-Hanafi, that he read: "Mā hādhā bi-shirā" (this is not for sale), meaning: this is not one who is bought.[[The report 19241 is in al-Farra's Maʿani al-Qur'an in the explanation of the verse.]]

* *

= He intends by this that they denied that someone like him could be enslaved, bought and sold.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: I do not permit reciting with this reading, because the readers of the metropolitan cities have agreed against it. We have already explained that what they have agreed upon, opposing it is not permissible.

* *

As for the "naṣb" of "basharan," it is from the dialect of the people of the Hijaz: when they drop the "bāʾ" from the predicate, they put it in the accusative, saying: "Mā ʿAmrun qā'iman" (ʿAmr is not standing). As for the people of Najd, their dialect is to put it in the nominative, saying: "Mā ʿAmrun qā'imun"; and from it is the saying of one of them, where he says: [[I did not identify who said it.]]

la-shattāna mā anwī wa yanwī banū Abī ... jamīʿan, fa-mā hādhāni mustawiyāni
tamannaw lī al-mawta alladhī yashʿabu al-fatā ... wa kullu fatan wa al-mawtu yaltaqiyāni

[[The Farra related both in his Maʿani al-Qur'an in the explanation of the verse.]]

As for the Qur'an, it came with the accusative in all of that, because it was revealed in the dialect of the people of the Hijaz.

* *

As for His words, "In hadha illa malakun karimun" (This is only a noble angel), he means: they said, "This is only an angel from among the angels," as:

19242 – Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: "In hadha illa malakun karim," he said: They said: "An angel from among the angels."

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on Surah 12, verse 32:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿She said: "That is the one about whom you blamed me. I did seek to seduce him, but he remained chaste. And if he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned, and he will surely be among the humiliated."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, exalted is His remembrance, says: The wife of the ruler (al-'Aziz) said to the women who had cut their hands, "This is what has befallen you when you saw him and looked at him, the bewilderment of mind, the loss of understanding, and infatuation, that made you so distracted that you cut your hands. It is the one about whom you blamed me for my love of him and the passion of my heart for him. You said, 'The wife of the ruler is infatuated with her young man with love; we see her in manifest error!'" Then she admitted to them that she had indeed sought to seduce him (tafsir al-murawada, "seeking to seduce," see the earlier discussion, p. 62, note 1, and the references there), and that what they had said about her concerning his matter was true. She said: ﴿I did seek to seduce him, but he remained chaste﴾ (fa-stasamma, "he sought protection," from al-'isma, "protection," see the earlier discussion, vol. 15, p. 331, note 2, and the references there), meaning, from what I sought from him in that matter. As related:

19243. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding Her words: ﴿That is the one about whom you blamed me. I did seek to seduce him, but he remained chaste﴾: "She said: after he had loosened the trousers, he refused. I do not know what had come over him."

19244. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿but he remained chaste﴾: that is, "he refused" (fa-stasa, "he refused").

19245. 'Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿fa-stasamma﴾: "He says: he refrained."

* *

As for His words ﴿And if he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned, and he will surely be among the humiliated﴾: she says, "And if he does not comply with what I call him to, which is my need for him" = ﴿he will surely be imprisoned﴾ (yusjanan, "he will be imprisoned," see the earlier discussion, p. 52) = "and he will surely be among those who are humiliated through confinement and imprisonment, and I will surely disgrace him" (see the earlier discussion of al-saghar, "humiliation," vol. 14, p. 200, note 2, and the references there).

* *

The pause (waqf) on His words "li-yusjanan" is made with the nun, because it is doubled (mushaddada), as in the saying of God: ﴿la-yubatti'anna﴾ (Surah al-Nisa': 72).

* *

As for His words ﴿wa-liyakunan﴾, the pause on it is made with an alif, because it is the light nun (al-nun al-khafifa, "the light nun"), which resembles the nun of i'rab (grammatical inflection, nunation) in nouns, in the speaker's words: "I saw a man (rajulan) near you." When one pauses on "al-rajul," one says "ra'aytu rajulan," and the nun becomes an alif. Likewise is this in "wa-liyakunan." A similar example is His words ﴿la-nasfa'an bi-l-nasiyah, nasiyatin﴾ (Surah al-'Alaq: 15–16), where the pause is made with an alif for the reason I mentioned. From this is the verse of al-A'sha:

"Pray at the times of the evenings and the forenoon,
and do not worship Satan, but worship God (fa'bada)."

[The footnote on the verse: From his Diwan, p. 103, and elsewhere in abundance. He said it when he was turning toward Islam, and then he died in the state of jahiliyya (pre-Islamic ignorance), and the report is well known. The version in his Diwan reads:

"And leave aside the stone idol that is set up, do not sacrifice to it,
and do not worship the idols, but worship God (fa'bada)."

"Pray at the times of the evenings and the forenoon,
and do not praise Satan, but praise God (fa-hmada)."

The second is the better of the two versions.]

In fact the original is "fa'bidan," but when one pauses on it, the pause is made with an alif.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 33:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "My Lord, prison is more beloved to me than that to which they invite me. And unless You turn away from me their plot, I might incline toward them and be among the ignorant."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This report from God indicates that the wife of the minister (al-'Aziz) had returned to Yusuf in soliciting him to yield himself to her, and threatened him with prison and confinement if he did not do what she invited him to. So he chose prison over what she invited him to of that. For had she not returned to him and threatened him with that, it would have been impossible for him to say: ﴿My Lord, prison is more beloved to me than that to which they invite me﴾, when he was not being invited to anything and was not being threatened with imprisonment.

* *

"As-sijn" (the prison) is confinement itself, and it is the house of confinement.

* *

It was read with a kasra on the sin by the reciters of all the great cities (amsar). The Arabs place nouns of place derived from verbs in the positions of the verbal nouns (masadir) [[The "verbs" here means the verbal nouns (masadir); see the glossary of terms earlier in this work.]]. They say: "The sun rose (talaʿat ash-shams) a rising (matlaʿan), and set (gharabat) a setting (maghriban)," so they use these, which are nouns, as substitutes for the verbal nouns. Likewise "as-sijn": if the sin of "as-sijn" is vowelled with a fatha, it is a proper verbal noun (masdar sahih).

* *

It has been reported from some earlier scholars that they read it, "as-sajnu ahabbu ilayya," with a fatha on the sin. I do not permit that reading, because the consensus of the authoritative reciters opposes it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: Yusuf said, "O Lord, confinement in prison is more beloved to me than what they invite me to of Your disobedience and what they solicit me to of immorality," as:

19246 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿He said, "My Lord, prison is more beloved to me than that to which they invite me"﴾: from fornication.

19247 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, saying: Yusuf said, and he turned to his Lord and sought His aid over what had befallen him [[In the manuscript: "wa-ahaf ila rabbihi wa-istaghathahu" (and he feared toward his Lord and sought His help); the correct reading in the first is what is in the printed edition, and in the printed edition "istaʿanahu" (sought His aid); I have kept what is in the manuscript. "Ada ila rabbihi" means: he feared and was apprehensive, so he took refuge in Him, seeking protection in Him.]] ﴿My Lord, prison is more beloved to me than that to which they invite me﴾, meaning: prison is more beloved to me than that I should commit what you dislike.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And unless You turn away from me their plot, I might incline toward them﴾, he means: And if You, O Lord, do not repel from me their action which they do to me in their soliciting me to yield myself to them [[See the explanation of "as-sarf" earlier, p. 49, note 1, and the references there. And the explanation of "al-kayd" earlier, p. 60, note 1, and the references there.]] — "I might incline toward them" — he says: I would lean toward them and follow them in what they desire from me and are pleased with.

* *

From the saying of the speaker: "Fulan inclined (sabā) toward such-and-such," and from it is the poet's verse: [[It is Yazid ibn Dabbah ath-Thaqafi.]]

Toward Hind my heart inclined… and Hind, like her, makes one incline.

[[Al-Aghani 7:102 (Dar al-Kutub), and Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:311, from verses of his whose opening line this is, and after it: "Hind is a maiden, a gazelle of a noble stock… and among the ailments people have found none like love."]]

* *

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

19248 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿I might incline toward them﴾, he says: I would follow them.

19249 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And unless You turn away from me their plot﴾, meaning: what I fear from them = ﴿I might incline toward them﴾.

19250 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And unless You turn away from me their plot, I might incline toward them and be among the ignorant﴾, he said: If there is not from You the help and protection, there will not be from me nor with me.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and be among the ignorant﴾, he means: and I would be, by my inclination toward them, among those who ignored Your right and opposed Your command and prohibition [[See the explanation of "al-jahl" earlier in volume 13, p. 332, note 1, 2, and the references there.]], as:

19251 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿and be among the ignorant﴾, meaning: an ignorant one, when I commit Your disobedience.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 34:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So his Lord responded to him and turned away from him their plotting. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (12:34).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: If someone says: What is the meaning of His saying, ﴿So his Lord responded to him﴾, when there was no request previously made by Joseph to his Lord, and he did not supplicate for their plotting to be turned away from him, but rather he only informed his Lord that prison was more beloved to him than disobedience to Him?

It is said: In his informing of that there is a complaint from him to his Lord about what he encountered from them. And in his saying, ﴿And unless You turn away from me their plotting, I will incline toward them﴾ (12:33), there is the meaning of a supplication and request from him to his Lord to turn away their plotting. For this reason, God, mentioned and exalted, said: ﴿So his Lord responded to him﴾. This is like the saying of one speaker to another: "If you do not visit me, I will humiliate you," and the other replies: "Then I will visit you," because in his saying, "If you do not visit me, I will humiliate you," there is the meaning of a command to visit.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: God responded to Joseph's supplication, so He turned away from him what the wife of the al-Aziz and her female companions desired from him of disobedience to God, as follows:

19252. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿So his Lord responded to him and turned away from him their plotting. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: That is, He saved him from committing sin with them, although some of what he feared from them had befallen him.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing﴾: it refers to Joseph's supplication when he asked that the women's plotting be turned away from him, and to the supplication of every supplicant among His creation. ﴿The All-Knowing﴾: of his request and need, and what is good for him, and of the needs of all His creatures and what is good for them. [[See the explanation of "the All-Hearing" and "the All-Knowing" in the earlier lexical indexes under (سمع) and (علم).]]

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, that they should imprison him for a time﴾ (Q 12:35).

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then it occurred to al-'Aziz, the husband of the woman who had solicited Joseph against himself.

* *

It was also said: "it occurred to them," although it is singular, because he was not named and was meant by his individual identity. This is similar to His saying: ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them"﴾ (Q 3:173). It was also said that the one who spoke this was a single person.

* *

It was also said: the meaning of His saying ﴿Then it occurred to them﴾ refers to the opinion they had held about abandoning Joseph altogether, and they came to think it best to imprison him, ﴿after they had seen the signs﴾, that is, the evidence of his innocence from the accusation the wife of al-'Aziz had made against him.

* *

Those "signs" were the tearing of the shirt from behind, the scratching of the face, and the cutting of their hands, as related:

1 9253 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Nasr ibn 'Awf, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs﴾, he said: Among the signs was the tear in the shirt and the scratching of the face. [[Report 19253: I have not found among the narrators one called "Nasr ibn 'Awf." What I believe is that he is "Nadr ibn 'Arabi al-Bahili," who narrates from 'Ikrimah, and from whom Waki' narrates. He has passed several times, see nos. 1307 and 5864. The distortion of his name has also occurred frequently.]]

1 9254 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from [Nasr], from 'Ikrimah, similarly. [[Report 19254: "Nasr ibn 'Awf," see the earlier note; he is "Nadr ibn 'Arabi."]]

1 9255 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs﴾, he said: the tearing of the shirt from behind.

1 9256 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿after they had seen the signs﴾, he said: the tearing of the shirt from behind.

1 9257 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid =

1 9258 -.... He said: And Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

1 9259 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿after they had seen the signs﴾, he said: "The signs" were their cutting of their hands and the tearing of the shirt.

1 9260 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: the tearing of the shirt from behind.

1 9261 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, to imprison him﴾, after his innocence of what he was accused of, from the tearing of his shirt from behind = ﴿to imprison him for a time﴾.

1 9262 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿after they had seen the signs﴾, the shirt and the cutting of the hands.

* *

As for His saying ﴿to imprison him for a time﴾, it means: they would imprison him until the time when they would carry out their decision. [[See the explanation of "al-hin" in earlier passages: 1:540 / 12:359.]]

* *

Allah made that imprisonment for Joseph, as is mentioned, a punishment for his intention toward the woman, and an expiation for his sin.

1 9263 - It was related to me from Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah, from Isra'il, from Khusayf, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿to imprison him for a time﴾: Joseph, peace be upon him, stumbled three stumbles: when he intended her, and was imprisoned; when he said, ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾, and he remained in prison several years, and Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his lord; and when he said to them, ﴿Indeed, you are thieves﴾, and they said, ﴿If he steals, a brother of his has stolen before﴾.

* *

It is mentioned that the cause of his imprisonment was the complaint of the wife of al-'Aziz to her husband about him and herself, as follows:

1 9264 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, to imprison him for a time﴾, he said: The woman said to her husband: "This Hebrew slave has disgraced me among the people; he makes excuses to them and tells them that I solicited him. I cannot bear to excuse myself with my excuse. So either permit me to go out and excuse myself, or imprison him as you imprisoned me." That is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, to imprison him for a time﴾.

* *

The scholars of Arabic grammar have disagreed about the reason for the entry of this "lam" in ﴿la-yasjununnahu﴾.

Some of the Basran grammarians said: it entered here because it is a place where "ayyu" (which) occurs, and since the interrogative particle enters it, the nun was added, because the nun occurs in interrogation. You say: "It occurred to them which of them they would surely take," meaning: it became clear to them.

* *

Some of the grammarians rejected this, saying: this is an oath, and the words "hal taqumun" are not an oath, whereas "la-taqumanna" can only be an oath.

* *

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: "badā lahum" carries the meaning of "qāla" (said), and "qāla" can introduce all kinds of speech, both an oath and an interrogative. Therefore it is permissible to say: "It occurred to them, Zayd has stood," and "It occurred to them, he will surely stand."

* *

It was also said: "al-hin" in this place is understood to mean seven years.

Those who said this:

1 9265 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-Maharibi narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿to imprison him for a time﴾, he said: seven years.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 36:

The interpretation of His, exalted is He, words: ﴿And there entered the prison with him two young men. One of them said, "Indeed, I see myself pressing wine." And the other said, "Indeed, I see myself carrying bread on my head, of which the birds eat. Inform us of its interpretation. Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers."﴾ (36)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And there entered the prison with Joseph two young men." This indicates an omitted element of the speech, which is: ﴿Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, that they should imprison him for a time.﴾ So they imprisoned him and put him into the prison, and "there entered with him two young men." By His saying ﴿And there entered the prison with him two young men﴾ he dispensed with mention of their putting Joseph into the prison, since it is understood.

* *

The two young men, as was related, [[See the explanation of "fata" (young man) above: 8:188 / 16:62.]] were two servants of the greatest king of Egypt, one of them his cupbearer and the other his baker, as related:

19266 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Joseph was cast into the prison, and "there entered with him two young men": two servants who belonged to the great king al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid. One of them was in charge of his drink and the other in charge of some of his affairs, in a displeasure that he had shown toward them. The name of one of them was "Mujlith" and the other "Nabu," and it was "Nabu" who was over the drink.

19267 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And there entered the prison with him two young men﴾, he said: One of them was the king's baker over his food, and the other was his cupbearer over his drink.

* *

The reason for the king's imprisonment of the two young men, as was related, was as follows:

19268 - Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Amr related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: The king became angry with his baker, having been informed that he intended to poison him, so he imprisoned him and imprisoned his cupbearer, thinking that he had colluded with him in that. So he imprisoned them both. This is the meaning of God's words: ﴿And there entered the prison with him two young men.﴾

* *

As for His words: ﴿One of them said, "Indeed, I see myself pressing wine."﴾ It is mentioned that when Joseph, upon him be blessings of God, was put into the prison, he said to those imprisoned there, who asked him about his work: "I interpret dreams." One of the two young men who had been put into prison with him then said to his companion: "Come, let us test him." As related:

19269 - Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: When Joseph entered the prison he said: "I interpret dreams." One of the two young men said to his companion: "Come, let us test this Hebrew slave," and so they both pretended to have seen something before him, and asked him, without having seen anything. The baker said: "Indeed, I see myself carrying bread on my head, of which the birds eat," and the other said: "Indeed, I see myself pressing wine."

19270 - Ibn WakI' and Ibn Humayd related to us, both saying: Jarir related to us, from Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa', from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, who said: The two companions of Joseph had seen nothing; they had merely dreamt false dreams in order to test his knowledge.

* *

Others said: The two young men asked him about a dream which they had truly seen, in sincerity and reality, and in belief in him for his knowledge of its interpretation.

Those who said this:

19271 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When the two young men saw Joseph, they said: "By God, young man, we have loved you since we saw you."

19272 - ... He said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: that Joseph said to them when they said that to him: "I beseech you by God, do not love me, for by God, no one has ever loved me without that love bringing trouble upon me. My aunt loved me and that love brought trouble upon me; then my father loved me and his love brought trouble upon me; then the wife of this companion of mine loved me and her love for me brought trouble upon me. So do not love me, may God bless you both!" He said: But they refused except to love him and be close to him wherever he was, and they were pleased by what they saw of his understanding and intellect. When they had been put into the prison they had seen a dream: "Mujlith" saw that he was carrying bread on his head, of which the birds ate, and "Nabu" saw that he was pressing wine. So they asked him about them, saying to him: ﴿Inform us of its interpretation. Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers﴾, if you do so.

* *

By His words: ﴿pressing wine﴾, is meant: "Indeed, I see in my sleep that I am pressing grapes." Likewise is it in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, as is reported from him.

19273 - Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Abu Salamah al-Sa'igh, from Ibrahim ibn Bashir al-Ansari, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, who said, in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed, I see myself pressing grapes [[Report 19273: "Abu Salamah al-Sa'igh" is "Rashid, Abu Salamah al-Sa'igh al-Fazari," who related from al-Sha'bi, Zayd al-Ahmasi, and others. He is biographed in al-Kabir 2/1/272 and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/485, and neither mentions any criticism of him.

"Ibrahim ibn Bashir al-Ansari" related from Ibn al-Hanafiyyah; he is biographed in al-Kabir 1/1/274 and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/89.

This report is mentioned by al-Bukhari in the biography of "Ibrahim ibn Bashir."]]

* *

It is mentioned that this is from the dialect of the people of Oman, who call grapes "khamr" (wine).

Those who said this:

19274 - It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, I see myself pressing wine﴾: he means pressing grapes, and it is in the dialect of the people of Oman, who call grapes "khamr."

19275 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us; and Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Salamah ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak: ﴿Indeed, I see myself pressing wine﴾, he said: grapes. The land of such-and-such call grapes "khamr."

19276 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿Indeed, I see myself pressing wine﴾, he said: grapes.

19277 - It was related to me from al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk, from Abu Hamzah, from Ikrimah, who said: He came to him and said: "I saw in what the sleeper sees that I planted a shoot of grapevine [[al-habalah (with fatha on the ha' and ba'): the branch of a grapevine, which is planted and grows.]], and it grew, and clusters came out on it, and I pressed them and gave the king to drink." He said: "You will remain in the prison three days, then you will go out and give him wine to drink."

* *

As for His words: (And the other said, "Indeed, I see myself carrying bread on my head, of which the birds eat. Inform us of its interpretation."), He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And the other of the two young men said: "Indeed, I see in my dream that I am carrying bread on my head," meaning: carrying it upon my head. "Fawq" has been used in place of "ʿala" [[See the explanation of "fawq" above: 13:430.]], and ﴿of which the birds eat﴾, meaning: from the bread.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Inform us of its interpretation﴾, meaning: tell us what the matter of what we have told you we saw in our dream will come to and return to, as:

19278 - al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Qasim related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Inform us of its interpretation﴾, he said: "its" [meaning the thing itself]. al-Harith said: Abu Ubayd said: Mujahid means that "the interpretation of a thing" is the thing itself. He said: From this comes "the interpretation of a dream," which is merely the thing to which it returns.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers﴾, the people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of the "ihsan" (goodness) with which the young men described Joseph. [[See the explanation of "ihsan" above in the lexicon entry (h-s-n).]]

Some of them said: It is that he would visit their sick, console their grieving, and when any of them was in need he would gather for him.

Those who said this:

19279 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Mansur related to us, saying: Khalaf ibn Khalifah related to us, from Salamah ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, who said: I was sitting with him in Balkh, and he was asked about His words: ﴿Inform us of its interpretation. Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers﴾. He was asked: What was Joseph's goodness? He said: When a person fell ill, he would stand by him; when he was in need, he would gather for him; and when he was constrained, he would widen for him.

19280 - Ishaq related to us, from Abu Isra'il, who said: Khalaf ibn Khalifah related to us, from Salamah ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak, who said: A man asked al-Dahhak about His words: ﴿Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers﴾, what was his goodness? He said: When a person fell ill in the prison, he would stand by him; when he was in need, he would gather for him; and when the place was constrained for him, he would widen it for him.

19281 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers﴾, he said: It has reached us that his goodness was that he would treat their sick, console their grieving, and strive for his Lord. He also said: When Joseph reached the prison he found in it people whose hope had been cut off and whose trials had grown severe, and their sorrow had lengthened, so he began saying: "Rejoice and be patient, you will be rewarded; indeed, there is a recompense for this, indeed there is a reward for this." They said: "Young man, may God bless you, how beautiful is your face and how good is your character. We have been blessed by your neighborhood; we would not wish, since we were imprisoned, to be anywhere else, because of what you tell us of reward, expiation and purity. Who are you, young man?" He said: "I am Joseph, son of the chosen of God, Jacob, son of the sacrificed one of God, Isaac, son of Abraham the friend of God." He was beloved. The keeper of the prison said to him: "Young man, by God, if I could, I would release you, but I will treat your neighborhood well and make your captivity good; so stay in whichever of the prison's rooms you wish."

19282 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Khalaf al-Ash'ari, from Salamah ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak concerning: ﴿Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers﴾, he said: He would make room for a man in his assembly, and would look after the sick.

* *

Others said: Its meaning is: ﴿Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers﴾, if you inform us of the interpretation of this dream of ours.

Those who said this:

19283 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: They asked him about their dream, saying to him: ﴿Inform us of its interpretation. Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers﴾, if you do so.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions in our view is the view we have reported from al-Dahhak and Qatadah.

* *

If someone says: What is the meaning of the speech if the matter is as you have said? You know that their request of Joseph that he inform them of the interpretation of their dream is not a report of his description as one who visits the sick, stands by them, and does good to the needy in something; rather, one says to a man: "Inform us of the interpretation of this, for you are knowledgeable." This is one of the contexts where description by knowledge is fitting, not by anything else?

It is said: The sense of that is that they said to him: "Inform us of the interpretation of our dream, being good to us in informing us of it, as we see you do good in all your deeds": ﴿Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 37:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said: No food will come to you as provision but I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is of what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion (millah) of a people who do not believe in Allah and who are, in the Hereafter, disbelievers.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Almighty God says: ﴿He said﴾ — Joseph, to the two young men who had asked him to interpret their dreams: ﴿No food will come to you﴾ — O two young men — in your sleep — ﴿as provision but I will inform you of its interpretation﴾ — while you are awake — ﴿before it comes to you.﴾

* *

What we have said on this matter is also what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

19284 — Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: 'Amr related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: Joseph said to them: ﴿No food will come to you as provision﴾ — in sleep — ﴿but I will inform you of its interpretation﴾ — in waking.

19285 — Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Joseph said to them: ﴿No food will come to you as provision﴾ — he means: in your sleep — ﴿but I will inform you of its interpretation.﴾

* *

By His words ﴿its interpretation﴾ is meant: what it will lead to and become, of the food which they saw in their dreams, that it had come to them.

* *

As for His words: ﴿That is of what my Lord has taught me﴾ — meaning: this which I mention, that I know it of the interpretation of dreams, is of what my Lord taught me, so I learned it — ﴿Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah﴾ — the statement came as a nominal clause (mubtada'), meaning: I have left the religion of a people; and the sense is: I did not incline to it. He began with this because the beginning contains the indication of its meaning.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah﴾ — he says: I have disassociated myself from the religion of those who do not affirm Allah and acknowledge His oneness (wahdaniyyah) [[See the explanation of "millah" above, 12:561, note 4, and the references there.]] — ﴿and who are, in the Hereafter, disbelievers﴾ — he says: and they, together with their abandonment of faith in the oneness of Allah, do not acknowledge the return (ma'ad) and resurrection, nor reward nor punishment.

* *

The word "they" (hum) was repeated twice, so it is said: ﴿and who are, in the Hereafter, they are disbelievers,﴾ because the phrase ﴿in the Hereafter﴾ intervened between them; thus the first "hum" became like a dropped element, and reliance fell on the second, as it is said: ﴿and they, in the Hereafter, they are certain﴾ [Surah al-Naml 27:3 / Surah Luqman 31:4], and as it is said: ﴿Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?﴾ [Surah al-Mu'minun 23:35].

* *

If one says: What is the import and meaning of this report from Joseph? And where is his answer to the two young men regarding what they asked him of the interpretation of their dreams, in this speech?

It is said to him: Joseph disliked to answer them concerning the interpretation of their dreams, because he knew the harm that would befall one of them. So he turned away from mentioning it and took up another matter, so that they would turn away from asking him for the answer to what they had asked.

* *

The people of knowledge (ahl al-'ilm) said something similar to this.

Mention of those who said that:

19286 — al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, I see myself pressing wine, and the other said: Indeed, I see myself carrying bread upon my head, of which the birds eat. Inform us of its interpretation﴾. He said: He disliked to interpret for them, and informed them of something they had not asked him about, to show them that he had knowledge. When the king wished to kill a person, he would prepare for him a specific food and send it to him. So Joseph said: ﴿No food will come to you as provision﴾, up to His words: ﴿you are grateful﴾. They did not accept (his offer), so he turned them away and disliked to interpret for them. They did not accept until he interpreted for them, so he turned them away and said: ﴿O two companions of the prison, are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾, up to His words: ﴿they know﴾. They did not accept until he interpreted for them, and he said: ﴿O two companions of the prison, as for one of you, he will give his lord wine to drink; and as for the other, he will be crucified and the birds will eat from his head.﴾ They said: We saw nothing; we were only playing! He said: ﴿The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire.﴾

* *

Abu Ja'far said: According to this interpretation which Ibn Jurayj gave, His words ﴿No food will come to you as provision﴾ refer to waking, not sleep. On this view, he informed them that he had knowledge of what the matter of the food coming to them from the king and from others would lead to, for he knew the kind which, if it came to them, would be a sign of the killing of whichever of them received it, and the kind which, if it came, would be a sign of something else; so he informed them that he had knowledge of this.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 38:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And I have followed the religion of my forefathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks﴾ [12:38]

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words ﴿And I have followed the religion of my forefathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob﴾, he means: I have followed their religion, not the religion of the people of polytheism. ﴿It was not for us to associate anything with Allah﴾, he says: It was not permissible for us to make a partner with Allah in His worship and obedience, rather what is incumbent upon us is to single Him out in divinity and worship. ﴿That is from the bounty of Allah upon us﴾, he says: my following the religion of my forefathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in Islam, and my abandoning the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah and who are disbelievers in the Hereafter, is from the bounty of Allah which He has bestowed upon us, so He favoured us when He honoured us with it. ﴿And upon mankind﴾, he says: and that is also from the bounty of Allah upon mankind, in that He sent to them callers to His monotheism and obedience. ﴿But most of mankind do not give thanks﴾, he says: but whoever disbelieves in Allah does not give thanks for that bounty of His upon him, because he does not know the one who bestowed it upon him, nor does he recognise the one who favoured him with it.

* *

And the people of interpretation have said similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

19287 - Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿That is from the bounty of Allah upon us﴾, that He made us prophets. ﴿And upon mankind﴾, he says: that He sent messengers to them.

19288 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿That is from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind﴾, it was mentioned to us that Abu al-Darda' used to say: "How many a grateful one for a blessing, not bestowed upon him by a benefactor who knows; and how many a bearer of knowledge is not a jurist."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 39:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O two companions of the prison, are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ (12:39)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: It is mentioned that Yusuf, peace be upon him, said this statement to the two young men who had entered the prison with him, because one of them was a polytheist. So he called him with this statement to Islam and to abandoning the worship of gods and idols. He said: ﴿O two companions of the prison﴾, meaning: O you who are in the prison. He called them "his companions" because they were in it, just as Allah, exalted is He, said to the people of Paradise: ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise; therein they will abide forever﴾, and likewise He said regarding the people of the Fire, and called them "its companions" because they were in it. [See the explanation of "al-sahib" (companion) in the previous lexical indexes under the root (ṣ-ḥ-b).]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾, He means: Is the worship of many scattered lords and gods that neither benefit nor harm better, or the worship of the one worshipped, who has no equal in His power and dominion, who has subdued every thing, humbling and subjecting it, so that it obeys Him willingly or unwillingly? [See the explanation of "al-Qahhar" (the Subduer) above at 13:42, note 1, and the references there.]

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

19289 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿O two companions of the prison, are separate lords better...﴾ up to His words: ﴿they do not know﴾. When the Prophet of Allah Yusuf knew that one of them would be killed, he called them to their share of good from their Lord and to their portion of their Hereafter.

19290 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿O two companions of the prison﴾ — Yusuf is saying it.

19291 - ... He said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

19292 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then he called them to Allah and to Islam, saying: ﴿O two companions of the prison, are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ That is: Is it better that you worship one God, or scattered gods that avail you nothing?

**The explanation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿What you worship besides Him are only names you and your fathers have named; God has sent down no authority for them. Judgment belongs only to God. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know﴾ (40).**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words ﴿What you worship besides Him﴾, He means: what you worship besides God.

He said ﴿What you worship﴾ after beginning the address to two people when He said ﴿O my two fellow prisoners﴾, because He intended by the address the one who was persisting in polytheism with God among the people of Egypt. So He said to the one addressed in this way: What you worship, along with whoever is upon what you are upon of worshipping idols. ﴿Only names you and your fathers have named﴾: this refers to their naming their idols "gods" and "lords," as an act of polytheism on their part and as a likening of these idols, through the names they gave them, to God, exalted is He above having any equal or like. ﴿God has sent down no authority for them﴾: He says, they named them with names for which God had not given them permission to name them, nor did He establish for them that those names were their names, neither as an indication nor as proof. Rather, it was their fabrication and invention. [[See the explanation of "authority" (al-sultan) above, 15:465, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿Judgment belongs only to God. He has commanded that you worship none but Him﴾: He says, He is the One who commanded that neither you nor all of His creation worship anything except God, to whom belongs divinity and worship exclusively, apart from everything else. As related:

19293. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, regarding His words ﴿Judgment belongs only to God. He has commanded that you worship none but Him﴾, he said: He founded the religion upon sincere devotion to God alone, with no partner.

* *

As for His words ﴿That is the upright religion﴾: He says, this which I have called you to, namely disavowal of worshipping anything other than God among the idols, and that you devote worship purely to God, the One, the Subduer, is the straight religion that has no crookedness in it, and the truth about which there is no doubt. [[See the explanation of "upright" (al-qayyim) above, 14:237.]] ﴿But most people do not know﴾: He says, but the people of polytheism with God are ignorant of this and do not know its reality.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 41:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O my two fellow prisoners! As for one of you, he will give his lord (to) drink wine; but as for the other, he will be crucified and birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decided about which you both inquire.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His exalted praise says, reporting the speech of Yusuf to the two who had entered the prison with him: ﴿O my two fellow prisoners! As for one of you, he will give his lord to drink wine﴾. He is the one who saw that he was pressing wine, and so he gives his lord to drink (i.e., his master, and he is their king) [[See the explanation of "lord" (al-rabb) above, p. 32, footnote 2, and the references there.]] "wine," meaning he will be the cupbearer of his master.

* *

19294 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿So he gives his lord to drink wine﴾, he said: "His master."

* *

As for the other, who saw that on his head was bread from which birds were eating, "he will be crucified and birds will eat from his head." It is reported that when he interpreted for them what they had told him they had seen in their dreams, they said: "We saw nothing!" So he said to them: ﴿The matter has been decided about which you both inquire.﴾ That is, the matter about which you both sought a ruling has been completed [[See the explanation of "qada" (decided) above, vol. 15, p. 151, footnote 1, and the references there.]], and God's judgment against you, according to what I told you, has become binding. [[See the explanation of "istifta'" (seeking a ruling) above, vol. 9, pp. 253, 430.]]

* *

Scholars have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

19295 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amarah, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, who said: The two who entered the prison with Yusuf said: "We saw nothing!" So he said: ﴿The matter has been decided about which you both inquire.﴾

19296 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Amarah ibn al-Qa'qa', from Ibrahim, from Abdullah: ﴿The matter has been decided about which you both inquire.﴾ He said: When they said what they said, he informed them, and they said: "We saw nothing!" So he said: ﴿The matter has been decided about which you both inquire.﴾

19297 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Amarah, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abdullah, concerning the two youths who came to Yusuf and the dream: they had only dreamed together in order to test him, and when he interpreted their dreams they said: "We were only playing!" He said: ﴿The matter has been decided about which you both inquire.﴾

19298 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Amarah, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, who said: The two companions of Yusuf saw nothing; they had only dreamed together in order to test his knowledge. One of them said: "Indeed I see myself pressing grapes," and the other said: "Indeed I see myself carrying bread upon my head from which birds eat?" ﴿Inform us of its interpretation; indeed we see you as one of the good-doers!﴾ He said: ﴿O my two fellow prisoners! As for one of you, he will give his lord to drink wine; but as for the other, he will be crucified and birds will eat from his head.﴾ When he interpreted, they said: "We saw nothing!" He said: ﴿The matter has been decided about which you both inquire.﴾ In accordance with what Yusuf interpreted.

19299 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: He said to the one: "As for you, you will be crucified and birds will eat from your head." And he said to the other: "As for you, you will return to your work, and your companion will be pleased with you." ﴿The matter has been decided about which you both inquire.﴾ Or as he said.

19300 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said ........... about which you both inquire. [[This report has a large part missing, so I placed dots in place of the omission.]]

19301 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: ﴿The matter has been decided about which you both inquire.﴾ At their saying: "We did not see a dream; we were only playing!" He said: "The dream has indeed come to pass as I interpreted it."

19302 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿about which you both inquire﴾, and he mentioned something similar.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And he said to the one of the two whom he thought would be saved, "Mention me to your lord." But Satan caused him to forget to mention him to his lord, so he remained in prison for several years﴾ (12:42)

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning is that He, exalted is His remembrance, said: Joseph said to the one of his two companions, the two who had asked him to interpret their dreams, whom he knew would be saved. [[See the explanation of "al-zann" (thought, supposition) in the earlier glossary of language entries under (ẓ-n-n).]] ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾ means: mention me to your master, [[See the explanation of "al-rabb" (lord) earlier, p. 107, note 1, and the references there.]] and inform him of my wrong, and that I am imprisoned without crime, as:

19303: Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: he said, meaning Joseph: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾, i.e., mention to the great king my wrong and my imprisonment for nothing. He said: I will do so.

19304: Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾, he said: to the one of the two prisoners who was saved, Joseph said: Mention me to the king.

19305: al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

19306: Ibn Wakf' related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Asbat: ﴿And he said to the one of the two whom he thought would be saved, "Mention me to your lord"﴾, he said: to the king of the land.

19307: Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾, he meant by that the king.

19308: al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And he said to the one of the two whom he thought would be saved, "Mention me to your lord"﴾, the one who was saved from the two prisoners; Joseph said: Mention me to the king.

19309: al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab informed us, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, that when he reached the prison door, a companion of his said to him: What is your need? Advise me of your need! He said: My need is that you mention me to your lord (other than the Lord), said Joseph. [[In the printed edition: "that you mention me to your lord, intending the Lord who owned Joseph," which differs from the manuscript. I have kept what is in the manuscript, but the manuscript here reads "to a lord" without the kaf; the correct reading is what I have given.]]

* *

Qatadah used to direct the meaning of "al-zann" (thought) in this place toward "al-zann," which is the opposite of certainty.

19310: Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And he said to the one of the two whom he thought would be saved, "Mention me to your lord"﴾, and the interpretation of dreams is only by supposition, so God establishes what He wills and nullifies what He wills.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What Qatadah said, that the interpretation of dreams is supposition, holds true for those other than the prophets. As for the prophets, it is not permissible for them to report a matter as occurring when it does not occur, or as not occurring when it does, while bearing witness to the reality of what they report as occurring or not occurring. For if that were permissible in their reports, one could not be secure about such things in all their reports. And if one cannot be secure in their reports, their proof against those to whom they were sent collapses. Given that, it is not permissible for them to report anything except what is true and correct. It is known, since the matter is as described, that Joseph did not state definitively what he reported to the two youths who asked him to interpret, saying to one of them: ﴿As for one of you, he will give his lord wine to drink; and as for the other, he will be crucified, and birds will eat from his head﴾, then confirm that with his words: ﴿The matter has been decided about which you both inquire﴾, in response to their saying: ﴿We have seen no dream﴾, unless he was certain that what he reported would occur and happen, that it would undoubtedly occur without doubt. And because of his certainty that this would happen, he said to the one of them who would be saved: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾. It is therefore clear that the view Qatadah stated about the meaning of His words ﴿And he said to the one of the two whom he thought would be saved﴾ is false.

* *

As for His words: ﴿But Satan caused him to forget to mention him to his lord﴾, this is a report from God, whose praise is exalted, about a lapse that befell Joseph at the hands of Satan. He forgot, because of it, the mention of his lord, through which, had he sought help from Him, He would have quickly delivered him from his situation. But he slipped because of it, and so his imprisonment was prolonged on its account, and his punishment was intensified for it, as:

19311: al-Harith related to me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, he said: Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Dab'i related to us, from Bistam ibn Muslim, from Malik ibn Dinar, who said: When Joseph said to the cupbearer: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾, it was said: O Joseph, have you taken someone other than Me as a guardian? I will surely prolong your imprisonment! So Joseph wept and said: O Lord, the multitude of trials has made my heart forget; I spoke a word, so woe to my brothers.

19312: al-Hasan related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: Had he not said the word he said, he would not have remained in prison as long as he did.

19313: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, and Ibn Wakf' said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, he said: Yunus related to us, from al-Hasan, who said: The Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "May God have mercy on Joseph; had it not been for his word, he would not have remained in prison as long as he did," meaning His words: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾. He said: Then al-Hasan would weep and say: When a matter befalls us, we turn to people.

19314: Ya'qub related to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿And he said to the one of the two whom he thought would be saved, "Mention me to your lord"﴾, he said: It was related to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: Had it not been for Joseph's word, he would not have remained in prison as long as he did.
