19315: Ibn Wakf' related to us, he said: 'Amr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: If Joseph had not said the word he said, he would not have remained in prison as long as he did, meaning: when he sought deliverance from other than God. [[The report 19315: "Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Khuzi al-Qurashi" is abandoned in narration, has munkar reports, is not trustworthy, and was accused of lying. He has been mentioned repeatedly, most recently at no. 17313.

This report has a very weak chain. al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7:39 at length, saying: "al-Tabarani related it, and in its chain is Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Qurashi al-Makki, who is abandoned." al-Tabari also related it in his Tarikh 1:177.

As for the other reports before and after it, they are mursal (reports whose chain omits a companion of the Prophet), and none of them constitutes proof.]]

19316: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: It reached me that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: Had Joseph not sought help from his lord, he would not have remained in prison as long as he did.

19317: Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was related to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) used to say: Had Joseph not sought intercession from his lord, he would not have remained in prison as long as he did; rather, he was only punished for seeking intercession from his lord.

19318: Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: He said to him: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾, and he did not mention him until the king saw the dream. That was because Satan caused Joseph to forget the mention of his lord, and he commanded him to mention the king and seek deliverance from him, so he remained in prison for several years, on account of his words: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾.

19319: al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: So he remained in prison for several years, as a punishment for his words: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾.

19320: ... he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: 'Abdullah related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, like the report of Muhammad ibn 'Amr, exactly.

19321: al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, like the report of al-Muthanna from Abu Hudhayfah.

* *

Muhammad ibn Ishaq used to say: Satan only caused the cupbearer to forget the matter of Joseph before their king.

19322: Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When he went out (meaning the one who supposed he would be saved from the two), he was restored to his position, and his companion was pleased with him, but Satan caused him to forget the mention of that to the king whom Joseph had told him to mention it to. So Joseph remained in prison for several years after that. He means, exalted is His praise: Joseph remained in prison, because of his saying to the one of the two prisoners who would be saved, "Mention me to your master," for several years, as a punishment from God for that.

* *

The people of interpretation differed about the quantity of the "bid'" (several, a few) for which Joseph remained in prison.

Some of them said: It is seven years.

Those who said so:

19323: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Muhammad Abu 'Uthmah related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: Joseph remained in prison seven years. [[Report 19323: "Muhammad, Abu 'Uthmah" is Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn 'Uthmah, mentioned repeatedly, most recently at no. 10142. See also nos. 5314, 5483. Muhammad ibn Bashshar's transmission from him, and his transmission from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah.]]

19324: Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿So he remained in prison for several years﴾, he said: seven years.

19325: al-Hasan related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: 'Imran Abu al-Hudhayl al-San'ani informed us, who said: I heard Wahb say: Job was afflicted with trial for seven years, Joseph was left in prison for seven years, and Nebuchadnezzar tortured him, so he was transformed among the beasts for seven years. [[Report 19325: "'Imran Abu al-Hudhayl al-San'ani" is 'Imran ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Murthid. "Abu al-Hudhayl" is trustworthy, heard Wahb ibn Munabbih, Ziyad ibn Fayruz, and al-Qasim ibn Tankhusrah. He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/301.

This report was related by Abu Ja'far in his Tarikh 1:177. In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads: "yajul fi al-sibaa" (he roams among the beasts), but the manuscript is unpointed. The correct reading is from the Tarikh, and by his words "hawwal fi al-sibaa" (he was transformed) he means: he was turned into one of the beasts.]]

19326: al-Muthanna related to me, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: They claim that it (meaning "bid'") is seven years, as Joseph remained.

* *

Others said: "Bid'" is what lies between three and nine.

Those who said so:

19327: Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Sulayman related to us, he said: Abu Hilal related to us, who said: I heard Qatadah say: "Bid'" is what lies between three and nine.

19328: Wakf' related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Isra'il, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿several years﴾, he said: what lies between three and nine.

* *

Others said: Rather, it is less than ten.

Those who said so:

19329: al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿several years﴾, less than ten.

* *

al-Farra' claimed that "bid'" is mentioned only with "ashr" (ten), and with "al-'ishrin" (twenty) up to ninety; and it is a "nayyif" (a little more than) between three and nine. [[Report 19327: "Ibn Bashshar" is Muhammad ibn Bashshar, mentioned repeatedly. "Sulayman" is Sulayman ibn Dawud ibn al-Jarud, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, the well-known imam, mentioned repeatedly.

"Abu Hilal" is Muhammad ibn Sulaym al-Rasibi, mentioned repeatedly, most recently at no. 15351.

In the printed edition and manuscript it reads "I heard Abu Qatadah," which is an error, since Abu Hilal al-Rasibi transmits from Qatadah.]] He said: That is how I saw the Arabs do it. They do not say "bid' wa-mi'ah" [[This phrasing is unclear. Ibn Bari is quoted in Lisan al-'Arab as saying: "He related from al-Farra', regarding His words 'bid' sinin' (several years), that 'bid'' is mentioned only with ten and twenty up to ninety, and it is not said after that," meaning one says "mi'ah wa-nayyif" (a hundred and a bit). Lisan al-'Arab, (b-d-' / bada').]] nor "bid' wa-alf" (several thousand). And when the numeral is for males, one says "bid'."

* *

Abu Ja'far said:

The correct view regarding "bid'" is from three up to nine, up to ten, and it is not less than three. Likewise, what exceeds a decade up to a hundred; and what exceeds a hundred, there is no "bid'" in it.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 43:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And the king said, "Indeed, I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears [of grain] and others dry. O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you can interpret visions."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, "And the king of Egypt said: Indeed, I see in a dream seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean cows." [[The word "ʿijāf" (lean) is not explained in this verse; he will explain it later in the following verses.]] He said, "Indeed, I see," and did not mention that he saw it in his sleep or otherwise, because the Arabs know from their usage that when one of them says, "I see that I do such and such," it is a report of his seeing that in his sleep, even if he does not mention sleep. Allah, may His praise be exalted, related the report in the manner that the Arabs customarily use among themselves.

* *

= ﴿And seven green ears⦆, meaning: and I see seven green ears of grain in my dream. = ﴿And others﴾, meaning: and seven others of grain ears = ﴿dry. O eminent ones﴾, [[See the explanation of "sunbulah" (ear of grain) above, 5:512–515.]] meaning: O nobles among my men and companions [[See the explanation of "al-mala'" (the eminent ones) above, 15:466, footnote 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿explain to me my vision﴾, interpret it, ﴿if you are for the vision﴾ interpreters, [[ "ʿabarah" is the plural of "ʿābir," who is the one who interprets the vision and explains it.]]

* *

Those who engaged in interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

19330- Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: Indeed Allah showed the king a vision in his dream that frightened him: he saw seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears and others dry. So he gathered the sorcerers, the soothsayers, the ḥuzāt, and the qāfah, [[The "ḥazaʾah" is the plural of "ḥāz," who is the soothsayer who guesses and estimates things by his conjecture; one who looks into the stars and their judgments by conjecture and estimation, and who sometimes hits the mark, is called "ḥazzāʾ." In Tarikh al-Tabari the form "al-ḥāzah wa al-qāfah" appears, as if the plural was formed with its last letter contrary to analogy. Its plural is also "ḥawāzī."

"Qāfah" is the plural of "qāʾif," who tracks traces and recognizes them, and knows a man's resemblance to his brother and his father.]] and he related it to them, and they said: ﴿Confused dreams, and we are not versed in the interpretation of dreams.﴾ [[The report 19330 was narrated by Abu Ja'far in his Tarikh 1:177, at length.]]

19331 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then the king al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid saw his vision that he saw, and it frightened him, and he knew that it was a true vision, but did not know its interpretation. So he said to the eminent ones around him from the people of his kingdom: ﴿Indeed, I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones﴾ up to His saying: ﴿versed﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 44:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "These are confused dreams, and we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, means: The chiefs whom the king of Egypt asked about the interpretation of his vision said: "Your vision is ʾaḍghāth aḥlām (confused dreams)," meaning that it is a jumble, a false vision with no reality to it.

* *

ʾAḍghāth is the plural of ḍighth (a bundle), and the original sense of ḍighth is a bundle of grass; dreams that are jumbled and have no interpretation are likened to it. Aḥlām is the plural of ḥulm, which is a dream that has not come true. Among the uses of ʾaḍghāth is the verse of Ibn Muqbil:

"A tender young woman, as if her bedding were laid with
ʾaḍghāth of basil on a cold morning (shamāl)."
[[I have not found this outside this place. Khawd is a tender young girl. Shamāl is the well-known wind, which is cold. How excellent is what Ibn Muqbil described, and how keen his eye!]]

And from the same usage is the saying of another:
[[I do not know who said it.]]

"He defends the protection of a fetus whose defender is few; a hungry one, like a bundle of herbs, gathered in the belly."
[[This is a line I have not found, and I cannot well explain it on its own.]]

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

19332 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah related to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿ʾaḍghāth aḥlām﴾, he said: confused.

19333 - Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿ʾaḍghāth aḥlām﴾, false.

19334 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, who said: When the king related his vision that he had seen to his companions, they said: ﴿ʾaḍghāth aḥlām﴾, that is, the works of dreams.

19335 - Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿ʾaḍghāth aḥlām﴾, he said: jumbles of dreams. ﴿And we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams﴾.

19336 - Ibn Wakiʿ related to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Abu Marzuq, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak who said: "ʾaḍghāth aḥlām", false.

19337 - ... related to me, saying: al-Muhaaribi related to me, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "Qalu ʾaḍghāth", he said: lies.

19338 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿ʾaḍghāth aḥlām﴾: they are the false dreams.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams﴾, it means: and we are not knowers of what false dreams come to. [[See the explanation of "taʾwīl" above, p. 98, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

The first bāʾ in "taʾwīl" is connected to "ʿālimīn" (learned), and the bāʾ in "ʿālimīn" is the one that enters the predicate along with "mā" which carries the sense of negation. The raising of "ʾaḍghāth aḥlām" is because the meaning of the statement is: this vision is nothing; rather, it is only ʾaḍghāth aḥlām.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 45–46:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the one of the two who had been delivered and remembered after a time said, "I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth."﴾ [12:45] ﴿Joseph, O truthful one, give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green spikes and others dry, that I may return to the people so that they may know.﴾ [12:46]

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "And the one of the two prisoners who had been delivered from death, who had interpreted the dream for Joseph, said..." ﴿And remembered﴾ means: he recalled what he had forgotten of the matter of Joseph and the need he had mentioned to the king, which he had asked Joseph, when he interpreted his dream, to mention to him, by his saying: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾ [12:42]. ﴿After a time﴾ means after an interval, as in the following:

19339 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, he said: after a period [see the explanation of "ummah" above...., comment:....., and the references there].

19340 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

19341 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

19342 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, after a period.

19343 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Asim, from Abu Razin, who said: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, he said: after a period.

19344 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

19345 - ...., saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, meaning: after a period.

19346 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, he said: he remembered after a period.

19347 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, after a period.

19348 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

19349 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Affan narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

19350 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, after a period.

19351 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Kathir said: ﴿After a time﴾: after a period. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿After a time﴾, after years.

19352 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, he said: after a period.

19353 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, that is: after a span of time.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This interpretation is according to the reading of those who read ﴿ba'da ummah﴾ with a damma on the alif and a shaddah on the mim, which is the reading of the reciters in the cities of Islam.

* *

It has been related from a group of the earlier generation that they read it "ba'da amah" with a fatha on the alif and a lightened mim, and the fatha on it means: after forgetfulness.

* *

Some have mentioned that the Arabs say from this: "amiha al-rajul ya'mahu amahan," when he forgot.

* *

Likewise, whoever reads it thus interprets it accordingly.

Mention of those who said so:

19354 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Affan narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he used to read "ba'da amahin" and explain it as: after forgetfulness.

19355 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Bahz ibn Asad narrated to us, from Hammam, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he read "ba'da amahin," saying: after forgetfulness.

19356 - Abu Ghassan Malik ibn al-Khalil al-Yahmadi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Abu Harun al-Ghanawi, from Ikrimah, that he read "ba'da amahin," and "al-amah" is forgetfulness. [Report 19356: "Malik ibn al-Khalil al-Yahmadi al-Azdi," "Abu Ghassan," a teacher of al-Tabari, narrated from him al-Nasa'i and others, biographed in al-Tahdhib.]

19357 - Ya'qub and Ibn Waki' narrated to me, both saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Abu Harun al-Ghanawi narrated to us, from Ikrimah, the like of it.

19358 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Harun said, and Abu Harun al-Ghanawi narrated to me, from Ikrimah: "ba'da amahin," after forgetfulness.

19359 - ...., saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah: "wa-dhakara ba'da amahin": after forgetfulness.

19360 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Ibn Abbas: that is, after forgetfulness.

19361 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "wa-dhakara ba'da amahin," he said: after his forgetfulness.

19362 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Nu'man Arim narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim Abi Umayyah al-Mu'allim, from Mujahid: that he read "wa-dhakara ba'da amahin."

19363 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Abu Marzuq, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, he said: after forgetfulness.

19364 - It was reported to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning his saying: "wa-dhakara ba'da amahin," he says: after forgetfulness.

* *

A third reading has also been mentioned, which is:

19365 - al-Muthanna narrated this to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Humayd, who said: Mujahid read "wa-dhakara ba'da amhin," with the mim jazm and lightened.

* *

It seems that whoever reads it thus intends the verbal noun from their saying "amah yaamahu amhan," and the interpretation of this reading is similar to the interpretation of whoever pronounces the alif and the mim with fatha.

* *

His saying: ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation﴾, meaning: I will inform you of its interpretation [see the explanation of "naba'" above in the language indexes, and its explanation "ta'wil" above, p. 119, comment 1, and the references there] ﴿so send me forth﴾, meaning: release me, that I may go and come to you with its interpretation from the one who knows it.

* *

In the speech there is an omission which was left unmentioned, being sufficiently indicated by what appears of what was left out, and that is: "So they sent him, and he came to Joseph and said to him": O Joseph, O truthful one [see the explanation of "al-siddiq" above, 8: 530-532 / 10: 485], as in:

19366 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The king said to the chiefs around him: ﴿Indeed I see seven fat cows﴾, the verse, and they said to him what they said, and Nabw heard what he heard and asked about its interpretation, [In the printed and manuscript editions: "heard" without a waw, and the correct reading includes it.] the mention of Joseph and what he had interpreted for him and his companion, and what came of that according to what was said, he said: ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth﴾. God says: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, that is, a span of time. So he came to him and said: O Joseph, the king has seen such and such, and he related the dream to him, and Joseph said in it what God mentioned to us in the Book, and its interpretation came to them like the break of dawn. Nabw went out from Joseph with what he had given them as interpretation of the king's dream, and informed him of what he had said.

* *

It has been said that the one of the two who was delivered only said "send me forth" because the prison was not in the city.

Mention of those who said so:

19367 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿And the one of the two who had been delivered and remembered after a time said, "I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth"﴾, Ibn Abbas said: the prison was not in the city, so the cupbearer went to Joseph and said: ﴿Give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows﴾, the verses.

* *

His saying: ﴿Joseph, give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green spikes and others dry﴾: its meaning is: give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows seen in the dream, eaten by seven of them that are lean; and concerning seven green spikes also seen, and seven others among them that are dry. As for "the fat of the cows," they are the years of abundance, as in:

19368 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones﴾, he said: As for the fat ones, they are years of abundance; and as for the seven lean ones, they are years of drought that produce nothing.

19369 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows﴾, the fat ones are the abundant, and the lean cows are the years of drought and barrenness.

* *

His saying: ﴿And seven green spikes and others dry﴾: as for ﴿the green﴾, they are the years of abundance; and as for ﴿the dry﴾, they are the years of drought and barrenness.

And "al-ijaf" is the plural of "ajif," which means the emaciated.

* *

His saying: ﴿That I may return to the people so that they may know﴾, meaning: that I may return to the people and inform them; ﴿so that they may know﴾, meaning: that they may know the interpretation of the dream about which I asked you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 45–46:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the one of the two who had been delivered and remembered after a time said, "I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth."﴾ [12:45] ﴿Joseph, O truthful one, give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green spikes and others dry, that I may return to the people so that they may know.﴾ [12:46]

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "And the one of the two prisoners who had been delivered from death, who had interpreted the dream for Joseph, said..." ﴿And remembered﴾ means: he recalled what he had forgotten of the matter of Joseph and the need he had mentioned to the king, which he had asked Joseph, when he interpreted his dream, to mention to him, by his saying: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾ [12:42]. ﴿After a time﴾ means after an interval, as in the following:

19339 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, he said: after a period [see the explanation of "ummah" above...., comment:....., and the references there].

19340 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

19341 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

19342 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, after a period.

19343 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Asim, from Abu Razin, who said: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, he said: after a period.

19344 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

19345 - ...., saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, meaning: after a period.

19346 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, he said: he remembered after a period.

19347 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, after a period.

19348 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

19349 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Affan narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

19350 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, after a period.

19351 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Kathir said: ﴿After a time﴾: after a period. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿After a time﴾, after years.

19352 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, he said: after a period.

19353 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, that is: after a span of time.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This interpretation is according to the reading of those who read ﴿ba'da ummah﴾ with a damma on the alif and a shaddah on the mim, which is the reading of the reciters in the cities of Islam.

* *

It has been related from a group of the earlier generation that they read it "ba'da amah" with a fatha on the alif and a lightened mim, and the fatha on it means: after forgetfulness.

* *

Some have mentioned that the Arabs say from this: "amiha al-rajul ya'mahu amahan," when he forgot.

* *

Likewise, whoever reads it thus interprets it accordingly.

Mention of those who said so:

19354 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Affan narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he used to read "ba'da amahin" and explain it as: after forgetfulness.

19355 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Bahz ibn Asad narrated to us, from Hammam, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he read "ba'da amahin," saying: after forgetfulness.

19356 - Abu Ghassan Malik ibn al-Khalil al-Yahmadi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Abu Harun al-Ghanawi, from Ikrimah, that he read "ba'da amahin," and "al-amah" is forgetfulness. [Report 19356: "Malik ibn al-Khalil al-Yahmadi al-Azdi," "Abu Ghassan," a teacher of al-Tabari, narrated from him al-Nasa'i and others, biographed in al-Tahdhib.]

19357 - Ya'qub and Ibn Waki' narrated to me, both saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Abu Harun al-Ghanawi narrated to us, from Ikrimah, the like of it.

19358 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Harun said, and Abu Harun al-Ghanawi narrated to me, from Ikrimah: "ba'da amahin," after forgetfulness.

19359 - ...., saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah: "wa-dhakara ba'da amahin": after forgetfulness.

19360 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Ibn Abbas: that is, after forgetfulness.

19361 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "wa-dhakara ba'da amahin," he said: after his forgetfulness.

19362 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Nu'man Arim narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim Abi Umayyah al-Mu'allim, from Mujahid: that he read "wa-dhakara ba'da amahin."

19363 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Abu Marzuq, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, he said: after forgetfulness.

19364 - It was reported to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning his saying: "wa-dhakara ba'da amahin," he says: after forgetfulness.

* *

A third reading has also been mentioned, which is:

19365 - al-Muthanna narrated this to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Humayd, who said: Mujahid read "wa-dhakara ba'da amhin," with the mim jazm and lightened.

* *

It seems that whoever reads it thus intends the verbal noun from their saying "amah yaamahu amhan," and the interpretation of this reading is similar to the interpretation of whoever pronounces the alif and the mim with fatha.

* *

His saying: ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation﴾, meaning: I will inform you of its interpretation [see the explanation of "naba'" above in the language indexes, and its explanation "ta'wil" above, p. 119, comment 1, and the references there] ﴿so send me forth﴾, meaning: release me, that I may go and come to you with its interpretation from the one who knows it.

* *

In the speech there is an omission which was left unmentioned, being sufficiently indicated by what appears of what was left out, and that is: "So they sent him, and he came to Joseph and said to him": O Joseph, O truthful one [see the explanation of "al-siddiq" above, 8: 530-532 / 10: 485], as in:

19366 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The king said to the chiefs around him: ﴿Indeed I see seven fat cows﴾, the verse, and they said to him what they said, and Nabw heard what he heard and asked about its interpretation, [In the printed and manuscript editions: "heard" without a waw, and the correct reading includes it.] the mention of Joseph and what he had interpreted for him and his companion, and what came of that according to what was said, he said: ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth﴾. God says: ﴿And remembered after a time﴾, that is, a span of time. So he came to him and said: O Joseph, the king has seen such and such, and he related the dream to him, and Joseph said in it what God mentioned to us in the Book, and its interpretation came to them like the break of dawn. Nabw went out from Joseph with what he had given them as interpretation of the king's dream, and informed him of what he had said.

* *

It has been said that the one of the two who was delivered only said "send me forth" because the prison was not in the city.

Mention of those who said so:

19367 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿And the one of the two who had been delivered and remembered after a time said, "I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth"﴾, Ibn Abbas said: the prison was not in the city, so the cupbearer went to Joseph and said: ﴿Give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows﴾, the verses.

* *

His saying: ﴿Joseph, give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green spikes and others dry﴾: its meaning is: give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows seen in the dream, eaten by seven of them that are lean; and concerning seven green spikes also seen, and seven others among them that are dry. As for "the fat of the cows," they are the years of abundance, as in:

19368 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones﴾, he said: As for the fat ones, they are years of abundance; and as for the seven lean ones, they are years of drought that produce nothing.

19369 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows﴾, the fat ones are the abundant, and the lean cows are the years of drought and barrenness.

* *

His saying: ﴿And seven green spikes and others dry﴾: as for ﴿the green﴾, they are the years of abundance; and as for ﴿the dry﴾, they are the years of drought and barrenness.

And "al-ijaf" is the plural of "ajif," which means the emaciated.

* *

His saying: ﴿That I may return to the people so that they may know﴾, meaning: that I may return to the people and inform them; ﴿so that they may know﴾, meaning: that they may know the interpretation of the dream about which I asked you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 47:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Said [Joseph], "You will plant for seven consecutive years as is your habit. Then whatever you harvest, leave it in its ears, except for a little of which you eat."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance says: Joseph said to the one who asked him about the king's dream: ﴿You will plant for seven years, as is your habit﴾, meaning: you will plant these seven years just as you used to plant the other years before them, according to your custom in the past.

* *

And "al-da'b" (habit, custom) [see the discussion of "al-da'b" above, 6:224, 225 / 14:19]. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"As your habit with Umm al-Huwayrith before her,
and her neighbour Umm al-Rabab at Ma'sil"

[The verse and its sourcing were mentioned above, 6:225.]

He means: as is your custom with her.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then whatever you harvest, leave it in its ears, except for a little of which you eat﴾, this was a counsel that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) gave to the people, an opinion he saw as beneficial for them, instructing them to conserve their food, as follows:

19370 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: The Prophet of God Joseph said to them: ﴿You will plant for seven consecutive years as is your habit﴾, to the end of the verse. The Prophet of God (ﷺ) only intended conservation.

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿Then after that will come seven hard years, which will consume what you have stored up for them, except for a little of what you keep safe.﴾ (12:48)

Abu Ja'far said: He means: After the seven years in which you sow consecutively will come seven hard years, meaning years of drought and famine. ﴿They will consume what you stored up for them﴾ means: in them will be eaten what you prepared in the seven fruitful years, of food and provisions.

* *

He, mighty is His praise, said ﴿yakulna﴾ (they will consume), describing the years as the ones who ﴿consume﴾, but the meaning is that the people of that region eat during them, as it was said:

[[He is Abdullah ibn Abd al-A'la ibn Abi Amra.]]

*Your day, O deceived one, is heedlessness and negligence,*
*and your night is sleep, and death is bound to you.*

*Are you awake today or dreaming,*
*and how can one bewildered and distracted sleep?*

*Had you been awake this morning, the flowing tears*
*would have scorched the rims of your two eyes.*

*Rather, you have been in long sleep, while there have drawn near*
*to you dreadful, great matters.*

*Your day, O deceived one, is heedlessness and negligence,*
*and your night is sleep, and death is bound to you.*

*You are delighted by what decays, and occupied with wishes,*
*as the sleeper is delighted by dreams in sleep.*

*Your striving is toward what you will later hate the outcome of;*
*so too in this world the beasts live.*

*Neither are you among the sleepers safe one day,*
*nor among the wakeful are you a watchful, resolute one.*

[[Al-Akhbar al-Tiwal: 333; Sirat Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz by Ibn al-Jawzi: 225; Tarikh Ibn Kathir 9: 206; and others. He means: are you awake today or dreaming...]]

So He described the day with heedlessness and negligence, and the night with sleep, because people are heedless and negligent in the day and sleep at night, and the addressees understand its meaning and what is intended by it.

* *

﴿Except for a little of what you keep safe﴾ means: except for a small amount of what you secure.

* *

*Ihsan* (preserving) means putting into a fortress (*hisn*), but what is meant by it is securing and storing.

* *

Those of ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation of the Qur'an) said things similar to what we have said about this.

Mentioning those who said that:

19371. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿They will consume what you stored up for them﴾, meaning: they will consume what you had set aside for food in them ﴿except for a little of what you keep safe﴾.

19372. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Then after that will come seven hard years﴾, and they are years of drought that leave the land barren, ﴿they will consume what you stored up for them, except for a little of what you keep safe﴾.

19373. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Then after that will come seven hard years﴾, and they are years of drought, ﴿they will consume what you stored up for them, except for a little of what you keep safe﴾, meaning what you store away.

19374. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abdullah told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿except for a little of what you keep safe﴾, meaning: what you store away.

19375. Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿what you keep safe﴾ means what you secure.

19376. Ibn Wakic told us, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿They will consume what you stored up for them, except for a little of what you keep safe﴾, he said: what you lift up (set aside).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: These statements regarding His words ﴿what you keep safe﴾, though the wording of those who said them differs, their meanings are close, and the root of the word and its interpretation is as I have explained.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then after that there will come a year in which people will be given rain, and in which they will press (juice)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is information from Yusuf, peace be upon him, to the people about what was not in the dream of their king, but it is from the knowledge of the unseen which God gave him as a proof of his prophethood and as evidence of his truthfulness, as:

19377. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: Then God increased him in knowledge of a year they had not asked him about, so he said: ﴿Then after that there will come a year in which people will be given rain, and in which they will press (juice)﴾.

* *

By His saying ﴿in which people will be given rain﴾ he means, with rain and downpour.

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as this.

Mention of those who said that:

19378. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Then after that there will come a year in which people will be given rain﴾, he said: in it they will be given rain.

19379. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Wasiti narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿in which people will be given rain﴾, he said: with rain.

19380. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Then after that there will come a year﴾, he said: He informed them of something they had not asked him about, and God had taught him it, ﴿a year in which people will be given rain﴾, with rain.

19381. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿in which people will be given rain﴾, with rain.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and in which they will press (juice)﴾, the people of interpretation differed regarding its explanation.

Some of them said: its meaning is: and in it they will press grapes, sesame and the like.

Mention of those who said that:

19382. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and in which they will press﴾, he said: the grapes and oil.

19383. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿and in which they will press﴾: sesame for oil, grapes for wine, and olives for olive oil.

19384. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿a year in which people will be given rain and in which they will press﴾, he means: rain will reach them, and they will press grapes in it, press olives in it, and press all kinds of fruits.

19385. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and in which they will press﴾, he said: they will press their grapes.

19386. Ibn Wakr' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿and in which they will press﴾, he said: the grapes.

19387. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Wasiti narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿and in which they will press﴾, he said: the olive oil.

19388. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "and in which they will press", he said: they used to press grapes and fruits.

19389. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and in which they will press﴾, he said: they will press grapes, olives and fruits from abundance. This is knowledge God taught Yusuf, which he had not been asked about.

* *

Others said: the meaning of His saying ﴿and in which they will press﴾ is: and in which they will milk.

Mention of those who said that:

19390. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Fudalah narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and in which they will press﴾, he said: in it they will milk.

19391. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, saying: al-Faraj ibn Fudalah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas used to read: "wa-fihi tu'sarun" with the letter ta', meaning: they will be milked.

* *

The readers differed in their recitation of this.

Some of the readers of Medina, Basra and Kufa read: ﴿wa-fihi ya'sirun﴾ with the letter ya', in the sense of what I described, from the statement of those who said: pressing of grapes and oils.

* *

The majority of the Kufan readers read: "wa-fihi ta'sirun", with the letter ta'.

Some of them read: "wa-fihi yu'sarun", meaning: they will be rained upon.

This is a recitation I do not consider permissible to recite, because it contradicts what the readers of the great cities agree upon.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this matter is that the reader has the choice in his recitation between the two other readings, as he wishes: if he wishes with the letter ya', in reference to the report about "the people", in the sense: in it the people will be given rain and in it they will press their grapes and oils; or if he wishes with the letter ta', in reference to His saying: ﴿except a little of what you store﴾, and addressing those whom He addressed with His saying: ﴿they eat what you have put forward for them, except a little of what you store﴾. Both are widely transmitted recitations in the cities, agreeing in meaning though the wording differs. This is because those addressed were undoubtedly such that when they were given rain and pressed, the people in their region were given rain and pressed; and likewise, when the people in their region were given rain and pressed, those addressed were given rain and pressed. So both have the same meaning, though the wording differs in the recitation.

* *

Some of those who lack knowledge of the sayings of the early generations among the people of interpretation, who explain the Qur'an by their own opinion according to the usage of Arabic, [[Meaning Abu 'Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna, who says this in his book Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 313, 314.]] direct the meaning of His saying ﴿and in which they will press﴾ to: in it they will be saved from drought and famine by rain, and he claims it is from "al-'asr" and "al-'usrah," which mean deliverance, from the saying of Abu Zubayd al-Ta'i:

Thirsty, crying for help, not being helped... and he had been the 'usrah of the one delivered

[[Amali al-Yazidi: 8, Jamharat Ash'ar al-'Arab: 138, Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 313, and al-Lisan (n-j-d) and ('-s-r), and others, from a qasidah in which he lamented his brother al-Lajlaj, who had died of thirst on the road to Mecca. Before it he says, and it is of fine poetry: ...]] that is, the one overcome. And from the saying of Labid:

So he spent the night, and the people had traveled the last part of their night, and he was not one who halts without being pressed.

[[His Diwan, qasidah 14, verse 12, Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 295, 314, al-Lisan ('-s-r), and others, from a qasidah in which he mentioned those of his people who perished. This verse concerns Qays ibn Juz' ibn Khalid ibn Ja'far, who went out on a raid and was victorious; when he returned, death overtook him suddenly on the back of his horse, as he spent the night on his horse as a sentry for his companions, wearing his armor, and the cold overcame him and killed him. Concerning that Labid says: ... The explanation is given in the notes of the source.]] i.e., the one overcome. 

This interpretation is refuted by the consensus of all the scholars among the Companions and the Successors, which suffices as evidence of its error.

* *

As for the view transmitted by al-Faraj ibn Fudalah from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, [[See no. 19391.]] it is a view with no meaning, because it contradicts what is known of Arabic usage and what is known of the statement of Ibn 'Abbas.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 50:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me." And when the messenger came to him, he said, "Return to your lord and ask him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot."﴾ (50)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His mention, exalted is He, means: When the messenger whom they had sent to Yusuf, the one who had said, ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth﴾, returned and informed them of the interpretation of the king's dream concerning Yusuf, the king came to know the reality of what had been told to him as its interpretation and its correctness, and the king said, "Bring me the one who interpreted my dream." As related:

19392. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: So the messenger went out from Yusuf with what he had given them as the interpretation of the king's dream, until he came to the king and informed him of what had been said. When he informed him of what was in his mind, it was as clear as daylight [in the printed edition: "like the daylight," but in the manuscript the writing is poor, and the correct reading is what I have established], and he knew that what he had said would come to pass as he had said, and he said, "Bring him to me."

19393. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, who said: 'Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: When the king's messenger came to him, he said, "Bring him to me."

* *

As for His words, ﴿And when the messenger came to him﴾, it means: when the king's messenger came to him calling him to the king. ﴿He said, "Return to your lord"﴾, meaning: Yusuf said to the messenger, "Return to your master" [see the explanation of "lord" earlier, p. 107, note 1, and the references there]. ﴿And ask him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands?﴾ He refused to go out with the messenger in response to the king until his innocence was established among them, given what they had accused him of concerning the women, [in the printed edition: "qadhafuhu," but I have corrected it to the correct reading from the manuscript: "qarafahu bi-l-shay'," meaning he accused him of it.] So he said to the messenger, "Ask the king what is the matter with the women who cut their hands, and the woman who had him imprisoned on account of her affair?" As related:

19394. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And when the messenger came to him, he said, "Return to your lord and ask him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands"﴾, and the woman who had him imprisoned on account of her matter, concerning what had occurred in that.

19395. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, who said: 'Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: When the king sent his messenger and he informed him, he said, ﴿Bring him to me﴾. When the messenger came to him and called him to the king, Yusuf refused to go out with him. ﴿And he said, "Return to your lord and ask him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands"﴾, the verse. Al-Suddi said: Ibn 'Abbas said: If Yusuf had gone out that day before the king knew of his situation, the Aziz would never have been free of resentment toward him! That is, "This is the one who solicited his wife."

19396. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from a man, from Abu al-Zinad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: May Allah have mercy on Yusuf, if he was a man of deliberation! If I had been the one imprisoned and then sent for, I would have gone out quickly; indeed, he was forbearing and a man of deliberation! [Report 19396: this is a hadith of weak chain, because the man who narrated from Abu al-Zinad is unidentified.]

19397. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, who said: Abu Salamah narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: If I had remained in prison as long as Yusuf remained, and then the caller came to me, I would have answered him, when the messenger came to him and said, ﴿Return to your lord and ask him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands﴾, the verse. [Report 19397: this is the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Amr from Abu Salamah, which Abu Ja'far narrates through three chains: this one, the next one, and numbers 19401 and 19402. Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi is trustworthy, and the group narrated from him, as already mentioned under no. 12822, and elsewhere before and after it. It is also transmitted through Muhammad ibn 'Amr by Ahmad in the Musnad of Abu Hurayrah, and Ibn Kathir quoted it with its chain and wording in his Tafsir 4:448, saying: "Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah." I was unable to locate it in the Musnad due to the length of Abu Hurayrah's section. Al-Haythami also cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7:40, saying: "I say: he has another hadith in the Sahih besides this one, narrated by Ahmad, and in it is Muhammad ibn 'Amr, who is good in hadith."]

19398. Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Sulayman ibn Bilal informed me, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the like of it. [Report 19398: a repetition of the previous one. Sulayman ibn Bilal al-Taymi is trustworthy, and the group narrated from him; he has been mentioned many times, the last under no. 11503.]

19399. Zakariyya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to us, who said: Sa'id ibn Tulayd narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: Bakr ibn Mudar narrated to me, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, from Yunus ibn Yazid, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: If I had remained in prison as long as Yusuf remained, I would have answered the caller. [Report 19399: Zakariyya ibn Aban al-Misri is Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri, the teacher of al-Tabari, mentioned before under nos. 5973 and 12803, and see what I wrote there about doubt concerning him. In the printed edition it read "al-Muqri'," which was a misreading of the manuscript's "al-Misri." This report has a sound chain, and al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih (Fath 8:277) from Sa'id ibn Tulayd, similar to it at length; see the following note.]

19400. Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the like of it. [Report 19400: another chain for the previous report. Al-Bukhari narrated it at length in his Sahih (Fath 6:293-295), and the Hafiz exhaustively explained and traced it there. Muslim also narrated it at length in his Sahih 2:183 / 15:122-123.]

19401. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, who said: 'Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, who said: Hammad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, reciting this verse: ﴿Return to your lord and ask him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot﴾: If I had been he, I would have hastened to answer and would not have sought an excuse. [Report 19401: Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad through this chain; see the note on no. 19397.]

19402. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, who said: Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit, from the Prophet ﷺ; and Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he recited: ﴿Return to your lord and ask him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands﴾, the verse, and the Prophet ﷺ said: If he had sent for me, I would have hastened to answer and would not have sought an excuse. [Report 19402: this is the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Amr from Abu Salamah, as I explained under no. 19397.]

19403. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: I have marveled at Yusuf, his patience and his generosity, and may Allah forgive him, when he was asked about the lean and fat cows; and if I had been in his place, I would not have informed them of anything until I stipulated that they release me.

And I have marveled at Yusuf, his patience and his generosity, and may Allah forgive him, when the messenger came to him; and if I had been in his place, I would have rushed them to the door, but he wanted to have an excuse. [Report 19403: this is a mursal hadith.]

19404. Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Return to your lord and ask him what is the matter with the women﴾: the Prophet of Allah, peace be upon him, wanted not to go out until he had an excuse.

19405. Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words: ﴿Return to your lord and ask him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands﴾: he said, Yusuf wanted an excuse before going out of the prison.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot﴾, it means: Indeed Allah, exalted is He, has knowledge of their conduct and their deeds which they did to me and which they do to others, nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He is the one who will recompense them for it. [See the explanation of "plot" (kayd) earlier, p. 88, note 2, and the references there; and the explanation of "Knowing" (alim) in the lexical indexes earlier under the root ʿ-l-m.]

* *

It has been said: the meaning of that is: indeed my master, al-Itfir the Aziz, the husband of the woman who solicited me, is Knowing of my innocence from the evil with which they accused me. [In the printed edition: "qadhafatni bihi," but the correct reading from the manuscript is: i.e., they accused me of it.]

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "What was your affair when you sought to seduce Joseph from himself?" They said, "Far be God from any evil in him!" The wife of the governor said, "Now the truth has come to light. It was I who sought to seduce him from himself, and he is surely of the truthful."﴾ (12:51)

Abu Ja'far said: In this speech there is something omitted, which is dispensed with because of what has been mentioned, and it is: "So the messenger returned to the king from Joseph with his message, and the king summoned the women who had cut their hands and the wife of the governor," and he said to them: ﴿What was your affair when you sought to seduce Joseph from himself?﴾ As is related:

19406 - Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: When the messenger came to the king from Joseph with what he had sent him, he gathered the women and said: ﴿What was your affair when you sought to seduce Joseph from himself?﴾

* *

By His words ﴿What was your affair﴾ he means: what was your matter and what was your situation? ﴿when you sought to seduce Joseph from himself﴾ [[See the explanation of "al-murawadah" (seduction) earlier, p. 86, note 1, and the references there.]] — so they answered him, saying: ﴿Far be God from any evil in him!﴾ ﴿The wife of the governor said, "Now the truth has come to light."﴾ [[See the explanation of "hasha lillah" (far be God) earlier, pp. 81–84.]] She says: now the truth has become clear and has been revealed and manifested. ﴿It was I who sought to seduce him from himself﴾ = and indeed Joseph is among the truthful in his saying: ﴿It was she who sought to seduce me from myself﴾.

* *

Like what we have said regarding the meaning of ﴿Now the truth has come to light﴾, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

19407 - Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abd Allah related to us, who said: Mu'awiyah related to us, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Now the truth has come to light﴾, he said: it became clear.

19408 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, who said: Abu Asim related to us, who said: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of God: ﴿Now the truth has come to light﴾, it became clear.

19409 - Ibn Waki' related to us, who said: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

19410 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, who said: Shababah related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

19411 - Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

19412 - Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Now the truth has come to light﴾, now the truth has become clear.

19413 - Al-Qasim related to us, who said: Al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

19414 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿Now the truth has come to light﴾, he said: it became clear.

19415 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, who said: Amr ibn Muhammad related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Now the truth has come to light﴾, he said: it became clear.

19416 - Ibn Waki' related to us, who said: Amr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, the like of it.

19417 - Al-Qasim related to us, who said: Al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hushaym related to us, who said: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.

19418 - Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The wife of the governor of Egypt, Ra'il, said: ﴿Now the truth has come to light﴾, i.e., now the truth has emerged and become clear, ﴿It was I who sought to seduce him from himself, and he is surely of the truthful﴾, regarding what Joseph had said of what she had claimed against him.

19419 - Ibn Waki' related to us, who said: Amr related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: The king said: Bring them to me! So he said: ﴿What was your affair when you sought to seduce Joseph from himself? They said, "Far be God from any evil in him!"﴾ But the wife of the governor informed us that she had sought to seduce him from himself, and he entered the house with her and untied his trousers, then tied them again afterwards, so you do not know what appeared to him.

Then the wife of the governor said: ﴿Now the truth has come to light.﴾

19420 - Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿Now the truth has come to light﴾, it became clear.

* *

The root of "hasahasa" (ḥaṣḥaṣa, to become manifest) is "ḥassa," but it was said "ḥaṣḥaṣa," as it was said ﴿fa-kubkibu﴾ [Surah al-Shu'ara': 94] from "kabba," and "kafkafa" from "kaff," and "dhardara" from "dharra." [[In the manuscript: "wa-radrada," in the root r-d; the correct reading appears to be that of the printed edition. "Al-dharduarah" means scattering a thing and dispersing it. "Dhar al-shay'" means to disperse it.]] The root of "al-ḥaṣṣ" is the uprooting of a thing; it is said of it: "ḥassa sha'rahu," when he uprooted it by shearing. What is intended in this place by His saying ﴿The truth has come to light﴾ [[In the printed edition: the phrase "bi-qawlihi" is omitted.]] is that falsehood and lying departed and were cut off, and the truth became clear and manifest.

The exposition concerning His words, exalted is He: ﴿That he may know that I did not betray him in secret, and that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers﴾ (52).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words ﴿That he may know that I did not betray him in secret﴾, he means: this act that I committed, namely my refusing the king's messenger and my not responding to his summons and going out to him, and my request that he ask the women who cut their hands about their affair when they cut their hands, I did it so that he may know that I did not betray him in his wife "in secret" – that is, I did not commit an indecency with her in his absence from me. [[See the explanation of "al-ghayb" (the unseen, absence) in the preceding indexes of vocabulary (gh-y-b).]] And if he did not commit that in his absence, then in his presence he is more worthy of being far from committing it, as:

19421 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yusuf said: ﴿That he may know﴾ – the Aziz (Ahl al-'Aziz), the master of Yusuf – ﴿that I did not betray him in secret﴾, that I would not have opposed him regarding his family in a way that he would not know.

19422 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, who said: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿That he may know that I did not betray him in secret﴾ – Yusuf says it.

19423 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, who said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿That he may know that I did not betray him in secret﴾ – Yusuf says it: "I did not betray my master."

19424 – ... He said: Ishaq narrated to us, who said: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿That he may know that I did not betray him in secret﴾ – he said: Yusuf says it.

19425 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿That he may know that I did not betray him in secret﴾ – he said: This is the statement of Yusuf.

19426 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, who said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Salim, from Abu Salih, concerning His words: ﴿That he may know that I did not betray him in secret﴾ – he said: It is Yusuf; he did not betray the Aziz regarding his wife.

19427 – It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words: "That he may know that I did not betray him in secret" – it is Yusuf who says: "I did not betray the king in secret."

* *

And His words: ﴿And that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers﴾ – he says: I did that so that my master may know that I did not betray him in secret, ﴿and that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers﴾ – he says: and that Allah does not make upright the deeds of those who betray trusts, nor does He guide their actions in betraying them. [[See the explanation of "al-huda" (guidance) in the preceding indexes of vocabulary (h-d-y), and the explanation of "al-kayd" (plot, scheme) previously on p. 137, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

The statement ﴿That he may know that I did not betray him in secret﴾ is connected to the words of the wife of the Aziz: ﴿I sought to seduce him, and he is certainly among the truthful﴾, for the listeners to know its meaning, like the connection of Allah's words ﴿And thus they do﴾ to the woman's words: ﴿And they make the honored people of its town abased﴾ [Surah al-Naml: 34]. This is because His words ﴿And thus they do﴾ are the predicate of a subject; and likewise Pharaoh's words to his companions in "Surah al-A'raf": ﴿So what do you advise?﴾, which is connected to the words of the chiefs: ﴿He wants to expel you from your land﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 110]. [[See what preceded, 13:20.]]

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil, except those on whom my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (12:53)

Abu Ja'far said: Yusuf, may God's blessings be upon him, is saying: "I do not absolve myself of error and failing, so that I declare myself pure." ﴿Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾ means: indeed, the souls of people command them to do what the soul desires, even if its desire is in something that does not please God. ﴿Except those on whom my Lord has mercy﴾ means: except that my Lord show mercy to whomever He wills of His creation, so that He saves him from following his soul's desire and obeying it in the evil it commands him to do. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

* *

The "mā" in His words ﴿except those on whom my Lord has mercy﴾ is in the accusative position, because it is a disconnected exception (istithnā' munqaṭi', an exception not of the same kind as what precedes it), like His words: ﴿nor will they be rescued, except by mercy from Us﴾ (Yasin 36:43-44), meaning: except that they be shown mercy. And "an," when it carries the meaning of a verbal noun, resembles "mā."

* *

By His words ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ He means that God is one who pardons the sins of whoever repents of his sins, by not punishing him for them and not exposing him because of them, and "Merciful" means that He will not punish him for them after his repentance.

* *

It has been mentioned that Yusuf said this statement because, when Yusuf said: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence﴾ (12:52), a certain angel said: "Nor on the day you desired her!" Then Yusuf said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾.

* *

It has also been said that the one who said to Yusuf, "Nor on the day you desired her, and untied your trousers!" was the wife of the Aziz, and Yusuf answered her with this reply.

* *

And it has been said that Yusuf said that on his own initiative.

* *

Those who said this:

19428 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the king gathered the women and asked them, "Did you seek to seduce Yusuf?" they said, "Hashā li-Llāh (God forbid)! We know no evil of him!" The wife of the Aziz said: ﴿Now the truth has become evident﴾ (12:51), to the end of the verse. Yusuf said: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence﴾. He said: Then Jibril said to him: "Nor on the day you desired what you desired!" So he said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾.

19429 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the king gathered the women, he said to them: "Did you seek to seduce Yusuf?" Then he mentioned the rest of the report, like the report of Abu Kurayb, from Waki'.

19430 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Pharaoh gathered the women, [[In the printed edition: "When the king gathered," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] he said: "Did you seek to seduce Yusuf?" Then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Jibril nudged him and said: "Nor when you desired her!" Yusuf said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾.

So he said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾.

Then he mentioned the rest of the report in the same way.

So Yusuf said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾.

So he said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾.

19435 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, with the like of it.

19436 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Mis'ar informed us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, like the report of Ibn Waki', from Muhammad ibn Bishr and Ahmad ibn Bashir, exactly.
