He said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾.

19439 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Salim, from Abu Salih, concerning His words: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence﴾, he said: This is the statement of Yusuf. He said: Then Jibril said to him: "Nor when you untied your trousers?" He said: Yusuf said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾, to the end of the verse.

19440 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Isma'il ibn Salim, from Abu Salih, similarly.

19441 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence﴾: It was mentioned to us that the angel who was with Yusuf said to him: "Remember what you desired." The prophet of God said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾.

19442 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: It reached me that the king said to him, when he said what he said: "Do you remember your desire?" So he said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil, except those on whom my Lord has mercy﴾.

19443 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah, concerning His words: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence﴾: The king said, and he struck him in the side: "O Yusuf, nor when you desired her?" He said: So he said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself﴾.

* *

Those who said: the one who said this to him was the woman.

19444 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence﴾: He said: Yusuf said it when he was brought in, so that the Aziz would know that he had not betrayed him in his household, and that God does not guide the scheme of the betrayers. Then the wife of the Aziz said: "O Yusuf, nor on the day you untied your trousers?" So Yusuf said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾.

* *

Those who said: the one who said this was Yusuf himself, without anyone reminding him, but he remembered what had previously passed from him in that matter.

19445 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence, and that God does not guide the scheme of the betrayers﴾: It is the statement of Yusuf to his king, when God showed him his innocence, and he mentioned that he had desired her and she had desired him. So Yusuf said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾, to the end of the verse.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 54:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me; I will select him for myself." So when he spoke with him, he said, "Indeed, you are today established and trustworthy in our presence."﴾ (54)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And the king said," meaning the greatest king of Egypt, who, as mentioned by Ibn Ishaq, was al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan.

Number 19446: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from him, with that.

* *

= When the king saw the innocence of Yusuf and recognised his trustworthiness and knowledge, he said to his companions: ﴿Bring him to me; I will select him for myself﴾, meaning: I will make him one of my chosen ones, to the exclusion of others.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So when he spoke with him﴾, meaning: when the king spoke with Yusuf and recognised his innocence and the greatness of his trustworthiness, he said to him: "Indeed, you, O Yusuf, are ﴿established and trustworthy in our presence﴾," meaning: you are established in what you wish, and whatever need arises for you in our presence, due to the elevation of your station and rank with us, you are trustworthy in whatever you are entrusted with.

Number 19447: Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: When the king found him to have an excuse, he said: ﴿Bring him to me; I will select him for myself﴾.

Number 19448: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿I will select him for myself﴾, he said: I will take him for myself.

Number 19449: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, who said: The king said: ﴿Bring him to me; I will select him for myself﴾. He said: The king said to him: "I wish to make you my special companion, except that I feel disdain for you eating with me."

Yusuf said: "I am more worthy to feel disdain, I am the son of Ishaq" — or: "I am the son of Isma'il" (Abu Ja'far was uncertain; in my book it reads: "Ibn Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah; Ibn Ibrahim, the friend of Allah").

Number 19450: Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, with similar wording, except that he said: "I am the son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah, son of Isma'il, the sacrificed one of Allah."

Number 19451: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, who said: The Aziz said to Yusuf: "There is nothing except that I love for you to share it with me, except that I love that you not share with me in my family, and that my servant not eat with me!" He said: "Do you disdain to eat with me? I am more worthy to feel disdain than you: I am the son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah, and son of Ishaq the sacrificed one, and son of Ya'qub, whose eyes turned white from grief."

Number 19452: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uqbah narrated to us, from Hamzah al-Zayyat, from Ibn Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, who said: When the Aziz saw Yusuf's courtesy, his shrewdness and his refinement, he invited him, and he would eat his midday and evening meals with him, apart from his servants. When what happened between him and the woman happened, she said to him: "Do you bring this one near! Tell him to eat his midday meal with the servants." He said to him: "Go and eat your midday meal with the servants." Yusuf said to him to his face: "Do you desire to eat with me" — or "do you disdain (taknaf)" [[It is said "nakafa min al-shay'" and "istankafa minhu" with the same meaning.]] — "I, by Allah, am Yusuf son of Ya'qub, the prophet of Allah, son of Ishaq the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim the friend of Allah."

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "Set me over the treasuries of the land; indeed I am a knowing guardian."﴾ (55)**

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: Joseph said to the king, "Set me over the treasuries of your land."

* *

"Khaza'in" is the plural of "khizana" (treasury).

* *

The "alif and lam" have been attached to "al-ard" (the land) as a substitute for the possessive pronoun (idafah), as the poet said: [[This is al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani.]]

*"And their dreams are not confused"* [[The line precedes and is cited in the sources: "They have a disposition which time has not given to anyone else among the people, and their dreams are not confused."]]

* *

This was a request from Joseph, peace be upon him, to the king that he appoint him over the food supply and the revenue of the country and over the management of its affairs. The king granted this to him, as has reached me, as related by:

19453: Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words, ﴿Set me over the treasuries of the land﴾: "Pharaoh had many treasuries, other than the food." He said: "So he handed over all his authority to him and gave him the judgment; his command and his judgment were binding."

19454: Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar related to us, from Shayba al-Dabbi, concerning His words, ﴿Set me over the treasuries of the land﴾, he said: "Over the safekeeping of the food." [[The report 19454: "Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar al-Tamimi" is among those whose narrations are to be avoided, especially his narrations from Muhammad ibn Humayd, as has passed under nos. 4038, 14365 and 17631.

"Shayba al-Dabbi" is "Shayba ibn Na'ama al-Dabbi," known as "Abu Na'ama," weak in narration and not to be used as evidence. He is biographed in al-Kabir 2/2/143, Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/335, Mizan al-I'tidal 1:452, and Lisan al-Mizan 3:159.

See the following chain, no. 19457.]]

* *

As for His words, ﴿indeed I am a knowing guardian﴾, the people of interpretation differed concerning its meaning.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: "Indeed I am a guardian of what you have entrusted to me, knowing of what you have placed in my charge."

Those who said this:

19455: Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning ﴿indeed I am a knowing guardian﴾: "Indeed I am a keeper of what you have entrusted to me, a knower of what you have placed in my charge." He said: "He did so."

19456: Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His words: ﴿indeed I am a knowing guardian﴾, he says: "A guardian of what you have placed in my charge, knowing of its matter."

19457: Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar related to us, from Shayba al-Dabbi, concerning His words: ﴿indeed I am a knowing guardian﴾, he says: "Indeed I am a guardian of what you have entrusted to me, knowing of the years of famine." [[The report 19457: see its explanation in the note on no. 19454.]]

* *

Others said: "Indeed I am a keeper of the reckoning, knowing of tongues (languages)."

Those who said this:

19458: Ibn Waki' told us, saying: Amr related to us, from al-Ash'ari: ﴿indeed I am a knowing guardian﴾, "a keeper of the reckoning, knowing of tongues."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views in our opinion is the view of those who said: The meaning of that is: "Indeed I am a guardian of what you have entrusted to me, knowing of what you have placed in my charge," because this comes right after His words, ﴿Set me over the treasuries of the land﴾, and his request to the king that he entrust him with the treasuries of the land. So his informing the king that he has expertise in this and is capable of it is more fitting than his informing him of his keeping of the reckoning and his knowledge of tongues. [[See the explanation of "hafiz" (guardian) above, 15:449, note 1, and the references there.

And the explanation of "alim" (knowing) is in the language indexes under (ʿ-l-m).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 56:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We established Joseph in the land, to take residence therein wherever he willed. We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will, and We do not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost.﴾ (56)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Thus We settled Joseph in the land [[See the explanation of "tamkin" (establishment, empowerment) above, p. 20, note 1, and the references there.]] — meaning the land of Egypt — ﴿to take residence therein wherever he willed﴾, that is: he takes for himself a dwelling in the land of Egypt wherever he wills, after imprisonment and constraint [[See the explanation of "tabawwu'" (taking residence) above, vol. 15, p. 198, note 3, and the references there.]] — ﴿We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will﴾, from among Our creation, just as We bestowed it upon Joseph; so We established him in the land after servitude and captivity, and after being thrown into the well — ﴿and We do not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost﴾, that is: We do not nullify the recompense of the deed of one who does good, obeys his Lord, acts upon what He commanded him, and refrains from what He forbade, just as We did not nullify the recompense of Joseph's deed when he did good and obeyed God. [[See the explanation of "ajr" (reward) and "ihsan" (doing good) in the lexical indexes above, under the roots (a-j-r) and (h-s-n).]]

* *

The establishment of God for Joseph in the land was as follows:

19459 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Joseph said to the king, ﴿Set me over the treasuries of the land; indeed I am a knowing guardian﴾, the king said: Indeed you have done so! So he appointed him over what they mention of the work of Itfir, and removed Itfir from what he had been upon. God says: ﴿And thus We established Joseph in the land, to take residence therein wherever he willed﴾, to the end of the verse. He said: It was related to me, and God knows best, that Itfir died in those nights, and that the king al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid married Joseph to the wife of Itfir, Ra'il; and when she entered upon him, he said: Is this not better than what you were seeking? He said: They claim that she said: O truthful one, do not blame me, for I was a woman, as you see, beautiful and graceful, in luxury and worldly comfort, and my husband did not approach women, while you were as God made you in your beauty and bearing, so my self overcame me regarding what you saw. They claim that he found her a virgin, so he lay with her, and she bore him two sons: Ephraim son of Joseph, and Manasseh son of Joseph.

19460 – Ibn Wakf'i related to me, saying: Amr related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿And thus We established Joseph in the land, to take residence therein wherever he willed﴾. He said: The king appointed him over Egypt, and he was the one in charge of its affairs; he handled its sale and commerce and all its matters. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And thus We established Joseph in the land, to take residence therein wherever he willed﴾.

19461 – Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿to take residence therein wherever he willed﴾: We gave him dominion over what exists in it wherever he wills of that world; he does in it what he wills, and authority over it was entrusted to him. He said: Had he willed to make Pharaoh subordinate under his hands and make him above him, he would have done so.

19462 – al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Abu Ishaq al-Kufi, from Mujahid, who said: The king who was with Joseph became Muslim.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 57:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who have believed and used to fear Allah﴾ (57).

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, says: "And the reward of Allah in the Hereafter" = ﴿is better for those who have believed﴾, meaning: for those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger, [better] than what He gave Yusuf in this world by establishing him in the land of Egypt = ﴿and used to fear Allah﴾, meaning: and used to be mindful of Allah, fearing His punishment by opposing His command and treating His prohibited things as lawful, so that they obey Him in His commands and His prohibitions.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 58:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the brothers of Joseph came and entered upon him, and he recognized them, but they did not recognize him.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿And the brothers of Joseph came and entered upon him, and he recognized them﴾, Joseph, ﴿but they, to him, were unrecognizing﴾, meaning they did not know him.

* *

The cause of their coming to Joseph, as it has been related to me, was as follows:

19463: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Joseph became settled in his kingdom, and came out of the trial he had been in, and the years of plenty, for which he had commanded them to prepare in anticipation of the years of famine that he had told them would come, had passed, people suffered hardship in every direction, and they came to Egypt seeking provisions from every town. Joseph, when he saw the hardship that had befallen the people, had made them equal among themselves [in the printed edition: "asa baynahum", and the correct reading is from the manuscript. "Asa bayn al-qawm" means he made them equal, made each one a peer of his fellow, i.e., like him], and he would not give a man more than one camel, nor give one man two camels, distributing among the people and widening provision for them [("al-taqsit" means division; he gave each person a portion, and this is from justice among them)]. So his brothers came, among those who came to him from the people, seeking provisions from Egypt, and he recognized them, but they were unrecognizing of him, because Allah willed to bring about for Joseph, peace be upon him, what He willed [in the printed edition: "ma arad", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is entirely correct].

19464: Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, who said: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: Hunger afflicted the people, until it reached the land of Ya'qub in which he was, so he sent his sons to Egypt, and kept back Joseph's brother Benjamin. When they entered upon Joseph, he recognized them, but they were unrecognizing of him. When he looked at them, he said: "Tell me your affair, for I find your situation strange!" They said: "We are a people from the land of Syria." He said: "What brought you?" They said: "We came to get food." He said: "You are liars, you are spies. How many are you?" They said: "Ten." He said: "You are ten thousand, each man of you a commander of a thousand. Tell me your story." They said: "We are brothers, sons of a truthful man, and we were twelve, and our father loved one of our brothers, and he went with us into the wilderness and perished there, and he was the dearest of us to our father." He said: "Then to whom did your father turn after him?" They said: "To a brother of ours, younger than him." He said: "How can you tell me that your father is truthful, when he loves the youngest of you more than the eldest? Bring me this brother of yours, that I may look upon him. ﴿But if you do not bring him to me, there will be no measure for you with me, nor shall you draw near.﴾ They said: ﴿We will seek to deceive his father about him, and indeed we will do it.﴾" He said: "Then put one of you as a pledge until you return." So they put Simeon forward.

19465: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and they, to him, were unrecognizing﴾, he said: they did not know him.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: "And when he had furnished them with their provisions, he said: Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts?" (59)

Abu Ja'far said: He means: when Yusuf loaded for his brothers the provisions of food, filling the camel of each man among them, he said to them: "Bring me a brother of yours from your father," so that I may load for you another camel, and you will gain by it the load of another camel. "Do you not see that I give full measure" [[See the explanation of "al-Iyfa'" (giving full measure) earlier, vol. 15, p. 492, note 1, and the references there.

And the explanation of "al-Kayl" (measure), earlier, vol. 15, p. 446, note 1, and the references there.]] so I do not short-change anyone. "And I am the best of hosts": I am the best of those among the people in this land who have hosted a guest from themselves, so I will host you.

As related:

19466 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "And I am the best of hosts": Yusuf says it: "I am the best of those who host in Egypt."

19467 - Ibn Humayd related to me, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Yusuf provisioned those he provisioned from the people, he loaded for each man among them a camel equal to their number, then he said to them: "Bring me a brother of yours from your father," I will give you another camel, or as he said, "Do you not see that I give full measure," that is, I do not short-change people in anything, "and I am the best of hosts," that is, better for you than anyone else, for if you bring him, your standing will be honoured and I will treat you well, and you will gain a camel beyond your number, for I give each one of you only one camel. "But if you do not bring him to me, there will be no measure for you with me, nor shall you come near," that is, do not come near my land.

19468 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words "Bring me a brother of yours from your father," meaning Benjamin, who was the full brother of Yusuf.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 60:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But if you do not bring him to me, there will be no measure [of grain] for you from me, and do not come near me.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His exalted remembrance says, reporting the statement of Yusuf to his brothers: ﴿But if you do not bring him to me﴾, meaning your brother from your father, ﴿then there will be no measure [of grain] for you from me﴾, meaning: there will be no food from me for you to measure out to yourselves; ﴿and do not come near me﴾, meaning: do not approach my land.

And His saying, ﴿and do not come near me﴾ (wa la taqrabun), is in the place of a jussive in the prohibition, and the "nun" is in the place of a nasb (accusative), and it was given a kasra because the ya' of the first person was omitted; the sentence is: wa la taqrabūnī (and do not come near me).

The discussion of the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "We will seek to win him over from his father, and we will surely do it."﴾ (61) ﴿And he said to his servants, "Put their merchandise back into their saddlebags, so that they may recognize it when they return to their family; perhaps they will come back."﴾ (62)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the brothers of Joseph said to Joseph when he said to them: ﴿Bring me a brother of yours from your father﴾, ﴿"We will seek to win him over from his father"﴾, and we will ask him to let him go with us until we bring him to you. [[See the explanation of "al-murawada" (seeking to win over) in what has preceded, p. 138, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿"And we will surely do it"﴾. They mean by this: "We will surely do what we told you we would do, namely, seek to win our father over concerning our brother, and we will certainly strive, as".

1946 9- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿"And we will surely do it"﴾, meaning: "We will certainly strive."

* *

As for His words: ﴿"And he said to his servants (fityan)"﴾, God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Joseph said to his "servants (fityan)", who were his attendants. [[See the explanation of "al-fata" (young man, servant) in what has preceded, p. 94, note 1, and the references there.]] As:

1947 0- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿"And he said to his servants"﴾, that is: to his attendants.

* *

﴿"Put their merchandise into their saddlebags"﴾, means: "Put back the price of the food that you took from them [[See the explanation of "al-bida'a" (merchandise, capital) in what has preceded, pp. 4–7.]] ''into their saddlebags''."

And "al-rihal" is the plural of "rahl" (saddlebag, pack-saddle); that is the plural of abundance. As for the plural of few, it is "arhul," which is the plural for numbers between three and ten.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said in the sense of "al-bida'a" what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

1947 1- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿"Put their merchandise..."﴾, that is: their silver (awraq).* [["Al-awraq" is the plural of "waraq" (with fatha then kasra), and "warq" (with two fathas), which is silver, or all wealth whatever it may be.]]

1947 2- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then he commanded that their merchandise, with which he had given them what he gave them of food, be put into their saddlebags, and they did not know.

1947 3- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: He said to his servant (fityatihi), while he was measuring out for them: "Put their merchandise into their saddlebags, so that they may recognize it when they return to their family; perhaps they will come back" to me.

* *

If someone says: For what reason did Joseph command his servants to put his brothers' merchandise into their saddlebags?

It is said: That may have several possible reasons:

The first: that he feared they would not have money with their father, since the year was a year of drought and famine, so taking that from them would harm them, and he wished that they would return to him.

Or: he wanted his father and brothers to have ample means with it, despite [their] small need of him,* [[In the manuscript: "wa-arada," and the correct reading is "aw" as in the printed edition. What is between the parentheses is also not in the manuscript, so I added it as an inference, because the meaning needs it.]] so he returned it to them without them knowing the reason for its return, out of generosity and benevolence.

And the third, which is that he wanted by this to ensure that they would not break their promise to return, when they found in their saddlebags the price of food that they had received and that others had come to own over them, in exchange for his food,* [[In the printed edition: "in exchange for their food." This was done because the meaning of the statement was obscure to him. It is undoubtedly a statement whose meaning is obscure; its meaning is that this price has come to be owned by others, and that those who gave them this food, in exchange for the price, have taken possession of it.]] and they would feel uneasy about keeping the price of food they had received until they paid it back to its owner, which would be more likely to make them return to him.

The discussion of the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "We will seek to win him over from his father, and we will surely do it."﴾ (61) ﴿And he said to his servants, "Put their merchandise back into their saddlebags, so that they may recognize it when they return to their family; perhaps they will come back."﴾ (62)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the brothers of Joseph said to Joseph when he said to them: ﴿Bring me a brother of yours from your father﴾, ﴿"We will seek to win him over from his father"﴾, and we will ask him to let him go with us until we bring him to you. [[See the explanation of "al-murawada" (seeking to win over) in what has preceded, p. 138, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿"And we will surely do it"﴾. They mean by this: "We will surely do what we told you we would do, namely, seek to win our father over concerning our brother, and we will certainly strive, as".

1946 9- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿"And we will surely do it"﴾, meaning: "We will certainly strive."

* *

As for His words: ﴿"And he said to his servants (fityan)"﴾, God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Joseph said to his "servants (fityan)", who were his attendants. [[See the explanation of "al-fata" (young man, servant) in what has preceded, p. 94, note 1, and the references there.]] As:

1947 0- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿"And he said to his servants"﴾, that is: to his attendants.

* *

﴿"Put their merchandise into their saddlebags"﴾, means: "Put back the price of the food that you took from them [[See the explanation of "al-bida'a" (merchandise, capital) in what has preceded, pp. 4–7.]] ''into their saddlebags''."

And "al-rihal" is the plural of "rahl" (saddlebag, pack-saddle); that is the plural of abundance. As for the plural of few, it is "arhul," which is the plural for numbers between three and ten.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said in the sense of "al-bida'a" what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

1947 1- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿"Put their merchandise..."﴾, that is: their silver (awraq).* [["Al-awraq" is the plural of "waraq" (with fatha then kasra), and "warq" (with two fathas), which is silver, or all wealth whatever it may be.]]

1947 2- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then he commanded that their merchandise, with which he had given them what he gave them of food, be put into their saddlebags, and they did not know.

1947 3- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: He said to his servant (fityatihi), while he was measuring out for them: "Put their merchandise into their saddlebags, so that they may recognize it when they return to their family; perhaps they will come back" to me.

* *

If someone says: For what reason did Joseph command his servants to put his brothers' merchandise into their saddlebags?

It is said: That may have several possible reasons:

The first: that he feared they would not have money with their father, since the year was a year of drought and famine, so taking that from them would harm them, and he wished that they would return to him.

Or: he wanted his father and brothers to have ample means with it, despite [their] small need of him,* [[In the manuscript: "wa-arada," and the correct reading is "aw" as in the printed edition. What is between the parentheses is also not in the manuscript, so I added it as an inference, because the meaning needs it.]] so he returned it to them without them knowing the reason for its return, out of generosity and benevolence.

And the third, which is that he wanted by this to ensure that they would not break their promise to return, when they found in their saddlebags the price of food that they had received and that others had come to own over them, in exchange for his food,* [[In the printed edition: "in exchange for their food." This was done because the meaning of the statement was obscure to him. It is undoubtedly a statement whose meaning is obscure; its meaning is that this price has come to be owned by others, and that those who gave them this food, in exchange for the price, have taken possession of it.]] and they would feel uneasy about keeping the price of food they had received until they paid it back to its owner, which would be more likely to make them return to him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 63:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So when they returned to their father, they said, "O our father, the measure has been withheld from us, so send with us our brother that we may measure [provisions], and indeed we will be its guardians."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, the Exalted and Remembered, says: When the brothers of Yusuf returned to their father, ﴿they said, "O our father, the measure has been withheld from us, so send with us our brother that we may measure,"﴾ meaning: the measure has been withheld from us beyond the measure that was given to us, and each man among us was given only the measure of one camel. ﴿So send with us our brother﴾, Benjamin, that he may take the measure for himself, the measure of another camel in addition to the measure of our camels. ﴿And indeed we will be his guardians﴾, from any harm befalling him on his journey.

* *

And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said this:

19474- Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: 'Amr related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: "So when they returned to their father, they said: O our father, the king of Egypt has honored us with an honor such that if a man from the sons of Ya'qub had been (in his position), he would not have honored us with such honor. He has taken Shum'un as a pledge and said: Bring me your brother this one, whom your father has become attached to after your brother who perished. If you do not bring him to me, do not approach my lands." Ya'qub said: ﴿Shall I entrust him to you except as I entrusted you with his brother before? But Allah is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.﴾" He said: Ya'qub said to them: When you come to the king of Egypt, convey my greetings to him, and say: Indeed our father prays for you and supplicates for you with what you have bestowed upon us.

19475- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: They set out until they came to their father, and their dwelling place, as some of the people of knowledge of the Arabs have mentioned to me, was in al-'Arabat of the land of Palestine, in the Ghawr of Syria. Others say: at al-Awlaj, on the side of al-Sha'b, below Hisma. [[In the manuscript: "min Hisso", and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]] He was a man of the desert, possessing sheep and camels. They said: O our father, we came to the best of men; he lodged us and honored our lodging, he measured for us and gave us full measure and did not defraud us, and he has commanded us to bring him a brother of ours from our father. He said: If you do not do so, do not approach me nor enter my land. Ya'qub said to them: ﴿Shall I entrust him to you except as I entrusted you with his brother before? But Allah is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.﴾

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿nakTAL﴾ (nakhtal / nakti'l).

The majority of the readers of Medina, and some of the readers of Mecca and Kufa, recited it ﴿نَكْتَلْ﴾ with the nun (we), meaning: we and he will measure.

* *

The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it "yakhtal" with the ya' (he), meaning: he will measure for himself, just as we measure for ourselves.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations with the same meaning. Whichever of them a reader recites, he is correct. This is because they only informed their father that the measure had been withheld from them beyond the number of their heads, saying: ﴿O our father, the measure has been withheld from us,﴾ then they asked him to send their brother with them so that he might measure for himself. So if he measures for himself and they measure for themselves, then the "brother" has been included in their number. Therefore, whether the report is given in the first person singular of the speaker's own self or in the plural on behalf of all of them, it is the same, since the meaning of the speech and what is intended by it is understood.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 64:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Shall I trust you with him except as I trusted you with his brother before? But Allah is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ (12:64)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: Their father Ya'qub said: "Shall I trust you with your brother, your full brother, whom you ask me to send with you, except as I trusted you with his brother Yusuf before?" That is, from before this.

* *

The reciters differed over the reading of His words: ﴿fa-Allahu khayrun hafizan⁠﴾.

The majority of the reciters of Madina, and some of the Kufans and Basrans, read it: ﴿fa-Allahu khayrun hifzan﴾, meaning: and Allah is better in guarding (hifzan, a verbal noun) than you.

* *

And the majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the people of Makka read it: ﴿fa-Allahu khayrun hafizan﴾ with an alif, interpreting "hafiz" (guardian, the active participle) as an explanation of "khayr" (best), as one says: "He is better as a man (khayru rajulin)," and the meaning is: Allah is the best of you as a guardian, with the "kaf and mim" (the pronoun referring to you) having been omitted.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is that they are two well-known readings, close in meaning, and each of them has been recited by scholars of the Qur'an. So whichever of the two a reciter reads, he is correct. This is because whoever describes Allah as the best of them in guarding has described Him as the best of them as a guardian, and whoever describes Him as the best of them as a guardian has described Him as the best of them in guarding.

* *

= ﴿And He is the most merciful of the merciful﴾: he says: Allah is the most merciful of those who show mercy to His creation. He shows mercy to my weakness in my old age, and to my loneliness in losing my son, so He will not let him be lost, but will keep him safe until He returns him to me out of His mercy.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when they opened their belongings, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what more could we want? This is our merchandise, returned to us. And we will bring provisions for our family, and guard our brother, and gain an extra camel-load. That is an easy measure."﴾ (12:65)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When the brothers of Joseph opened their belongings, which they had carried from Egypt from Joseph's place, ﴿they found their merchandise﴾, and that was the price of the food they had measured out from him, ﴿returned to them﴾. ﴿They said, "O our father, what more could we want? This is our merchandise, returned to us"﴾. This means that they said to their father: "What do we want? This is our merchandise, returned to us!" They said this to comfort him, because of what had been done for them in returning their merchandise to them. [[In the printed edition: "returned to him" (ردت إليه), but the correct reading is what has been established.]]

* *

When the sentence is understood in this sense, "mā" (what) is an interrogative in the accusative position, governed by the verb ﴿nabghī﴾ (we want).

* *

Qatadah also interpreted it this way.

19476. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿mā nabghī﴾: "It means: What more do we want beyond this? Our merchandise has been returned to us, and he has given us full measure."

* *

As for His words ﴿wa-namīru ahlanā﴾ (and we will bring provisions for our family), it means: we will seek food for our family and buy it for them.

* *

It is said from this root: "Māra fulānun ahlahu yamīruhum maīran" (so-and-so provided his family with food), and from it is the saying of the poet: [[I do not know who said it, and I did not find the verse in any source, although I think I recognize it.]]

*I sent you out to bring provisions, but you lingered for a year,*
*so when will your aid come to the one you aid?*

* *

﴿wa-naḥfaẓu akhānā﴾ (and guard our brother), whom you send with us. ﴿wa-nazdādu kayla baʿīr﴾ (and gain an extra camel-load): it means we will add to our loads of food the load of one camel, measured out for us, which is the load of another camel of ours. ﴿dhālika kaylun yasīr﴾ (That is an easy measure): it means that this is a small load. As reported:

19477. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, regarding ﴿wa-nazdādu kayla baʿīr﴾: He said: Each man among them had the load of one camel, and they said: "Send our brother with us, so that we gain the load of one camel." Ibn Juraij said: Mujahid said: "Kayla baʿīr" is the load of a donkey. He said: This is a dialectal usage. Al-Qasim said: Mujahid meant that "ḥimār" (donkey) is called "baʿīr" in some dialects.

19478. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿wa-nazdādu kayla baʿīr﴾: "It means: the load of a camel."

19479. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿wa-nazdādu kayla baʿīr﴾: "We would count one camel along with our camels," ﴿dhālika kaylun yasīr﴾.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "I will never send him with you until you give me a solemn covenant in God's name that you will surely bring him back to me, unless you are completely overcome." Then, when they gave him their solemn covenant, he said, "God is witness over what we say."﴾ (66)**

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: Ya'qub said to his sons, "I will not send your brother with you to the king of Egypt" ﴿until you give me a covenant (mawthiqan) from God﴾, meaning, until you give me a covenant from God. Al-mithaq (covenant) means what one is bound by, such as an oath or a pledge. [[See the explanation of "al-mithaq" above, 14:82, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿That you will surely bring him to me﴾ means you will surely bring me your brother. ﴿Unless you are encircled﴾ means unless all of you are overwhelmed by something that prevents you from bringing him to me. [[See the explanation of "al-ihatah" (encirclement) above, 15:462, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

What we have said on this matter is also what the people of ta'wil (interpretation) said.

Those who said so:

19480. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿When they gave him their covenant﴾, he said: "Their pledge."

19481. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Abdullah told us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

19482. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Shababah told us, saying: Warqa' told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his words: ﴿Unless you are encircled﴾: "Unless you all perish."

19483. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid—

19484. He said: And Ishaq told us, saying: Abdullah informed us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

19485. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿Unless you are encircled﴾, he said: "Unless you are overpowered to the point that you cannot bear it."

19486. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding his words: ﴿Unless you are encircled﴾: "Unless some matter befalls you that destroys you all, and that would be an excuse for you before me."

* *

As for His words, ﴿Then, when they gave him their covenant﴾, meaning, when they gave him their pledges, ﴿he said﴾, meaning Ya'qub: ﴿God is witness over what we say﴾, meaning over what you and I say. ﴿Is Guardian (wakil)﴾ means He is a witness over us, regarding the fulfilment of everything we say. [[See the explanation of "al-wakil" above, 15:220, note 3, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 67:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he said, "O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from various gates. And I cannot avail you against Allah in the least. Judgment is only for Allah. upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who rely [indeed] rely."﴾ (12:67)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, mentioned and exalted, says: Ya'qub said to his sons when they wished to leave him for Egypt to obtain food: "O my sons, do not enter Egypt by one road, but enter by various gates."

* *

It is related that he said this to them because they were men of beauty and bearing, [[In the printed edition: "wahybah" (awe), but in the manuscript it is "wahmah" (concern), undotted, and it will come again in the same way later; I will correct it without noting this correction in the other places.]] so he feared the evil eye for them if they entered together as a group by one road, and they were the sons of one man; so he commanded them to separate when entering it. As follows:

19487. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Yazid al-Wasiti related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿Do not enter from one gate, but enter from various gates﴾. He said: He feared the evil eye for them.

19488. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿O my sons, do not enter from one gate﴾: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) feared the evil eye for his sons, for they were of striking form and beauty.

19489. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And enter from various gates﴾. He said: They had been given form and beauty, so he feared for them the souls of people.

19490. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And he said, "O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from various gates"﴾. He said: Ya'qub, peace be upon him, feared the evil eye for them.

19491. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿Do not enter from one gate﴾: Ya'qub feared the evil eye for his children.

19492. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab related to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b: ﴿Do not enter from one gate﴾. He said: He feared the evil eye for them.

19493. ... He said: 'Amr related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: Ya'qub, peace be upon him, feared the evil eye for his sons, so he said: ﴿O my sons, do not enter from one gate﴾. It is said: These are the sons of one man! But enter from various gates.

19494. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When they resolved to depart — meaning the sons of Ya'qub — Ya'qub said: ﴿O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from various gates﴾. He feared for them the eyes of people, because of their appearance, and that they were the sons of one man.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And I cannot avail you against Allah in the least﴾, it means: I cannot repel from you any of the decree of Allah which He has decreed upon you, whether small or great, because His decree is executed upon His creation [see the explanation of "aghna" previously, 15:472, note 1, and the references there]. ﴿Judgment is only for Allah﴾, meaning: judgment and decision belong only to Allah, not to anything else; for He judges among His creation as He wills, His judgment is executed upon them, He decides concerning them, and His decree is not turned back. ﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾, meaning: upon Allah I have relied and trusted Him concerning you and concerning your protection by Him, until He returns you to me while you are safe and sound, not relying on your entering Egypt if you enter it by various gates. ﴿And upon Him let those who rely rely﴾, meaning: and to Allah let those who entrust their affairs entrust them [see the explanation of "tawakkul" previously, 15:545, note 1, and the references there].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 68:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they entered from where their father had commanded them, it did not avail them against Allah at all, but it was a need within the soul of Ya'qub, which he fulfilled. And indeed, he was one of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.﴾ (68)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: When the sons of Ya'qub entered ﴿from where their father had commanded them﴾, and that was their entering Egypt by separate gates, ﴿it did not avail them﴾ — their entering it in that manner — ﴿against them﴾ from the decree of Allah which He had decreed concerning them, and which He had made certain, ﴿at all, but it was a need within the soul of Ya'qub, which he fulfilled﴾. Rather, they fulfilled a wish of Ya'qub by entering not through one gate, out of fear of the evil eye upon them, so that his soul was at ease that they would not be struck by something from that quarter or that some harm would befall them because of it. As:

19495 — Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Shababa related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿but it was a need within the soul of Ya'qub, which he fulfilled﴾, fear of the evil eye upon his sons.

19496 — Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

19497 — ... He said: Ishaq informed us, saying: Abdullah related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

19498 — Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿but it was a need within the soul of Ya'qub, which he fulfilled﴾, he said: fear of the evil eye upon them.

19499 — Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning His saying: ﴿but it was a need within the soul of Ya'qub, which he fulfilled﴾, he said: what he feared for his sons from the eyes of people, because of their appearance and their number.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, he was one of knowledge because of what We had taught him﴾, He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And indeed Ya'qub was one of knowledge through Our teaching him.

* *

It has been said: its meaning is, "And indeed he was one of retention of what We had placed in his breast of knowledge."

* *

Reports differ from Qatada concerning this:

19500 — Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: ﴿And indeed, he was one of knowledge because of what We had taught him﴾: i.e., from what We had taught him.

19501 — Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatada: ﴿And indeed, he was one of knowledge because of what We had taught him﴾, he said: indeed he was one who acted upon what he knew.

19502 — ... He said: Al-Muthanna said: Ishaq said: Abdullah said: Sufyan said: ﴿Indeed he was one of knowledge﴾, from what We had taught him. And he said: One who does not act is not a person of knowledge.

* *

= As for His saying: ﴿but most of the people do not know﴾, He, may His praise be exalted, says: But most people, other than Ya'qub, do not know what he knew, because We withheld that from them, so they did not know it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 69:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When they entered upon Joseph, he drew his brother to himself and said, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not be distressed by what they used to do."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, says: When the sons of Ya'qub entered upon Joseph, ﴿he drew his brother to himself﴾, meaning: he took his brother, his full brother (from the same father and mother), to himself. [See the explanation of "al-iwa'" (taking in, sheltering) earlier, vol. 15, p. 422, note 1, and the references there.]

* *

His sheltering of him was as follows: [In the printed edition the text read: "and his brother by the same father was…", which misread the manuscript; the manuscript has "wa-kull iwawahu iyyahu" without dots, and this is the correct reading.] As:

19503 – Ibn Wakr' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿When they entered upon Joseph, he drew his brother to himself﴾: He recognised his brother, so he lodged them in a dwelling and provided them with food and drink. When night came, he brought them bedding and said, "Let each two brothers among you sleep on a mat." [The "mithal" (with a kasra on the m), plural "mithal" (with two dammas), is the bedding, a mattress; it is said in a hadith that he entered upon Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and in the house there were worn furnishings and a worn mithal, i.e., a worn-out mattress. It is also said it is the striped covering spread out among the woollen coloured coverings.] When the youth was left alone, Joseph said, "This one will sleep with me on my bed." So he spent the night with him, and Joseph kept smelling his scent and embracing him until morning. Rubil began to say, "We have never seen anything like this! Get him away from us!"

19504 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When they entered upon Joseph – meaning the sons of Ya'qub – they said, "This is our brother whom you ordered us to bring you; we have brought him to you." It was mentioned to me that he said to them, "You have done well and you have been right, and you will find that (treatment) with me," or as he said. Then he said, "I see you are men, and I wished to honour you." He called [the steward of] his hospitality [in the printed edition, "da'a dafatahu", which I find has no sense; in the manuscript as I have recorded it, but it is not correct without what I have added between the brackets], and said: "Lodge each two men separately, then honour them and treat them well." Then he said, "I see that this man you have brought has no second with him, so I will take him to myself, and his lodging will be with me." So he lodged them two by two in separate dwellings, and lodged his brother with himself, and took him to himself. When he was alone with him, he said, "Indeed, I am your brother; I am Joseph, so do not be distressed by anything they did to us in the past, for God has been good to us. Do not inform them of anything I have told you." God says: ﴿When they entered upon Joseph, he drew his brother to himself and said, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not be distressed by what they used to do."﴾

19505 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿When they entered upon Joseph, God drew his brother to himself﴾: he embraced him, lodged him, and he was Binyamin.

19506 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil narrated to me, saying: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say – when he was asked about the saying of Joseph: ﴿When they entered upon Joseph, God drew his brother to himself and said, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not be distressed by what they used to do."﴾ – how did he respond when he took him by the drinking-cup, when his brother had told him [that he was his brother], and you claim that he remained disguised toward them, plotting against them until they returned? And the origin of "al-za'im" in the speech of the Arabs: the one who stands in charge of the affairs of a people; likewise "al-kafil" and "al-hamil." And the origin of "al-za'im" in the speech of the Arabs: the one who stands in charge of the affairs of a people; likewise "al-kafil" and "al-hamil." Therefore it was said: the leader of a people is their za'im and their manager. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 73:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "By God, you know well that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and we were not thieves."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, means: The brothers of Joseph said, ﴿By God (tallah)﴾, meaning: "by God" (wallah).

* *

This "ta" in ﴿tallah﴾ is only a "waw" that was changed into a "ta," as was done in "al-tawrah" (the Torah), which derives from "warrayt" (I concealed). Likewise "al-turath" (inheritance), which derives from "warithta" (you inherited), and "al-tukhamah" (indigestion), which derives from "al-wakhamah" (heaviness). In all of these the "waw" was changed into "ta." The "waw" in all these letters belongs to nouns, but it is not so in ﴿tallah﴾, because it is only the "waw" of the oath, and it was made a "ta" because of how often it ran on the tongues of the Arabs in their oaths, in their saying "wallah." So this word was singled out by being changed into a "ta." Whoever says this about the Name of God says "tallah." One does not say "talrahman" or "talrahim," nor with any of God's other names, nor with anything else one swears by; this is said only with "tallah" alone.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed you know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land﴾, it means: You certainly know that we did not come to disobey God in your land. [[See the explanation of "corruption in the land" in the previous lexical indices (fasad).]]

* *

This is also what a group of the people of interpretation said.

Mention of those who said this:

19555- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding His saying, ﴿They said, "By God, you know well that we did not come to cause corruption in the land,"﴾ he said: We did not come to disobey in the land.

* *

If someone says: What was the knowledge of those to whom it was said, ﴿Indeed you know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land﴾, that they had not come for that, such that those who said it felt free to say it?

It is said: They felt free to say it because, as is mentioned, they had returned the merchandise they had found in their saddlebags, so they said: If we were thieves, we would not have returned to you the merchandise we found in our saddlebags.

It is also said: They had become known on their journey and travel for not wronging anyone and not taking what was not theirs, so they said this when it was said to them: ﴿Indeed you are thieves.﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 74–75:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "What is the recompense for it, if you are liars?" (74) They said, "Its recompense is: whoever is found in his saddlebag, then he himself is its recompense. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers."﴾ (75)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His mention, exalted is His remembrance, says: The companions of Yusuf said to his brothers: "What is the reward for theft (al-saraq) if you are liars in your claim ﴿that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and we were not thieves﴾?" ﴿They said: "Its recompense is: whoever is found in his saddlebag, then he himself is its recompense."﴾ His exalted praise says: The brothers of Yusuf said: The reward for theft is that whoever has the stolen item found among his belongings, ﴿then he himself is its recompense﴾. He means: the one in whose saddlebag that is found, his reward is to be handed over to the person he stole from, so that he is enslaved to him. ﴿Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ means: thus do We deal with whoever commits wrong, doing what is not permissible for him, by taking another's property through theft.

* *

The exegetes said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

19556 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿then he himself is its recompense﴾, that is: he is handed over by it. ﴿Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾, that is: thus do we act toward whoever steals from us.

19557 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: It reached us regarding His saying: ﴿They said, "What is the recompense for it, if you are liars?"﴾ They informed Yusuf of what was ruled in their land: that whoever steals is taken as a slave. So they said: ﴿Its recompense is: whoever is found in his saddlebag, then he himself is its recompense.﴾

19558 – Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Amr related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿They said, "What is the recompense for it, if you are liars?" They said, "Its recompense is: whoever is found in his saddlebag, then he himself is its recompense."﴾ You take him, and he is yours.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: They said: the reward for theft, the one found with the stolen item in his saddlebag, is as if it were said: its reward is the enslavement of the one found in his saddlebag, and then "enslavement" was omitted, since its meaning was known. Then the speech begins anew, saying: ﴿he himself is its recompense; thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾.

* *

It may also bear another interpretation: that its meaning is: They said: the reward for theft, the one in whose saddlebag the theft is found, the thief is its recompense. In that case the first "its recompense" (jaza'uhu) would be nominative by the predicate clause following it, and it would be nominative by the pronoun referring back to it in "huwa" (he), with "huwa" being the one that raises the second "jaza'uhu" (its recompense). [In the printed edition: "rafi'" (raising); I have kept what is in the manuscript. This second interpretation is repeated twice in the manuscript.]

* *

A third interpretation is possible: that "man" (whoever) is the conditional particle (jaza'iyyah), and is nominative by the pronoun referring back to it in the "ha'" in "rahlihi" (his saddlebag), and the first "al-jaza'" (recompense) is nominative by the pronoun referring back to it in "wujida" (was found), and the "fa'" (then) in "fahuwa" is the response of the conditional. The second "al-jaza'" is nominative by "huwa." The meaning of the speech then becomes: They said: the recompense for theft is that whoever is found to have stolen in his saddlebag, then he himself is its reward, he is enslaved and held in bondage. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an on the interpretation of this verse, for he mentioned these interpretations in wording other than this.]]

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿So he began with their bags before his brother's bag, then he brought it out from his brother's bag. Thus did We plan for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother under the king's law, unless God willed. We raise by degrees whom We will, and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows.﴾ (12:76)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Joseph searched their bags and their saddlebags, seeking by this the king's drinking-cup. He began his search with the bags of his brothers from their father, going through them one bag after another, before the bag of his brother from both father and mother. He delayed searching it, then searched it last, and he brought out the cup from his brother's bag.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) said things in accordance with what we have said. Those who said this:

19559. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿So he began with their bags before his brother's bag﴾. It was mentioned to us that whenever he searched a bag he would seek God's forgiveness, out of guilt at what he had accused them of, until only his brother remained. He was the youngest of the people. He said: "I do not think this one has taken anything!" They said: "Yes, so search him!" [["Bala" (yes): consider its use in a context other than answering a negation, as explained earlier in the note on no. 16987, and the references there. His words "istabrihi" (search him) come from "al-istibra'" (seeking to clear something). The hamza was softened; its original form is "wa-istabri'hu." "Al-istibra'" means seeking to be cleared of something, whether it was suspicion, a defect, or a blemish.] Surely they knew where they had placed their drinking-vessel. ﴿Then he brought it out from his brother's bag﴾.

19560. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: ﴿Then he brought it out from his brother's bag﴾. He said: Every time he opened a bundle he sought forgiveness, repenting of what he had done, until he reached the youth's bundle. He said: "I do not think this one has taken anything!" They said: "Yes, so search him!"

19561. Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: ﴿So he began with their bags before his brother's bag﴾. When only the youth's saddlebag remained, he said: "This youth could not have taken it!" They said: "By God, he will not be left until you search his saddlebag, so we may go away with your mind at ease." He put his hand in and brought it out of his saddlebag. [[In the printed edition: "fa-astakhrajaha" (then he brought it out), and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

19562. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When the messenger said to them: ﴿And for whoever brings it, a camel's load, and I guarantee it﴾, they said: "We do not know him among us, nor with us." He said: "You shall not depart until I search your goods, and I will excuse you in seeking it from you!" He began with their bags, one bag after another, searching them and looking at what was in them, until he passed to his brother's bag and searched it, and he brought it out from it. He seized him by the neck and went back with him to Joseph. God says: ﴿Thus did We plan for Joseph﴾.

19563. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It was mentioned to us that whenever he searched the goods of one of them, he sought forgiveness from his Lord, out of guilt, though he knew exactly where the one he sought was! Until only his brother remained, and he knew that his target was in him. He said: "I do not think this youth took it, and I do not mind not searching his goods!" His brothers said: "It would be better for your mind and ours that you search his goods too." When he opened his goods, he brought out his target from it. God said: ﴿Thus did We plan for Joseph﴾.

* *

The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya) differed regarding the pronoun "ha'" and the "alif" in His words: ﴿Then he brought it out from his brother's bag﴾.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: they refer to "al-sawa'" (the drinking-cup). He used the feminine form, and God had said ﴿for whoever brings it, a camel's load﴾, because he meant "al-sawa'". He said: "al-Sawa'" is masculine, but some make "al-sawa'" feminine, and here "al-saqaya" (the drinking-vessel) is meant, which is feminine. He said: They are two names for one thing, like "al-thawb" (garment) and "al-mihlafa" (wrapper), masculine and feminine for one thing.

* *

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said regarding His words: ﴿Then he brought it out from his brother's bag﴾: he intended the feminine of "al-sariqa" (the theft). He said: And if "al-sawa'" carries the meaning of "al-sa'" [[In the printed edition: "wa-in lam yakun al-sawa'" (and if the cup were not), adding "lam", which corrupts the sentence. He meant that "al-sa'" is both masculine and feminine, and for this reason "al-sawa'" was made feminine.] then this feminine form may come from that. He said: And if you wish, you may make it for the feminine of "al-saqaya." He said: "Al-sawa'" is masculine, and "al-sa'" is feminine and masculine. Whoever makes it feminine says "thalath asu'" (three sa's), like "thalath adur" (three circles), and whoever makes it masculine says "asw'a" like "abwab" (doors).

* *

Another of them said: "Al-sawa'" was made feminine when it was made feminine because "al-saqaya" was intended by it, and it was made masculine when it was made masculine, because "al-sawa'" was intended by it. He said: This is like "al-khiwan" and "al-ma'ida" (table), and "sinan al-rumh" (the spearhead) and "'aliyatuhu" (its upper part), and what resembles that among things in which two names are combined: one masculine and the other feminine.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Thus did We plan for Joseph﴾, He says: Thus did We act for Joseph, [[See the explanation of "al-kayd" (scheming) earlier, p. 141, note 1, and the references there.] so that he might take his brother from his full brothers, with their acknowledgement that he had the right to take him from them and hold him in his hands, and to keep him from them. That is because, when it was said to them: "What is the penalty for it, if you are liars?" they said: "The penalty for one who stole the cup is that whoever is found with it in his saddlebag is himself held in bondage for it." That was their ruling in their law. So God planned for Joseph, as He described to us, until he took his brother from them, and he remained with him under their judgement and God's arrangement for him.

* *

As for His words: ﴿He could not have taken his brother under the king's law﴾, He says: Joseph could not have taken his brother under the rule of the king of Egypt, his judgement, and the obedience owed to him by them, because it was not part of that king's judgement and decree that anyone be enslaved for theft. So it was not possible for Joseph to take his brother under the ruler of his land, unless God willed, by the scheme He devised for him, until those among his brothers and companions in whose bag the cup was found yielded to their own judgement against him, and their hearts were content to surrender.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an said things in accordance with what we have said. Those who said this:

19565. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.
