19567. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿He could not have taken his brother under the king's law, unless God willed﴾. He said: Except a stratagem God devised, by which Joseph made an excuse. Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿Thus did We plan for Joseph﴾. He said: "We acted."

19568. Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿Thus did We plan for Joseph﴾. He says: We acted for Joseph.

19569. It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Thus did We plan for Joseph﴾: He says: We acted for Joseph.

* *

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿He could not have taken his brother under the king's law﴾.

Some of them said: It means: he could not have taken his brother under the king's authority.

Those who said this:

19570. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿He could not have taken his brother under the king's law﴾, he says: under the king's authority.

19571. It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿He could not have taken his brother under the king's law﴾, he says: under the king's authority.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: under his judgement and decree.

Those who said this:

19572. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿He could not have taken his brother under the king's law unless God willed﴾, he says: it was not in the king's judgement that a man be enslaved for theft.

19573. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿under the king's law﴾. He said: That was not in the king's law. He said: his judgement.

19574. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih Muhammad ibn Layth al-Marwazi narrated to us, from a man whom he named, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Abu Mawdud al-Madini, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: ﴿They said: "The penalty is that whoever is found in his saddlebag, he himself is the penalty"﴾ = ﴿Thus did We plan for Joseph; he could not have taken his brother under the king's law﴾. He said: The king's law does not seize one who has stolen in principle, but God planned for his brother, until they spoke what they spoke, and He took them by their words, and that was not in the king's judgement. [[Report 19574: "Muhammad ibn Layth al-Marwazi", "Abu Salih": I have found no biography of him in any of the sources before me. "Abu Mawdud al-Madini" is "Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Sulayman al-Hudhali," who was a storyteller (qass) for the people of Medina. He was a man of devotion and virtue, and he was a speaker who admonished. He saw Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and other Companions. He is trustworthy (thiqa), and is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim, 2/2/384.]]

19575. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, who said: It reached him regarding His words: ﴿He could not have taken his brother under the king's law﴾: he said: the king's ruling was that whoever stole would be made to pay double the penalty.

19576. Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿He could not have taken his brother under the king's law﴾, he says: under the king's judgement.

19577. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿He could not have taken his brother under the king's law﴾: that is, by injustice, but God planned for Joseph so that he might keep his brother with him.

19578. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿He could not have taken his brother under the king's law﴾: he said: It is not in the king's law that a thief be taken for his theft. He said: The judgement among the prophets, Jacob and his sons, was that a thief be taken for his theft as a slave held in bondage.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Although the wording of those who said these things differs regarding the meaning of "the king's law" (din al-malik), their meanings are close, because whoever takes him under the king's authority deals with him according to his action, and so he takes him with his consent, not otherwise. [[In the printed edition: "fa-yurinahu akhdhahu idha lam yughayyirhu" (so it shows us his taking when he did not change it), which is a corrupted sentence with no meaning. In the manuscript some of it is unpointed, and its correct reading, God willing, is what I have given. The copyist erred in writing, because he did not read well from the original from which he copied, so he made "bi-ridahu" into "fa-yurinahu," and made "la" into "lam." As for "bi-ghayrihi" it is unpointed in the manuscript.] That is a ruling by him upon him, and his ruling upon him is his judgement.

* *

The root of "al-din" (law, religion, in this sense "obedience") is obedience. I have explained this in other places, with its evidence, sufficient so that it need not be repeated here. [[See the explanation of "al-din" earlier, 3:571 / 6:273, 274, and other places in the indices of language, under (d-y-n).]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿unless God willed﴾, as follows:

19579. Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿unless God willed﴾, but We acted for him, in that they said: ﴿The penalty is that whoever is found in it, he himself is the penalty﴾.

19580. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿unless God willed﴾: except by a pretext God devised, by which Joseph made an excuse.

* *

As for His words: ﴿We raise by degrees whom We will﴾, the readers differed in their recitation of it.

Some of them recited it: "naraf'u darajati man nasha'" with "al-darajat" annexed to "man" (whom), meaning: We raise the ranks of whom We will, raising his stations and his degrees in this world through knowledge over others, as We raised Joseph's rank and station in this world above the stations and ranks of his brothers. [[See the explanation of "al-daraja" (degree) earlier, 14:173, note 6, and the references there.]]

* *

Others recited it: ﴿naraf'u darajatin man nasha'﴾, with tanwin on "darajat," meaning: We raise whom We will to ranks and degrees in knowledge above others, as We raised Joseph. So "man" in this reading is in the accusative, and in the first reading it is in the genitive. We explained this in "Surat al-An'am." [[See what has passed, 11:505.]]

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an said things in accordance with what we have said. Those who said this:

19581. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said regarding His words: ﴿We raise by degrees whom We will﴾: Joseph and his brothers were given knowledge, so We raised Joseph above them in knowledge.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Above every scholar is one who is more knowing than him, until that ends with God. He meant by this that Joseph was more knowing than his brothers, and above Joseph is one more knowing than Joseph, until that ends with God.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an said things in accordance with what we have said. Those who said this:

19582. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Amir al-Aqadi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abd al-A'la al-Tha'labi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that he narrated a story, and a man present said: ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "What an evil thing you said! Indeed God is the All-Knowing, and He is above every scholar."

19583. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us = and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us = from Sufyan, from Abd al-A'la, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas narrated a story, and a man present said: "Praise be to God, ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾!" Ibn Abbas said: "The Scholar is God, and He is above every scholar."

19584. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abd al-A'la, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: We were with Ibn Abbas, and he narrated a story, and a man was astonished and said: "Praise be to God, ﴿over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾!" Ibn Abbas said: "What an evil thing you said! God is the All-Knowing, and He is above every scholar."

19585. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Israil informed us, from Salim, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾. He said: One is more knowing than this one, and this one is more knowing than this one, and God is above every scholar.

19586. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas informed us, from Abd al-A'la, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾. He said: God is the All-Aware, the All-Knowing, above every scholar.

19587. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: Israil informed us, from Abd al-A'la, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾. He said: God is above every scholar.

19588. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us = and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us = from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: A man asked Ali about a question, and he answered it. The man said: "It is not so, but rather such and such." Ali said: "You are right and you are wrong, ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾."

19589. Yaqub and Ibn Wakī' narrated to me, both saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Khalid, from Ikrima regarding His words: ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾. He said: The knowledge of God is above everyone.

19590. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Nadr, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾. He said: God, Mighty and Majestic.

19591. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ya'la ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abd al-A'la, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾. He said: God is more knowing than everyone.

19592. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ibn Shubrumah, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾. He said: No scholar is there except that above him is a scholar, until knowledge ends with God.

19593. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Asim narrated to us, saying: Juwayriya narrated to us, from Bashir al-Hujaymi, who said: I heard al-Hasan recite this verse one day: ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾, then he paused and said: "By God, no scholar has passed away upon the face of the earth without there being above him one more knowing than him, until knowledge returns to the One who taught it."

19594. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ali narrated to us, from Jarir, from Ibn Shubrumah, from al-Hasan: ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾. He said: Above every scholar is a scholar, until knowledge ends with God.

19595. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾, until knowledge ends with God, from Whom it began, and from Whom scholars learned, and to Whom it returns. In the recitation of Abdullah: "wa-fawqa kulli 'alimin 'alim" (and over every scholar is one who knows).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says to us: How was it permissible for Yusuf to put the drinking-cup in his brother's baggage, and then accuse innocent people of theft [[ "يسرق" meaning he attributes them to theft; "سرقة يسرقه" (with the letter ra' doubled) means he attributed that to him.]] and say: ﴿O caravan, you are surely thieves﴾?

It is said: His saying ﴿O caravan, you are surely thieves﴾ is only a report from God about a caller who called out with it, not a report about Yusuf. It is possible that the caller made this call when he lost the cup, without knowing what Yusuf had done. It is also possible that the caller made this call on Yusuf's command, and that he permitted the order to call out this accusation, because he knew that they had committed theft on some previous occasion; so he ordered the caller to address them by describing them as thieves, while Yusuf meant that theft, not that they had stolen the cup. Some scholars of interpretation have said that this was a mistake on Yusuf's part, and God punished him by the brothers' response to him: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his has stolen before﴾, and we have already mentioned the reports on this earlier. [[See what has passed, nos. 19559 - 19563, for he would seek forgiveness every time he searched one of their containers, out of remorse for what he had done. Abu Ja'far meant that Yusuf knew he was mistaken in his action. As for the brothers' reply to him, no mention of it has passed earlier.]]

**The commentary on His words, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "If he steals, a brother of his stole before him." So Joseph kept it hidden within himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, "You are in a worse position, and Allah knows best what you allege."﴾ (12:77)**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿They said, "If he steals, a brother of his stole before him,"﴾ meaning his brother from his father and mother, who is Joseph. As evidence:

19596. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Shababa related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his stole before him,﴾ that it refers to Joseph.

19597. Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

19598. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah related to us, from Warqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his stole before him,﴾ he said: It means Joseph.

19599. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿Then a brother of his stole before him,﴾ he said: Joseph.

* *

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have differed concerning the "theft" with which they accused Joseph.

Some of them said: It was an idol belonging to his maternal grandfather, which he broke and threw onto the road.

Those who said this:

19600. Ahmad ibn Amr al-Basri related to us, saying: Al-Fayd ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Mis'ar related to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his stole before him,﴾ he said: Joseph stole an idol belonging to his maternal grandfather, broke it, and threw it on the road, so his brothers used to reproach him for that. [[The report: 19600 "Ahmad ibn Amr al-Basri," a teacher of al-Tabari, has already passed as no. 9875 and 13928, and the discussion about him is at the first number. Al-Fayd ibn al-Fadl al-Bajali al-Kufi is biographed in al-Kabir 4/1/140 and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/88, and neither mentions any criticism of him. In the printed edition it read "al-Ays," which is a mistake, because the manuscript is clear there as I have written it. This report was also related by Abu Ja'far in his History 1:182.]]

19601. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿Then a brother of his stole before him,﴾ it was mentioned that he stole an idol belonging to his maternal grandfather, so they reproached him for it.

19602. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his stole before him,﴾ they intended by that to disparage the Prophet of Allah, Joseph. The theft for which they blamed him was an idol belonging to his maternal grandfather, which he took. The Prophet of Allah had intended by it only good, but they found fault with him.

19603. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his stole before him,﴾ he said: Joseph's mother had ordered Joseph to steal an idol belonging to her brother, which he worshipped, and she was a Muslim.

* *

Others said regarding this:

19604. Abu Kurayb related it to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: I heard my father say: The sons of Ya'qub were eating a meal when Joseph saw a bone (irq) and hid it. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "Joseph was compelled to a bone," which is pure error; the copyist joined "idh" (when) to the word after it, "nazara" (saw). "Irq" (with fatha and sukun) is a bone with meat on it; if there is no meat on it, it is "irah" (with damma on the ayn).]] So they reproached him for that: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his stole before him.﴾ [[The report: 19604. Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:182, at length.]]

* *

Others said regarding this:

19605. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid Abu al-Hajjaj, who said: The first trial that befell Joseph, as it reached me, was that his paternal aunt, the daughter of Ishaq, who was the eldest child of Ishaq, had Ishaq's girdle (mintaqa) with her, and they used to inherit it by seniority. Whoever among them had it in his keeping [[In the printed edition: "Whoever among them was singled out with it," differing from the manuscript, which spoils the sense and drops it. The correct reading, from the manuscript and the History, is "ikhtanaha," meaning he stole it.]] had it as a captive (salam) not to be contested, to do with it as he wished. When Ya'qub had a son, Joseph, he had handed him to his paternal aunt to nurse him, [[In the printed edition: "had nursed him his aunt," and I have affirmed what is in the History. As for the manuscript, it is unpointed. His words "hadanahu 'ammatuhu" here is a verb with two objects, and this transitive usage is not among those mentioned by the lexicographers. The lexicons mention "hadanat al-mar'a al-sabiyy" when a woman takes charge of a child to guard and raise him, and she is the "hadina," who gathers the child to herself and cares for him. This form with two objects is sound and ancient in the analysis of Arabic, meaning: she gave him to her to nurse. This is among what may be added to them, if Allah wills.]] so he was with her and in her charge, and no one loved anything as much as she loved him. Until he grew up and reached several years, and Ya'qub's heart became attached to him [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "waqa'at" without a waw, and the correct reading is with it, as in al-Tabari's History. His words "waqa'at nafsuhu 'alayhi" mean he longed for him intensely. This is a figurative usage not recorded in the lexicons, and it is extremely fine and precise in expressing the state of the soul; see after his words, "I cannot bear that he be absent from me for an hour," which is evidence for the meaning I have deduced.]] he came to her and said: O sister, hand Joseph over to me, for by Allah I cannot bear to be without him for an hour! She said: By Allah, I will not leave him. [[In the printed edition: "She said: By Allah ..." differing from the manuscript, and this also agrees with al-Tabari's History.]] By Allah, I cannot bear that he be absent from me for an hour! [[Her words "By Allah, I cannot bear..." are not in al-Tabari's History; they are an addition in the manuscript.]] He said: By Allah, I will not leave him! She said: Then leave him with me for some days; I will look at him and be consoled about him, perhaps that will console me for him, or as she said. When Ya'qub left her, she set about Ishaq's girdle and tied it under Joseph's clothes, then said: Ishaq's girdle is missing; look for who took it and who has it. It was searched for, and then she said: Search the people of the house! [[In the printed edition: "uksyfu," and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript and the History.]] They searched them and found it with Joseph. She said: By Allah, he is my captive (salam), and I will do with him as I wish. He said: Ya'qub came to her and she told him the news, and he said to her: You and that, if he did that, he is your captive; I can do nothing else. So she kept him, and he could not be freed until she died. He said: That is what Joseph's brothers meant when he did to his brother what he did when he took him: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his stole before him.﴾ [[The report: 19605. Up to this point, Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:170.]]

= Ibn Humayd said. Ibn Ishaq said: When the sons of Ya'qub saw what Joseph's brothers had done, and had no doubt that he had stole, they said, out of grief for him, since it had entered into their souls, reproaching him: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his stole before him.﴾ When Joseph heard it, he said, ﴿You are in a worse position,﴾ secretly within himself, ﴿and he did not reveal it to them,﴾ = ﴿and Allah knows best what you allege.﴾ [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "asafan 'alayhim" (out of grief over them), which hardly makes sense. The manuscript also had "fi anfusina" (within ourselves), which the printed edition corrected to "fi anfusihim," and it is correct.]]

* *

His words: ﴿So Joseph kept it hidden within himself and did not reveal it to them, [he] said, "You are in a worse position, and Allah knows best what you allege,"﴾ by His words ﴿kept it hidden,﴾ he meant: he concealed it. [[See the explanation of "al-israr" (secrecy) earlier, p. 7, note, and the references there.]]

* *

He said ﴿kept it hidden﴾ in the feminine, because he meant by it "the word," which is: ﴿You are in a worse position, and Allah knows best what you allege.﴾ It would have been permissible had it come in the masculine, as it was said: ﴿That is among the tidings of the unseen﴾ [Surah Hud 11:49] and ﴿That is among the tidings of the towns﴾ [Surah Hud 11:100].

* *

He referred to "the word" pronominally, though no antecedent had been mentioned before it. The Arabs often do this when the intended meaning is understood by those who hear the speech. This is like the saying of Hatim al-Ta'i:

"O Ma'wiyya, wealth does not benefit a man when the death-rattle comes upon him one day and his chest is constricted."
[[From his Diwan, p. 39, and elsewhere, from his well-known ode, and after it he says, which is among the finest poetry: "When those I love lower me into a grave with smooth sides, its walls dusty; and they depart hastily, shaking their palms, saying: The digging has wounded our fingertips!" "Mal'uda" means a grave dug with a niche (lahd). "Zalkh" means smooth; whoever stands on it slips and falls down into it.]] He means: when the chest is constricted with the soul, so he referred to the soul pronominally without mentioning it, since in his words "when it rattles one day" there is an indication to the hearer of his speech of what he meant by "and it constricts it." Similarly is the word of Allah: ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they were tried, then strove and endured, indeed your Lord, after it, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:110], where He said "after it," though no feminine noun had been mentioned before.

* *

The people of ta'wil said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

19606. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿So Joseph kept it hidden within himself and did not reveal it to them,﴾ as for what he kept hidden within himself, it is his words: ﴿You are in a worse position, and Allah knows best what you allege.﴾

19607. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿So Joseph kept it hidden within himself and did not reveal it to them, he said, "You are in a worse position, and Allah knows best what you allege,"﴾ he said this statement.

19608. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿So Joseph kept it hidden within himself and did not reveal it to them,﴾ he said: He kept hidden within himself His words: ﴿You are in a worse position, and Allah knows best what you allege.﴾

* *

As for His words: ﴿and Allah knows best what you allege,﴾ it means: Allah knows best what you lie about in what you attribute to his brother Benjamin. [[See the explanation of "al-wasf" (description) earlier: 15:586, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

The people of ta'wil said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

19609. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Shababa related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿You are in a worse position, and Allah knows best what you allege,﴾ they say: Joseph said it.

19610. Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

19611. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Abdullah related to us, from Warqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

19612. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿and Allah knows best what you allege,﴾ that is: what you lie about.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech, then, is: ﴿So Joseph kept it hidden within himself and did not reveal it to them,﴾ he said: You are in a worse position with Allah than the one you describe as having stolen, and more wicked in place, because of your previous deeds; and Allah knows your lying, even though many of those present among the people are ignorant of it.

* *

It is mentioned that when the cup was found in the baggage of Joseph's brother, the people blamed one another, as:

19613. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Amr related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: When the theft was brought out from the lad's baggage, they were struck dumb, and said: O sons of Rachel, you never cease to bring us trouble! When did this cup get taken? [[In the printed edition: "hatta akhadhta" (until you took), and the correct reading is from the manuscript and the History.]] Benjamin said: Rather, the sons of Rachel, from whom trouble never ceases for you! You took my brother and destroyed him in the wilderness! This cup was placed in my baggage by the one who placed the silver coins in your baggage! They said: Do not mention the silver coins, or we will be taken for them! When they entered upon Joseph, he called for the cup and tapped it, then brought it to his ear, and said: This cup of mine tells me that you were twelve men, and that you went off with a brother of yours and sold him. When Benjamin heard it, he stood and prostrated to Joseph, then said: O King, ask this cup of yours about my brother: is he alive? [[In the History: "where is he," but in the manuscript: "is he alive."]] He tapped it and said: He is alive, and you will see him. Benjamin said: Then do with me what you will, for if he knows of me, he will rescue me. Joseph went in and wept, then performed ablution, then came out. Benjamin said: O King, I want you to strike this cup of yours, and it will tell you the truth; ask it who stole it and put it in my baggage. He tapped it and said: This cup of mine is angry, and it says: How do you ask me about my companion, when you have seen with whom you were? [[In the printed edition alone: "ruwiyat" (you were seen).]] He said: When the sons of Ya'qub became angry, no one could withstand them. Rubil became angry and said: O King, by Allah, either you release us or I will cry out a cry such that no pregnant woman in Egypt will fail to miscarry what is in her womb! Every hair on Rubil's body stood up and came out of his clothes. Joseph said to his son: Stand by Rubil's side and touch him. Whenever one of the sons of Ya'qub became angry, the other would touch him and his anger would leave; so the lad went to his side and touched him, and his anger left. Rubil said: Who is this? Surely in this land there is a seed of Ya'qub's offspring! [[Al-bazr (with fatha and sukun) means offspring; one says "ma akthara bazrahu," meaning how numerous his offspring are.]] Joseph said: Of Ya'qub? Rubil became angry and said: O King, do not mention Ya'qub, for he is the Chosen One of Allah (sariyy Allah), [[In the History: "Israil Allah." What is in the commentary seems to be correct, because "iyl" means "God," and "isra" is joined to it; "isra" seems to mean "sara" (chosen), meaning the one who was chosen by Allah. There is much disagreement about the explanation of this.]] son of the one who was sacrificed to Allah, son of the Friend of Allah. Joseph said: [[In the printed edition, "in" is omitted from his words: "in kunta sadiqan" (if you are truthful).]] Then you are truthful, if you were truthful. [[The report: 19613. Abu Ja'far related it at length in his History 1:182, 183.]]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 12, verse 78:

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿They said, "O chief of authority, indeed he has a father, an elderly man, so take one of us in place of him. Indeed, we see you are of the doers of good."﴾ (78)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, the Exalted, says: The brothers of Yusuf said to Yusuf: ﴿O chief of authority﴾, meaning, O king [[See the explanation of "al-'Aziz" earlier, p. 62, note 5, and the references there.]] ﴿Indeed, he has a father, an elderly man﴾, weak with age, [and] attached to his love, meaning Ya'qub. ﴿So take one of us in place of him﴾, meaning take one of us instead of Binyamin, and release him. ﴿Indeed, we see you are of the doers of good﴾, meaning: indeed, we see you are of the doers of good in your actions.

* *

And Muhammad ibn Ishaq said concerning this:

19614 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Indeed, we see you are of the doers of good﴾, meaning: we see that from you as goodness, if you do [it].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 79:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿He said, "We seek refuge in God that we should take anyone except him with whom we found our property; indeed we would then be wrongdoers."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said:

He, the Exalted, says: Yusuf said to his brothers, ﴿"Maʿādh Allāh"﴾ (I seek refuge in God).

* *

The Arabs do this with every verbal noun (maṣdar) that they place in the position of "yaf'alu" and "tafʿalu": they put it in the accusative, as in their saying, "ḥamdan lillāh, wa shukran lah" (praise be to God, and thanks to Him), meaning: I praise God and I thank Him.

* *

The Arabs say in this regard "maʿādha Allāh" and "maʿādhata Allāh," adding the feminine ending (hāʾ). Just as they say, "mā aḥsana maʿnāh hādhā al-kalām" (how fine its meaning is, this speech). And they say "ʿawdh Allāh," "ʿawdhat Allāh," and "ʿiyādh Allāh." They also say, "Allāhumma ʿāʾidhan bika" (O God, I seek refuge in You), as if it were said: "U'īdhu bika ʿāʾidhan" (I seek refuge in You, seeking refuge), or "ad'ūka ʿāʾidhan" (I call upon You, seeking refuge).

* *

= ﴿That we should take anyone except him with whom we found our property﴾: he says, I seek the protection of God from taking an innocent person for a guilty one. [[See the explanation of "ʿādha" above, p. 32, note 1, and the references there.]] As:

19615 – Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, who said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿He said, "We seek refuge in God that we should take anyone except him with whom we found our property; indeed we would then be wrongdoers."﴾ He says: If we took other than the one in whose possession we found our property, we would then be doing what is not ours to do, and oppressing the people.

19616 – Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, who said: ʿAmr narrated to us, from Asbāṭ, from al-Suddi: ﴿They said, "O chief of the land, indeed he has an aged father, so take one of us in his place; indeed we see you are among the good-doers." He said, "We seek refuge in God that we should take anyone except him with whom we found our property; indeed we would then be wrongdoers."﴾ He said: Yusuf said, "When you come to your father, convey my greetings to him and say to him: The king of Egypt prays that you will not die until you see your son Yusuf, until he knows that in the land of Egypt there are truthful men like him."

The Exposition of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 80:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So when they despaired of him, they withdrew to confer privately. The eldest of them said, "Did you not know that your father had taken an oath from you in the name of Allah, and before this you had failed in regard to Joseph? So I will never leave this land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me, and He is the best of judges."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: ﴿So when they despaired of him﴾, when they gave up hope that Joseph would be released from Benjamin and that he would take one of them in his place, and that he would grant them what they had asked of him in that regard.

* *

As for His words ﴿istay'asu﴾ (despaired), it is of the form "istaf'alu," from "ya'isa al-rajulu min kadha yay'asu" (the man despaired of such-and-such), as:

19617 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿So when they despaired of him﴾: they despaired of him, and saw his severity in his affair.

* *

As for His words ﴿khalasu najiyyan﴾ (they withdrew to confer privately), it means that some of them said to others, conferring in private, with no one else mixing with them.

* *

"Najiyy" (private conference) refers to the group of people conferring, and it is applied to both the singular and the plural, as one says "rajul 'adl" (a just man) and "rijal 'adl" (just men), and "qawm zawr" and "fitr" (deceitful people). It is a verbal noun from the speech of the speaker: "najawtu fulanan anjuhu najiyyan" (I conferred privately with so-and-so), made into an attribute and description. As evidence that it is as we have mentioned, the words of God, exalted is He, ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant (najiyyan)﴾ [Surah Maryam: 52], where it describes a single person, and in this place ﴿khalasu najiyyan﴾ where it describes a group. The plural of "najiyy" is "anjiyah," as Labid said:

"And I witnessed the anjiyah of al-Afaqah, high, my ankle and the companions of kings are witnesses..." [Diwan of Labid, qasidah 7, verse 7; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 315, from verses he says to his daughter Basrah, mentioning his long life, saying to her: "I have grown weary of life and its length, and of people's asking: How is Labid?" "And I sang for a long time before the course of Dahis..." "If the stubborn soul had immortality..." "And I witnessed..."]

"The course of Dahis" is the well-known account of Dahis and al-Ghabra' and their racing, on account of which the war between 'Abs and Dhubyan lasted forty years. His words "sabtan" mean an age (dahran).

"Al-Afaqah" is the name of a place where the famous day occurred between Labid and al-Rabi' ibn Ziyad al-'Absi. "Ardaf al-muluk" comes from "al-ridf," which is the one who is with the king and stands in for him when he rises from his assembly.

The word "najwa" is also used for a group of men, as the Exalted said: ﴿And when they are in private conference (najwa)﴾ [Surah al-Isra': 47], and He said: ﴿There is no private conference (najwa) of three﴾ [Surah al-Mujadilah: 7], and they are the people who confer privately. "Najwa" may also be a verbal noun, as Allah said: ﴿Private conference is only from Satan﴾ [Surah al-Mujadilah: 10]. One says from it: "najawtu anjuw najwa," and so in this place it is the private conferring itself. From it is the saying of the poet [al-Salatan al-'Abdi]:

"My son, the deceit of men's private conferences has appeared, so be, in your secret, a concealer of the private conference..." [Sharh al-Hamasah 3: 112; al-Shi'r wa al-Shu'ara' 479; al-Khizanah 1: 308, and others. It is from his well-known counsel which he gave to his son, in which he says: "Gray hair has whitened the young, and has wasted the old, the going of the morning and the passing of the evening..." Then he says after the witness verse: "Your secret, when it is with a man, and the secret of three, is not hidden."

"Al-Hubb" (with a kasra on the ha') means guile, and "al-Khabb" (with a fatha) means a crafty person.]

Thus "najwa" and "najiyy" in this verse have the same meaning, which is private conferring, and the poet combined the two dialects.

* *

Scholars of interpretation have said in line with what we have said regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿they withdrew to confer privately﴾.

Those who said that:

19618 - Ibn Wakf'i narrated to us, he said: 'Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿So when they despaired of him they withdrew to confer privately﴾: Shim'un withdrew from them, and he had been holding him as a pledge; they left each other alone, conferring among themselves.

19619 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿they withdrew to confer privately﴾: they withdrew by themselves to confer privately.

19620 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿they withdrew to confer privately﴾: that is, some of them were alone with others. Then they said: "What do you think?"

* *

As for His words ﴿The eldest of them said﴾, the scholars differed regarding who is meant.

Some of them said: It refers to their eldest in intellect and knowledge, not in age, and this is Shim'un. They said: Ruben was older than him by birth.

Those who said that:

19621 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words ﴿The eldest of them said﴾: He is Shim'un who stayed behind, and the elder than him, or: the elder of them, by birth, is Ruben.

19622 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Shababah narrated to us, he said: Waqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿The eldest of them said﴾: Shim'un who stayed behind, and the elder than him by birth is Ruben.

19623 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

19624 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq informed us, he said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿The eldest of them said﴾, he said: Shim'un who stayed behind, and the eldest of them by birth is Ruben.

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers to their eldest in age, and this is Ruben.

Those who said that:

19625 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿The eldest of them said﴾, and he is Ruben, brother of Joseph, and he is his maternal cousin, and he is the one who forbade them from killing him.

19626 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿The eldest of them said﴾, he said: Ruben, and he is the one who advised them not to kill him.

19627 - Ibn Wakf'i narrated to us, he said: 'Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿The eldest of them said﴾ in knowledge [In the printed and manuscript editions: "in knowledge," and I found nothing to confirm that the report means the same as the heading, that is, in place of "in knowledge," "in age"] = ﴿Did you not know that your father had taken an oath from you in the name of Allah, and before this you had failed in regard to Joseph? So I will never leave this land﴾, the verse. Ruben remained in Egypt, and the nine returned to Ya'qub and informed him of the news. He wept and said: "My sons, every time you go, you lose one! You went once and lost Joseph, you went a second time and lost Shim'un, and now you go and lose Ruben!"

19628 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿So when they despaired of him they withdrew to confer privately﴾, he said: "What do you think?" Then Ruben said, as was mentioned to me, and he was the eldest of the people: ﴿Did you not know that your father had taken from you a solemn pledge in the name of Allah, that you would bring him back to me unless you are encompassed? And before this you failed in regard to Joseph﴾, the verse.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions on this matter is the view of those who said: by His words ﴿The eldest of them said﴾ is meant Ruben, because they all agree that he was the eldest of them in age. When the Arabs are addressed and it is said to them, "So-and-so is the eldest of the people," without any qualifier, they understand only one of two meanings: either in leadership over them and nobility, or in age. As for intellect, when they intend that, they attach a qualifier and say: "He is the eldest of them in intellect." When it is stated without such a qualifier, only what I have mentioned is understood.

The scholars of interpretation have also said that Shim'un did not have leadership and nobility over his brothers, even though he had the knowledge and intellect to the degree that God gave him. So it is known that he is not the one meant by His words ﴿The eldest of them said﴾. If that is so, then only the other sense remains, which is seniority in age. Those mentioned have all said: Ruben was the eldest of the people in age, and thus the view we have chosen is confirmed.

* *

As for His words ﴿Did you not know that your father had taken an oath from you in the name of Allah﴾, it means: Did you not know, O people, that your father Ya'qub had taken from you the covenants and pledges of Allah: [See the explanation of "al-mawthiq" earlier, p. 163, note 1, and the references there] that you would bring him back to him all together, unless you are encompassed [by enemies]? ﴿And before this you failed in regard to Joseph﴾ [I have added the text of the verse, though it is not established in the manuscript or the printed edition], and before this deed of yours, your neglect regarding Joseph. He means: Did you not know before this your failure regarding Joseph? If the interpretation of the speech is directed to this which we have stated, then "ma" is in the accusative position.

It is permissible that His words ﴿And before this you failed in regard to Joseph﴾ be a predicate of an inchoative, and His words ﴿Did you not know that your father had taken an oath from you in the name of Allah﴾ be a complete statement, so "ma" is then in the nominative position, as if it were said: "And before this was your failure regarding Joseph," so "ma" would be in the nominative governed by "min qabl" (before).

It is also permissible that the "ma" be a superfluous particle in the speech [in the printed edition: "which is a connecting particle," and in the manuscript: "which is a connecting particle," and I preferred what I have written; "al-silah" means the superfluous particle, see the glossary of terms earlier], so the meaning of the speech becomes: "And before this you failed in regard to Joseph." [In the printed edition: "your failure regarding Joseph," and the correct form is what I have written, because "ma" is superfluous here.]

* *

As for His words ﴿So I will never leave the land﴾ in which I am, that is Egypt, and I will not depart from it, ﴿until my father permits me﴾ to leave it, as:

19629 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿So I will never leave the land﴾ in which I am today, ﴿until my father permits me﴾, to leave it.

19630 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: Shim'un said: ﴿I will never leave the land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me, and He is the best of judges.﴾

* *

As for His words ﴿or Allah decides for me﴾, that is, or my Lord decides for me to leave it and abandon my brother Benjamin, otherwise I will not depart. ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾, that is: Allah is the best of those who judge and the most just of those who decide between people. [See the explanation of "al-hukm" earlier in the lexical indexes (h-k-m).]

* *

Abu Salih used to say regarding this:

19631 - al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Sabi'i narrated to me, he said: 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His words ﴿until my father permits me or Allah decides for me﴾, he said: "With the sword."

* *

It seems that Abu Salih directed the interpretation of His words ﴿or Allah decides for me﴾ to mean: or Allah decides for me by war against whoever prevents me from departing with my brother Benjamin to his father Ya'qub, so that I fight him.

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Return to your father and say: "O our father, your son has committed theft. We testify only to what we know, and we were not guardians over the unseen."﴾ (81)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, is informing about what Rubil said to his brothers when Yusuf seized their brother with the drinking cup that had been taken out of his bag: "Return, my brothers, to your father Ya'qub and say to him: O our father, your son Binyamin has stolen."

* *

The reading of this word, with a fatha on the sin and the ra and without doubling, is: ﴿Your son has stolen﴾ (inna ibnaka saraqa).

* *

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "inna ibnaka suriqa," with a damma on the sin and a shadda on the ra, in the passive form whose subject is not named, meaning: he was stolen from = ﴿and we testify only to what we know﴾.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of this.

Some of them said: its meaning is: "We did not say that he stole except on the apparent basis of our knowledge that this is so, because the king's drinking cup was found in his bag and not in the bags of others."

Those who said this:

19632 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Return to your father⌝, for I did not return until his command came to me⌝ = ﴿and say: O our father, your son has committed theft. We testify only to what we know⌝, i.e.: the theft has been found in his baggage, while we were looking; we have no knowledge of the unseen⌝ = ﴿and we were not guardians over the unseen⌝.

* *

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "We did not testify before Yusuf that the thief is seized for his theft except on the basis of what we knew."

Those who said this:

19633 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Ya'qub, peace be upon him, said to them: "This man does not know that the thief is seized for his theft except from your statement!" So they said: ﴿We testified only to what we knew⌝, we did not testify that the thief is taken for his theft except on that which we knew. He said: The ruling among the prophets, Ya'qub and his sons, was that the thief be taken for his theft as a slave, and be enslaved.

* *

His words: ﴿and we were not guardians over the unseen﴾ mean: we did not think that your son would steal, and our affair would come to this; we only said ﴿and we will guard our brother⌝ from that against which we had a way to guard him.

* *

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

19634 - al-Husayn ibn al-Hurayth Abu 'Ammar al-Marwazi narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Yazid, from 'Ikrima: ﴿and we were not guardians over the unseen﴾. He said: We did not know that your son would steal.

19635 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and we were not guardians over the unseen﴾: we did not perceive that he would steal.

19636 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and we were not guardians over the unseen﴾. He said: We did not perceive that he would steal.

19637 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and we were not guardians over the unseen﴾. He said: We did not perceive that he would steal.

19638 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid; and Abu Sufyan, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: "and we were not guardians over the unseen." He said: We did not suppose nor perceive that he would steal.

19639 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿and we were not guardians over the unseen﴾. He said: We did not see that he would steal.

19640 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿and we were not guardians over the unseen﴾. He said: We did not suppose that your son would steal.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations in our view regarding His words ﴿We testified only to what we knew⌝ is the statement of those who said: "We did not testify that your son stole except by what we knew from seeing the cup in his bag," because it follows His words ﴿your son has stolen⌝; so it is more fitting that it be a report of their testimony to that, than that it be a report about something separate.

* *

It is mentioned that "al-Ghayb" (the unseen), in the language of Himyar, is precisely the night. [[This is a rare meaning of "al-Ghayb" in tafsir, which I have not found in any of the lexicographical books available to us.]]

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 82:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And ask the town in which we were, and the caravan in which we came, and indeed we are truthful﴾.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: It means: even if you suspect us, and do not believe us about what we say, that your son stole. ﴿Ask the town in which we were﴾, which is Egypt, meaning: ask those among its people [who are there]. ﴿And the caravan in which we came﴾, which is the caravan we were in, [[See the explanation of "al-'ir" (caravan) above, pp. 173–174.]] that we came back with, concerning the news of your son and the truth of what we informed you about his theft. [[Saraqa al-shay' yasriquhu sarqan (with a fathah on both letters), and sarqan (with a fathah on the sin and a kasrah on the ra'), and sariqah.]] For you will test the truth of that. ﴿And indeed we are truthful﴾ concerning what we have told you about his news.

* *

Those who engage in interpretation have said the same as what we have said.

Those who said this:

19641 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And ask the town in which we were﴾, which is Egypt.

19642 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿And ask the town in which we were﴾, he said: they mean Egypt.

19643 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Ruwbil recognised, in the retort of his words to his brothers, that they were people of suspicion in the eyes of their father, because of what they had done with Yusuf. And their words to him: ﴿Ask the town in which we were and the caravan in which we came﴾, for they knew what we knew and witnessed what we witnessed, even if you do not believe us, ﴿and indeed we are truthful﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 83:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said: Rather, your souls have beautified for you a matter, so patience is fitting. Perhaps Allah will bring them all to me. Indeed, He is the Knowing, the Wise﴾ (12:83).

Abu Ja'far said: There is an omission in the statement, and it is: So the brothers of Benjamin returned to their father, and Ruben stayed behind, and they told him the news. When they told him that he had stolen, he said: ﴿Rather, your souls have beautified for you a matter﴾, meaning: Rather, your souls have made appealing to you a matter you resolved upon and desired (see the explanation of "taswil" (embellishment, making appealing) above, 15:583). ﴿So patience is fitting﴾, meaning: my patience regarding what has befallen me from the loss of my son is a beautiful patience, with no lamenting or complaining in it (see the explanation of "sabr jamil" (beautiful patience) above, 15:584). ﴿Perhaps Allah will bring me my sons, all of them﴾, so that He returns them to me. ﴿Indeed, He is the Knowing﴾, of my solitude, of their loss and my grief over them, and of the truth of what they say versus his lie. ﴿The Wise﴾, in His management of His creation (see the explanations of "al-'Alim" (the Knowing) and "al-Hakim" (the Wise) above, from the lexical indexes, under ('-l-m) and (h-k-m)).

* *

It is said of this root: "Ma fati'tu aqulu dhalika" (I did not cease saying that), and "ma fata'tu" is a dialectal variant, "afti'u" and "afta'u," "fata'an" and "futu'an."[[His saying "afti'u" appears this way in the manuscript and the printed edition, and nothing in the lexicographical books supports what Abu Ja'far said; it is very strange.]] It is also related: "ma aftat'tu bihi" (I did not cease with it). Among its examples is the verse of Aws ibn Hajar:

*So it did not cease, until as if its dust*
*Was a canopy of a windy day, raised high.*[[His Diwan, verse 17, poem 12; al-Lisan (sh-r-m). Its wording in both is: "fa-ma fatiat khayl ka-anna ghubaruha."]]

And his other saying:[[This is also a saying of Aws ibn Hajar.]]

*So horses did not cease to return and call out,*
*And some of them overtake and some fall behind.*[[His Diwan, poem 17, verse 10; Jamharat al-Lugha 3:287; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:316; al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 1002.]]

Meaning: "so it did not cease."

The "la" (not) is omitted from His words ﴿tafta'u﴾, though it is intended in the meaning of the speech. This is because when an oath is followed by a positive statement, it is not accompanied by a negation, and the lam that answers oaths is not dropped. This is like the speaker's saying: "By God, I will surely come to you." When what follows is negated, it is preceded by "ma" or "la." Since its position was known, it was omitted from the speech, because the listener knows the meaning of the speech.[[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an in its commentary on this verse.]] Among its examples is the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

*I said, "By God's oath, I will stay sitting, *
*Even if they cut off my head before you and my limbs."*[[This verse and its takhrij were previously mentioned, 4:425; al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an may be added to it.]]

So "la" was omitted from his saying "abrahu qa'idan" (I will not cease sitting) for the reason I have mentioned, as another poet said:

*"No, by the life of my father, Dahma', she has not ceased to be honored*
*Among her people, while the spark strikes the tinder."*[[Al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, in its commentary on this verse; Mushkil al-Qur'an, 174; al-Khizanah 4:45-46; Sharh Shawahid al-Mughni, 278. In the printed and manuscript editions it reads "ma qabla al-zand," which is a clear error.]]

He means: "she has not ceased."

As for His words ﴿until you become wasted away﴾, He says: until you become one whose body is weakened and whose mind is deranged.

* *

The original meaning of "harad" is corruption in the body and the mind from grief or love. Among its examples is the verse of al-'Arji:

*I am a man whom love has seized and made me "harad,"*
*Until I am worn away, and illness has wasted me.*[[His Diwan, 5; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah, 317; al-Lisan (h-r-d).]]

By his saying "fa-ahradani," he means: it melted me and left me "muhradan" (wasted away). It is said of this: "rajul harad" (a man is harad), "imra'ah harad" (a woman is harad), "qawm harad" (people are harad), "rajulan harad" (two men are harad), in one form for masculine and feminine, and for the dual and plural. Some Arabs say for the male "harid" and for the female "haridah." When this word is described in this way, it is made dual and plural, and masculine and feminine. "Harad" is always used in the singular and is not made feminine, because it is a verbal noun. When it is formed as "fa'il," according to the usage of nouns, it takes on what nouns take in terms of dual, plural, masculine and feminine. Some of them recorded, by report: "rajul muhrad," when he is afflicted with pain, and cited a verse on this:

*The horses pursued him for a whole day,*
*And if they had overtaken him, he would have become "muhrad."*[[I did not find the verse nor know its speaker.]]

It is mentioned that from this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*I see the man of many camels becoming "muhrad,"*
*Like a sick camel in the encampments.*[[His Diwan, 77; al-Lisan (h-r-d).]]
