19709. We were told by al-Qasim, who said: We were told by al-Husayn, who said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿I only complain of my anguish﴾: Ibn Abbas said: "bathhi" (بثي) means my concern.

19710. We were told by Ibn Humayd, who said: We were told by Salama, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Ya'qub said, out of knowledge of Allah: ﴿I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know﴾, because of what he saw of their harshness, their coarseness, and the evil of their speech to him: [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "lafzuhum bihi" (their utterance to him), which is not correct; the correct reading is what has been adopted, meaning their rudeness in what they addressed him with in speech.]] "I did not complain of that to you"; ﴿and I know from Allah what you do not know﴾.

19711. We were told by Ibn Wakic, who said: We were told by Abu Usama, from Awf, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah﴾: He said: "My need and my grief to Allah."

19712. We were told by al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, who said: We were told by Hawdha ibn Khalifa, who said: We were told by Awf, from al-Hasan, the same.

* *

It has also been said: "al-bathth" (البث) is the intensest grief. [[This is the wording of Abu Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (the book on the figurative language of the Qur'an), 1:317.]] In my view it derives from "bathth al-hadith" (broadcasting the news), and what is meant is: "I only complain of my news, which I am in, of concern, and I broadcast my account and my grief to Allah."

* *

19713. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, who said: We were told by Abu Asim, who said: We were told by Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Awf, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿I only complain of my anguish﴾: He said: "My grief."

19714. We were told by Ibn Bashshar, who said: Yahya ibn Sa'id told me, from Awf, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿I only complain of my anguish and my grief﴾: He said: "My need."

* *

As for His words, ﴿and I know from Allah what you do not know﴾, Ibn Abbas used to say about it, as has been reported from him:

19715. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me on his authority, who said: My father told me, who said: My uncle told me, who said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words, ﴿and I know from Allah what you do not know﴾: He says: "I know that Yusuf's dream is true, and that I will indeed prostrate to him."

19716. We were told by Ibn Wakic, who said: We were told by Amr, from Asbat, from al-Sudi, who said: Regarding ﴿I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah and I know from Allah what you do not know﴾, he said: When they informed him of the king's summons, Ya'qub's soul was stirred, and he said: "There is no truthful person (siddiq) on earth except a prophet!" So he hoped, and said: "Perhaps it is Yusuf." [[This report is confused in wording; I fear that there is a omission or a distortion in it.]]

19717. We were told by Bishr, who said: We were told by Yazid, who said: We were told by Sa'id, from Qatada, regarding ﴿He said: I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah﴾ to the end of the verse: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah, Ya'qub, was never struck by any affliction except that he brought his good opinion of Allah with him.

19718. We were told by Ibn Humayd, who said: We were told by Hakkam, from Isa ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan, who said: It was said: "How far did Ya'qub's grief over his son reach?" He said: "He grieved like seventy bereaved mothers." He was asked: "What reward did he have?" He said: "The reward of a hundred martyrs." He said: "And his opinion of Allah did not deteriorate for an hour of night or day."

19719. We were told by Ibn Humayd again, who said: We were told by Hakkam, from Abu Mu'adh, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the same.

19720. We were told by Ibn Humayd, who said: We were told by Salama, from al-Mubarak ibn Mujahid, from a man of the Azd, from Talha ibn Musarrif al-Iyami, who said: "Three things you should not mention, and you should avoid mentioning them: do not complain of your illness, do not complain of your calamity, and do not praise yourself." He said: I was informed that Ya'qub ibn Ishaq was visited by a neighbour of his, who said to him: "O Ya'qub, why do I see you broken and worn out, when you have not reached the age your father reached?" He said: "What has broken me and worn me out is the concern and remembrance of Yusuf with which Allah has tried me!" Then Allah revealed to him: "O Ya'qub, do you complain of Me to My creation?" He said: "O Lord, a sin I committed; forgive it for me!" He said: "I have indeed forgiven you." And after that, whenever he was asked, he would say: ﴿I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know﴾.

19721. We were told by Amr ibn Ali, who said: Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il told me, who said: We were told by Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: It reached me that Ya'qub grew so old that his eyebrows fell over his cheeks, so he would lift them with a cloth. A man said to him: "What has brought you to what I see?" He said: "The length of time and the abundance of sorrows." Then Allah revealed to him: "O Ya'qub, do you complain of Me?" He said: "A sin; forgive it."

19722. We were told by Ibn Humayd, who said: We were told by Yahya ibn Wadih, who said: We were told by Thawr ibn Yazid, who said: Ya'qub entered upon Pharaoh with his eyebrows fallen over his eyes. He said: "What has brought you to this, O Ibrahim?" They said: "It is Ya'qub." He said: "What has brought you to this, O Ya'qub?" He said: "The length of time and the abundance of sorrows." Allah said: "O Ya'qub, do you complain of Me?" He said: "O Lord, a sin I committed; forgive it for me."

19723. We were told by Amr ibn Ali, who said: We were told by Abd al-Wahhab, who said: We were told by Hisham, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who said: Jibril (Gabriel) entered upon Yusuf in the prison, and recognized him, and said: "O king, whose face is beautiful, whose fragrance is good, who is honoured by his Lord, will you not tell me about Ya'qub, is he alive?" He said: "Yes." He said: "O king, whose face is beautiful, whose fragrance is good, who is honoured by his Lord, what has his grief reached?" He said: "The grief of seventy bereaved mothers." He said: "O king, whose face is beautiful, whose fragrance is good, who is honoured by his Lord, is there any reward in that?" He said: "The reward of a hundred martyrs."

19724. We were told by Ibn Humayd, who said: We were told by Salama, from Ibn Ishaq, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Mujahid, who said: I was told that Jibril came to Yusuf (ﷺ) while he was in Egypt, in the form of a man. When Yusuf saw him, he recognized him, and rose to him, and said: "O king, whose fragrance is good, whose garments are pure, who is honoured by his Lord, do you have any knowledge of Ya'qub?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "O king, whose garments are pure, who is honoured by his Lord, how is he?" He said: "His sight has gone." He said: "O king, whose garments are pure, who is honoured by his Lord, what took away his sight?" He said: "The grief over you." He said: "O king, whose fragrance is good, whose garments are pure, who is honoured by his Lord, what is he given for that?" He said: "The reward of seventy martyrs."

19725. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la told me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Abu Shurayh said: "I heard someone narrate that Yusuf asked Jibril: 'What has the grief of Ya'qub reached?' He said: 'The grief of seventy bereaved mothers.' He said: 'What has his reward reached?' He said: 'The reward of seventy martyrs.'"

19726. ... He said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, who said: Jibril entered upon Yusuf in the well or in the prison, and Yusuf said to him: "O Jibril, what has my father's grief reached?" He said: "The grief of seventy bereaved mothers." He said: "What has his reward from Allah reached?" He said: "The reward of a hundred martyrs."

19727. Al-Muthanna told me, who said: We were told by Ishaq, who said: We were told by Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim, who said: Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil told me, who said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: Jibril brought Yusuf the good news while he was in the prison. He said: "Do you know me, O truthful one (al-siddiq)?" He said: "I see a pure form and a good spirit, not like the spirits of the sinners." He said: "I am the messenger of the Lord of the worlds, and I am the Trustworthy Spirit." He said: "What brought you to enter the place of the wrongdoers, when you are the best of the good, the chief of those brought near, and the trustee of the Lord of the worlds?" He said: "Do you not know, O Yusuf, that Allah purifies houses by the purity of prophets, and that the land they enter is the purest of lands, and that Allah has purified the prison and what surrounds it through you, O purest of the pure and son of the purified? [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "ya tahra al-tahirin" (O purity of the pure); the correct reading is what has been adopted.]] It is only purified through the excellence of your purity and the purity of your righteous, sincere fathers!" He said: "How can I have the name of the truthful, when you count me among the sincere, while I have entered the place of the wrongdoers and been named among the astray and corrupt?" [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "wa sumitu bi-l-dallin al-mufsidin" (I was named with the astray and corrupt); this is not correct; the correct reading is what has been adopted. See after his words: "wa samma-ka Allah fi al-siddiqin" (Allah named you among the truthful).]] He said: "Your heart was not tempted, and you did not obey your mistress in disobedience to your Lord; for that reason Allah named you among the truthful, counted you among the sincere, and joined you to your righteous fathers." He said: "Do you have knowledge of Ya'qub, O Trustworthy Spirit?" He said: "Yes; Allah granted him beautiful patience, and tested him with grief over you, so he is restrained (kazim)." He said: "What is the measure of his grief?" He said: "The grief of seventy bereaved mothers." He said: "What reward does he have, O Jibril?" He said: "The measure of a hundred martyrs."

19728. We were told by Ibn Humayd, who said: We were told by Jarir, from Layth, from Thabit al-Bunani, who said: Jibril entered upon Yusuf in the prison, and Yusuf recognized him. He came to him and greeted him, and said: "O king, whose fragrance is good, whose garments are pure, who is honoured by his Lord, do you have any knowledge of Ya'qub?" He said: "Yes." He said: "O king, whose fragrance is good, whose garments are pure, who is honoured by his Lord, do you know what he has done?" He said: "His eyes have turned white." He said: "O king, whose fragrance is good, whose garments are pure, who is honoured by his Lord, from what?" He said: "From grief over you." [[In the manuscript: "He said: His eyes have indeed turned white from grief over you"; the exchange of question and answer between the two statements has been omitted.]] He said: "O king, whose fragrance is good, whose garments are pure, who is honoured by his Lord, what has his grief reached?" He said: "The grief of seventy bereaved mothers." He said: "O king, whose fragrance is good, whose garments are pure, who is honoured by his Lord, does he have any reward for that?" He said: "Yes, the reward of a hundred martyrs."

19729. We were told by Ibn Wakic, who said: We were told by Amr, from Asbat, from al-Sudi, who said: Jibril came to Yusuf while he was in the prison, and greeted him. He came to him in the form of a man, of handsome face, of good fragrance, and clean garments. Yusuf said to him: "O king, whose face is beautiful, honoured by his Lord, whose fragrance is good, tell me, how is Ya'qub?" He said: "He grieved over you a severe grief." He said: "What has his grief reached?" He said: "The grief of seventy bereaved mothers." He said: "What has his reward reached?" He said: "The reward of seventy or a hundred martyrs." Yusuf said: "Then with whom has he taken refuge after me?" He said: "With your brother Benjamin." He said: "Do you think I will meet him ever?" He said: "Yes." Yusuf wept when his father was reunited with him after that, then said: "I do not mind what I have suffered, if Allah has shown him to me."

19730. ... He said: We were told by Amr ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrima, who said: Jibril came to Yusuf while he was in the prison, and greeted him. Yusuf said to him: "O king, honoured by his Lord, whose fragrance is good, whose garments are pure, do you have any knowledge of Ya'qub?" He said: "Yes, how intense is his grief!" He said: "O king, honoured by his Lord, whose fragrance is good, whose garments are pure, what reward does he have?" He said: "The reward of seventy martyrs." He said: "Do you think I will meet him?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then Yusuf's soul was content."

19731. We were told by Ibn Humayd, who said: We were told by Jarir, from Layth, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When Ya'qub entered upon the king, and his eyebrows had fallen over his eyes, the king said: "What is this?" He said: "The years and the sorrows," or: "The worries and the sorrows." His Lord said: "O Ya'qub, did you complain of Me to My creation? Did I not do this and that for you?"

19732. We were told by al-Hasan ibn Yahya, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: al-Thawri informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, from Muslim ibn Yasar, raising it to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever broadcasts his grief does not endure." [[In the manuscript: "man babba fa-lam nasir" (with an illegible letter and the mark of ta' above it indicating an error); what is in the printed edition, the text of al-Durr al-Manthur 4:31, is adopted.]] Then he recited: ﴿I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah﴾.

19733. Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Amili told me, who said: We were told by Abu Usama, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, who said: From the time Yusuf left Ya'qub's side until the day he returned, eighty years passed, during which grief did not leave his heart; he wept until his sight was gone. Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, on the earth at that time there was no creature more honoured by Allah than Ya'qub (ﷺ)."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 87:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O my sons, go and search out news of Joseph and his brother, and despair not of relief from God. Surely none despairs of relief from God except the disbelieving folk﴾.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When Ya'qub (Jacob) longed for Yusuf (Joseph), he said to his sons: ﴿O my sons, go﴾ to the place from which you came and where you left your two brothers, ﴿and search out news of Yusuf﴾, meaning: seek Yusuf and get information about his whereabouts.

* *

The origin of "tahassus" (searching out, seeking news) is the reflexive form "tafa''ul" from "hiss" (sense, perception).

* *

﴿And his brother﴾ meaning Binyamin. ﴿And despair not of relief from God﴾, meaning: do not give up hope that God will bring us relief from the grief we are in over Yusuf and his brother, by bringing them back to us from Him. ﴿Surely none despairs of relief from God﴾ meaning: none gives up on His deliverance and mercy or cuts off hope in it [[see the explanation of "yaas" (despair) in the earlier part, vol. 9, p. 516]]. ﴿except the disbelieving folk﴾, meaning: the people who deny His power to bring about whatever He wills.

* *

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

19734- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿O my sons, go and search out news of Joseph and his brother﴾, in Egypt; ﴿and despair not of relief from God﴾, he said: of God's deliverance, that He return Joseph.

19735- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and despair not of relief from God﴾, meaning: of God's mercy.

19736- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, similarly.

19737- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then Ya'qub said to his sons, while he held good opinion of his Lord along with the grief he was in: ﴿O my sons, go﴾ to the lands from which you came, ﴿and search out news of Joseph and his brother, and despair not of relief from God﴾, that is, of His deliverance. ﴿Surely none despairs of relief from God except the disbelieving folk.﴾

19738- It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying: ﴿and despair not of relief from God﴾, that it means: of God's mercy.

19739- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and despair not of relief from God﴾, he said: of God's deliverance, who will relieve you of the distress you are in.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 88 (part 1 of 2):

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So when they entered upon him, they said: "O Chief! Adversity has touched us and our family, and we have come with meager merchandise, so give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable."﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The speech contains an omission, which is dispensed with by mention of what appears, of what has been dropped. It is: they set out returning to Egypt until they reached it, and entered upon Yusuf. ﴿So when they entered upon him, they said: "O Chief! Adversity has touched us and our family"﴾, meaning hardship from drought and famine [[See the explanation of "al-durr" (adversity) in the indexes of language earlier, under (d-r-r).]] ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise"﴾. As related:

19740. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said, "And they set out for Egypt, returning to it." ﴿"with meager merchandise"﴾: that is, little, which would not suffice for what they used to trade with, unless he overlooked it for them, and they had seen what had befallen their father, and how affliction followed him regarding his son and his sight, until they came to Yusuf. So when they entered upon him they said: ﴿"O Chief!"﴾, hoping that he would have mercy on them regarding their brother [[In the printed edition: "rajaa" (hoping); I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which has the same meaning.]] ﴿"Adversity has touched us and our family."﴾

* *

By His words ﴿"we have come with meager merchandise" (muzjāh)﴾ is meant dirhams or currency that is not acceptable as payment for food except to one who would overlook it.

* *

The root of *al-izjā'* is driving by pushing, as al-Nabighah al-Dhubyani said:

*"The wind blew from the direction of Dhu Uruul, driving with the night its clouds, the cold thin ones."* [[His Diwan: 52. "Dhu Uruul" is a mountain in the lands of Ghatafan. "Al-sarrād" is thin cold cloud driven and swept along by the wind. "Al-siram" is the plural of "sirmah," meaning pieces of cloud. Before the verse: "Why did you not ask the Banu Dhubyan about my lineage, when the smoke enveloped the white-haired and the aged?" From verses in which he mentions his generosity in a time of drought and winter.]] That is, it drives and pushes. From it is the saying of al-A'sha of Banu Tha'labah:

*"The giver of a hundred white camels and their servant, pregnant camels driving their young behind them."* [[His Diwan: 25, from his qasidah on Qays ibn Ma'd Yakrib, some verses of which have passed. "Al-hijan" are white camels, the noble camels. "Al-ūdh" is the plural of "ā'idh," a she-camel recently given birth.]]

And the saying of Hatim:

*"For the sake of Malhan, a guest pushed on, and a widow driving with the night a widow."* [[It is not in his Diwan. Ibn Burri recited it without attribution (Lisan: r-m-l). It is evident that the poetry is Hatim's, because "Malhan" is his cousin Malhan ibn Harithah ibn Sa'd ibn al-Hashraj al-Ta'i. I had come upon some verses of this poetry, then lost them today.]]

That is, she drives him before her, as he is weak and unable to walk. Therefore it was said ﴿"with meager merchandise"﴾, because it is not passing currency, and it is accepted only by way of tolerance, at a discount on the part of those who take it. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "on the benefit of those who take it," and the correct reading is what I have adopted, God willing, as the following reports indicate. If it is read "on the payment (daf')," there is no harm in that.]]

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed in explaining the meaning of this, though the meanings of their explanations are close.

Mention of the statements of the people of interpretation regarding this:

19741. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿"with meager merchandise"﴾, he said: "Inferior, counterfeit dirhams that are not accepted unless a discount is applied."

19742. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ he said: "The inferior ones that are not accepted unless a discount is applied."

19743. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ he said: "Worn out, the sack, the rope, and the thing." [[Al-khalaq: the worn-out.]]

19744. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah who said: I heard Ibn Abbas, and he was asked about His words: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ he said: "The ruin of goods: the rope, the sack, and the thing." [[Al-rath (with a fatha on the ra') and al-rathah (with a kasrah), and al-ratheeth: the base, worn-out thing of any kind.]]

19745. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

19746. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ he said: "'Al-bidā'ah' (merchandise) means dirhams, and 'al-muzjāh' means not of consequence." [[See the explanation of "al-bidā'ah" earlier: p. 4, 156.]]

19747. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Ibn Abi Ziyad, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Unmarketable, of no consequence."

19748. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, saying: Abu Husayn narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ Sa'id said: "Deficient." Ikrimah said: "Dirhams that are fusul." [[Fusul is the plural of fasl (with a fatha and then a sukun), meaning the worst, vilest of anything. It is said: "fusul dirhams," that is, counterfeit.]]

19749. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah, the like of it.

19750. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ one of them said: "Deficient." And the other said: "Inferior."

19751. ... and with that chain: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, who said: "It was ghee and wool."

19752. Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, who said: A man asked Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, while I was with him, about His words: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ and he said: "Little. The goods of the Bedouins: wool and ghee."

19753. Ishaq ibn Ziyad al-Qattan Abu Ya'qub al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Balkhi narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari narrated to us, from Marwan ibn Amr al-Udhri, from Abu Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ he said: "Pine nuts and the green seed." [[Report 19753: "Ishaq ibn Ziyad al-Qattan, Abu Ya'qub al-Basri," a teacher of al-Tabari whose biography I have not found. It has passed as no. 14146, where it is "al-Attar al-Nasri," and then no. 17430, where it is "Ishaq ibn Ziyadah al-Attar," with a ta' added. I have no means to decide this until I find something that indicates it. "Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Balkhi" passed as no. 14146, and there too Ishaq ibn Ziyad narrated from him. "Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari" has passed several times, the last being 15446. As for "Marwan ibn Amr al-Udhri," I have not found mention of him in the biographical books, and I fear there is an error in it. As for "Abu Isma'il," I have not determined who he is, because of the obscurity in this chain.]]

19754. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Yazid ibn al-Walid, from Ibrahim, regarding His words: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ he said: "Little. Do you not hear His words, 'Fill our mounts (fa-awqir rikābanā)'? And they recite it that way." [[That is, the companions of Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, as you will see in the following report.]]

19755. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, that he said: "I think it is only the little, because in the codex of Abd Allah it is: 'and fill our mounts (wa-awqir rikābanā),' meaning His words, 'muzjāh'."

19756. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Yazid, from Ibrahim, who said: "Little. Did you not hear His words, 'and fill our mounts'?"

19757. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan: "Bidā'ah muzjāh." Sa'id said: "The inferior." And al-Hasan said: "The little."

19758. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Yazid, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, who said: "The goods of the Bedouins are ghee and wool."

19759. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from Ata', who said: "Dirhams that are not of consequence." [[In the manuscript: "laysa bi-ṭā'il," and there is no harm in it.]]

19760. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿"muzjāh,"﴾ he said: "Little."

19761. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿"muzjāh,"﴾ he said: "Little."

19762. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

19763. ... he said: Qabisah ibn Uqbah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ he said: "Some wool and some ghee."

19764. ... he said: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Mansur, from al-Hasan, who said: "Little."

19765. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from one who narrated to him, from Mujahid: ﴿"muzjāh,"﴾ he said: "Little."

19766. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

19767. ... he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Ikrimah, who said: "Deficient." And Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Fusul."

19768. ... he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ he said: "Inferior."

19769. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "Unmarketable, not passing."

19770. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "Unmarketable."

19771. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abdah narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "Unmarketable, of no consequence."

19772. It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿"with meager merchandise,"﴾ he says: "Unmarketable, not passing."

19773. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ he said: "Deficient." And Ikrimah said: "In it is a tolerance (tajawwuz)."

19774. ... he said: Isra'il narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The inferior dirhams that are not accepted unless with a deduction."

19775. ... he said: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, who said: "The worthless dirhams [[Rudhal: it is said 'this is rudhal' and 'this is rudhāl' (with a damma on the ra'), meaning below base, inferior, vile. In the manuscript it is 'al-rudhl,' which has the same meaning.]] that are not accepted unless with a deduction." [[The report (19775) in the printed edition reads "Isra'il from Ibn Abi Najih," differing from the manuscript, where it was: "from Abu Yahya," as if he meant to write "Najih," then made it "Yahya," without dots. "Abu Yahya" is Abu Yahya al-Qattat al-Kufi, who narrates from Mujahid, and he has passed as no. 12139, 15697.]]

19776. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: "Dirhams in which there is permissibility (jawāz)."

19777. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ meaning: "small (yasirah)."

19778. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of it.

19779. Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ he said: "Al-muzjāh" is the little.

19780. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿"and we have come with meager merchandise,"﴾ that is, little, not reaching what we used to buy with from you, unless you overlook it for us.

* *

And His words: ﴿"So give us full measure"﴾ ... [[There is no doubt in my mind that something has fallen out of Abu Ja'far's statement in the explanation of "awfi lana" (give us full measure), of which only his words "bihā" (with it) remain, so I placed these dots. The meaning of that is evident; it seems he wrote: "complete for us our rights in measure with it, and give us..." See the explanation of "al-iifā'" (full measure) earlier: 12: 224, 554.]] ﴿"with it"﴾ and give us what you used to give us before, for the good price and the acceptable full dirhams that are not rejected, as related:

19781. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿"So give us full measure,"﴾ that is, give us what you used to give us before, for our merchandise is meager.

19782. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿"So give us full measure,"﴾ he said: "As you used to give us for the good dirhams."

* *

And His words: ﴿"and be charitable to us"﴾ means, may He be exalted in remembrance: they said, "And show us favor by what lies between the price of the good and the inferior, and do not reduce for us the price of your food because of the inferiority of our merchandise." ﴿"Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable"﴾ means: Indeed, Allah rewards those who show favor to the needy with their wealth. [[See the explanation of "al-taṣaddug" (charity) earlier: 9: 31, 37, 38 / 14: 369.]]

* *

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

19783. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿"and be charitable to us,"﴾ he said: "Show favor by what is between the good and the inferior."

19784. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿"So give us full measure and be charitable to us,"﴾ "do not reduce the price for us because of the inferiority of our dirhams."

* *

They differed regarding charity: was it lawful for the prophets before our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), or was it forbidden?

Some of them said: It was not lawful for any of the prophets, peace be upon them.

Mention of those who said that:

19785. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "No prophet ever asked for charity, but they said: ﴿'We have come with meager merchandise, so give us full measure and be charitable to us,'﴾ do not reduce the price for us."

* *

And there is what is related from Ibn Uyaynah:

19786. Al-Harith narrated to me, with it, saying: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: It is related from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah that he was asked: "Was charity forbidden to any of the prophets before the Prophet (ﷺ)?" He said: "Did you not hear His words: ﴿'So give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable.'﴾"

= Al-Harith said: Al-Qasim said: Ibn Uyaynah goes to the view that they did not say that except while charity was lawful for them, being prophets, for charity was only forbidden to Muhammad (ﷺ) and to them. [[In the printed edition: "(ﷺ) but not upon them," differing from the manuscript. It seems he thought that the phrase "and upon them" is conjoined to "it was forbidden for Muhammad ... and upon them." It is evident that what is meant is "(ﷺ) and upon them," that is, "and may blessings be upon them."]]

* *

Others said: He meant by His words ﴿"and be charitable to us"﴾: "and be charitable to us by returning our brother to us."

Mention of those who said that:

19787. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His words: ﴿"and be charitable to us,"﴾ he said: "Return our brother to us."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This view that we have mentioned from Ibn Juraij, although it is a view with some basis, is not the preferred view regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿"and be charitable to us."﴾ For "charity" in the common usage of [the Arabs] [[In the printed edition: "in the common usage," and in the manuscript: "in common usage is only," and there is an undoubted omission in the text. The omission occurred because "common usage" is the last word on the page and "innamā" is at the beginning of the other page, so the copyist erred, and I have inferred this addition that is between the brackets.]] is only a man giving someone in need some of his property, seeking Allah's reward for it, [[In the printed edition: "giving the man someone in need," which is an error and an alteration of the manuscript's text with no basis; the correct reading is what is in the manuscript, as I have adopted. And his words "in need" are the object of the verbal noun in "giving the man..."]] and although every kindness is a charity, directing the interpretation of Allah's speech to the predominant meaning in the speech of those in whose language the Qur'an was revealed is more fitting and more appropriate.

* *

The like of what we have said regarding this was said by Mujahid.

[19788] Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, who said: I heard Mujahid, and he was asked: "Is it disliked for a man to say in his supplication, 'O Allah, give me charity (tasaddaq 'alayya)'?" He said: "Yes, for charity is only for one who seeks reward."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 89:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said: "Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother, when you were ignorant?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: It is mentioned that when his brothers said to him, ﴿O Chief! Hardship has touched us and our family, and we have come with meager merchandise, so give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable﴾, Joseph, peace be upon him, was overcome by tenderness and disclosed to them what he had been concealing from them about his affair, as:

19789 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: It was mentioned to me that when they spoke to him with these words, his self overcame him, and his tears flowed as he wept. Then he disclosed to them what he had been hiding from them, saying: ﴿Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother, when you were ignorant?﴾ He did not mean by mentioning his brother what he himself had done to him when he took him, but to distinguish between him and his brother, since they had done to Joseph what they had done.

19790 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, who said: 'Amr narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿So when they entered upon him, they said: "O Chief! Hardship has touched us and our family"﴾, to the end of the verse, who said: He then had mercy on them, and said to them: ﴿Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother, when you were ignorant?﴾

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the statement is: Do you remember what you did with Joseph and his brother, when you separated them and did what you did, while you were ignorant? That is, in a state of ignorance of the outcome of what you were doing to Joseph, and of where his affair and yours would end up.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 90:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿They said, "Are you indeed Joseph?" He said, "I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has been gracious to us. Indeed, whoever fears Allah and is patient – then indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The brothers of Joseph said to him when Joseph said that to them, ﴿"Are you indeed Joseph?"﴾ He said, "Yes, I am Joseph"= ﴿"and this is my brother. Allah has been gracious to us"﴾ by bringing us together after you had separated us= ﴿"Indeed, whoever fears [Allah] and is patient"﴾, meaning: indeed, whoever fears Allah, watching over Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience= ﴿"and is patient"﴾, meaning: and restrains himself, holding it back from what Allah has forbidden him, whether in speech or action, when a calamity from Allah befalls him= ﴿"then indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost"﴾, meaning: Allah does not nullify the reward of his good deeds and the recompense of his obedience to Him in what He has commanded and forbidden him.

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words: ﴿"Are you indeed Joseph?"﴾ (ʾa-innaka la-anta Yūsuf).

The majority of the reciters of the regional centres recited it: ﴿ʾa-innaka﴾, as an interrogative.

* *

It is mentioned that in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b it is: "ʾa-anta Yūsuf" (Are you Joseph?).

* *

It is narrated from Ibn Muhaysin that he recited: "innaka la-anta Yūsuf" (Indeed you are Joseph), as a declarative, not as an interrogative.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is the recitation of those who recited it as an interrogative, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it.

* *

19791 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When he said that to them – meaning his words: ﴿"Do you know what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?"﴾ – the veil was lifted and they recognised him, and they said: ﴿"Are you indeed Joseph?"﴾, and the verse.

19792 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: One who heard Abdullah ibn Idris mention it narrated to me, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿"Indeed, whoever fears [Allah] and is patient"﴾, he said: whoever fears the disobedience of Allah and is patient over the prison.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 91:

**The exegesis (ta'wil, interpretation) of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "By Allah, Allah has certainly preferred you over us, and we were indeed sinners."﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may His praise be exalted, means: The brothers of Joseph said to him, "By Allah, Allah has certainly favoured you over us, and has preferred you with knowledge, forbearance and virtue." ﴿And we were indeed sinners﴾ means: In what we did, in what we did to you, in separating you from your father and your brother, and in the rest of our conduct which we committed against you, we were nothing but sinners, meaning: we were mistaken (mukhti'in).

* *

It is said of this verb: "Khati'a fulan yakhta'u khata'an wa khit'an, and akhta'a yukhti'u ikhta'an" [see the explanation of "khati'a" in what has passed, 2:110 / 6:134]. From this is the saying of Umayya ibn al-Iskar:

*"And two emigrants who enveloped him... by the life of Allah, they have erred and sinned (khaba)."*

[The verse has passed with its takhrij and the correction of its transmitted version, 2:110 / 7:529, and it is to be added to it: Majaz al-Qur'an, 1:113, 318. In the printed and manuscript text here, "wa khaaban" appears with a kha', and Abu Ja'far explained it at 7:529 as meaning "they sinned," from "al-hawb," which is sin. That is the correct reading, God willing.]

* *

Those who engaged in ta'wil (interpretation) said something similar to what we have said. Those who said so:

19793. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: When Joseph said to them, ﴿I am Joseph, and this is my brother﴾, they made excuse to him and said: ﴿By Allah, Allah has certainly preferred you over us, and we were indeed sinners﴾ for what we had done to you.

19794. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿By Allah, Allah has certainly preferred you over us﴾, and that was after he had made himself known to them. He means: Allah made you a forbearing man.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 12, Verse 92:**

**On the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of the meaning) of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿He said: "No reproach upon you today. May God forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Yusuf said to his brothers, ﴿No reproach﴾, meaning: no rebuke (ta'yir) upon you [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "taghyir," with a ghayn. The correct reading is what I have recorded, with an unpointed ʿayn, which is the plain sense of the language. I have corrected it everywhere it occurs after this.]], and no corruption of what is between me and you of sanctity and the right of brotherhood. Rather, for you I have pardon and forgiveness.

* *

Those who engage in ta'wil have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

19795. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿No reproach upon you﴾: he did not reproach them for their deeds.

19796. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, regarding His words, ﴿No reproach upon you today﴾: he said: Sufyan said: no rebuke (ta'yir) upon you.

19797. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿He said, "No reproach upon you today"﴾: that is, no censure upon you today from me regarding what you did.

19798. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: They apologized to Yusuf, and he said, ﴿No reproach upon you today﴾, meaning: I will not mention your sin to you.

* *

As for His words, ﴿May God forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾: this is a supplication from Yusuf for his brothers, that God forgive them their sin regarding what they did to him and the wrong they committed. He means: may God pardon you your sin and your wrong, and cover it over for you. ﴿And He is the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾: meaning, God is the Most Merciful of the merciful toward whoever repents of his sin [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "mimman tab," and the correct wording is what I have recorded.]] and turns back in obedience to Him by repenting of his disobedience. As follows:

19799. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿May God forgive, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾: when they acknowledged their sin.

**Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿Go with this shirt of mine and cast it over my father's face; he will regain his sight. And bring me all your family﴾ (12:93)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: It is reported that when Yusuf (ﷺ) made himself known to his brothers, he asked them about their father. They said: "His sight has gone from grief!" At that, he gave them his shirt and said to them: ﴿Go with this shirt of mine.﴾

* *

Those who said this:

19800. Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: Amr related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: Yusuf said to them: "What has my father done since I left?" They said: "When Benjamin was taken from him, grief blinded him." He said: ﴿Go with this shirt of mine and cast it over my father's face; he will regain his sight. And bring me all your family.﴾

* *

As for His words ﴿he will regain his sight﴾, meaning: he will return (ya'ud) to sight.[[This meaning is recorded in the lexicons under the root "a-t-a" with the sense of "return" ('ada). It is a rare meaning that none of the lexicographers available to me has noted.]] ﴿And bring me all your family﴾ means: bring me all of your people.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And when the caravan set out, their father said: "I surely smell the scent of Yusuf, unless you think me senile."﴾ (12:94)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When the caravan of Ya'qub's sons departed from Yusuf, heading toward Ya'qub,[[See the explanation of "fasala" in what has preceded, 5:338.]] their father Ya'qub said: ﴿I surely smell the scent of Yusuf.﴾

It is mentioned that the wind asked its Lord for permission to bring Ya'qub the scent of Yusuf before the bearer of good news reached him. Permission was granted, and it brought him the scent.

* *

Those who said this:

19801. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Shurayh told me, from Abu Ayyub al-Hawzani, who related to him, saying: The wind asked permission to bring Ya'qub the scent of Yusuf when he sent the shirt to his father, before the bearer of good news reached him, and it was granted. Ya'qub said: ﴿I surely smell the scent of Yusuf, unless you think me senile.﴾ [[The report 19801: "Abu Shurayh" is Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh ibn Abd Allah al-Ma'afiri, a trustworthy narrator from whom the whole body of compilers related; he has passed under no. 6199. As for "Abu Ayyub al-Hawzani," I have not been able to identify him. Al-Tabari mentioned him by his kunya here and in his History (1:185), and related this report with the same wording.]]

19802. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And when the caravan set out, their father said: "I surely smell the scent of Yusuf, unless you think me senile."﴾ He said: A wind arose and brought him the scent of Yusuf from a distance of eight nights, and he said: ﴿I surely smell the scent of Yusuf, unless you think me senile.﴾ [[The report 19802: "Abu Sinan" is al-Shaybani al-Akbar, Dirar ibn Murra, a trustworthy narrator who has passed under nos. 17336 and 17337. The report will come after no. 19804 and what follows it. "Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl" is Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl al-Anazi, a trustworthy narrator who has passed under no. 13932.]]

19803. Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And when the caravan set out﴾ — he said: A wind arose and brought the scent of Yusuf's shirt from a distance of eight nights.

19804. Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Dirar, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: Ya'qub smelled the scent of Yusuf from a distance of eight nights.

19805. Ibn Wakic and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, both saying: Sufyan ibn Uyayna related to us, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, who said: I was beside Ibn Abbas when he was asked: "From how far did Ya'qub smell the scent of the shirt?" He said: "From a distance of seven or eight nights."

19806. Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, who said: My companions said to me: "You visit Ibn Abbas; ask him for us." I said: "I will not ask him about anything, but I will sit behind the couch, and when the people of Kufa come to him and ask about their needs and mine, I will listen." I heard him say: Ya'qub smelled the scent of Yusuf's shirt from a distance of eight nights. Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl said: I then said: "That is like the distance between Basra and Kufa."

19807. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Ali ibn Asim related to us, from Dirar ibn Murra, from Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: Ya'qub smelled the scent of Yusuf's shirt from a distance of eight nights. He said: I said to myself: "That is like the distance between Basra and Kufa."

19808. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us — and Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: My father related to us [both chains] — from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿I surely smell the scent of Yusuf﴾ — he said: He smelled the scent of Yusuf's shirt from a distance of eight nights. He said: I said to him: "That is as the distance between Basra and Kufa." The wording is that of the report of Abu Kurayb.

19809. al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Asim and Ali related to us, both saying: Shu'ba informed us, saying: Abu Sinan informed me, saying: I heard Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse: ﴿I surely smell the scent of Yusuf﴾ — he said: He smelled its scent from a distance equal to that between Basra and Kufa.

Abu Ja'far said: We have already shown that the root meaning of "tafnid" is corruption. Given that, weakness, senility, lying, loss of mind, and all senses of corruption enter into "tafnid," because the root of all of them is corruption. Corruption in the body is senility, loss of the mind, and weakness; corruption in action is lying and blaming without cause. For this reason Jarir ibn Atiyya said:

O my blamers, leave off reproach and stop; love has lasted long, and you have prolonged the "tafnid."[[His Diwan, p. 169, from a long qasida of his. The verse's reading in the Diwan is an error; the correct form is what is here, "wa aqsira," with the letter ra, from "al-iqsar," meaning to desist from doing something.]]

That is: blame. Thus it has become clear, since the matter is as we have described, that the sayings of those we have mentioned regarding His words ﴿unless you think me senile﴾, despite the variety of their expressions about its interpretation, are close in meaning, and the apparent sense of the revelation admits all of them, since there is no indication in the verse that it refers to some of these meanings rather than others.

**Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿Go with this shirt of mine and cast it over my father's face; he will regain his sight. And bring me all your family﴾ (12:93)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: It is reported that when Yusuf (ﷺ) made himself known to his brothers, he asked them about their father. They said: "His sight has gone from grief!" At that, he gave them his shirt and said to them: ﴿Go with this shirt of mine.﴾

* *

It is a rare meaning that none of the lexicographers available to me has noted.]] ﴿And bring me all your family﴾ means: bring me all of your people.

Abu Ja'far said: We have already shown that the root meaning of "tafnid" is corruption. Given that, weakness, senility, lying, loss of mind, and all senses of corruption enter into "tafnid," because the root of all of them is corruption. Corruption in the body is senility, loss of the mind, and weakness; corruption in action is lying and blaming without cause. For this reason Jarir ibn Atiyya said:

O my blamers, leave off reproach and stop; love has lasted long, and you have prolonged the "tafnid."[[His Diwan, p. 169, from a long qasida of his. The verse's reading in the Diwan is an error; the correct form is what is here, "wa aqsira," with the letter ra, from "al-iqsar," meaning to desist from doing something.]]

That is: blame. **The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He: ﴿They said, "By God, you are surely in your old error."﴾ (12:95)**

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, He says: The ones to whom Ya'qub (Jacob) said, from among his sons, ﴿Indeed, I smell the scent of Yusuf, if you did not think me senile﴾, said: "By God, O man, you are surely in your old error and your old lapse [[In the manuscript: "li-fi hitamika fi dhalika al-qadim", undotted, and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition. But there it is written "khata'ika" in place of "khata'ika"... both have the same meaning. It will come in other places, and I will correct it to the manuscript's form.]] regarding your love for Yusuf and your remembrance of him, not forgetting him or consoling yourself for him."

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said something similar to what we have said.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verses 99–100 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation (*ta'wil*, meaning explanation or interpretation) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So when they entered upon Joseph, he drew his parents to himself and said, "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security." And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. And he said, "O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you from the desert after Satan had caused a breach between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: When Jacob, his sons and their households entered upon Joseph, ﴿he drew his parents to himself﴾, meaning he took his parents into his embrace [[See the explanation of "al-iwa'" (taking in, sheltering) above, p. 169, note 1, and the references there.]] and said to them, ﴿"Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security."﴾

* *

If someone says: How could Joseph say to them, ﴿"Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security,"﴾ after they had already entered it, when God, mighty and majestic, has informed us that when they entered upon Joseph, he drew his parents to himself, and then said this to them?

It is said: The people of interpretation have differed on this.

Some of them said: Jacob and his sons entered Egypt, and Joseph drew his parents to himself before they entered Egypt. They said: This is because Joseph went out to meet his father as an honour to him before he entered Egypt, and drew him to himself, then said to him and to those with him, ﴿"Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security,"﴾ before entering it.

Mention of those who said this:

19877 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: "They brought to him their families and dependants. When they reached Egypt, Joseph spoke to the king who was above him, and he went out, he and the kings, to meet them. When they reached Egypt, he said, ﴿Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security,﴾ = ﴿When they entered upon Joseph, he drew his parents to himself.﴾"

19878 – al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Farqad al-Sabakhi, who said: When the shirt was cast upon his face, he regained his sight, and said, ﴿"Bring me all your family,"﴾ so Jacob and Joseph's brothers were brought. When he drew near, Joseph was informed that he had drawn near to him, so he went out to meet him. He said: The people of Egypt rode with him, for they held him in reverence. When one of them drew near to the other, Jacob was walking, leaning on a man of his sons called Yahudha (Judah). He said: Jacob looked at the horses and the people and said, "O Yahudha, is this the Pharaoh of Egypt?" He said, "No, this is your son!" He said: When each of them drew near to the other, Joseph went to begin with the greeting of peace, but he was prevented from doing so, and Jacob was more entitled to that and more excellent, so he said: "Peace be upon you, O you who removes sorrows from me." He said it thus: "O you who removes sorrows from me." [[He means that he said this with the verb "dhahaba" transitive, from their saying "dhahaba bihi" and "adhhabahu," meaning he removed it, as if he said: "O one who removes sorrows from me." This is a strange reading, and it is noted because of its strangeness. Observe the precision of our transmission even in such reports. But the people of deviation wish to play with these clear proofs, so that people fall into doubt about the reports of their Prophet and the narrations of their transmitters, but God surrounds them.]]

19879 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj said: It reached me that Joseph and the king went out with four thousand men to meet Jacob and his sons.
= He said: Someone who heard Ja'far ibn Sulayman relating from Farqad al-Sabakhi also narrated to me, saying: Joseph went out to meet Jacob, and the people of Egypt rode with Joseph = then he mentioned the rest of the report, similar to the report of al-Harith from 'Abd al-'Aziz.

* *

Others said: Rather, His words ﴿if God wills﴾ are an exception to Jacob's words to his sons: ﴿"I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you."﴾ He said: This is from what is delayed in meaning but placed earlier. They said: The meaning of the speech is: He said, "I will ask my Lord to forgive you, if God wills; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." Then, when they entered upon Joseph, he drew his parents to himself, and said, "Enter Egypt," and he raised his parents.

Mention of those who said this:

19880 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿He said, "I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you soon, if God wills"﴾ = and between that is what has been mentioned by the placement of the Qur'an.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: He means Ibn Jurayj's words: "and between that is what has been mentioned by the placement of the Qur'an," that between His words ﴿"I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you"﴾ and His words ﴿"if God wills"﴾ there has intervened speech that has come between them, and its place, in his view, is to be right after His words ﴿"I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you."﴾

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in our opinion, is what al-Suddi said: that Joseph said this to his parents and to those with them of their children and households before they entered Egypt, when he met them, because this is so in the apparent sense of the revelation. There is no indication to support what Ibn Jurayj said, and there is no justification for moving any part of God's Book from its place or delaying it from its position, except by clear proof.

* *

It is said: By His words ﴿"he drew his parents to himself"﴾ is meant his father and his maternal aunt. Those who held this view said: Joseph's mother had died before, and at that time with Jacob was his aunt, his mother's sister, whom he had married after his mother.

Mention of those who said this:

19881 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿So when they entered upon Joseph, he drew his parents to himself﴾, he said: his father and his maternal aunt.

* *

Others said: Rather, it was his father and his mother.

Mention of those who said this:

* *

His words ﴿"And he said, 'Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security,'"﴾ refer to what you were in, in your desert, of barrenness and famine.

* *

His words ﴿"And he raised his parents upon the throne"﴾ mean: upon the couch, as:

His words ﴿"And they fell down before him in prostration"﴾ mean: Jacob, his sons and his mother fell down in prostration to Joseph.

* *

* *

Those who mentioned "the prostration was a greeting among them" only meant that it was from them as a matter of custom, not in the manner of worship from some of them to others. What shows that this has always been among people's customs, even before Islam, not in the manner of worship from some to others, is the saying of A'sha Bani Tha'laba:

*When he came to us after the drowsiness of the night,*
*we prostrated to him and raised 'ammar* [[The Diwan, p. 39. This verse is from his ode praising Qays ibn Ma'd Yakrib. He had gone out with him on one of his raids, and al-A'sha nearly fell into captivity, but Qays rescued him. He mentioned that and said: "O night that I spent in La'la'," which is like the wandering of a stranger who fears captivity. "When he came to us..." La'la' is a place between Kufa and Basra. In the first verse he mentions his anxiety, his great distress and bewilderment when Qays was delayed, while he himself was nearly falling into the enemy's captivity. When Qays came, he rescued him and those with him, so they prostrated to him and greeted him. The word "'ammar" is disputed in its interpretation: it was said to be the turban or the skullcap; it was also said to be sweet basil, raised for the king by which he is greeted; and it was said: they raised their voices, saying "May God make you live long."
In the printed edition it reads "wa-rafa'na al-'amara," but I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the Diwan and other sources.]]

* *

His words ﴿"O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true"﴾ mean: Joseph said to his father: "O my father, this prostration which you and my mother and my brothers have made to me ﴿= is the interpretation of my vision from before﴾," meaning: what my vision came to, which I had seen [[See the explanation of "ta'wil" above, p. 119, note 1, and the references there.]], namely his vision that he had seen before his brothers' treatment of him, what they did: that eleven stars and the sun and the moon were prostrating to him = ﴿"my Lord has made it true"﴾, meaning: my Lord has realised it, since its interpretation has come about correctly.

* *

[[See the explanation of "nazgh" above, 13:333; and this second verbal noun "al-nuzugh" is one that the lexicons have not mentioned, so it should be confirmed in its place in them.]]

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills﴾, meaning: indeed my Lord is possessed of kindness and skilful arrangement for whatever He wills. 19939 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills﴾: He showed kindness to Yusuf and arranged for him until He brought him out of the prison, brought his family from the desert, and removed from his heart the incitement of Satan and his stirring up of his brothers.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Knowing﴾, of the interests of His creation and other matters, nothing of the beginnings of affairs or their outcomes is hidden from Him, ﴿the All-Wise﴾, in His management.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verses 99–100 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation (*ta'wil*, meaning explanation or interpretation) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So when they entered upon Joseph, he drew his parents to himself and said, "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security." And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. And he said, "O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you from the desert after Satan had caused a breach between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: When Jacob, his sons and their households entered upon Joseph, ﴿he drew his parents to himself﴾, meaning he took his parents into his embrace [[See the explanation of "al-iwa'" (taking in, sheltering) above, p. 169, note 1, and the references there.]] and said to them, ﴿"Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security."﴾

* *

If someone says: How could Joseph say to them, ﴿"Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security,"﴾ after they had already entered it, when God, mighty and majestic, has informed us that when they entered upon Joseph, he drew his parents to himself, and then said this to them?

It is said: The people of interpretation have differed on this.

Some of them said: Jacob and his sons entered Egypt, and Joseph drew his parents to himself before they entered Egypt. They said: This is because Joseph went out to meet his father as an honour to him before he entered Egypt, and drew him to himself, then said to him and to those with him, ﴿"Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security,"﴾ before entering it.

Mention of those who said this:

19877 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: "They brought to him their families and dependants. When they reached Egypt, Joseph spoke to the king who was above him, and he went out, he and the kings, to meet them. When they reached Egypt, he said, ﴿Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security,﴾ = ﴿When they entered upon Joseph, he drew his parents to himself.﴾"

19878 – al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Farqad al-Sabakhi, who said: When the shirt was cast upon his face, he regained his sight, and said, ﴿"Bring me all your family,"﴾ so Jacob and Joseph's brothers were brought. When he drew near, Joseph was informed that he had drawn near to him, so he went out to meet him. He said: The people of Egypt rode with him, for they held him in reverence. When one of them drew near to the other, Jacob was walking, leaning on a man of his sons called Yahudha (Judah). He said: Jacob looked at the horses and the people and said, "O Yahudha, is this the Pharaoh of Egypt?" He said, "No, this is your son!" He said: When each of them drew near to the other, Joseph went to begin with the greeting of peace, but he was prevented from doing so, and Jacob was more entitled to that and more excellent, so he said: "Peace be upon you, O you who removes sorrows from me." He said it thus: "O you who removes sorrows from me." [[He means that he said this with the verb "dhahaba" transitive, from their saying "dhahaba bihi" and "adhhabahu," meaning he removed it, as if he said: "O one who removes sorrows from me." This is a strange reading, and it is noted because of its strangeness. Observe the precision of our transmission even in such reports. But the people of deviation wish to play with these clear proofs, so that people fall into doubt about the reports of their Prophet and the narrations of their transmitters, but God surrounds them.]]

19879 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj said: It reached me that Joseph and the king went out with four thousand men to meet Jacob and his sons.
= He said: Someone who heard Ja'far ibn Sulayman relating from Farqad al-Sabakhi also narrated to me, saying: Joseph went out to meet Jacob, and the people of Egypt rode with Joseph = then he mentioned the rest of the report, similar to the report of al-Harith from 'Abd al-'Aziz.

* *

Others said: Rather, His words ﴿if God wills﴾ are an exception to Jacob's words to his sons: ﴿"I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you."﴾ He said: This is from what is delayed in meaning but placed earlier. They said: The meaning of the speech is: He said, "I will ask my Lord to forgive you, if God wills; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." Then, when they entered upon Joseph, he drew his parents to himself, and said, "Enter Egypt," and he raised his parents.

Mention of those who said this:

19880 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿He said, "I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you soon, if God wills"﴾ = and between that is what has been mentioned by the placement of the Qur'an.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: He means Ibn Jurayj's words: "and between that is what has been mentioned by the placement of the Qur'an," that between His words ﴿"I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you"﴾ and His words ﴿"if God wills"﴾ there has intervened speech that has come between them, and its place, in his view, is to be right after His words ﴿"I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you."﴾

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in our opinion, is what al-Suddi said: that Joseph said this to his parents and to those with them of their children and households before they entered Egypt, when he met them, because this is so in the apparent sense of the revelation. There is no indication to support what Ibn Jurayj said, and there is no justification for moving any part of God's Book from its place or delaying it from its position, except by clear proof.

* *

It is said: By His words ﴿"he drew his parents to himself"﴾ is meant his father and his maternal aunt. Those who held this view said: Joseph's mother had died before, and at that time with Jacob was his aunt, his mother's sister, whom he had married after his mother.

Mention of those who said this:

19881 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿So when they entered upon Joseph, he drew his parents to himself﴾, he said: his father and his maternal aunt.

* *

Others said: Rather, it was his father and his mother.

Mention of those who said this:

19882 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿So when they entered upon Joseph, he drew his parents to himself﴾, he said: his father and his mother.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views is what Ibn Ishaq said, because that is the more common usage among people and the customary meaning of "parents" (*abawayn*) among them, unless what is said about Joseph's mother having died before that is established by a proof that must be accepted, in which case it would then be accepted.

* *

His words ﴿"And he said, 'Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security,'"﴾ refer to what you were in, in your desert, of barrenness and famine.

* *

His words ﴿"And he raised his parents upon the throne"﴾ mean: upon the couch, as:

* *

His words ﴿"And they fell down before him in prostration"﴾ mean: Jacob, his sons and his mother fell down in prostration to Joseph.

* *

When Jacob's sons gathered to him, they entered upon Joseph; when they saw him they fell down before him in prostration, and that was the greeting of kings in that era = his father, his mother and his brothers.

19902 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿And they fell down before him in prostration﴾, he said: The greeting of the people that day was that some of them prostrated to others.

19905 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿And they fell down before him in prostration﴾, he said: A greeting among them.

19906 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And they fell down before him in prostration﴾, he said: That prostration was for his nobility, as the angels prostrated to Adam for his nobility; it was not a prostration of worship.

* *

Those who mentioned "the prostration was a greeting among them" only meant that it was from them as a matter of custom, not in the manner of worship from some of them to others. What shows that this has always been among people's customs, even before Islam, not in the manner of worship from some to others, is the saying of A'sha Bani Tha'laba:

*When he came to us after the drowsiness of the night,*
*we prostrated to him and raised 'ammar* [[The Diwan, p. 39. This verse is from his ode praising Qays ibn Ma'd Yakrib. He had gone out with him on one of his raids, and al-A'sha nearly fell into captivity, but Qays rescued him. He mentioned that and said: "O night that I spent in La'la'," which is like the wandering of a stranger who fears captivity. "When he came to us..." La'la' is a place between Kufa and Basra. In the first verse he mentions his anxiety, his great distress and bewilderment when Qays was delayed, while he himself was nearly falling into the enemy's captivity. When Qays came, he rescued him and those with him, so they prostrated to him and greeted him. The word "'ammar" is disputed in its interpretation: it was said to be the turban or the skullcap; it was also said to be sweet basil, raised for the king by which he is greeted; and it was said: they raised their voices, saying "May God make you live long."
In the printed edition it reads "wa-rafa'na al-'amara," but I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the Diwan and other sources.]]

* *

His words ﴿"O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true"﴾ mean: Joseph said to his father: "O my father, this prostration which you and my mother and my brothers have made to me ﴿= is the interpretation of my vision from before﴾," meaning: what my vision came to, which I had seen [[See the explanation of "ta'wil" above, p. 119, note 1, and the references there.]], namely his vision that he had seen before his brothers' treatment of him, what they did: that eleven stars and the sun and the moon were prostrating to him = ﴿"my Lord has made it true"﴾, meaning: my Lord has realised it, since its interpretation has come about correctly.

* *
