And His saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills﴾, meaning: indeed my Lord is possessed of kindness and skilful arrangement for whatever He wills. [[See the explanation of "al-latif" above, 12:22.]] And of His kindness and skilful arrangement is that He brought me out of the prison and brought my family from the desert after the distance of the dwelling that was between me and them, and after what I had been in of servitude, bondage and captivity, as in what follows:

19939 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills﴾: He showed kindness to Yusuf and arranged for him until He brought him out of the prison, brought his family from the desert, and removed from his heart the incitement of Satan and his stirring up of his brothers.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Knowing﴾, of the interests of His creation and other matters, nothing of the beginnings of affairs or their outcomes is hidden from Him, ﴿the All-Wise﴾, in His management.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 12, verse 101:**

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the dominion and taught me of the interpretation of narrations (ta'wil al-ahadith), Originator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.﴾ (12:101)

Abu Ja'far said: His remembrance, the Exalted, says: Joseph said, after God had gathered his parents and brothers to him, extended over him the worldly blessings and honour that He extended, and established him in the land, longing to meet his righteous forefathers: ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the dominion﴾, meaning: of the kingship of Egypt. ﴿And taught me of the interpretation of narrations﴾, meaning: of the interpretation of dreams. [[See the explanation of "ta'wil" (interpretation) earlier, p. 271, note 1, and the references there.]] Enumerating God's blessings upon him and thanking Him for them. ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾: he says, "O Originator of the heavens and the earth, O their Creator and Maker." [[See the explanation of "fatir" earlier, 15:357, note 2, and the references there.]] ﴿You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter﴾: he says, "You are my Protector in my worldly life against those who oppose me and intend me harm, by Your help, and You nourish me in it with Your blessings, and You are my guardian in the Hereafter by Your grace and mercy." [[See the explanation of "wali" (protector) earlier in the lexical indices (w-l-y).]] ﴿Cause me to die as a Muslim﴾: he says, "Take me to Yourself as a Muslim." [[See the explanation of "tawaffi" (taking to oneself/causing to die) earlier, 15:218, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿And join me with the righteous﴾: he says, "And join me with my righteous forefathers, Abraham, Isaac, and those before them from Your prophets and messengers."

* *

It has been said: no prophet wished for death before Joseph.

Those who said this:

19940 – Ibn Wakî' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the dominion and taught me of the interpretation of narrations﴾, the verse: Ibn 'Abbas used to say: [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "Ibn 'Abbas said, saying", and the correct form is what I have set down; see the following report, no. 19942.]] the first prophet to ask God for death was Joseph.

19941 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding His words ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the dominion﴾ ... the verse: He longed to meet his Lord and loved to join Him and his forefathers, so he asked God to take him and join him with them. No prophet ever asked for death except Joseph, when he said: "My Lord, You have given me of the dominion and taught me of the interpretation of narrations," the verse. Ibn Juraij said: In some recitations of the Qur'an, among the prophets: "Take me (tawaffani)." [[I have not found any evidence in the Qur'an for what Ibn Juraij said! Perhaps it is an error, for the prohibition against wishing for death is explicit in the Sunnah.]]

19942 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous﴾: when He gathered his household and cooled his eye, and he was then immersed in the growth of the world, its dominion and its abundance, [[In the printed edition: "immersed in the bounties of the world"; in the manuscript: "immersed in the bounties of the world", undotted, and this is the correct reading. By "al-nabt" (growth) here is meant abundant and plentiful wealth and flourishing blessing. It has come in a hadith that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to some Arabs: "Are you a people of house or of growth?" They said: "We are a people of house and of growth." And they explained it as: we are at the extreme of nobility and at the extreme of growth, i.e., wealth grows at our hands.

And what I have said is more sound as an interpretation of this hadith and of this report.]] so he longed for the righteous before him. Ibn 'Abbas used to say: no prophet ever wished for death before Joseph.

19943 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr informed us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, who said: When He gathered his household for Joseph and blessings were perfected upon him, he asked to meet his Lord, saying: ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the dominion and taught me of the interpretation of narrations, Originator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.﴾ Qatadah said: No one has ever wished for death, prophet or otherwise, except Joseph.

19944 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: More than one person narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: that Joseph, the prophet (ﷺ), when He gathered him with his father and brothers, and he was then king of Egypt, longed for God and for his righteous forefathers, Abraham and Isaac, and said: ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the dominion and taught me of the interpretation of narrations, Originator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.﴾

19945 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And taught me of the interpretation of narrations﴾: he said: the explanation (al-'ibarah).

19946 – It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous﴾: he says, "Cause me to die in Your obedience, and forgive me when You take me."

19947 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Joseph said, when he saw what he saw of God's honour and grace upon him and upon his family, when God gathered his household for him, returned him to his father, and brought him together with him in what he was in of dominion and joy: ﴿O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of old; my Lord has made it true﴾, to His words ﴿Indeed He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.﴾ Then Joseph became mindful and mentioned that what he was in of this world was perishing and passing, so he said: ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the dominion and taught me of the interpretation of narrations, Originator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.﴾

* *

It is mentioned that the sons of Jacob, who did to Joseph what they did, were asked forgiveness for by their father; God then turned to them, pardoned them, and forgave their sin.

Those who said this:

19948 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Salih al-Murri, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Indeed God, blessed and exalted, when He gathered Jacob's household and cooled his eye, his sons withdrew to speak privately, and some of them said to others: "Do you not know what you did, and what the old man suffered from you, and what Joseph suffered from you?" They said: "Yes!" He said: "Then their pardon of you deceives you; how will you face your Lord?" So their matter settled upon going to the old man, and they sat before him, while Joseph sat beside his father. They said: "O our father, we have come to you about a matter we have never come to you about like it, and a calamity has befallen us the like of which has never befallen us!" until they stirred him, and the prophets are the most merciful of creatures. He said: "What is wrong with you, my sons?" They said: "Do you not know what we did toward you, and what we did toward our brother Joseph?" He said: "Yes!" They said: "Have you not both pardoned us?" They said: "Yes!" They said: "Your pardon will not avail us anything if God has not pardoned us!" He said: "What do you want, my sons?" They said: "We want you to ask God on our behalf. When the revelation comes to you from God that He has pardoned what we did, our eyes will be cooled and our hearts will be at rest; otherwise there will never be any coolness of eye for us in this world." He said: The old man rose, faced the qibla, and stood; Joseph stood behind his father, and they stood behind the two of them, humbled and humble. He said: He supplicated and Joseph said "Amin," but he was not answered concerning them for twenty years. [Salih al-Murri said: "He kept them in fear."] He said: Until, at the end of the twenty years, Gabriel (ﷺ) descended upon Jacob, peace be upon him, and said: "Indeed God, blessed and exalted, has sent me to you to give you good news that He has answered your supplication concerning your sons, that He has pardoned what they did, and that He has taken their covenant after you for prophethood." [[The report 19948: "Salih al-Murri" is "Salih ibn Bashir ibn Wada' al-Murri," a denounced narrator, a storyteller whose narrations are abandoned; mentioned under no. 9234.

And "Yazid al-Raqashi" is "Yazid ibn Aban al-Raqashi," a storyteller, whose narrations are abandoned; mentioned several times before, the last being no. 11408.

And this report is ruined because of these two abandoned storytellers, Salih al-Murri and Yazid al-Raqashi.]]

19949 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Harith narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu 'Imran al-Juni, who said: By God, if the killing of Joseph had gone through, God would have made them all enter the Fire. But God, may His praise be great, held back Joseph's soul so that His command concerning him might be fulfilled, and as mercy toward them. Then he says: By God, God did not relate their story to reproach them with it; indeed they were prophets, among the people of Paradise. Rather, God related their story to us so that His servant would not despair.

* *

It is mentioned that Jacob died before Joseph, and he entrusted Joseph with a bequest and commanded him to bury him beside the grave of his father Isaac.

Those who said this:

19950 – Ibn Wakî' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, who said: When death came to Jacob, he bequeathed to Joseph that he should bury him beside Abraham and Isaac. When he died, myrrh was applied to him, and he was carried to Syria. He said: When they reached that place, 'Isau (Esau), the brother of Jacob, [[In the printed edition: "'Ays"; I have set down what is in the manuscript, and later it will come as "al-'Ays" with the definite article; in the people's book he is "'Esau," who was the eldest son of Isaac and the brother of Jacob.]] came and said: "He outdid me in the supplication; by God, he will not outdo me at the grave!" He refused to let them bury him. When they were delayed, Hisham ibn Dan ibn Jacob [[In the printed edition: "Hisham ibn Dar"; it did not correctly read the manuscript, and Jacob's son in the people's book is "Dan," as I have set down.

And this "Hisham" is, in the people's book, "Hushaym."]] said, for he was deaf, to some of his brothers: "Why will my grandfather not be buried?" They said: "This is his uncle who prevents it!" He said: "Show me where he is." When he saw him, Hisham raised his hand and struck the head of 'Ays with a blow, so that his eyes fell upon the thigh of Jacob. So they buried them in one grave.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 102:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿That is of the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. And you were not with them when they were resolved upon their plan while they were scheming.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: This report that I have informed you of, concerning Joseph, his father Jacob, his brothers, and all else that is in this surah, is ﴿of the news of the unseen﴾, meaning: of the reports of the unseen that you did not witness and did not observe. [[See the explanation of "nabaʾ" (news) and "ghayb" (the unseen) in the linguistic indexes above, under the roots n-b-ʾ and gh-y-b.]] But We reveal it to you and make it known to you, so that We may strengthen your heart with it, fortify your breast, and that you may be patient over the harm that befell you from your people for the sake of God, and know that the messengers of God before you, when they were patient over what befell them in that regard, and took pardon, and were commanded to enjoin what is right, and turned away from the ignorant, they gained victory, were supported with triumph, were established in the lands, and overcame those among their enemies and the enemies of the religion of God whom they confronted. God, blessed and exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Follow their example, O Muhammad, and trace their traces. ﴿And you were not with them when they were resolved upon their plan while they were scheming.﴾ He says: You were not present with the brothers of Joseph when they resolved and their opinions agreed and their determinations were firm to throw Joseph into the bottom of the well. [[See the explanation of "ijmaʿ" (resolve/consensus) in the earlier volumes: vol. 15, pp. 147, 148, 573.]] That was their scheming, of which God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿while they were scheming﴾, as follows:

1995 1: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And you were not with them﴾, meaning Muhammad ﷺ, saying: You were not with them when they were throwing him into the bottom of the well, ﴿while they were scheming﴾, that is, against Joseph.

1995 2: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta' al-Khurasani, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And you were not with them when they were resolved upon their plan while they were scheming﴾, the verse, he said: They were the sons of Jacob.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 103:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you should strive eagerly, are not believers﴾ (Yusuf 12:103).

Abu Ja'far said: He, mighty is His praise, says: And most of the polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, are not [believers], even if you were eager that they believe in you, confirm you, and follow what you have brought them from your Lord, they would not be confirmers of you nor followers of you.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you do not ask them for any reward for it. It is only a reminder for the worlds.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to Muhammad ﷺ: And you do not ask them, O Muhammad, these people who deny your prophethood, refuse to affirm you and to acknowledge what you have brought them from your Lord, for anything in return for what you call them to, namely sincerely worshipping your Lord, abandoning the worship of idols, and obeying the Most Merciful. ﴿Any reward﴾ means: any recompense or payment from them. [[See the explanation of "al-ajr" (reward) in the lexical indexes of earlier volumes, under (a-j-r).]] Rather, your reward and the wage of your work are with Allah. He means: you do not ask them for a recompense for this, so that they would say to you: "You only want by calling us to follow you that we give up our wealth to you if you ask us for it." Since you do not ask them for this, it was incumbent upon them to know that you call them to what you call them to only in obedience to your Lord's command and as sincere counsel to them, and that they should not suspect you of deceit.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿It is only a reminder for the worlds﴾, Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: What your Lord has sent you with, O Muhammad, of prophethood and messengership, ﴿is only a reminder﴾, meaning: only an admonition and reminder for the worlds, that they may take heed and be reminded by it. [[See the explanation of "al-dhikr" (reminder) in the lexical indexes of earlier volumes, under (dh-k-r).]]

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, mighty and majestic, says: How many a sign and a lesson and a proof there is in the heavens and the earth belonging to God. [See the explanation of "ka'ayyin" (how many) above, 7:263.] These include the sun, the moon and the stars and similar signs of the heavens, and the mountains, seas, plants, trees and other signs of the earth. ﴿They pass by them﴾ means they witness them, yet they pass by them turning away from them, not taking heed of them, and not reflecting on them and on what they indicate of the oneness of their Lord, and that divinity is fitting only for the One, the Subduer, who created them and created everything and arranged it.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said so:

19953 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by﴾. In the codex of Ibn Mas'ud it reads "yamshuna 'alayha" (they walk upon it). "The heavens and the earth are two great signs."

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted says: Most of these people, whose description He mentioned in His words, ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while turning away from it﴾ [12:105], do not affirm faith in God, that He is their Creator, their Provider, and the Creator of everything, ﴿except that they are associating partners [with Him]﴾ [12:106], in their worship of idols and statues, their taking of other gods besides Him, and their claim that He has a son. Exalted is God above what they say.

* *

Those who engage in ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

19954. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: Imran ibn Uyayna told us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating partners [with Him]﴾, he said: This is their faith: when they are asked, "Who created the heavens? Who created the earth? Who created the mountains?" they say, "God." And yet they are associators.

19955. Hannad told us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas told us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, regarding His words, ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating partners [with Him]﴾, he said: You ask them, "Who created them? Who created the heavens and the earth?" and they say, "God." That is their faith in God, while they worship other than Him.

19956. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Wakī' told us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Amir and Ikrimah, regarding ﴿And most of them do not believe in God...﴾, the two of them said: They know that He is their Lord and that He created them, yet they associate others with Him.

19957. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: My father told us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Amir and Ikrimah, similar to that.

19958. ... He said: Ibn Numayr told us, from Nadr, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating partners [with Him]﴾, he said: This is their faith: when they are asked, "Who created the heavens?" they say, "God." And when they are asked, "Who created them?" they say, "God." Yet they still associate others with Him.

19959. ... He said: Abu Nu'aym told us, from al-Fadl ibn Yazid al-Thumali, from Ikrimah, who said: It is the saying of God: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "God"﴾ [31:25; 39:38]. So when they are asked about God and His attributes, they describe Him with other than His attributes, they ascribe a son to Him, and they associate others with Him.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Shababa told us, saying: Warqa' told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating partners [with Him]﴾, [he said:] their faith is their saying, "God is our Creator, who provides for us and causes us to die."

19961. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating partners [with Him]﴾: their faith is their saying, "God is our Creator, who provides for us and causes us to die."

19962. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating partners [with Him]﴾: their faith is their saying, "God is our Creator, who provides for us and causes us to die." This is a faith alongside the association of worshipping other than Him.

He said: Ishaq told us, saying: Abdullah told us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating partners [with Him]﴾, he said: Their faith is their saying, "God is our Creator, who provides for us and causes us to die."

19964. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: Hani' ibn Sa'id and Abu Mu'awiya told us, from Hajjaj, from al-Qasim, from Mujahid, who said: They say, "God is our Lord, and He provides for us," and yet they associate others with Him.

19965. Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: Their faith is their saying, "God is our Creator, who provides for us and causes us to die."

He said: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Abu Tumayla told us, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Ikrimah and Mujahid and Amir, that they said regarding this verse, ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating partners [with Him]﴾: No one exists who does not know that God created him and created the heavens and the earth. He says: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "God"﴾ [31:25; 39:38], ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "God"﴾ [43:87], and if you asked them who provides for you from the sky and the earth, they would surely say, "God."

19970. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Amr ibn Awn told us, saying: Hushaym told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: They used to associate others with Him in their talbiyah (the pilgrims' chant).

19971. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: Ibn Numayr told us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ata': ﴿And most of them do not believe in God...﴾, the verse, he said: They know that God is their Lord, yet they associate others with Him.

Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Amr ibn Awn told us, saying: Hushaym told us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ata', regarding His words, ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating partners [with Him]﴾, he said: They know that God is their Creator and their Provider, yet they associate others with Him.

19973. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: He said: I heard Ibn Zayd say: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God...﴾, the verse, he said: No one worships alongside God other than Him except that he is a believer in God, and knows that God is his Lord, and that God is his Creator and Provider, yet he associates others with Him. Do you not see how Abraham said: ﴿Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your ancestors? Indeed they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds﴾ [26:75–77]? Do you not see how the Arabs used to say in their talbiyah: "Here I am, O God, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You, You possess it and what it possesses"? The polytheists used to say this.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 12, Verse 107:

The explanation (ta'wil, interpretation) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Do they then feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming punishment from Allah, or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they are unaware?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His Majesty, may His praise be exalted, says: Do these people feel secure, those who do not acknowledge that Allah is their Lord except while they are polytheists in worshipping other than Him? ﴿That there will not come upon them an overwhelming punishment from Allah﴾, one that envelops them, from the punishment and chastisement of Allah, because of their polytheism toward Allah [[See the explanation of "al-ghashiyah" (the overwhelming) above, 12:435, 436.]], ﴿or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly﴾, the Resurrection coming upon them unexpectedly while they remain in their polytheism and disbelief in their Lord [[See the explanation of "al-sa'ah" (the Hour) above, 11:324. And the explanation of "al-baghtah" (suddenly) above, 11:325, 360, 368 / 12:576 / 13:297.]], so that Allah, mighty and majestic, makes them abide forever in its Fire, while they do not know of its coming or its occurrence.

* *

Those who engaged in ta'wil (exegesis) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 108:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and whoever follows me. And glory be to Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say, O Muhammad: This is the call to which I invite, and the path I am upon, of calling to the Oneness of Allah and sincerely devoting worship to Him alone, apart from the gods and idols, and of attaining obedience to Him and abandoning disobedience to Him⦆ — ﴿my way﴾ (sabili), meaning my path and my call. [[See the discussion of "al-sabil" in the preceding linguistic indices (s-b-l).]] ﴿I invite to Allah alone, having no partner⦆ — ﴿with insight﴾ (ʿala basirah), meaning with that, and with certain knowledge from me of it, I myself; and those who follow me and believe in me and affirm me also invite to Him with insight. [[See the discussion of "al-basirah" previously: 12:23, 24 / 13:343, 344.]] ﴿And glory be to Allah⦆ — His exalted remembrance says to him: Say, declaring Allah free of imperfection and magnifying Him above having any partner in His dominion or any worshipped one besides Him in His authority. ﴿And I am not of those who associate⦆ — meaning: I am innocent of the people who associate others with Him; I am not one of them, and they are not of me. [[See the discussion of "subhan" previously in the linguistic indices (s-b-ḥ).]]

* *

Those who interpreted the verse said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

19981 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding His saying: ﴿Say: This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight⦆, he said: This is my call.

19982 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Say: This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight⦆, he said: "This is my way" — this is my command, my sunnah, and my method. ﴿Invite to Allah with insight, I and whoever follows me⦆ — he said: And it is a right, by Allah, upon whoever follows him that he invite to what he invited to, and remind by the Qur'an and admonition, and forbid the disobedience of Allah.

19983 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding His saying: ﴿Say: This is my way⦆, he said: This is my call.

19984 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi': ﴿Say: This is my way⦆, he said: This is my call.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 109:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿We sent not before you [as messengers] except men to whom We revealed, from among the people of the towns. Have they not traveled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Then will you not reason?﴾ [12:109]

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And We did not send, O Muhammad, before you except men, not women nor angels," ﴿to whom We revealed﴾ Our signs, by calling them to obey Us and to devote worship to Us alone, ﴿from among the people of the towns﴾, meaning: from among the people of the cities (amsar), not the people of the desert (al-badawi). [See the explanation of "al-qaryah" (town) above, 8:453 / 12:299.] As:

19985 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed from among the people of the towns﴾, that they were more knowledgeable and more forbearing than the people of the 'amud [("ahl al-'amud": the 'amud (with a fatha on the 'ayn) is the wooden pole standing in the middle of a tent, and akhbiyah are the tents of the desert dwellers. So "ahl al-'amud" means the people of the desert, as the context here indicates, and as Ibn Zayd explained in his tafsir of this verse when he said: "The people of the towns are more knowledgeable and more forbearing than the people of the desert" (Tafsir Abi Hayyan 5:353). Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Asas: "Those who live in tents are called ahl 'amud, ahl 'imad, and ahl 'imd." The author of al-Lisan also cited a verse: "The people of the 'amud are not of our people, nor are the camels grazed by us of any worth." This is the saying of a man who disowns being of the desert people, so he mentions the qualities that desert people are known for and by which they are desert people.]].

*  *

As for His words: ﴿Have they not traveled through the land and seen﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Have these polytheists who deny you, O Muhammad, and reject your prophethood, and reject what you have brought them of the oneness of Allah and sincere obedience and worship to Him, not traveled in the land ﴿and seen how was the end of those before them﴾, when they denied Our messengers? Did We not inflict Our punishment upon them, destroying them by it, and save Our messengers and their followers from it, so that they would reflect upon that and take heed?

*  *

Those who said this:

19986 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said regarding His words: ﴿We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed﴾, he said: They said: ("Allah did not send down anything upon a human [6:91]"). He said: And His words: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you should strive, will not be believers. And you do not ask them for it any reward﴾ [12:103-104], and His words: ﴿And how many a sign within the heavens and the earth they pass by it﴾ [12:105], and His words: ﴿Do they feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming punishment from Allah﴾ [12:107], and His words: ﴿Have they not traveled through the land and seen?﴾ — whom We destroyed? He said: All of that He said to the Quraysh: "Have they not traveled through the land and looked into their remains, so that they would take heed and reflect?"

*  *

As for His words: ﴿And the home of the Hereafter is better﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: This is Our action in this world toward the people of Our guardianship and obedience: that when Our punishment descended upon the people of Our disobedience and of associating others with Us, We saved them from it; and what is in the Hereafter is better for them.

*  *

[The omission of what we have mentioned is sufficient by the indication of His words: ﴿And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾, and "the home" is idafa-ed to "the Hereafter," which is itself "the Hereafter," because their wording differs, as it is said: ﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty﴾ [56:95], and as it is said: "I came to you the year of the first, and the night of the first, and the day of Thursday" [This is a summary of al-Farra's words in Ma'ani al-Qur'an regarding the explanation of the verse.] and as the poet said: [The speaker of this is unknown.]

Do you praise Fa'sa and disparage 'Abs? Lo, may Allah's mother [be bereaved] of you, you hybrid!
And if the dwellings of 'Abs became desolate upon you, you would know humiliation with the certainty of knowledge.
[Both verses were transmitted by al-Farra in Ma'ani al-Qur'an regarding the explanation of the verse. In the printed edition it read "wa law afzat" which is utter error, and in the manuscript "wa law afarat" without dots, which is a misreading. "Al-hajin" is the offspring of an Arab with a non-Arab woman. "Aqwat al-dar" means it became desolate and emptied of its inhabitants. The apparent meaning of this poem is that its speaker said it about a man of the Banu 'Abs who was a hybrid, and he praised Fa'sa and disparaged his own people for forsaking him. So he says to him: If 'Abs departed from its place and left you alone in it, you would know humiliation with the certainty of knowledge.]

That is: knowing it with certainty. [In the printed edition and manuscript: "'irfanan bihi," and what appears to be correct is what was established. In al-Farra: "'irfanan yaqinan" without "lahu," which is better.]

*  *

Abu Ja'far said: So the interpretation of the statement is: "And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah," by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions.

*  *

As for His words: ﴿Then will you not reason?﴾, He says: Will these polytheists not truly reason about what We say to them and inform them of, regarding the evil end of disbelief and the outcome to which the state of its people leads, along with what they have witnessed, seen and heard of what befell the disbelieving nations before them who denied the messengers of their Lord? [In the printed edition: "bima qablahum min al-umam," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 110 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our help came to them, and whomever We willed was delivered. And Our punishment is not averted from the criminal people.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns﴾. They called those to whom We sent them, and they denied them and rejected what they brought from God. ﴿Until, when the messengers despaired﴾, those whom We sent to them, from among them, that they would believe in God [see the explanation of "istay'asa" (despaired) above, pp. 203, 204, and the indexes of language, root y-'-s], and would confirm them in what they brought from God. ﴿And thought that they had been denied﴾: those nations who denied, to whom We sent them, thought that the messengers whom We sent had been denying them regarding what they had told them about God, namely His promise to them of their victory over them. ﴿Our help came to them﴾.

He said: Hammad narrated to us, from Kulthum ibn Jabr, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said to me: A leader of your leaders asked me about this verse, so I said: the messengers despaired of their people, and their people thought that the messengers had lied. [Note: See the two preceding reports, nos. 20008, 20009.]

20015 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied﴾: the messengers despaired that their people would believe in them, and their people, the polytheists, thought that the messengers had lied about what God had promised them of His help against them, and that they had been broken to. He recited: ﴿Our help came to them﴾, and said: then the victory came to the messengers at that time. He said: Ubayy used to recite it: "kudhdhibu" [with the passive, "they were denied"].

20016 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Ayyub ibn Abi Safwan, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, that he said: ﴿Until, when the messengers despaired﴾ of the faith of their people = ﴿and thought that they had been denied﴾, and the people thought that they had lied to them regarding what they brought them. [Note: "Sa'id" is "Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arouba". As for "Abu al-Mutawakkil", I do not know who he is; it will come that al-Bukhari and Ibn Abi Hatim have "al-Mutawakkil", yet I do not know exactly who he is. "Ayyub ibn Abi Safwan": this is how "Ayyub ibn Safwan" appears in al-Bukhari's Tarikh al-Kabir, i.e., it is also said thus; Ibn Abi Hatim mentions only "Ayyub ibn Safwan, client of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith", and there is much confusion in Ibn Abi Hatim's entry. Al-Bukhari said in his entry: "'Abd al-A'la said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Mutawakkil, from Ayyub ibn Safwan, client of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Hashimi, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Umm Hani', from the Prophet (ﷺ)", meaning concerning the Duha prayer. Then he mentioned it in another chain thus: "Ayyub ibn Abi Safwan", as here. Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Ayyub ibn Safwan, client of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, narrated from al-Mutawakkil, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith; Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arouba narrated from him", and this is a confusion, and I think the correct version is: "Al-Mutawakkil narrated from him, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, and Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arouba narrated from al-Mutawakkil." This is a report whose chain is problematic, as you see, and we have no way out of it until we find something that guides to the correct reading.]

20017 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: Their people thought that their messengers had lied to them regarding what they had promised them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 110 (part 2 of 3):

20018 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Jahsh ibn Ziyad al-Dabbi, from Tamim ibn Hadhlam, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Mas'ud say concerning this verse: "until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied," he said: The messengers despaired of their people's faith, that they would believe in them, and their people thought, when the matter was delayed, that the messengers had been denied, with the light pronunciation (takhfif). [[The report: 20018 - "Jahsh ibn Ziyad al-Dabbi," who narrated from Tamim ibn Hadhlam; Sufyan al-Thawri, Jarir, Muhammad ibn Fudayl and Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated from him. They mentioned no criticism of him. He is listed in al-Kabir 1/2/251 and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/550.
And "Tamim ibn Hadhlam al-Dabbi," one of the companions of Ibn Mas'ud, reliable, few narrations, the group (of compilers) narrated from him. It has passed under no. 13623, in the biography of his son.]]
20019 - Abu al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu al-Mu'alla, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning his saying: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired﴾, he said: The messengers despaired of the victory of their people, and the people of the messengers thought that the messengers had denied them. [[The report: 20019 - "Abu al-Mu'alla," is al-Attar, Yahya ibn Maymun; it has passed shortly under no. 20010.]]
20020 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Thabit narrated to us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "until, when the messengers despaired that they would believe them, and their people thought that the messengers had denied them." [[The report: 20020 - "Amr ibn Thabit ibn Hormuz al-Bakri," narrated from his father, very weak, not reliable, has passed under nos. 641, 680, 5969.
And his father "Thabit ibn Hormuz," al-Haddad, Abu al-Miqdam, reliable, has passed under nos. 641, 680, 5969, 16645.]]
20021 - ... He said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: "until, when the messengers despaired that their people would confirm them, and their people thought that the messengers had denied them."
20022 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak concerning his saying: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired﴾, he says: They despaired of their people responding to them and believing in them; "and they thought," he says: the people of the messengers thought that the messengers had denied them the promise.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The reading according to this interpretation that we have mentioned, in his saying ﴿kudhdhibu﴾, is with a damma on the kaf and the light pronunciation of the dhal. This is also the reading of some of the Qur'an readers of Madinah and the general body of the Qur'an readers of Kufa.
We chose this interpretation and this reading because it follows his saying: (And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns. Have they not travelled in the land and seen how was the end of those before them?), so this is evidence that the despair of the messengers was from the faith of their people who were destroyed, and that the pronoun in his saying ﴿and they thought that they had been denied﴾ refers only to those before them from the destroyed nations. This becomes clearer also by God's following, in the context of the report about the messengers and their nations, his saying: ﴿so whom We will is saved﴾, since those who were destroyed are the ones who thought that the messengers had denied them, [[In the manuscript: "inna alladhina uhlikû", and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]] so they denied them, thinking that they had denied them.
* *
Some of those who read this reading went in a direction other than the interpretation we chose, and directed its meaning to: until, when the messengers despaired of the faith of their people, and the messengers thought that they had been denied in what they were promised of victory.
Mention of those who said that:
20023 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Juraij narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: Ibn Abbas read: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied﴾, and said: They were human beings; they were weakened and despaired.
20024 - ... He said: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me, from Ibn Abbas, that he read: ﴿and thought that they had been denied﴾, with the light pronunciation. Ibn Juraij said: I say as one says: "akhlifu" (they were made to break the promise). Abdullah said: Ibn Abbas said to me: They were human beings. And Ibn Abbas recited: ﴿until the Messenger and those who believed with him say: When is the help of God? Certainly the help of God is near﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 214] = Ibn Juraij said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: He takes it to mean that they were weakened, so they thought they had been made to break the promise.
20025 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah, that he read: (until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied), with the light pronunciation. Abdullah said: That is what you dislike.
20026 - ... He said: Abu Amir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, that a man asked Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied﴾, he said: That is what you dislike = with the light pronunciation.
20027 - ... He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied﴾. I said: "kudhibu"! He said: Yes, were they not human beings?
20028 - Al-Harith narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his saying: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied﴾, he said: They were human beings; they had thought.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: This is an interpretation and a saying; other than it of the interpretations is more correct in my view, [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "this is the interpretation and saying of other than..." with the addition "ahl" (people of), which does not hold, for if he meant that he would have said "and the saying of other than them", since the report was received from Abdullah ibn Abbas and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. What confirms my omission of this addition is his later saying: "and its opposite of the saying...".]] and its opposite of the saying is more fitting to the attributes of the prophets and messengers, if it were permissible that they doubt God's promise to them and be uncertain of the truth of His report, while they witnessed of the proofs and signs of God what the people they were sent to did not witness, so that they would be excused in that; but the people they were sent to are more deserving of excuse than them. [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "an al-mursal ilayhim" without the fa', which is required in the answer of the condition in his saying: "and the messengers, if it is permissible that they doubt ... then the people they were sent to ...".]] This is a saying which, if anyone says it, its matter is not hidden.
* *
This interpretation that we mentioned last from Ibn Abbas was mentioned to Aisha, and she rejected it most strongly, as has been related to us.
Mention of the transmission of that from her, may God be pleased with her:
20029 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Juraij narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: Ibn Abbas read: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied﴾, and said: They were human beings, they were weakened and despaired. Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: So I mentioned that to Urwah, and he said: Aisha said: Far be it from God! God never told His Messenger anything except that he knew it would happen before he died, but trials continued upon the messengers until the prophets thought that those who followed them had denied them. So she used to read it: "qad kudhdhibu", with emphasis. [[The report: 20029 - "Uthman ibn Umar ibn Fars al-Abdi," reliable, the group narrated from him, has passed many times. Ibn Juraij is the well-known Imam.
And "Ibn Abi Mulaykah" is "Abdullah ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah," the group narrated from him, has passed many times.
This is a sound chain, related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 8: 140), through the route of Ibrahim ibn Musa, from Hisham, from Ibn Juraij.]]
20030 - ... He said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me that Ibn Abbas read: ﴿and thought that they had been denied﴾, with the light pronunciation. Abdullah said: Then Ibn Abbas said to me: They were human beings, and Ibn Abbas recited: ﴿until the Messenger and those who believed with him say: When is the help of God? Certainly the help of God is near﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 214] = Ibn Juraij said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: He takes it to mean that they were weakened, so they thought they had been made to break the promise. Ibn Juraij said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: Urwah informed me from Aisha that she opposed that and rejected it, and said: God did not promise Muhammad ﷺ anything except that he knew it would be, until he died; but trials continued upon the messengers until they thought that those with them among the believers had denied them. Ibn Abi Mulaykah said in the hadith of Urwah: Aisha used to read it: "wa-zannu annahum qad kudhdhibu," with emphasis, for denial. [[The report: 20030 - a repetition of the previous one; it is a sound chain.]]
20031 - ... He said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Salih ibn Kaysan narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, from Aisha, who said: I said to her the saying of God: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied﴾, and she said: Aisha said: They were certain that they had been denied. I said: "kudhibu." She said: Far be it from God, the messengers did not think that of their Lord; they were only followers of the messengers, and when the revelation was delayed from them and the trial intensified upon them, the messengers thought that their followers had denied them = ﴿Our help came to them﴾. [[The report: 20031 - with this chain, from "Abd al-Aziz ibn Abd Allah, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from Salih ibn Kaysan," related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 8: 277-279) = in full.
The wording of Abu Ja'far is extremely abridged. Ibn Hajar wrote an excellent, comprehensive commentary on this hadith.]]
20032 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aisha, who said: "until, when the man despaired of those among their people who denied them, that they would confirm them, and the messengers thought that those among their people who had believed had denied them, then God's help came to them at that time." [[The report: 20032 - and this is a sound chain to Aisha.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: This is what has been related on this matter from Aisha, except that she used to read "kudhdhibu," with emphasis and a damma on the kaf, in the sense of what we mentioned from her: that the messengers thought of their followers who had believed in them that they had denied them, so they turned away from their religion, out of impatience for the victory.
We have already explained that what we choose from the reading and interpretation in this word, apart from it, is particular to this letter.
* *
Others who read his saying "kudhdhibu" with a damma on the kaf and emphasis on the dhal said the meaning is: until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing in them and confirming them, and the messengers thought, in the sense of "and were certain," that their nations had denied them, our help came to the messengers. They said that "thinking" here means "knowing," from the saying of the poet: [[He is Duraid ibn al-Simmah.]]
So think of them, with two thousand armed horsemen, girded, whose nobles are among the coated armour of the Persian mail.
[[It has passed with a different transmission of the verse, vol. 2: p. 18, note 1, and I explained that there.]]
* *
Mention of those who said that:
20033 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan = and this is the saying of Qatadah =: until, when the messengers despaired of the faith of their people, and thought that they had been denied, meaning: they were certain that there was no good nor faith among their people = ﴿Our help came to them﴾.
* *
20034 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired﴾, he said: of their people = ﴿and thought that they had been denied﴾, he said: and knew that they had been denied = ﴿Our help came to them﴾.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: With this reading, the general body of the readers of Madinah, Basra and Syria used to read, meaning with emphasis on the dhal of "kudhdhibu" and a damma on its kaf.
* *
This interpretation to which al-Hasan and Qatadah went, when read with emphasis on the dhal and a damma on the kaf, contradicts all the sayings we have mentioned from all the Companions whose sayings we have related, because none of them directed "thinking" in this place to the meaning of knowledge and certainty, whereas "thinking" is used by the Arabs in the place of knowledge concerning what is known from report or from a source other than direct witnessing and observation. As for what is known through direct witnessing and observation, "thinking" is not used for it; one hardly says "I think myself alive, and I think myself a human being," meaning "I know myself to be a human being, and I know myself to be alive." The messengers whose nations denied them, there is no doubt that they were witnesses to their nations, and that their nations' denial of them was heard by them, so it would be said of them: they thought about their nations that they had denied them.
* *
A saying was related from Mujahid on this matter which is contrary to all the sayings of the earlier authorities whom we named and whose sayings we mentioned, and an interpretation contrary to theirs, and a reading other than the reading of all of them. It is that, as was reported from him, he used to read: "wa-zannu annahum qad kadhabu," with a fatha on the kaf and the dhal, and light pronunciation of the dhal.
Mention of the transmission from him in this:
20035 - Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Abu Ubayd narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, that he read it: "kadhabu," with a fatha on the kaf, with light pronunciation.
* *
= And he interpreted it as follows:
20036 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: the man despaired that their people would be punished, and their people thought that the messengers had lied = ﴿Our help came to them﴾; he said: Our help came to the messengers. Mujahid said: He said in "al-Mu'min" [[" al-Mu'min" is Surat Ghafir, i.e., the Surah of the Believer of the family of Pharaoh.]] ﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what knowledge they had﴾, he said: their saying: "We have more knowledge than them, and we will not be punished." And His saying: ﴿and what they used to mock encompassed them﴾ [Surat Ghafir: 83], he said: what their messengers brought of the truth encompassed them.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: This is a reading I do not consider permissible to recite with, [[In the printed edition alone: "and this reading," which made the sentence meaningless.]] because of the consensus of the authority of the readers of the cities against it. Even if the reading were permissible, it would allow an interpretation better than what Mujahid interpreted, namely: until, when the messengers despaired of the punishment of God for their people who denied them, and the messengers thought that their people had lied and forged against God in their disbelief in them = and "thinking" would then be directed toward the meaning of knowledge, as Hasan and Qatadah interpreted.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿so whom We will is saved﴾, the readers differed in its recitation.
The general body of the readers of Madinah, Makkah and Iraq read: "fa-nunjī man nashā'," with light pronunciation and two nuns, [[In the printed edition the word "light pronunciation" was dropped; in the manuscript it read: "fa-nunjī, light, man nashā', with two nuns"; what I have written is more appropriate and better.]] meaning: so We save whom We will of Our messengers and of the believers in Us, but not the disbelievers who denied Our messengers, when Our help came to the messengers.
* *
Those who read it this way argued that it was written in the mushaf with one nun, while its rule is that it should have two nuns, because one of the two nuns is a letter from the root of the word, from "anjā yunjī," and the other "nun" which comes to indicate the future, from the verb of a plural speaker reporting about themselves; for these are two letters, I mean the two nuns, of one kind, and the second of them is hidden from being pronounced in speech, so it was dropped in writing, and the written one was relied upon instead of the dropped one, as is done with the two letters where one is assimilated into the other.
* *
Some of the Kufans read it with this meaning, except that he assimilated the second nun and doubled the jim.
* *
Another of them read it with a doubled jim and a fatha on the ya', meaning it was done to him from: "najjaytuhu, unajjihi" (I rescued him, I rescue him).
* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 110 (part 3 of 3):

Some of the Meccan readers (al-qurra') recited it as "فَنَجَا مَنْ نَشَاءُ" with a fatha on the nun and without doubling, from "najā yanjū" (to be saved).[[In the manuscript: "من نجا عذاب الله من نشاء ينجو" and in the printed edition: "من نجا من عذاب الله من نشاء ينجو". The word "من" was added to make the sentence grammatically sound. However, I am certain that the correct reading is what I have recorded, as was done with its counterparts above, and the copyist added what he added in error.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading of this, in our view, is the reading of the one who recited "فَنُنْجِي مَنْ نَشَاءُ" with two nuns, because that is the reading upon which the readers in the major cities (al-amsar) agree. Whoever departs from it by some of the variants we have mentioned stands alone in his recitation against the proof on which the readers have united. It is not permissible to oppose what has been widely transmitted as the recitation of the readers of the major cities.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: "So We save the messengers and whom We will of Our believing servants when Our help comes," as related:
20037 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "فَنُنْجِي مَنْ نَشَاءُ" (fa-nunji man nasha'): "So We save the messengers and whom We will" = ﴿and Our punishment is not averted from the criminal people﴾. That was because God, blessed and exalted, sent the messengers, and they called their peoples and informed them that whoever obeyed would be saved, and whoever disobeyed would be punished and perish.
* *
His saying ﴿and Our punishment is not averted from the criminal people﴾ means: Our retribution and Our seizing will not be turned back from those among the people of disbelief in Us whom We seize, and from the people who committed crimes, disbelieving in God, opposing His messengers and what they brought them from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 111:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding. It [the Qur'an] is not a narration invented, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, in the stories of Joseph and his brothers there is a lesson for people of intellect and reason, by which they may take heed, and an admonition by which they may be warned. [[See the explanation of "qisas" (stories) above, vol. 15, p. 558, note 1, and the references there.

And the explanation of "ibrah" (lesson) above, vol. 6, pp. 242–243.]] That is because God, may His praise be exalted, after Joseph had been thrown into the well to perish, and then sold as a slave for a base price, and after captivity and long imprisonment, made him king of Egypt, established him in the land, raised him above those among his brothers who had intended him harm, and brought him together with his parents and brothers by His power, after a long period, bringing them to him from a distant, remote journey. Then He, may His praise be exalted, said to the polytheists of Quraysh, from the people of His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Indeed, there was for you, O people, in their stories a lesson, if you had taken heed from it: that He who did that to Joseph and his brothers is not incapable of doing the like for Muhammad ﷺ, [[In the printed edition: "an yaf'al mithlahu" (that he should do the like of it), a misreading of the manuscript, with "an" added on its own account.]] by bringing him out from among you, then making him prevail over you, establishing him in the lands, and supporting him with armies and men from among followers and companions, even if hardships befall him and days, nights, eras and times pass over him.

* *

Mujahid used to say: The meaning of that is: Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for Joseph and his brothers.

Narrations to this effect:

20038 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson﴾, for Joseph and his brothers.

20039 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: a lesson for Joseph and his brothers.

20040 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

20041 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding﴾, he said: Joseph and his brothers.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Although this view which Mujahid stated has a meaning that the interpretation can bear, what we have said about it is more fitting, because this comes right after the report about our Prophet ﷺ and his people among the polytheists, and right after their threats and warnings concerning disbelief in God and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and it is detached from the report about Joseph and his brothers. Moreover, it is a general report about all people of understanding, that their stories are a lesson for them, not specified for some of them over others. Since the matter is as we have described, it is more likely to be a report that it is a lesson for others. The narration we mentioned from Mujahid, [from] the narration of Ibn Jurayj, [[I added "min" between the brackets to make the sentence sound right; it is not in the printed edition or the manuscript.]] is more likely to be from his own words, because that agrees with the view we have stated.

* *

His words: ﴿It is not a narration invented﴾ mean: this statement is not a narration that is fabricated, falsely attributed, or guessed at. [[See the explanation of "iftira'" (fabrication) above in the language indexes under (fa-ra-ya).]] As follows:

20042 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿It is not a narration invented﴾, and "al-fariyya" is lying.

* *

﴿But a confirmation of what was before it﴾: He says: but it is a confirmation of what was before it of the books of God that He sent down before it to His prophets, such as the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms, confirming all of them and bearing witness that all of them are truth from God. As follows:

20043 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿But a confirmation of what was before it﴾, and the Furqan is a confirmation of the books before it, and bears witness to them.

* *

His words: ﴿And a detailed explanation of all things﴾: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: it is also a detailed explanation of everything the servants need, from clarifying God's command and prohibition, His lawful and unlawful, and obedience and disobedience. [[See the explanation of "tafsil" (detailed explanation) above in the language indexes under (fa-sa-la).]]

* *

His words: ﴿And guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: it is a clarification of His command and a guidance for whoever has lost the path of truth and become blind to it, when he follows it and is guided by it out of his misguidance; and "mercy" for whoever believes in it and acts by what is in it, rescuing him from God's wrath and painful punishment, and bequeathing to him in the Hereafter His gardens and eternal abiding in lasting bliss. ﴿For a people who believe﴾ means: for a people who affirm the Qur'an and what is in it of God's promise and warning, His command and prohibition, so they act upon its commands and refrain from its prohibitions.

* *

End of the commentary on Surah Yusuf.
